instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C. Place peeled garlic cloves in a small oven-safe dish. Cover completely with olive oil. Add 2 thyme sprigs. Cook in oven for 45-60 minutes, until cloves are very soft and golden. Set aside.

Drain canned San Marzano tomatoes. Pass tomatoes through a fine-mesh sieve or food mill to create a smooth puree. Discard seeds and skins. In a small saucepan, combine puree with 50ml red wine. Simmer gently over low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened and flavors are concentrated. Season with salt and pepper.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Arrange small mounds (approx. 15g each) of finely grated Parmesan cheese, leaving space between them. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crisp. Remove from oven. Immediately drape over a rolling pin or bottle to create a curved shape, or leave flat. Let cool and harden.

Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper on all sides. Heat a heavy-bottomed skillet (cast iron preferred) over high heat until smoking. Add a thin layer of olive oil. Carefully place beef medallions in skillet. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness, forming a deep brown crust. Add 20g butter and remaining thyme sprigs to pan during last minute of cooking. Baste beef with melted butter.
Remove beef from skillet. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Rest for 5-7 minutes.

Reheat San Marzano puree gently. Place a spoonful of puree on one side of a large, warm plate. Create an artistic 'tear' or 'swirl' with the back of the spoon. Position one rested beef medallion beside the puree. Arrange 2-3 confit garlic cloves elegantly near the beef. Place one Parmesan tuile upright or gently leaning against the beef or puree. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Lemon & Olive Stuffed Cabbage Rolls
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents as a single, refined portion of Turkish Fermented Lemon & Olive Stuffed Cabbage Rolls. Three to four plump, tightly rolled cabbage parcels, each about 8 cm long and 3 cm wide, are arranged neatly in a slight arc on a handcrafted, matte cream-beige ceramic plate, leaving ample negative space. The blanched cabbage leaves are a soft, muted green, slightly translucent, revealing the tender, light-colored rice and herb-flecked filling within. A subtle sheen of olive oil coats the rolls. The surface of the rolls shows the distinct lines of the cabbage leaf wraps. Garnish includes a small sprig of fresh dill and a few paper-thin slices of fresh lemon, artfully placed to enhance natural color and texture. The background is minimalist, a light natural wood or stone surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly visible. Lighting is soft, natural, and diffused, highlighting the organic textures and earthy colors of the dish. A traditional small, ornate Turkish fork or a simple wooden spoon rests beside the plate. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced and uncrowded composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature, as is traditional for 'zeytinyağlı' dishes.
Offer a side of plain yogurt (or plant-based alternative) for a traditional accompaniment.
Serve with additional fresh lemon wedges for squeezing.

ingredients.name: Vegetable broth (made from cabbage trimmings, onion peels)

instructions: Prepare cabbage: Carefully remove outer leaves from cabbage. Blanch leaves in boiling salted water for 5-7 minutes until pliable. Drain. Cut out thick veins. Reserve inner cabbage core and trimmings for broth.
Make broth: Combine reserved cabbage core, trimmings, and onion peels in a pot. Add 1 litre water. Simmer for 30 minutes. Strain to get 750 ml broth.

Prepare filling: In a large bowl, combine rinsed rice, finely diced onions, finely chopped fermented lemons, chopped olives, tomato paste, chopped parsley, dill, mint, 50 ml olive oil, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes. Mix well.
Roll cabbage: Lay a blanched cabbage leaf flat. Place a spoonful of filling near the stem end. Fold in sides. Roll tightly from bottom to top. Repeat with remaining leaves and filling.

Arrange and cook: Line the bottom of a large pot with a few reserved blanched cabbage leaves or trimmings to prevent sticking. Tightly arrange rolled cabbage rolls in layers in the pot. Drizzle with remaining 50 ml olive oil.

Add liquid: Pour prepared vegetable broth over the rolls. Place a heatproof plate on top to keep rolls submerged. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, for 45-50 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Rest and serve: Remove from heat. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing cabbage trimmings and onion peels for a flavorful vegetable broth.
The use of fermented lemons adds a complex, tangy depth while extending the shelf life of ingredients.
This dish is naturally plant-forward, relying on rice and vegetables for its core.
traditional_techniques: Zeytinyağlı (dishes cooked in olive oil and served cold or at room temperature)
Sarma (the art of rolling fillings into leaves)

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef and Mushroom Risotto is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto features a fluid, creamy consistency that flows naturally across the plate. It is not molded or dry. Deeply seared 3cm chunks of beef and quartered golden-brown cremini mushrooms are distributed throughout the glossy, pale rice. The dish is finished with a sprinkle of finely minced fresh parsley. The bowl rests on a dark wood table in a modern bistro setting. A clean white cotton napkin and a polished silver spoon sit beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures of the tender meat and earthy mushrooms. The arrangement is professional, organic, and clean with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a shallow bowl (piatto piano) to allow the risotto to spread.
Provide extra grated Parmesan on the side.
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti.
instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pan. Set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until golden brown. Remove and set aside.
Lower heat to medium. Melt half the butter.
Add onion and garlic. Sauté until translucent.
Add rice. Toast for 2 minutes while stirring.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid evaporates.
Add one ladle of warm stock. Stir constantly until absorbed.
Repeat stock process until rice is al dente.
Fold in the seared beef and mushrooms.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining butter and parmesan.
Adjust consistency with a splash of stock if needed. Risotto must be fluid.
Garnish with parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Do not rinse the rice; the starch is essential for creaminess.
Ensure the stock is warm to maintain a consistent cooking temperature.
The beef should remain in whole chunks to preserve its juices.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Beef and Mushroom Bruschetta
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, inviting single serving of Savory Beef and Mushroom Bruschetta is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate with a slight rim, resting on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table. Two to three generous slices of golden-brown toasted baguette are piled high with a rich, savory topping. The topping features well-browned ground beef chunks, tender, earthy slices of cremini mushrooms, and finely diced, translucent onion, all glistening slightly from the flavorful sauce. Abundant grated Parmesan cheese crowns each bruschetta, with fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley scattered over. The arrangement is casual and natural, with components slightly overlapping, suggesting a home-cooked meal. The lighting is warm and natural, evoking a cozy kitchen setting. A casually placed, simple cloth napkin sits beside the plate, and a plain water glass is subtly visible in the soft-focused background, completing the homely scene.
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground beef. Cook until browned, breaking it apart with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Remove beef from skillet. Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook until mushrooms are tender and liquid has evaporated, about 7-10 minutes.

Return browned beef to the skillet with the mushroom mixture. Pour in beef broth. Simmer for 5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and liquid to reduce slightly. Season with salt and black pepper. Stir in half of the chopped parsley.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Arrange baguette slices on a baking sheet. Lightly brush with olive oil. Toast in the oven for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Spoon generous amounts of the beef and mushroom mixture onto each toasted baguette slice.
Top each bruschetta with freshly grated Parmesan cheese. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Mexican Rice with Roasted Corn
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant reddish-orange Mexican rice is artfully plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The fluffy, distinct rice grains are studded with golden roasted corn kernels and tender, charred julienned poblano peppers. Small, bright red diced tomatoes are interspersed throughout, along with finely minced white onion. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves garnishes the top, providing a fresh contrast. A bright lime wedge rests beside the rice. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin. In the background, subtly blurred, are a small terracotta serving bowl and a few warm corn tortillas, suggesting a traditional Mexican meal. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Offer a side of salsa fresca or crema
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss corn kernels and whole poblano pepper with 5 ml olive oil. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until corn is lightly charred and poblano skin blisters. Remove from oven.
Place roasted poblano in a sealed bag for 10 minutes. Peel, core, and dice the poblano. Set aside.
Roughly chop tomatoes and half of the onion. Blend with broth, garlic, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper until smooth. Set aside.
Finely dice remaining half of the onion. Heat 25 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add rice to the pot. Toast for 3-5 minutes, stirring constantly, until grains are slightly opaque.
Pour the blended tomato mixture over the rice. Stir well. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not stir during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice with a fork. Stir in roasted corn kernels and diced poblano pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with lime wedges.
notes: For extra heat, add a diced jalapeño or serrano pepper to the tomato blend.
Ensure the rice is fully covered with liquid during simmering for even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Ham and Potato Enchiladas
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a rustic, oval ceramic baking dish, showcasing a single portion of three golden-brown corn enchiladas. The tortillas are generously coated in a vibrant, rich red roja sauce, showing slight charring from roasted tomatoes and jalapenos. A blanket of melted, bubbly Monterey Jack cheese covers the top, with some edges slightly browned. Fresh, bright green chopped cilantro is sprinkled over the cheese, adding a pop of color and texture. The enchiladas are plump, hinting at the savory potato, diced ham, and black bean filling within. The baking dish rests on a simple wooden table surface. A small, clean white porcelain bowl holds a dollop of Mexican crema nearby, and a lime wedge is placed beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an inviting and hearty casual dining scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Mexican crema or sour cream.
Offer lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Accompany with a small side of arroz rojo (Mexican red rice).
Provide extra fresh cilantro for garnish.
instructions: Prepare Potato Filling: Boil diced potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain. Mash lightly. Mix mashed potatoes with diced ham and rinsed black beans. Season with salt and pepper.

Roast Sauce Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. On a baking sheet, toss halved tomatoes, chopped jalapenos, quartered onion, and garlic cloves with 15ml vegetable oil. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly charred.
Blend Roja Sauce: Transfer roasted vegetables to a blender. Add chicken broth, cumin, oregano, and chili powder. Blend until smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Prepare Tortillas: Heat remaining 15ml vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Briefly warm each tortilla for 10-15 seconds per side until pliable. Set aside.

Assemble Enchiladas: Spread a thin layer of roja sauce on the bottom of a 23x33 cm baking dish. Fill each warm tortilla with approximately 60g of the potato-ham-bean mixture. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the baking dish. Repeat for all tortillas.

Bake Enchiladas: Pour remaining roja sauce over the rolled enchiladas. Sprinkle evenly with shredded Monterey Jack cheese. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and sauce is simmering.
Serve: Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro. Serve hot with a dollop of Mexican crema or sour cream on the side.
notes: Adjust jalapeno quantity for desired spice level.
For a vegetarian option, omit ham and add more beans or corn.
traditional_techniques: Warming tortillas to make them pliable.

recipes.recipe_name: Duck Prosciutto with Compressed Fig, Black Garlic Puree, and Chili Oil
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine, matte white bone china plate, allowing abundant negative space. Thin, translucent slices of rich, ruby-red duck prosciutto are draped naturally, creating soft, organic folds on one side of the plate. Adjacent, a cluster of deep purple-brown compressed fig quarters, their cut sides revealing a dense, jewel-like flesh, are thoughtfully arranged. Their surface glistens subtly from the balsamic infusion. Small, artful smears of a glossy, jet-black black garlic puree are strategically placed on the white plate, providing a striking contrast. A delicate drizzle of vibrant, clear red chili oil weaves across the figs and prosciutto, adding a subtle sheen and a pop of color. A few tiny, vibrant green micro arugula leaves are precisely placed atop the figs, offering a fresh accent. The overall composition is asymmetrical and fluid, emphasizing natural shapes and textures with architectural precision. The plate rests on a polished dark grey marble surface. A single, precisely folded white linen napkin and a silver fork are positioned elegantly to the side. Dramatic, focused lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sculptural quality.

ingredients.name: Dried Red Chilies (e.g., Arbol or Calabrian, deseeded)

instructions: Place black garlic cloves in a small blender. Add 5 ml extra virgin olive oil. Blend until a smooth, thick puree forms. Season with a pinch of flaky sea salt. Set aside.

Heat remaining 45 ml extra virgin olive oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add deseeded dried red chilies. Gently infuse for 10 minutes. Do not burn chilies. Strain oil through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding chilies. Let cool completely.

Wash and pat figs dry. Quarter each fig. Place fig quarters in a vacuum seal bag with aged balsamic vinegar. Vacuum seal on high pressure. Alternatively, place figs and balsamic in a small, rigid container, cover tightly, and refrigerate for 30 minutes, turning occasionally.
Arrange 30 g of duck prosciutto slices artfully on each plate, allowing natural folds. Place 4-5 compressed fig quarters around the prosciutto.

Dot small amounts of black garlic puree artfully on the plate. Drizzle a small amount of chili oil over the figs and prosciutto. Garnish with a few micro arugula or micro basil leaves. Finish with a tiny pinch of flaky sea salt and a grind of black pepper over the prosciutto and figs.

recipes.recipe_name: Compressed Fig, Whipped Feta, and Crispy Bacon Bites
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a large, matte white or light grey modern designer sharing platter, showcasing an ultra-minimalist, artistic composition with abundant negative space. Irregularly shaped, deep purple compressed fig cubes are artfully scattered, their glossy surfaces reflecting light. Adjacent to them, delicate, ethereal clouds of whipped feta are piped, their pristine white offering a stark, creamy contrast. Scattered amongst these elements are amber-hued, shatteringly crisp bacon shards, providing a textural crunch and savory depth. A vibrant, clear red chili-infused olive oil is precisely drizzled in a flowing, organic line across the composition. The dish is garnished sparingly with tiny, fresh green thyme leaves. The setting features a pristine white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, focused lighting casts elegant shadows, highlighting the dish's sophisticated textures and colors against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lay bacon strips on a baking sheet. Bake 12-15 minutes until very crisp. Drain on paper towels. Cool completely. Break into irregular shards.

Wash and quarter the figs. In a small bowl, combine 50 ml water, white balsamic vinegar, and honey. Place fig quarters in a vacuum seal bag with the liquid. Vacuum seal to compress. Refrigerate 30 minutes. If no vacuum sealer, gently simmer figs in the liquid for 5 minutes until just tender. Cool completely and drain.

Combine feta cheese, heavy cream, and 15 ml olive oil in a high-speed blender. Blend until perfectly smooth and airy. Pass the whipped feta through a fine-mesh sieve for an ultra-smooth consistency. Transfer to a piping bag.

Thinly slice the red chili. In a small saucepan, gently warm 85 ml olive oil with the sliced chili over very low heat for 10 minutes. Do not let it smoke. Remove from heat and let steep 15 minutes. Strain the chili oil through a fine sieve, discarding the solids.

To plate, arrange the compressed fig cubes artfully on a large sharing platter. Pipe small, delicate dots or quenelles of the whipped feta around the figs. Scatter the crispy bacon shards amongst the components. Drizzle the chili-infused olive oil in an elegant, flowing line across the dish. Garnish sparingly with tiny fresh thyme leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Fig, Whipped Feta, Tomato Fluid Gel
recipes.visual_description: A single small starter portion is presented on a pristine, matte white bone china plate. Abundant negative space surrounds the elegantly arranged components. Two caramelized, halved figs, their deep purplish-brown skin contrasting with the lighter, honey-glazed cut surface, are nestled beside a creamy, organic swirl of whipped white feta. A delicate, translucent ruby-red pool of tomato fluid gel glistens nearby, its vibrant color providing a precise counterpoint. A sparse scattering of vibrant red chili threads adds a subtle pop of color and texture, complemented by a few tiny, verdant micro basil leaves. The arrangement is natural and flowing, avoiding rigid geometry. The plate rests on a luxurious grey-veined marble surface, illuminated by dramatic, focused lighting casting soft shadows, with an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Prepare Tomato Fluid Gel: Blend tomatoes. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve to extract clear juice (approx. 200ml). Heat juice gently. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a simmer, whisking constantly for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set (approx. 1 hour). Once set, blend the gel until smooth and fluid. Pass through a fine sieve. Keep chilled.
Prepare Whipped Feta: Combine feta cheese and cream cheese in a food processor. Process until very smooth and light. Season with black pepper. Transfer to a piping bag or small bowl. Keep chilled.

Sear Figs: Halve each fig lengthwise. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Place fig halves cut-side down. Sear for 2-3 minutes until caramelized and slightly softened. Drizzle with honey during the last minute of searing.

Assemble: On each plate, create a small, organic swirl or dollop of whipped feta. Place two seared fig halves next to the feta. Gently spoon a small pool or delicate line of tomato fluid gel onto the plate. Garnish precisely with a few red chili threads and micro basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Fig, Whipped Feta, Tomato Consommé
recipes.visual_description: An individual starter portion is presented on a pristine round white bone china plate, showcasing a minimalist, organic composition. Two seared fig halves, their deep purple skins contrasting with the golden-brown caramelized flesh, are placed with their cut sides facing upwards. Beside them, a perfectly formed quenelle of ethereal white whipped feta rests delicately. A translucent, golden almond tuile shard stands elegantly, adding architectural height and crisp texture. A small pool of clear, amber-hued tomato consommé encircles the figs, providing a subtle sheen. The dish is garnished with two tiny, vibrant green basil micro-leaves, adding a precise pop of color. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing their individual beauty and precision. The setting features a premium grey-veined Carrara marble surface, a precisely folded white linen napkin, and dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows, creating an ultra-minimalist, luxurious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Tomato Consommé: Roughly chop tomatoes. Combine with thyme, crushed garlic, a pinch of sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a pot. Add 100 ml water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 15 minutes. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids gently to extract liquid. Discard solids. Allow liquid to cool. Whisk egg white lightly. Stir egg white into cooled tomato liquid. Return to low heat. Bring slowly to a simmer without stirring, allowing a raft to form. Simmer 10 minutes. Carefully ladle clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Whipped Feta: Crumble feta into a food processor. Add 50 ml olive oil and 20 ml water. Process until very smooth and airy, scraping down sides. Season with black pepper. Transfer to a piping bag or small bowl. Keep chilled.

Prepare Almond Tuiles: Preheat oven to 160°C. Finely grind blanched almonds in a food processor. In a small bowl, whisk melted butter, 10 ml water, and flour until smooth. Stir in ground almonds. Spread mixture very thinly (almost transparent) onto a silicone baking mat. Bake 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Remove from oven, let cool completely on the mat until firm. Break into irregular, delicate shards.

Sear Figs: Halve each fig lengthwise. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Place figs cut-side down. Sear 2-3 minutes until caramelized and slightly softened. Remove from heat. Deglaze pan with white wine vinegar, swirling to coat figs.

Plate Dish: Place two seared fig halves on one side of each plate, cut-side up. Pipe or carefully spoon a small quenelle of whipped feta next to the figs. Artistically place one almond tuile shard on the plate. Pour a small amount of warm tomato consommé around the figs, or serve in a small, elegant shot glass beside the main plate. Garnish with 1-2 tiny fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Chai-Spiced Chocolate Cheesecake
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of Chai-Spiced Chocolate Cheesecake rests on a clean white porcelain plate. The cheesecake exhibits a smooth, glossy, deep brown surface from the rich chocolate, contrasting with the lighter, golden-brown biscuit crust visible at its base. The slice is cleanly cut, revealing the dense, creamy texture within. A delicate scattering of finely grated dark chocolate shavings adorns the top. The plate features moderate negative space, enhancing the dessert's presentation. A small, simple silver dessert fork is placed beside the plate on a light wooden table surface. The scene is bathed in soft, natural, even lighting, creating a refined bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Grease and line a 20cm springform pan.
Crush digestive biscuits into fine crumbs. Mix with melted butter. Press firmly into the bottom of the prepared pan. Bake for 10 minutes. Cool.
In a large bowl, beat softened cream cheese and sugar until smooth.
Beat in eggs one at a time until just combined. Do not overmix.
Stir in sour cream, vanilla extract, and cooled chai tea.
Gently fold in melted dark chocolate until streaks disappear.
Pour filling over the cooled crust.
Place springform pan in a larger roasting pan. Pour hot water into the roasting pan to reach halfway up the sides of the springform pan (water bath).
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until edges are set but center still jiggles slightly.
Turn off oven. Leave cheesecake in oven with door ajar for 1 hour.
Remove from water bath. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Chill in refrigerator for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, before serving.
Garnish with chocolate shavings before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Goat Milk Donuts
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, Chocolate gluten-free dairy-free donuts American cuisine, Gluten-free dairy-free (cow-free) non-egg goat milk Donuts with dark glaze!
recipes.visual_description: A comforting display of baked chocolate goat milk donuts, presented on an everyday ceramic plate with a rustic, slightly chipped rim. The donuts are dark brown, with a smooth, glossy dark chocolate glaze that coats the top. A few donuts are casually stacked, some slightly overlapping, showing their natural round shape. One donut might be gently broken to reveal its tender, moist interior texture. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and minor imperfections. instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a donut pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together rice flour, 50g cocoa powder, granulated sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
In a separate medium bowl, whisk together goat milk, melted cocoa butter, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spoon batter into a piping bag or a large Ziploc bag with a corner snipped off. Pipe batter evenly into donut pan cavities, filling about two-thirds full.
Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.

Dip cooled donuts into the dark glaze. Place back on the wire rack to allow excess glaze to drip off and set.

Ensure cocoa butter is fully melted before incorporating into wet ingredients.

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 6-cavity donut pan.
Melt cocoa butter gently. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk together rice flour, cocoa powder, sugar, baking powder, and salt.

Slowly whisk the melted cocoa butter into the wet ingredients.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spoon batter into prepared donut cavities. Fill about two-thirds full.
Bake 10-12 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Cool donuts in pan for 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

Dip top of each cooled donut into glaze. Place back on wire rack to set.
Serve immediately or store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Gluten-Free Goat Milk Chocolate Cake
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, Chocolate gluten-free dairy-free donuts American cuisine, Gluten-free dairy-free (cow-free) goat milk Donut!
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of dark chocolate cake is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dessert plate. The cake features three distinct layers of moist, rich, dark brown crumb, separated by generous, glossy layers of smooth, dark cocoa butter chocolate frosting. The top of the slice is also covered with a thin, even layer of the same frosting. A delicate dusting of fine cocoa powder lightly covers the top surface. Beside the cake, a single fresh, vibrant red raspberry is placed as a simple, contrasting garnish. The plate rests on a warm-toned simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver dessert fork. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the cake's textures and deep chocolate color, with a subtle, blurred restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled with a dessert fork.
Pair with a glass of goat milk or coffee.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 15 cm round cake pans with rice flour.
In a large bowl, whisk together rice flour, cocoa powder, granulated sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together goat milk, eggs, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.
Stir in hot water until batter is smooth and thin.
Divide batter evenly between prepared cake pans.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cakes in pans for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
For the cocoa butter chocolate frosting, melt cocoa butter in a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of simmering water. Do not let water touch bowl.
Remove from heat. Whisk in powdered sugar and 30 ml of goat milk until smooth. Add more goat milk, 5 ml at a time, until desired spreading consistency is reached.
Once cakes are completely cool, level tops if needed. Place one cake layer on a serving plate.
Spread a generous layer of cocoa butter chocolate frosting over the first cake layer.
Place the second cake layer on top. Frost the top and sides of the cake evenly.
Garnish with fresh raspberries if desired.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are at room temperature for best cake texture.
Use high-quality unsweetened cocoa powder for rich flavor.
For a thicker frosting, reduce the amount of goat milk used.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken & Artichoke Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Rustic Chicken & Artichoke Bake is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight off-white glaze, showcasing its comforting, hearty appeal. Thick chunks of golden-seared chicken breast are nestled in a creamy, off-white sauce, visibly studded with tender, quartered artichoke hearts and dark, firm black beans. The sauce has a rich, slightly bubbly texture from baking. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a touch of freshness. The chicken is plump and juicy, retaining its natural shape. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, suggesting a home kitchen setting. Soft, warm overhead lighting illuminates the dish, creating a cozy atmosphere. A simple, silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a casually placed, textured linen napkin.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in cottage cheese, grated Parmesan, chicken broth, and oregano. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring constantly.
Return seared chicken breasts to the skillet. Add quartered artichoke hearts and rinsed black beans around the chicken.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Sauce should be bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Gluten-Free Goat Milk Chocolate Sheet Cake with Cocoa Butter Ganache

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 23x33 cm baking pan with rice flour.
Whisk rice flour, cocoa powder, granulated sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk goat milk, vegetable oil, eggs, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Stir in hot water. Batter will be thin.
Pour batter into prepared pan. Spread evenly.
Bake 30-35 minutes. Or until a toothpick inserted into center comes out clean.
Cool cake completely in pan on a wire rack.
For the Ganache: Melt cocoa butter in a heatproof bowl over a double boiler or in short microwave bursts.
Whisk in cocoa powder and powdered sugar until smooth.
Gradually whisk in goat milk until ganache is smooth and pourable.
Stir in vanilla extract and a pinch of salt.
Assembly: Pour ganache evenly over cooled cake.
Allow ganache to set slightly before slicing.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are at room temperature for best results.
Do not overbake the cake; it will dry out.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken Sausage Artichoke Soup
recipes.special_requests: low carb, easy to cook cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Chicken Sausage Artichoke Soup is presented in a deep, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. The rich, golden-amber chicken broth cradles generous chunks of browned chicken breast (2-3 cm cubes) and thick slices of savory Italian sausage (1 cm rounds). Quartered artichoke hearts, retaining their natural green-grey hue, are nestled among the meats, alongside soft, translucent diced onion. The soup is topped with a generous layer of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and a vibrant sprinkle of roughly chopped fresh green parsley. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm wooden dining table with visible grain, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen. A simple, off-white linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and inviting, creating a cozy and comforting atmosphere. A sturdy, rustic soup spoon rests next to the bowl. The presentation is homely, unpretentious, and inviting, emphasizing comfort and rustic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed green beans or a simple mixed green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar for a complete low-carb meal.

ingredients.name: Canned artichoke hearts (packed in water, drained)

instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2-3 cm cubes. Slice sausage into 1 cm rounds. Dice onion. Mince garlic. Quarter drained artichoke hearts.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add sausage slices. Cook until browned on all sides. Remove sausage from pot. Set aside.
Add chicken cubes to the pot. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return cooked chicken and sausage to the pot. Add quartered artichoke hearts. Simmer for 10-15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Ladle soup into bowls. Grate fresh Parmesan cheese over each serving. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: For an extra layer of flavor, brown the sausage and chicken well to create fond at the bottom of the pot.
Adjust seasoning to your preference. A pinch of red pepper flakes can add a subtle kick.

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a 6-cavity donut pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together rice flour, 50g cocoa powder, granulated sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk oat milk, 60g melted cocoa butter, vanilla extract, and apple cider vinegar.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Whisk until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spoon batter into a piping bag or a large Ziploc bag with a corner snipped off.
Pipe batter evenly into donut cavities, filling about two-thirds full.

recipes.recipe_name: Poached Chicken Mousse Canapés with Artichoke & Chard Crisp
recipes.visual_description: An elegant array of 8-12 canapés presented on a premium white Carrara marble slab. Each canapé features a small, pale green dollop of smooth artichoke purée. Adjacent to it, a perfectly formed, airy quenelle of off-white chicken mousse sits with architectural precision. A delicate, irregular dark green Swiss chard crisp is artfully placed atop the mousse, providing a textural contrast. A precise, vibrant red-orange drizzle of chili-garlic oil adds a final touch of color and sheen. The arrangement is minimalist, with abundant negative space between each element, creating a sophisticated and refined visual. The setting is clean, with a pristine white linen napkin folded precisely in the background, under dramatic professional lighting with soft shadows.
instructions: Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Cool. Finely shred or chop chicken.
For chicken mousse, combine shredded chicken, cottage cheese, 15g grated Parmesan, a pinch of salt and pepper. Blend until smooth. Adjust seasoning.
For artichoke purée, blend drained artichoke hearts with 10ml olive oil and a splash of chicken poaching liquid until very smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
For Swiss chard crisps, blanch chard leaves briefly. Pat dry thoroughly. Brush with a thin layer of olive oil. Bake at 150°C until crisp, about 10-15 minutes. Break into irregular pieces.
For chili-garlic oil, thinly slice 1 garlic clove and combine with dried chili flakes in 40ml olive oil. Gently heat until fragrant, do not brown garlic. Strain solids.
Finely dice remaining garlic clove and a small amount of onion. Sauté until translucent. Incorporate into the chicken mousse for subtle flavor if desired.

To assemble, place a small dollop of artichoke purée on a serving platter. Form a small quenelle or mound of chicken mousse next to the purée. Top with a Swiss chard crisp. Drizzle with chili-garlic oil. Repeat for 8-12 pieces.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Swiss Chard Fritters with Spicy Black Bean Dip
recipes.visual_description: Small, round chicken and Swiss chard fritters are arranged casually on a clean, white porcelain sharing platter, with some negative space around them. The fritters are golden-brown on the exterior with visible flecks of dark green Swiss chard and light specks of parmesan. Their interiors are tender and moist, revealing finely diced chicken and small pieces of pasta. A small, white ceramic ramekin of creamy, dark purple-black spicy black bean dip sits beside the fritters. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green cilantro is scattered over the fritters, and a few leaves adorn the dip, providing a fresh contrast. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting. The overall presentation is professional and approachable, highlighting the quality ingredients and refined casual nature of the snack.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water until cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Cool completely. Finely dice or shred the cooked chicken.
Wash Swiss chard. Remove tough stems. Finely chop the leaves.
Finely dice the onion. Mince 2 garlic cloves.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and chopped Swiss chard. Sauté until chard is wilted and tender, about 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat and cool.
Cook small pasta according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well. Finely chop the cooked pasta.

In a large bowl, combine diced chicken, sautéed onion and chard mixture, chopped pasta, grated Parmesan, cottage cheese, and 3 grams of dried chili flakes. Season with salt and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Form the mixture into small, uniform fritter patties, about 3 cm in diameter and 1 cm thick. This recipe should yield approximately 16-20 fritters.

Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Place fritters in the hot pan without overcrowding. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through.

For the black bean dip, mince the remaining 2 garlic cloves. In a food processor, combine rinsed black beans, minced garlic, remaining 2 grams of dried chili flakes, and 30 ml of water (or more for desired consistency). Process until smooth and creamy. Season with salt to taste.
Serve chicken and Swiss chard fritters immediately with the spicy black bean dip on the side. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Molten Chocolate Cake with Goat Milk Crémeux and Cocoa Nibs Tuile
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, Chocolate gluten-free dairy-free donuts American cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated dessert centered on a pristine white bone china plate. A dark, rich molten chocolate cake, perfectly round with a slightly crisp exterior, sits as the focal point, its top gently domed. Beside it, a single, perfectly formed quenelle of creamy, off-white goat milk crémeux rests, its surface smooth and inviting. Two or three irregular, thin shards of dark brown cocoa nibs tuile are artfully placed, leaning against the cake and crémeux, providing sharp textural contrast. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing their precise placement and the dish's minimalist design. The composition is organic and flowing, avoiding rigid geometry. Lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows that highlight the textures of the cake's crust, the crémeux's smoothness, and the tuile's delicate crispness. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface with a crisply folded white linen napkin in the corner, conveying a sophisticated, high-end dining experience.
instructions: Prepare Goat Milk Crémeux: In a saucepan, combine goat milk, heavy cream, and vanilla bean paste. Heat until simmering. In a bowl, whisk egg yolks and 50g granulated sugar until pale. Gradually temper the hot milk mixture into the egg yolk mixture. Return to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon (82°C). Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. Chill completely over an ice bath. Once cold, churn in an ice cream maker according to manufacturer's instructions until desired consistency. Transfer to a container and freeze.

Prepare Cocoa Nibs Tuile: Preheat oven to 160°C. In a bowl, cream softened butter and powdered sugar until light. Whisk in egg white until smooth. Fold in rice flour and cocoa nibs. Spread a very thin, even layer of batter onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely. Break into irregular shards.

Prepare Molten Chocolate Cake: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease and lightly flour four 150ml ramekins with rice flour. In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water, melt cocoa butter. Remove from heat. Whisk in cocoa powder until smooth. In a separate bowl, whisk remaining 50g granulated sugar, eggs, and egg yolks until light and fluffy. Gradually fold the melted chocolate mixture into the egg mixture. Gently fold in rice flour and salt until just combined. Divide batter evenly among prepared ramekins. Bake for 12-14 minutes, or until edges are set but center is still soft and molten. Let rest 1 minute.

Plate the dish: Invert each molten chocolate cake onto the center of a chilled dessert plate. Place a small quenelle of goat milk crémeux beside the cake. Arrange 2-3 cocoa nibs tuile shards artistically around the cake and crémeux. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Artichoke Stuffed Conchiglie
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of Creamy Chicken and Artichoke Stuffed Conchiglie is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Three large, plump pasta shells are nestled in a vibrant, rich red tomato sauce, which pools elegantly around them. The shells are visibly stuffed with a creamy, textured filling of shredded chicken, finely chopped swiss chard, and small diced artichoke pieces. A light golden-brown crust from baked parmesan cheese glistens atop some shells. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese is lightly sprinkled over the dish, and a few bright green basil leaves are artfully placed for a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a fork, knife, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.

ingredients.name: swiss chard, tough stems removed, finely chopped
canned artichoke hearts, drained and finely diced
Salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions: Cook chicken: Place chicken breasts in a saucepan. Cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 15-20 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken, cool slightly, then shred using two forks.
Cook pasta: While chicken cooks, boil conchiglie shells in salted water according to package directions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.

Prepare filling: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and chopped swiss chard. Cook until chard wilts, about 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, cooked onion-chard mixture, diced artichoke hearts, cottage cheese, and 100 g Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Prepare sauce: In the same skillet, add crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Assemble: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Spread about half of the tomato sauce evenly on the bottom of a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Carefully stuff each cooked conchiglie shell with the chicken and cheese filling. Arrange stuffed shells in a single layer over the sauce in the baking dish.
Pour remaining tomato sauce over the stuffed shells. Sprinkle generously with extra Parmesan cheese.
Bake: Cover the baking dish with foil. Bake for 20 minutes. Remove foil and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes, until cheese is bubbly and lightly golden.
Serve: Let rest for a few minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef and Mushroom Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Slow-Braised Beef and Mushroom Stew is presented in a deep, wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. The rich, dark brown, glossy gravy coats tender, substantial 3-4 cm chunks of braised beef. Plump, sautéed cremini mushroom halves and whole, soft pearl onions are interspersed throughout the stew. Bright orange carrot rounds provide a pop of color. The dish is generously sprinkled with vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley, adding freshness. A thick, golden-brown slice of toasted sourdough bread with a rustic crust leans elegantly against the bowl's rim. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, showcasing the hearty stew. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a neutral-toned cotton napkin placed neatly beside the bowl, and standard European flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and rich colors, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a casual restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette can complement the richness of the stew

ingredients.name: Mixed mushrooms (e.g., cremini, shiitake)
ingredients.quantity: 400g, cleaned, larger ones halved or quartered

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled, cut into 2 cm rounds

instructions: Pat beef chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Dredge lightly in flour.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the pot. Add diced yellow onions and carrots. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender.
While stew simmers, melt remaining 15g butter in a separate pan over medium heat.
Add pearl onions. Sauté until lightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes. Remove from pan.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
After beef is tender, stir in sautéed pearl onions and mushrooms into the stew. Simmer for another 15 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Toast sourdough bread slices until golden brown and crisp.
Ladle hot stew into deep bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with toasted sourdough.
notes: Ensure beef is well-browned for maximum flavor before braising.
For best results, use a good quality dry red wine that you would enjoy drinking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Fermented Potato Gratin and Charred Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Fermented Potato Gratin and Charred Broccoli is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The plate sits on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood surface. A thick, perfectly seared beef medallion, displaying a rich brown crust and tender interior, anchors the composition. Adjacent to the beef, a precisely cut rectangular portion of golden-brown fermented potato gratin shows layers of thinly sliced potatoes, with a subtly crisp, bubbling top. Scattered around the main elements are vibrant green charred broccoli florets, exhibiting distinct dark char marks and a tender-crisp texture, arranged organically to maintain white space. The overall presentation is minimalistic, clean, and highlights the natural beauty and textures of each ingredient. No excessive garnishes, only the pure form of the food. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, casting gentle shadows. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded neatly beside the plate. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural plant life in soft focus, emphasizing an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Peel potatoes. Slice thinly, 2-3mm thick. Use a mandoline for even slices.
In a bowl, combine crème fraîche, minced garlic, thyme leaves, 100ml vegetable broth, 5ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Layer potato slices tightly in a small oven-safe dish (approx. 20x15cm).
Pour crème fraîche mixture over potatoes. Ensure liquid covers potatoes.
Bake for 45-50 minutes. Potatoes should be tender. Top should be golden and bubbly.
Let gratin rest 10 minutes before serving.
Wash broccoli. Cut into medium florets. Use stem for vegetable stock if desired.
Toss florets with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Heat a cast iron pan or grill pan over high heat until smoking.
Add broccoli florets. Cook 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally. Florets should char in spots and remain tender-crisp.
Remove from heat.
Pat beef medallions dry with paper towel. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 10ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Add beef medallions. Sear 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove beef from pan. Let rest 5 minutes on a cutting board.
Cut gratin into 4 equal portions.
Place one gratin portion on each plate.
Place a seared beef medallion next to gratin.
Arrange charred broccoli florets naturally around the beef and gratin.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Broccoli Stem and Red Onion Turşu with Beef Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single small starter portion is presented on a cream-colored, handcrafted ceramic plate with an organic, slightly uneven rim. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. In the center, a small, artful mound of vibrant green fermented broccoli stem batons (2 cm long) is arranged naturally, interspersed with translucent, pale pink slivers of thinly sliced pickled red onion. The textures are crisp-tender and slightly yielding. A small, dark, glossy pool of rich beef glaze is drizzled alongside the turşu, catching the soft, natural light. The background is clean and minimalist, featuring a hint of an undyed linen napkin in natural beige and a small, culturally appropriate element like a tiny olive branch or a traditional Turkish tea glass in the soft focus. The composition is uncluttered, allowing ample negative space to highlight the dish. The entire plate is visible, showcasing an authentic Turkish starter presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refreshing meze to stimulate appetite.
Can be accompanied by a small piece of fresh, crusty bread.
instructions: Wash broccoli stems. Peel tough outer layer. Cut stems into 2 cm long batons.
Peel red onion. Slice thinly into half-moons.
Peel garlic cloves. Lightly crush.
Sterilize a 1-liter glass jar.
Pack broccoli batons and onion slices tightly into the jar. Distribute crushed garlic among vegetables.
In a saucepan, combine water, vinegar, and salt. Heat until salt dissolves. Do not boil.
Pour hot brine over vegetables in the jar. Ensure vegetables are fully submerged. Leave 2 cm headspace.

Seal jar tightly. Store at room temperature away from direct sunlight for 3-5 days. Burp daily if active fermentation occurs. Refrigerate once desired tanginess is reached. Fermentation time varies with temperature.
For the beef glaze, pour beef stock into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce stock by simmering uncovered until it thickens to a syrupy consistency. This takes 20-30 minutes. It should coat the back of a spoon. Set aside.
To serve, drain desired amount of fermented broccoli and onion. Arrange a small portion elegantly on a starter plate.
Drizzle a small amount of beef glaze over and around the turşu. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe utilizes often-discarded broccoli stems, promoting zero-waste cooking.
Fermentation extends the shelf life of seasonal vegetables and enhances flavor.
Adjust fermentation time based on desired sourness and crunch.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken, White Bean Puree, Fermented Chili Emulsion, Herb Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is elegantly presented on a pristine white bone china plate. A creamy, fluid swoosh of smooth white bean puree anchors the composition. Two thick, golden-crusted chunks of perfectly cooked chicken breast are arranged naturally on the puree, showcasing their tender interior. Vibrant crimson dots and delicate lines of glossy fermented chili emulsion are strategically placed around the chicken and puree, adding a striking color contrast and a hint of controlled heat. A light, artful scattering of golden-brown herb crumble, featuring tiny green flecks of parsley and chives, provides textural intrigue. Abundant negative space surrounds the central elements, emphasizing the minimalist aesthetic. The dish rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates subtle shadows, enhancing depth and sophistication. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits beside the plate, completing the refined setting.
instructions: For the White Bean Puree: Combine drained cannellini beans, chicken stock, and heavy cream in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes. Transfer to a high-speed blender. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For the Herb Crumble: Melt 20g butter in a small pan over medium heat. Add panko breadcrumbs. Toast until golden brown and crispy. Remove from heat. Stir in chopped parsley and chives. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.

For the Fermented Chili Emulsion: In a small bowl, combine fermented chili sauce and 15ml neutral oil. Whisk vigorously to emulsify. Gradually whisk in xanthan gum if desired, for stability. Set aside.

For the Chicken: Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml neutral oil and 30g butter in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Once butter foams, carefully place chicken breasts in the skillet. Sear 4-5 minutes until deep golden brown crust forms. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken 5 minutes before slicing.

To Plate: Spoon a generous dollop of warm white bean puree onto the center of each plate. Create a gentle swoosh. Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick chunks. Arrange chicken pieces artfully on the puree. Drizzle or dot the fermented chili emulsion around the chicken and puree. Sprinkle herb crumble sparingly over the dish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, White Bean Mousseline, Crispy Panko, Fermented Chili Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a crisp exterior, rests elegantly on a matte white designer plate. The chicken is presented as a thick, whole piece. Beside it, a flowing, organic swoosh of velvety smooth, creamy white bean mousseline provides a soft contrast. Scattered precisely near the chicken and mousseline are golden, crisp panko breadcrumbs, adding textural intrigue. A vibrant, deep amber fermented chili glaze is artfully drizzled over the chicken and around the plate, creating delicate lines and pooling subtly. A few emerald microgreens are meticulously placed as a minimal garnish. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting each element with architectural precision. The dish is set on a premium grey veined Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits beside the plate. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and sophistication. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring maximum focus on the meticulously crafted dish.

ingredients.name: Cannellini beans, canned, drained and rinsed
Fermented chili paste (e.g., Gochujang or specialty hot sauce)

instructions: Prepare chicken: Brine chicken breasts in 5% salt water solution for 30 minutes. Rinse thoroughly. Pat very dry with paper towels.

Cook chicken: Place chicken breasts in a vacuum-sealable bag. Seal, removing all air. Sous-vide at 63°C for 1.5 hours. Alternatively, pan-sear directly. If pan-searing, cook 6-8 minutes per side until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken 5 minutes.

Make mousseline: Melt 15g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add shallot; cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add drained cannellini beans and 150ml chicken stock. Simmer 5 minutes. Transfer to a high-speed blender. Add heavy cream and 20g butter. Blend until exceptionally smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare crispy panko: Melt remaining 15g butter in a small skillet over medium heat. Add panko. Toast, stirring constantly, until golden brown and crisp. Remove from heat. Season lightly with salt.

Create chili glaze: In a small saucepan, combine fermented chili paste, rice vinegar, honey, minced garlic, and remaining 100ml chicken stock. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until mixture thickens to a glossy glaze, about 8-10 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a smooth consistency.

Sear chicken (if not sous-vide): Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Sear chicken, skin-side down (if applicable), until golden brown and crisp, about 4-5 minutes. Flip. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from heat. Rest 5 minutes.

Assemble dish: Place a generous swoosh of white bean mousseline on one side of each plate. Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions or serve whole. Arrange chicken on or next to the mousseline. Drizzle fermented chili glaze artfully over and around the chicken. Sprinkle crispy panko next to the chicken. Garnish with a few microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Hot Honey Chicken with Smoked Black Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Crispy Hot Honey Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, crispy chicken thighs are centrally placed, their textured breading glistening with a light drizzle of reddish-orange hot honey glaze. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of dark, whole smoked black beans is spooned, showing a slight sheen. The chicken is whole, not sliced. Freshly chopped green chives are scattered over both the chicken and beans, providing a vibrant color contrast. The composition is balanced and professional, with appropriate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. A white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors, set against a subtle, blurred modern bistro background.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up a breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten eggs, one with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each chicken thigh in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs. Press crumbs firmly onto chicken.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add breaded chicken.
Cook chicken 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Place on a wire rack to rest.
In a small saucepan, combine hot sauce and honey. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Stir until well combined. Remove from heat.
In the same skillet (or a clean one), add drained black beans. Stir in smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder. Cook 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until heated through and fragrant.
Serve chicken immediately. Drizzle hot honey glaze over chicken. Spoon smoked black beans alongside. Garnish with fresh chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Green Pea Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Chicken and Green Pea Risotto is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto, with its fluid consistency, is mounded gently, revealing tender chicken chunks (2-3 cm diced) and vibrant green peas throughout. The chicken pieces are golden-brown from searing, contrasting with the pale, rich risotto. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped bright green parsley adorns the top, alongside a few scattered whole green peas, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish is clean, balanced, and inviting, resting on a simple light wooden surface. A silver spoon and a folded white linen napkin are placed beside the bowl. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors without harsh shadows. The presentation is professional yet approachable, emphasizing the dish's comforting elegance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto loses its ideal texture quickly.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a light, crisp Italian white wine.
instructions: Heat vegetable stock in a separate pot. Keep it hot over low heat.
Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from the pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the pot. Add finely diced shallot and minced garlic. Sauté until softened and fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the grains until translucent around the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Begin adding hot vegetable stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each ladleful to be mostly absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 18-20 minutes.
After about 15 minutes of adding stock, stir in the green peas and cooked chicken chunks.
Continue adding stock and stirring until the rice is al dente – tender but still with a slight bite. The risotto should be creamy and fluid, not stiff.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and freshly grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute to achieve a creamy consistency (mantecatura).
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half into the risotto.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure the vegetable stock is hot when adding to the rice; this prevents the cooking process from slowing down.
Stirring constantly is key to achieving the characteristic creamy texture of risotto.
Do not overcook the chicken; it will finish cooking in the risotto.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Mushroom Essence, Broccoli Puree, Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: The dish is plated on an exquisite, large round bone china plate, resting on a polished grey veined marble surface. A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, its skin deep golden-brown and exquisitely crisp, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Adjacent, a vibrant, silky-smooth broccoli puree forms an organic sweep, its rich green contrasting the chicken. Three slender, crisp-tender asparagus spears, bright green with subtle char, are artfully arranged, adding linear elegance. A glistening, amber-toned mushroom essence is delicately drizzled around the components, creating an abstract, fluid pattern on the pristine white negative space. The composition is minimalist, emphasizing ingredient quality and precision. A tiny sprig of fresh parsley provides a final, precise touch. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded precisely, and elegant silver flatware complete the luxurious setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp white wine, such as a Chardonnay or Sauvignon Blanc.
Present individually portioned, as is customary in fine dining.

ingredients.name: Mixed wild mushrooms
ingredients.quantity: 500g (400g for essence base, 100g sliced for sautéing)

instructions: Mushroom Essence:
Slice 400g mushrooms. Sauté mushrooms and 2 cloves crushed garlic in a dry pan until deeply browned.
Add 500ml chicken stock and 2 thyme sprigs. Simmer 30 minutes.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids.
Pass liquid through a coffee filter or cheesecloth for clear essence.
Reduce essence over low heat until concentrated (approx. 100ml). Season with salt. Keep warm.
Broccoli Puree:
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath.
Blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp (3-4 minutes).
Immediately transfer broccoli to ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Blend blanched broccoli with 50ml heavy cream, 2 cloves garlic, 15g butter, and a splash of cooking water if needed, until completely smooth.
Pass puree through a fine-mesh sieve for ultra-smooth texture. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Asparagus:
Trim woody ends from asparagus spears.
Blanch asparagus in boiling salted water for 1-2 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp.
Immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain well.
Lightly sear asparagus in a hot pan with a drizzle of olive oil for 1 minute to add char. Season with salt and a squeeze of lemon juice. Keep warm.
Chicken Breast:
Preheat water bath for sous-vide to 63°C.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Place in vacuum-seal bags.
Cook sous-vide for 1.5 hours.
Remove chicken from bags. Pat skin very dry with paper towels.
Heat 15g butter and 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp.
Flip chicken. Cook for 2-3 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest chicken 5 minutes before plating.
Plating:
Spoon a generous dollop of broccoli puree onto one side of each plate, creating an organic sweep or natural mound.
Place one pan-seared chicken breast (whole piece, not sliced) beside the puree.
Arrange 3 asparagus spears artfully next to the chicken or across the puree.
Drizzle mushroom essence around the chicken and puree.
Garnish with a few tiny parsley leaves or finely chopped parsley for color contrast.
notes: Ensure all purees and essences are perfectly smooth and warm before plating.
Pat chicken skin extremely dry for maximum crispness.
Do not overcrowd the plate; embrace negative space.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato, Mushroom, and Basil Salad with Roasted Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, homely salad presented on a simple ceramic plate. Diced roasted chicken pieces are casually mixed among halved bright red cherry tomatoes and earthy brown sautéed mushroom slices. Fresh green basil leaves are generously scattered throughout, adding a pop of color and freshness. The salad is lightly coated in a glossy, golden balsamic vinaigrette, showing a delicate sheen. Shaved Parmesan cheese curls are sprinkled over the top, adding a creamy white contrast. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, reflecting a home-cooked meal. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by everyday flatware and a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the dressing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Season chicken breast with salt and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest, then dice into 1-2 cm cubes.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add sliced mushrooms and cook until golden and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine halved cherry tomatoes, cooked mushrooms, diced roasted chicken, and fresh basil.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 45ml olive oil, balsamic vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Add mixed greens to the bowl if using. Toss lightly.
Transfer salad to serving plates. Garnish with shaved Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Refined Beef Consommé with Mushroom Cappelletti and Potato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Refined Beef Consommé is presented in a wide, shallow, matte white bone china bowl, resting on a polished grey veined marble surface. The consommé is a brilliant, deep amber, perfectly clear. At the center, three to four delicate, golden-hued Cappelletti are artfully arranged, showcasing their elegant folded shape. Alongside, three to four small, impeccably turned white potato spheres sit, smooth and pristine. A subtle, dark amber drizzle of honey-balsamic reduction gently swirls across the elements. The composition is minimalist and precise, with abundant negative space. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a sharp triangle, is placed to the side. Dramatic, professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's architectural precision and premium textures. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish remains the sole focus.
instructions: Prepare Consommé Base: Cut beef shin into large chunks. Roast beef bones and shin in oven at 200°C for 30 minutes until browned. Rough chop 150g carrots, 150g onions, and all celery. In a large stock pot, brown roasted beef and bones. Add chopped vegetables, tomatoes, tomato paste. Sauté 5 minutes. Deglaze with red wine. Add thyme, bay leaves, peppercorns, and cold water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer gently for 4-6 hours, skimming impurities. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill overnight.

Clarify Consommé: Skim all fat from chilled broth. In a separate bowl, mix ground beef, remaining 100g finely diced carrots, 100g finely diced onions, and egg whites. Slowly whisk this raft mixture into the cold broth. Heat gently, stirring constantly until raft forms. Stop stirring. Simmer for 1 hour without disturbing. Carefully ladle clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Season with salt.

Prepare Cappelletti Filling: Remove 100g tender beef from the braised shin. Finely chop. Dice mushrooms finely. Sauté mushrooms in olive oil until golden. Add chopped braised beef. Cook 2 minutes. Cool. Mix with grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Season.

Form Cappelletti: Roll fresh pasta dough very thin. Cut into 5cm squares. Place a small amount of filling in the center of each square. Fold into triangles. Press edges to seal. Bring two opposite points of the triangle together and press to form a cappelletto. If using dried cappelletti, cook al dente.

Prepare Potato Spheres: Peel potatoes. Use a melon baller to create small, uniform spheres (approx. 2cm diameter). Blanch potato spheres in salted boiling water until tender but firm (approx. 5-7 minutes). Drain. Keep warm.
Prepare Honey-Balsamic Reduction: In a small saucepan, combine honey and balsamic vinegar. Bring to a simmer. Reduce until slightly thickened and syrupy. Do not over-reduce.

Assemble and Serve: Bring clarified consommé to a gentle simmer. Cook cappelletti in the consommé until tender (2-3 minutes for fresh, longer for dried). For each serving, place 3-4 cappelletti and 3-4 potato spheres in a wide, shallow bowl. Ladle hot consommé around the elements. Drizzle a small amount of honey-balsamic reduction over the elements. Serve immediately.
notes: Achieving a perfectly clear consommé requires patience and careful skimming.
The quality of beef and red wine significantly impacts the consommé's depth of flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Chicken, Chickpea, and Lentil Tagine
recipes.visual_description: Chicken pieces, braised until fork-tender, are nestled amongst plump chickpeas and soft lentils in a rich, amber-hued sauce. The sauce, naturally thickened, glistens with a hint of olive oil, showcasing flecks of aromatic spices. Bright green chopped cilantro and parsley are generously sprinkled over the dish, providing a fresh contrast. Tangy, golden preserved lemon wedges and dark, briny Kalamata olives are strategically placed, adding bursts of color and flavor. The dish is served in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl or a traditional tagine base. The chicken is presented as whole pieces. The background features a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and a subtle traditional Moroccan tea glass, bathed in soft, natural light, creating an inviting, authentic casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fluffy couscous
Accompany with warm crusty khobz (Moroccan flatbread) for scooping

ingredients.name: Preserved lemon, rind only, thinly sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or tagine over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side 3 minutes. Remove chicken; set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, drained chickpeas, and rinsed green lentils.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them into the liquid and vegetables.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot.
Braise for 45-50 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is fork-tender. Lentils should be cooked through.
Stir in the thinly sliced preserved lemon rind and pitted Kalamata olives.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Chicken and Potato Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Aloo Murgh is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. A mound of fluffy, steamed long-grain basmati rice occupies one side. Beside it, the curry features large 4cm chunks of moist chicken and 3cm cubes of tender potato. The sauce is a rich, deep orange-brown with visible textures of sautéed onions. Two bright green chilies, slit lengthwise, are nestled among the chicken pieces. Freshly chopped green coriander is scattered across the curry for contrast. The bowl rests on a rustic dark wood surface. A small side dish of pickled vegetables and a copper spoon accompany the meal. Natural light emphasizes the glossy sauce and soft textures of the rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lime wedges
Accompany with mango chutney
Traditional copper serving spoon
Serve with warm garlic naan
instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Soak in water for 20 minutes.
Boil 600ml water. Add soaked rice. Simmer 12 minutes until tender. Drain.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium heat. Add cumin seeds.
Add diced onions. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and slit chilies. Cook for 1 minute.
Cut chicken into 4cm chunks. Add to pot. Sear until browned.
Add turmeric, garam masala, and 3cm potato cubes. Season with salt.
Pour in 200ml water. Cover with a tight lid. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with chopped coriander. Serve hot with rice.
notes: Ensure onions are well-browned for a deep sauce color
Use waxy potatoes so they do not break apart during the simmer
Soaking the basmati rice ensures long, separate grains

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Bell Pepper Chicken with Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented on a handcrafted, creamy beige ceramic plate atop a light bamboo surface. Soft natural light highlights the dish. A fluffy mound of earthy brown rice anchors the left. To its right, a whole, seared chicken thigh, golden-brown with crisped skin, rests unsliced.
