A single, small sprig of fresh cilantro or a thin slice of red bird's eye chili is placed beside a few of the fritters, providing a pop of natural green or red. The lighting is soft and natural, casting gentle shadows that enhance the texture. The background is minimalist, with a hint of blurred green foliage, reinforcing the eco-conscious and natural aesthetic. No ornate garnishes or rigid patterns are used; the composition is clean, simple, and ingredient-focused, celebrating the natural beauty of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm.
Often served as a side dish or snack in Indonesia.

ingredients.name: Red Chili (small, deseeded, finely minced, optional)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Cauliflower: Wash 200 g cauliflower florets. Place in a clean jar. Dissolve 5 g sea salt in 250 ml non-chlorinated water. Pour brine over cauliflower. Ensure cauliflower is submerged. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Taste for desired tang. Drain liquid; reserve for other uses. Roughly chop fermented florets.
Prepare Fritter Mixture: In a large bowl, combine chopped fermented cauliflower, cooked rice, finely diced red onion, minced garlic, and minced chili (if using).
Add rice flour, tapioca starch, egg (or aquafaba), salt, white pepper, and palm sugar. Mix thoroughly until well combined. The mixture should be firm enough to shape.
Shape Fritters: Take small portions (about 20-25 g) of the mixture. Form into small, flattened discs or oval shapes, about 4-5 cm in diameter.
Fry Fritters: Heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry fritters in batches until golden brown and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Remove fritters from oil. Place on a wire rack or paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve: Arrange fritters elegantly on a serving platter. Garnish with optional crispy shallots or a small herb sprig.
notes: Using day-old rice helps achieve a better texture for the fritters.
The liquid from fermented cauliflower can be used in dressings or stocks to minimize waste.
Adjust salt based on the salinity of your fermented cauliflower.

recipes.recipe_name: Polenta Cremosa con Granchio e Funghi al Pesto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, golden polenta is presented in the center of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The polenta is spread naturally, forming a rich base. Piled atop the polenta is a vibrant, savory mixture of tender shredded crab meat, earthy brown sliced cremini mushrooms, diced red bell pepper, and golden caramelized pineapple cubes. The colors are balanced, with the warm hues of the ragu contrasting the yellow polenta. A bright green basil pesto is generously drizzled over the entire dish, creating flowing lines of color. A scattering of golden toasted panko breadcrumbs and small pine nuts provides textural contrast and a finishing touch. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, with traditional Italian flatware placed neatly to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and fresh ingredients. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, allowing the dish to be the clear focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the creamy polenta and ragu.
Pair with a crisp, dry Italian white wine, such as a Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon as an accompaniment.

ingredients.name: Fresh pineapple, cut into 1 cm cubes

instructions: Heat 20 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Increase heat slightly. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 7-8 minutes.
Stir in pineapple cubes. Cook for 3-4 minutes until lightly caramelized.
Gently fold in crab meat. Cook for 2 minutes to heat through. Season the crab mixture with salt and pepper. Set aside and keep warm.
In a separate saucepan, bring vegetable broth to a simmer over medium-high heat. Gradually whisk in polenta, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low. Cook polenta, stirring frequently, for 25-30 minutes until creamy and thick. Add more broth if polenta becomes too stiff.
Remove polenta from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a small dry pan, toast breadcrumbs and pine nuts over medium-low heat until golden brown and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
To serve, spoon creamy polenta onto individual plates. Top with a generous portion of the warm crab and mushroom mixture.
Drizzle basil pesto over the crab mixture and polenta. Garnish with toasted breadcrumbs and pine nuts. Serve immediately.
notes: For best flavor, use fresh, high-quality crab meat. If using canned, drain thoroughly.
Adjust polenta consistency by adding more hot broth if it becomes too thick during cooking.
The basil pesto can be homemade or good quality store-bought.
traditional_techniques: Soffritto (building a flavor base for the ragu)

recipes.recipe_name: Pesto-Crusted Lamb Loin with Pineapple Bell Pepper Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pesto-Crusted Lamb Loin is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The lamb, cut into a thick, juicy medallion, displays a golden-brown, textured crust flecked with green basil and small pine nut pieces. Its interior shows a tender pink hue, indicating perfect doneness. Beside the lamb, a vibrant mound of finely diced pineapple, red and yellow bell pepper, and red onion relish adds a fresh, colorful contrast. Its bright colors pop against the plate. Sautéed brown cremini mushroom slices and soft yellow onion pieces are artfully arranged nearby, adding an earthy tone. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered as a garnish, along with a few toasted pine nuts. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, with a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred restaurant background. The composition is clean, professional, and inviting, with appropriate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a light green salad
Accompany with crusty bread to sop up juices
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.

Prepare pesto crust. In a food processor, combine breadcrumbs, half of basil leaves, 2 cloves minced garlic, half of pine nuts, 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Pulse until coarse crumbs form. Do not overmix.
Pat lamb loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear lamb loin on all sides until golden brown. About 2 minutes per side.
Remove lamb from heat. Press pesto crust mixture firmly onto the seared lamb loin, covering all sides.
Transfer pan with lamb to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches desired doneness. Rest lamb for 10 minutes before slicing into thick medallions.
While lamb roasts, prepare relish. In a bowl, combine diced pineapple, red and yellow bell peppers, and red onion. Add 15 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Heat remaining 10 ml olive oil in a separate pan over medium heat. Add sliced yellow onion and remaining 2 cloves minced garlic. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate, spoon a bed of pineapple bell pepper relish onto each plate. Place a thick slice of pesto-crusted lamb medallion on top or beside the relish. Arrange sautéed mushrooms and onions next to the lamb. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and a few toasted pine nuts.

recipes.recipe_name: Basil Pine Nut Lamb Roulades with Roasted Pineapple Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. A vibrant, smooth, golden-orange roasted pineapple and bell pepper sauce forms an inviting pool at the base. Nestled atop the sauce are two to three thick, succulent chunks of seared lamb roulade, displaying a rich golden-brown crust and a hint of the herbaceous, pine nut-studded stuffing peeking from the cut ends. The lamb chunks are arranged organically, not fanned, showcasing their robust form. A scattering of fresh, bright green basil leaves provides a vibrant contrast and aromatic garnish. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and balanced with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, standard flatware, and a folded cotton napkin positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a subtle, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Finely dice half the onion, 150g mushrooms, and 2 garlic cloves.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion, mushrooms, and garlic until softened. Remove from heat.
In a bowl, combine sautéed vegetables, 50g breadcrumbs, 30g pine nuts, and half of the chopped basil. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Cut the 600g lamb into 4 equal pieces. Place each piece between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound each piece evenly to a 5mm thickness.
Spread the stuffing mixture evenly over each pounded lamb piece. Roll each piece tightly into a cylinder. Secure with kitchen twine or toothpicks.
Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear the lamb roulades until well browned on all sides. Remove roulades from the pan.
Dice the remaining half onion, 1 large red bell pepper, and 2 garlic cloves. Dice the 200g fresh pineapple.
Add the remaining 30ml olive oil to the same pan. Sauté the diced onion, bell pepper, and garlic until softened. Add the diced pineapple. Cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in 150ml stock. Bring to a simmer. Return the seared lamb roulades to the pan.
Cover the pan. Transfer to the preheated oven. Cook for 25-30 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the lamb reaches 75°C.
Remove roulades from the pan. Let them rest for 5 minutes. Remove twine or toothpicks.
Carefully transfer the sauce mixture from the pan to a blender. Blend until smooth. Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice each lamb roulade into 2-3 thick chunks. Do not fan out slices.
To serve, ladle a pool of sauce onto each plate. Arrange the lamb chunks over the sauce. Garnish with the remaining fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Pineapple Glazed Lamb Meatballs
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Pineapple Glazed Lamb Meatballs presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Four to five golden-brown, round lamb meatballs are clustered on one side of the plate, their exteriors showing a slight crispness from searing. A glossy, amber-hued pineapple glaze is generously drizzled over and around the meatballs, with small, soft pineapple chunks visible within the glaze. Adjacent to the meatballs, a vibrant medley of sautéed vegetables is neatly arranged. This includes earthy brown cremini mushroom slices and bright red and yellow bell pepper juliennes, cooked to a tender-crisp texture. A few fresh, green basil leaves are scattered over the meatballs and vegetables for a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface. A folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting from the side, creating soft shadows and highlighting the food's textures. The background is a subtly blurred, casual restaurant setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Combine ground lamb, breadcrumbs, diced onion, minced garlic, chopped basil, egg, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl. Mix thoroughly until just combined.
Form the mixture into 16-20 uniform meatballs.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear meatballs in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Transfer seared meatballs to a baking dish if skillet is not oven-safe.
Bake meatballs for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While meatballs bake, prepare the glaze. In a small saucepan, combine pineapple chunks, soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, and grated ginger. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cook glaze for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until pineapple softens and sauce slightly thickens. Mash some pineapple chunks with a fork if a smoother glaze is desired.
In the same skillet used for meatballs, add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Add sliced mushrooms and julienned bell peppers.
Sauté vegetables over medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange cooked meatballs on individual plates. Drizzle generously with pineapple glaze.
Serve sautéed mushrooms and bell peppers alongside the meatballs. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Beetroot and Seared Duck Salad with Coffee-Berry Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist culinary art piece on a pristine white bone china plate, set on light grey veined marble. Dramatic lighting highlights architectural precision and abundant negative space. The organic composition features precisely cut roasted beetroot (cubes, thin rounds) in red and golden hues, artfully scattered. Thinly sliced raw chioggia beetroot adds textural contrast. Two to three succulent, thick chunks of seared duck breast, glazed with a glossy coffee-berry gastrique, are nestled among vegetables. Meat is whole, not fanned. Small sprigs of bright green micro arugula provide fresh color. Tiny goat cheese crumbles are strategically placed. The rich, dark gastrique is artfully drizzled, pooling elegantly on the plate, connecting elements. A single fresh blackberry or herb sprig serves as precise garnish. A perfectly folded white linen napkin completes the elegant setting.

ingredients.name: fresh micro arugula or tender baby spinach
fresh goat cheese, crumbled or whipped

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Wash and trim beetroots. Toss 2 beetroots (e.g., red and golden) whole with 15ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and thyme. Wrap tightly in foil. Roast for 45-60 minutes until tender. Let cool, then peel and cut into precise shapes: some small cubes (5x5mm), some thin rounds (2mm thick). Keep colors separate. For the remaining 2 beetroots (e.g., chioggia), peel and slice very thinly (1-2mm) using a mandoline. Season these raw slices lightly.

In a small saucepan, combine coffee liqueur, blackberry schnapps, cranberry juice, red wine vinegar, and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until the mixture is syrupy and coats the back of a spoon (about 10-15 minutes). Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.

Score the duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern, being careful not to cut into the meat. Season generously with salt and pepper. Place duck breast skin-side down in a cold, oven-safe pan. Render fat over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden. Pour off excess fat. Flip duck breast. Sear flesh side for 2-3 minutes. Transfer pan to preheated oven (180°C) and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 60°C (140°F) for medium-rare. Rest duck breast for 5 minutes. Slice into 2-3 small, thick, elegant chunks per serving (total 8-12 pieces). Lightly brush the duck pieces with a small amount of the prepared gastrique.

On each of four large, minimalist white plates, artfully arrange the roasted beetroot cubes and rounds, alternating colors and textures. Place the thin raw beetroot slices curled or layered elegantly. Scatter a small amount of micro arugula or baby spinach amongst the beetroot. Place 2-3 pieces of seared, glazed duck breast amidst the vegetables. Crumble or pipe small dollops of goat cheese strategically on the plate.

Drizzle the coffee-berry gastrique artfully over the salad components, allowing some to pool elegantly on the plate. Garnish with a fresh blackberry or a tiny herb sprig if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the sweetness of the gastrique based on the tartness of the cranberry juice.
For optimal duck breast texture, ensure it is rested adequately before slicing.
Experiment with different beetroot varieties for varied colors and subtle flavor differences.

recipes.recipe_name: Sop Kaldu Sapi Kembang Kol Fermentasi
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Sop Kaldu Sapi Kembang Kol Fermentasi is presented in a handcrafted, earthy ceramic bowl in a cream or beige tone. The clear, golden beef broth forms the base. Visible within the broth are pristine white fresh cauliflower florets and slightly more opaque, small fermented cauliflower florets, alongside small, precisely diced carrot pieces. The arrangement is natural and unforced. A generous sprinkle of golden-brown crispy rice is scattered over the top, providing a textural contrast. Delicate, crisp fried shallots (bawang goreng) are sprinkled alongside thinly sliced green spring onion, adding color and aroma. A fresh lime wedge rests elegantly on the rim of the bowl, ready to be squeezed. The setting features a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, emphasizing natural textures. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige hue complements the sustainable aesthetic. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its clean composition. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of green plants, creating an eco-conscious and serene dining atmosphere. All elements are presented with mindful spacing, avoiding any overcrowding, and showcasing the inherent beauty of each ingredient.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with steamed white rice
A side of sambal (chili paste)
A lime wedge for squeezing
instructions: Prepare Fermented Cauliflower (3-5 days in advance): Wash 200g small cauliflower florets. Dissolve 5g sea salt in 250ml filtered water to make brine. Place florets in a clean glass jar. Pour brine over florets. Ensure florets are fully submerged using a weight. Cover jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate once ready.

Make Beef Broth: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast beef bones for 30 minutes until browned. Combine roasted bones, 1.5 litres water, quartered onion, chopped carrot, smashed garlic, bruised lemongrass, sliced galangal, kaffir lime leaves, bay leaves, and black peppercorns in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer uncovered for 3-4 hours. Skim impurities as needed. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Season broth with salt to taste. Keep warm.

Prepare Crispy Rice (Zero-Waste): Spread 100g cooked rice thinly on a baking sheet. Bake at 150°C for 30-45 minutes until completely dry and crispy. Alternatively, deep-fry small clumps of dried rice in 1 tablespoon hot vegetable oil until golden and puffed. Drain on paper towel.

Prepare Fried Shallots (Bawang Goreng): Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add thinly sliced shallots. Fry slowly, stirring often, until golden brown and crispy. Do not burn. Remove shallots with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towel. Reserve oil for other uses if desired.

Assemble Soup: Bring the strained beef broth to a gentle simmer. Add 200g fresh cauliflower florets and 1 medium diced carrot to the broth. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp. Stir in the prepared fermented cauliflower florets. Simmer for 1 minute to warm through. Adjust salt and white pepper if needed.
Serve: Ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with crispy rice, fried shallots, and sliced spring onion. Serve immediately with a lime wedge on the side.
notes: The fermented cauliflower requires preparation 3-5 days in advance of cooking the soup.

recipes.recipe_name: Pisto Manchego con Chorizo y Queso Fresco
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, vibrant Pisto Manchego is served in a shallow, handcrafted ceramic bowl with a matte, earthy finish. Diced red and green bell peppers, sweet carrots, and tender zucchini are gently sautéed, forming a colorful medley. Small, browned rounds of chorizo are interspersed throughout the vegetable base. Crumbled queso fresco is delicately scattered over the top, adding a creamy white contrast. A few fresh parsley leaves provide a pop of green. The dish is presented with a natural, unforced mounding, showcasing the individual textures of the vegetables and chorizo. The overall palette is warm and inviting, against a light, reclaimed wood table. A simple, undyed linen napkin and a side of crusty artisan bread complete the authentic Spanish setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with crusty artisan bread for dipping.
Can be served as a side dish, a tapa, or a light main course.
instructions: Dice red bell pepper, green bell pepper, carrots, zucchini, and onion into 1 cm cubes.
Mince garlic.
Slice chorizo into 1 cm rounds.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat.
Add chorizo rounds. Cook until browned and crisp. Remove chorizo from skillet, set aside. Leave rendered fat in pan.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add diced carrots and bell peppers. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly softened.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced zucchini to the skillet. Cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 20-25 minutes. Vegetables should be very tender.
Uncover and cook for another 5-10 minutes. Allow excess liquid to evaporate. The pisto should be thick.
Return cooked chorizo to the pisto. Stir to combine and heat through.
Crumble queso fresco.
Chop fresh parsley.
notes: This recipe emphasizes seasonal vegetables and a hearty, traditional Spanish preparation.
Use high-quality fresh chorizo for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrilleras de Cerdo con Tomate Fermentado y Jerez
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of rich, dark mahogany-brown pork cheek ragoût is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. Two to three whole, fork-tender pork cheeks are nestled in a rustic, slightly chunky sauce, showcasing their natural, braised form. The sauce is flecked with deep red fermented tomato pieces and vibrant green thyme. Ample negative space surrounds the dish. A few small, fresh thyme sprigs garnish the ragoût. The plate rests on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded beside. A small, rustic ceramic bowl holds crusty Spanish bread. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, with a blurred green plant in the minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Spanish bread (Pan de pueblo) for dipping the sauce.
Accompany with a simple side salad dressed with olive oil and sherry vinegar.
Pair with a glass of the same dry red wine used in the braise.
instructions: Trim excess fat from pork cheeks. Season thoroughly with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork cheeks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add diced red onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return pork cheeks to the pot. Add sherry, pork stock, fresh thyme sprigs, bay leaf, and fermented tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 2.5-3 hours, or until pork cheeks are fork-tender. Alternatively, braise in an oven at 160°C (325°F).
Remove pork cheeks from the pot. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing on solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Return sauce to pot.
Reduce sauce over medium-high heat until it thickens slightly to desired consistency. Skim any excess fat.
Return pork cheeks to the thickened sauce. Heat gently. Serve warm.
notes: For zero-waste, make pork stock from any pork bones or trimmings.

Fermented tomatoes can be lacto-fermented cherry tomatoes or a fermented tomato paste for deeper flavor. To make quick fermented tomatoes: pack clean cherry tomatoes into a clean jar. Add 2% salt by weight (e.g., 6g for 300g tomatoes). Cover with non-chlorinated water. Seal loosely and let ferment at room temperature for 3-7 days until tangy and slightly bubbly. Refrigerate.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Potato and Tomato Fritters
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate, placed on a well-worn light wooden kitchen table. Three golden-brown, rustic potato fritters, approximately 8 cm in diameter, are casually stacked or arranged slightly overlapping in the center of the plate. Their surfaces are visibly crispy with a slightly irregular, homemade texture, showing flecks of grated potato. A small, round, unpretentious ceramic bowl, perhaps a complementary light blue or green, sits beside the fritters, filled with a vibrant red fresh tomato dip. The dip is chunky, revealing small diced pieces of red tomato, a few finely diced white onion pieces, and green specks of chopped fresh parsley. A scattering of fresh parsley leaves is lightly sprinkled over the fritters for a touch of green. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere. The scene evokes comfortable, everyday home dining, with generous, inviting portions.
instructions: Grate peeled potatoes coarsely. Place grated potato in a clean kitchen towel. Squeeze out excess moisture thoroughly.
In a large bowl, combine grated potato, 30g plain flour, egg, salt, and pepper. Mix well to form a batter.
Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Spoon 2-3 tablespoons of potato mixture per fritter into the hot oil. Flatten slightly with the back of a spoon to form rounds, approximately 7-8 cm in diameter. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Cook fritters for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Ensure potatoes are cooked through. Adjust heat as needed to prevent burning.
Transfer cooked fritters to a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. Keep warm. Repeat with remaining batter, adding more oil as needed.
For the tomato dip: In a small bowl, combine diced fresh tomatoes, finely diced red onion, minced garlic, and chopped fresh parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Stir well.
Serve warm fritters immediately with the fresh tomato dip on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Italian Tomato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Rustic Italian Tomato Soup is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, inviting reddish-orange hue. The soup has a hearty, slightly chunky texture from blended tomatoes, with visible flecks of herbs. A few vibrant green fresh basil leaves are casually scattered on the surface, adding a pop of color and freshness. The bowl sits on a well-worn, rustic wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. Beside the bowl, a piece of crusty, golden-brown Italian bread, torn not sliced, rests on a simple linen napkin. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, illuminated by warm, soft ambient light, evoking a comforting and authentic Italian home meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping
A drizzle of extra virgin olive oil over the soup

ingredients.name: Ripe tomatoes (e.g., San Marzano or plum)

instructions: Roughly chop tomatoes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped tomatoes, vegetable broth, and sugar (if using).
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes.
Remove from heat. Use an immersion blender to blend soup to desired consistency. Or carefully transfer to a regular blender in batches.
Season with salt and pepper. Add red pepper flakes if desired.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.
notes: This recipe serves 4 people.
Adjust blending time for smoother or chunkier soup as preferred.

recipes.recipe_name: Earth Bowl with Fermented Cherry & Umami Dust
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the 'Earth Bowl' is presented in a handcrafted, deep ceramic bowl with an earthy, matte finish, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The dish features a rich, dark black lentil and wild mushroom stew, showcasing whole, firm lentils and sautéed mushrooms—some whole, others halved or quartered, highlighting natural forms. A creamy dollop of off-white cashew ricotta rests in the center. Around the ricotta, a few vibrant, glossy lacto-fermented cherries offer a pop of deep ruby red. The composition is subtly dusted with a fine, dark, savory umami powder. A few fresh parsley leaves are sparsely placed for natural green. Plating is minimalistic, respecting negative space, allowing each ingredient to stand out. The scene is bathed in soft, diffused natural light, emphasizing organic textures and earthy colors. An undyed linen napkin is casually draped nearby, alongside a simple ceramic spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a hearty, plant-forward main course.
Enjoy with fresh, crusty sourdough bread for dipping.
Pair with a light, crisp fermented beverage like kombucha or water kefir.
instructions: Prepare vegetable broth: Combine onion skins, carrot ends, celery ends, mushroom stems, and any other clean vegetable scraps in a pot. Cover with 1.5 L water. Simmer for 45 minutes. Strain. Discard solids or compost.
Rehydrate dried shiitake mushrooms: Place dried shiitake in a small bowl. Cover with 100 ml hot water. Let stand 15 minutes. Reserve liquid. Slice rehydrated mushrooms.

Prepare cashew ricotta: Soak cashews in hot water for 30 minutes. Drain. Blend cashews with plant milk, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, and a pinch of salt until smooth and creamy. Adjust consistency with more plant milk if needed.

Prepare umami dust: Finely grate or shave milk chocolate. Spread on a baking sheet. Dehydrate in a very low oven (around 50°C) for 1-2 hours until completely dry and brittle. Alternatively, use a food dehydrator. Once dry, combine with dried porcini powder, smoked paprika, and sea salt flakes. Grind into a fine powder using a spice grinder or mortar and pestle. Store in an airtight container.
Cook lentils: Rinse black lentils. In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.

Add lentils, rehydrated shiitake, reserved shiitake liquid, vegetable broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf to the pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer 25-30 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Stir occasionally.

Prepare fresh mushrooms: While lentils cook, clean and trim fresh wild mushrooms. Leave small mushrooms whole. Halve or quarter larger mushrooms. In a separate pan, sauté mushrooms in a little olive oil over medium-high heat until golden brown and tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf from the lentil stew. Stir in sautéed mushrooms. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.

To serve: Ladle lentil and mushroom stew into deep ceramic bowls. Place a dollop of cashew ricotta in the center of each bowl. Arrange a few lacto-fermented cherries around the ricotta. Lightly dust the dish with the prepared umami dust. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: The lacto-fermented cherries can be prepared days in advance. If unavailable, a small amount of balsamic glaze with fresh cherries can be used as a substitute, though it will alter the flavor profile.
The umami dust can be made in a larger batch and stored for future use on other savory dishes.
For maximum zero-waste, consider using the leftover liquid from soaking cashews for the ricotta in smoothies or other recipes.

recipes.recipe_name: Cherry Chocolate Baked Cheesecake
recipes.visual_description: A comforting Cherry Chocolate Baked Cheesecake is presented on a simple, round, white ceramic plate with a subtle lip, resting on a well-used wooden kitchen table. A single generous wedge slice is removed and placed on a smaller matching plate beside the main cake. The slice clearly displays the dark, compact chocolate biscuit crust, the creamy, pale ivory cheesecake filling, and the glistening, deep red cherry topping with whole pitted cherries. Fine, delicate milk chocolate shavings are scattered over the cherries on both the whole cake and the slice. The scene is bathed in warm, natural kitchen light, creating soft, inviting shadows. A simple, casually placed cloth napkin and a dessert fork complete the homely, lived-in atmosphere of a family dining area.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served chilled with a cup of coffee or hot tea.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Grease and line a 18 cm springform pan.
Crush biscuits into fine crumbs. Mix with melted butter. Press firmly into the bottom of the prepared pan. Chill for 15 minutes.
In a large bowl, beat softened cream cheese and 150g sugar until smooth. Do not overmix.
Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing until just combined after each addition.
Stir in milk, vanilla extract, and 5g cornstarch until smooth.
Pour filling over the chilled biscuit crust.

Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until edges are set and center slightly jiggles. Turn off oven, leave cheesecake inside with door ajar for 1 hour. Remove and cool completely on a wire rack. Chill for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
For cherry topping: Combine cherries, 50g sugar, and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
In a small bowl, whisk 10g cornstarch with 15ml cold water to make a slurry. Stir into the simmering cherries.
Cook, stirring, until the mixture thickens. Remove from heat and cool completely.
Before serving, spoon the cooled cherry topping over the chilled cheesecake. Shave milk chocolate over the top using a vegetable peeler or grater.
notes: Ensure cream cheese is at room temperature for a smooth, lump-free batter.
Do not overbake the cheesecake; a slight jiggle in the center is ideal for a creamy texture.
Cooling the cheesecake slowly in the oven helps prevent cracks.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Vanilla Celebration Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of Classic Vanilla Celebration Cake rests on a simple, round white ceramic plate. The slice reveals two layers of light, airy vanilla sponge separated by a generous layer of creamy white vanilla buttercream. The top and sides of the slice are also coated in buttercream, with a few rustic swirls. In the background, the remaining whole cake, lightly frosted with more rustic swirls, sits on a wooden cake stand on a well-used wooden dining table. The table features a casually placed, folded beige linen napkin and a plain fork. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The colors are natural: golden-brown cake, off-white buttercream. The focus is on the inviting texture and homemade appeal of the cake.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 15cm round cake tin. Line base with baking paper.
Beat 150g butter and 150g caster sugar in a bowl until pale and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time. Beat well after each addition.
Stir in 1 tsp vanilla extract.
Fold in 150g self-raising flour gradually until just combined.
Add 2 tbsp milk. Mix gently.
Pour batter into prepared tin. Smooth top.
Bake 25-30 minutes. Cake is done when a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool in tin for 10 minutes. Transfer to wire rack to cool completely.
For buttercream: Beat 100g softened butter in a clean bowl until soft.
Gradually add 200g icing sugar. Beat until smooth.
Stir in 1 tsp vanilla extract and 1-2 tbsp milk. Beat until light and fluffy.
Once cake is completely cool, slice horizontally into two even layers.
Spread half the buttercream on the bottom layer.
Place top layer on. Spread remaining buttercream over top and sides of the cake.
Decorate simply as desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Tuscan Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of roasted chicken and vegetables is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is the focal point, resting amidst a colorful medley of roasted vegetables. Large potato wedges, their skins slightly browned and interiors tender, are scattered around the chicken. Burst cherry tomatoes add pops of vibrant red, some slightly collapsed from roasting. Caramelized onion wedges and a few whole, softened garlic cloves are visible. Fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs are casually placed over the dish, providing an aromatic garnish and a touch of green. The overall presentation is rustic yet refined, showcasing the natural textures and rich colors of the ingredients. The plate is well-proportioned with moderate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table with natural, even lighting, a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard flatware.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to absorb pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with balsamic vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, onion wedges, halved cherry tomatoes, smashed garlic cloves, rosemary, and thyme.
Drizzle vegetables and herbs with olive oil. Toss to coat evenly. Season with salt and pepper.
Nestle seasoned chicken thighs among the vegetables in the roasting pan.
Roast for 45-50 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and the skin is golden and crisp. Potatoes should be tender and lightly browned.
If the pan appears dry during cooking, add a splash of chicken broth.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Braised Chicken with Fermented Tomato and Crispy Potato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Braised Chicken is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, resting on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A golden-brown, skin-on chicken thigh, cooked whole, is centered on the plate. It is generously spooned with a rich, deep red fermented tomato sauce that pools naturally around its base. The sauce exhibits a smooth, velvety texture. Arranged artfully around the chicken, with ample negative space, are several thin, golden-crisp potato discs, approximately 5cm in diameter. Their irregular, natural edges and varied shades of golden-brown highlight their crispy texture. A small, vibrant green sprig of fresh thyme or rosemary is placed gently on top of the chicken. The entire composition is clean and minimalist, celebrating the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of natural light and a green plant, maintaining focus on the dish. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded neatly beside the plate, and simple, sustainable flatware rests nearby.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Base (at least 3 days in advance): Dice 800g tomatoes. Place in a clean jar. Add 10g salt. Stir well. Cover loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until tangy. Blend into a smooth sauce.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Sear Chicken: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear until skin is golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip. Sear other side for 2 minutes. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Build Sauce: Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Braise Chicken: Pour fermented tomato sauce into the pan. Add chicken stock, thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a simmer. Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.

Cook: Cover the pan. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is tender. Remove from oven. Remove chicken. Keep warm. Reduce sauce on stovetop if needed, until slightly thickened.

Prepare Crispy Potato Discs: While chicken braises, peel potatoes. Slice very thinly into rounds (1-2mm thickness) using a mandoline or sharp knife. Toss potato discs with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Cook Potato Discs: Arrange potato discs in a single layer on a baking sheet. Bake in the same oven at 180°C (350°F) for 20-30 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and crispy.

Serve: Place one braised chicken thigh on each plate. Spoon generous amount of fermented tomato sauce over and around the chicken. Arrange crispy potato discs artfully around the chicken. Garnish with a fresh sprig of thyme or rosemary.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Potato Tomato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of rustic potato tomato soup fills a deep, earthy ceramic bowl, showcasing its comforting, chunky texture. Diced potatoes and crushed tomatoes create a rich, warm red-orange base, with softened onion and minced garlic visible throughout. The soup is topped with a vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped green basil, offering a pop of color and aromatic freshness. It is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple, slightly rumpled beige cloth napkin beside the bowl. A sturdy metal soup spoon rests casually. The setting evokes a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, bathed in warm, natural lighting, highlighting the homely appeal of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced potatoes, crushed tomatoes, oregano, and vegetable broth.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer, covered, 20-25 minutes, until potatoes are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Mash some potatoes in the pot with a fork for a rustic texture. Do not blend.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with chopped fresh basil. Serve hot.
notes: Adjust potato mashing to desired rustic consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato & Pickled Pimento Sustainable Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Spanish salad is presented on a handcrafted, earth-toned ceramic plate, showcasing natural textures and minimalistic plating. Diced ripe tomatoes, crisp, thin strips of quick-pickled pimento peppers, and tender chickpeas are artfully arranged, interspersed with finely sliced red onion. A light, smoky paprika vinaigrette subtly coats each ingredient, highlighting their natural colors and textures. The salad is garnished with freshly chopped parsley and a delicate sprinkle of minced red chili, adding a fresh green and a touch of fiery red. The composition is clean and unforced, emphasizing the pure beauty of the sustainable ingredients. The plate rests on a light bamboo surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin, under soft, natural lighting. The background is minimal, featuring subtle greenery, enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Slice pimento peppers into thin strips. In a small jar, combine sliced pimentos with 100 ml water, 15 ml sherry vinegar, 5 g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Cover and quick-pickle for at least 30 minutes.
Dice ripe tomatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Finely slice red onion. Mince fresh red chili (remove seeds for less heat) and garlic.
Drain canned chickpeas and rinse well.

Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together extra virgin olive oil, remaining 15 ml sherry vinegar, smoked paprika, hot sauce, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper. Add 15 ml of the pimento pickling liquid to the dressing for enhanced flavor and zero-waste.
In a large mixing bowl, combine diced tomatoes, finely sliced red onion, drained chickpeas, and drained quick-pickled pimento strips.
Pour the prepared dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to ensure all components are evenly coated.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Garnish the salad with chopped parsley and a few additional minced chili pieces if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Braised Pork with Tomato, Basil, and Green Peppercorn
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of rustic braised pork is centered on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. Two thick, tender chunks of slow-cooked pork shoulder, rich brown from searing, rest partially submerged in a vibrant, thick red tomato and basil sauce. The sauce clings to the pork, showcasing the tender, fall-apart texture of the meat. Specks of crushed green peppercorns are visible in the sauce, alongside soft, diced vegetables like carrot and celery. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are casually torn and scattered over the pork and sauce, adding a pop of color and aromatic freshness. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. A simple linen napkin is casually placed beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and natural colors. The entire plate is visible, with modest negative space. A small, simple ceramic bowl of soft yellow polenta or a slice of crusty rustic bread might be visible slightly in the background, out of focus, as a traditional accompaniment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with creamy polenta, mashed potatoes, or crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Pat pork chunks dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove pork and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften and become translucent.
Stir in crushed green peppercorns. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Dissolve shrimp paste in a small amount of warm water, then stir into the sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared pork chunks to the pot. Ensure pork is mostly submerged in the liquid. If needed, add a little more broth.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Turn pork chunks halfway through cooking.
Remove pork from the pot. If the sauce is too thin, increase heat to medium-high and simmer, uncovered, until it thickens to desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Return pork to the sauce. Stir in fresh torn basil just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Mexican Shrimp & Avocado Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Grilled Mexican Shrimp & Avocado Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The dish features a generous bed of fresh, crisp mixed salad greens as the base. Artfully arranged over the greens are plump, golden-pink grilled shrimp, whole and not sliced, showcasing their char marks. Alongside the shrimp are creamy, bright green avocado cubes, precisely diced to maintain their shape. Thinly sliced red onion adds a delicate purple accent. Crispy, golden-brown corn tortilla strips are scattered over the top, providing a textural contrast. A light, vibrant lime-cilantro vinaigrette is visibly drizzled over the ingredients. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. A simple cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, with a subtly blurred, casual restaurant-style background. A small bowl of fresh lime wedges is positioned near the plate, enhancing the cultural authenticity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lime wedges for individual preference.
Offer a side of fresh pico de gallo or salsa roja.
Can be accompanied by warm corn tortillas.

ingredients.name: Mixed salad greens (e.g., romaine, butter lettuce)

instructions: Pat shrimp dry. In a bowl, combine 2 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper. Add shrimp. Toss to coat. Marinate 15 minutes.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill shrimp 2-3 minutes per side, until opaque and cooked through (internal temperature 74°C). Do not overcook. Set aside.
Break corn tortilla chips into large, rustic strips.
For the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk remaining 2 tbsp lime juice, 4 tbsp olive oil, chopped fresh oregano, salt, and pepper. Stir in chopped cilantro.
Dice avocados into 2 cm cubes. Thinly slice red onion.
In a large bowl, gently toss salad greens with half of the dressing. Arrange greens on four individual white porcelain plates.
Artfully arrange grilled shrimp and avocado cubes over the greens on each plate. Scatter red onion slices.
Drizzle remaining dressing over the shrimp and avocado. Top with crispy tortilla strips.
Serve immediately with extra lime wedges on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Pomodoro Piccante
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Pomodoro Piccante is artfully arranged on a round, shallow white porcelain plate. Two golden-brown seared chicken thighs, their crispy skin glistening, are placed centrally. They are generously coated with a rich, rustic tomato sauce, featuring vibrant red halved cherry tomatoes, some burst open, and tender strips of red bell pepper. Thin slices of red chili are scattered throughout, adding color and a hint of heat. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are torn and sprinkled over the dish as a garnish. The sauce lightly coats the chicken and pools minimally on the plate. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. It rests on a simple, light wooden table surface, illuminated by natural, even lighting. A small, rustic loaf of crusty Italian bread, torn into a few pieces, is placed beside the plate. Standard European flatware and a folded white linen napkin complete the casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the flavorful tomato sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.quantity: 1, thinly sliced (seeds removed for less heat)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, sliced bell pepper, minced garlic, and sliced red chili to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften and onion is translucent.
Stir in dried oregano. Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes until wine slightly reduces.
Add halved cherry tomatoes and chicken broth to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the sauce.
Cover the pan. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove lid. Increase heat slightly if sauce is too thin. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes to reduce sauce if desired.
Stir in fresh basil leaves just before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Ricotta & Incir Tartlet
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly presented Ricotta & Incir Tartlet rests centered on a smooth, unglazed cream-colored ceramic plate. The tartlet features a golden-brown, rustic whole wheat crust, subtly speckled from its sourdough discard inclusion, with a gently crimped edge. Inside, the creamy, pale ivory ricotta filling is softly baked, showcasing its smooth texture. Adorning the top are thinly sliced fresh figs, their deep purple skins contrasting with the lighter pink flesh, arranged in an organic, overlapping pattern. A light drizzle of dark, glossy pekmez (grape molasses) gently cascades over the figs and filling, adding a rich hue. A scattering of bright green, finely crushed pistachios provides a vibrant textural and color accent. The plate is placed on a light, natural wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the tartlet's natural beauty and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a small cup of strong Turkish coffee (Türk kahvesi)
Enjoy with a glass of traditional black Turkish tea (çay)

ingredients.name: Orange blossom water or vanilla extract

instructions: Combine flour, butter, and salt in a bowl. Rub butter into flour until crumbly.
Add sourdough discard and ice water. Mix until dough forms. Do not overmix.
Form dough into a disk. Wrap and chill 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Roll dough 3mm thick on a lightly floured surface.
Cut four 10cm circles. Line tartlet molds with dough.
Prick bottoms with a fork. Chill 15 minutes.
Line tartlet shells with parchment paper and pie weights.
Blind bake crusts 15 minutes. Remove weights. Bake 5 more minutes until lightly golden. Cool completely.
Combine ricotta, honey/pekmez, egg yolk, and orange blossom water in a bowl. Mix until smooth.
Pour filling into cooled tartlet crusts.
Bake 15-20 minutes, or until filling is set and lightly golden. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Slice fresh figs thinly.
Arrange fig slices artfully on top of each cooled tartlet.
Drizzle lightly with extra pekmez if desired. Sprinkle with crushed pistachios before serving.
notes: Use very ripe, seasonal figs for best flavor and sweetness.
Adjust honey or pekmez quantity to your preferred sweetness level.
This recipe highlights zero-waste by utilizing sourdough discard and seasonal produce.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato-Mustard Confit
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and tender, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside the chicken, a vibrant mound of sautéed broccoli florets and bright red and yellow bell pepper strips adds a pop of color and texture. A rich, glossy pool of rustic tomato-mustard confit, with softened, burst cherry tomatoes and flecks of garlic and thyme, is spooned gracefully alongside the chicken. The dish is garnished simply with a few fresh green basil leaves, providing a fresh aromatic contrast. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic flatware, under natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing textures, evoking a modern bistro ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.

Prepare Tomato-Mustard Confit: In a medium oven-safe pan, combine cherry tomatoes, sliced garlic, half of the diced shallots, 30ml olive oil, and 2 thyme sprigs. Season with salt and pepper. Stir gently. Roast in preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, until tomatoes soften and burst.
Remove confit from oven. Stir in Dijon mustard. Mash some tomatoes lightly to create a saucy consistency. Keep warm.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 4 minutes per side, until golden brown.
Transfer skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Cook 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, loosely tented with foil.
Prepare Vegetables: In the same skillet used for chicken, add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter. Add remaining shallots and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add broccoli florets and bell pepper strips. Sauté 5-7 minutes, until tender-crisp. Add white wine or chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan. Season with salt and pepper.

To Serve: Place a portion of sautéed vegetables on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of Tomato-Mustard Confit next to the vegetables. Place a whole pan-seared chicken breast on the plate. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully rested after cooking to retain juices.
Adjust mustard quantity in confit to your preference for tanginess.

recipes.recipe_name: White Truffle Chicken Velouté with Potato Espuma and Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A deep, wide, pristine white bone china bowl holds the dish. The luxurious, ivory-hued chicken velouté forms a smooth, reflective base. A delicate, cloud-like mound of aerated potato espuma floats gracefully in the center, its ethereal texture contrasting with the velouté below. A single, thin, golden-brown Parmesan crisp is placed artfully on the rim of the bowl, or delicately leaning into the espuma, adding architectural interest and a textural counterpoint. A barely perceptible whisper of vibrant red cayenne pepper dusts the espuma, offering a hint of warmth and a precise pop of color. Finely diced chicken pieces (5mm cubes) are precisely arranged beside the espuma, adding substance. Abundant negative space surrounds the central composition, emphasizing the dish's minimalist elegance. The bowl rests on a polished, grey-veined Carrara marble surface. A precisely folded white linen napkin in a triangular shape is positioned to the left. The background is an ultra-minimalist, soft grey, allowing the dish to be the sole focus. Dramatic, directional lighting casts subtle, elongated shadows, enhancing the depth and sophistication. High-end, modern silver flatware is placed subtly beside the bowl.
instructions: Gently poach chicken breasts in 500 ml chicken stock until cooked through (75°C internal). Remove chicken, cool, then finely dice into 5mm cubes. Set aside.
In a saucepan, melt 20 g butter. Sauté minced shallot until translucent. Deglaze with white wine, reduce by half. Add 1 L chicken stock. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Whisk in heavy cream and 3 ml white truffle oil into the velouté base. Season with sea salt and white pepper. Pass the velouté through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

Peel and dice potatoes into 1 cm cubes. Boil in lightly salted water until very tender. Drain completely. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a bowl. Whisk in 10 g butter, remaining 2 ml white truffle oil, and a splash of warm milk or cream if needed, until perfectly smooth. Season. Transfer to a 0.5 L culinary siphon. Charge with one N2O cartridge. Shake well. Keep warm in a bain-marie.

Preheat oven to 180°C. On a silicone mat or parchment-lined baking sheet, spread 4 small (approx. 5 cm diameter) circles of grated Parmesan. Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely on the sheet.

Pour 200 ml hot velouté into the center of each warmed deep bowl. Gently dispense a sphere of potato espuma onto the velouté. Place one Parmesan crisp delicately leaning against the espuma or on the rim. Lightly dust the espuma with a pinch of cayenne pepper. Garnish with a few finely diced chicken pieces beside the espuma.

recipes.recipe_name: Orange-Ginger Beef Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Asian-inspired stir-fry is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Thinly sliced, seared beef pieces, glistening with a rich, glossy orange-ginger soy sauce, are loosely piled atop a bed of fresh, crisp mixed salad greens. The beef, browned at the edges, contrasts with the soft, earthy sliced button mushrooms and translucent, tender onion slivers. Bright red chili slices and dark, halved black olives are interspersed throughout the stir-fry, adding pops of color and texture. A sprinkle of bright green chopped green onions garnishes the dish. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table. A set of elegant chopsticks and a small white rice bowl are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed rice on the side.
Use chopsticks for eating.
instructions: Prepare beef marinade. In a bowl, combine 30ml soy sauce, 15ml rice vinegar, half orange zest, half orange juice, half grated ginger, and half minced garlic.
Add beef slices to marinade. Toss to coat. Let marinate 15 minutes.

In a small bowl, whisk remaining 30ml soy sauce, 15ml rice vinegar, remaining orange zest, remaining orange juice, remaining ginger, remaining garlic, cornstarch, and sesame oil. Set aside. This is the stir-fry sauce.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat.
Remove beef from marinade. Reserve marinade. Sear beef in batches until browned. Do not overcrowd pan. Cook 1-2 minutes per side. Remove beef from pan.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to wok. Add sliced onion. Stir-fry 2 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms and thinly sliced red chili. Stir-fry 3-4 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Pour stir-fry sauce into wok. Stir constantly until sauce thickens.
Return beef to wok. Add halved olives. Toss to coat with sauce. Cook 1 minute until heated through.
Serve immediately over fresh salad greens. Garnish with chopped green onions.
notes: Adjust red chili quantity to preferred spice level. Remove seeds for less heat.
Ensure wok is very hot before adding beef to achieve a good sear.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef and Garlic Shrimp with Crispy Potato Hash and Citrus Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single refined portion is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centered on a rustic wooden table surface. A bed of golden-brown, crispy small-diced potato hash forms the base, showcasing varied textures. Tender, seared beef chunks (approximately 2-3 cm) are strategically placed atop the hash, displaying a rich, caramelized crust. Alongside the beef, succulent, garlic-ginger seared shrimp, vibrant pink-orange in color, are artfully arranged. A bright, fresh salad of crisp mixed greens, thin cucumber rounds, sweet orange segments, and thinly sliced red onion is nestled beside the hash. Sliced black olives are scattered within the salad. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or cilantro and delicate slices of red chili, adding color and a hint of spice. The overall presentation is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. A simple set of silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are placed beside the plate, all bathed in soft, natural, even lighting from above, creating a modern bistro ambiance.
instructions: Cut beef into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Peel and small dice potatoes into 1 cm cubes. Rinse under cold water. Pat very dry with paper towels.
Finely dice half of the white onion. Thinly slice the remaining half for the salad.
Mince 4 garlic cloves. Thinly slice the remaining 2 garlic cloves.
Thinly slice fresh red chili. Mince ginger.
Slice mushrooms. Pit and slice olives.
Segment the orange. Thinly slice cucumber into rounds.
Prepare citrus vinaigrette: Whisk together 30 ml olive oil, juice of half lemon, juice of half orange, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper.

Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced potatoes. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and crispy. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from skillet and set aside.
In the same skillet, add a splash more olive oil. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms and half of the sliced chili. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned. Return crispy potatoes to skillet. Stir to combine. Keep warm.

In a separate skillet, heat 15 ml olive oil over high heat. Add beef chunks. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until browned. Reduce heat to medium. Cook for another 2-4 minutes for medium-rare to medium doneness. Remove beef. Set aside.

In the same skillet, add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Add shrimp, sliced garlic, minced ginger, and remaining sliced chili. Sauté for 2-3 minutes per side until shrimp are pink and cooked through. Add soy sauce. Stir to coat. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine mixed salad greens, sliced cucumber, orange segments, sliced onion, and sliced olives. Toss with citrus vinaigrette.

To plate: Create a bed of potato hash on each plate. Arrange seared beef chunks and garlic shrimp on top of the hash. Place a portion of citrus salad beside the hash. Garnish with fresh parsley or cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken Milanese with Fresh Mozzarella and Rosemary Potato Batons
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown crispy chicken cutlet, generously topped with glistening melted fresh mozzarella and a vibrant red and green tomato concasse, rests on a clean white round porcelain plate. Beside the chicken, a neat, slightly mounded pile of golden-brown rosemary potato batons provides a contrasting texture. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. The dish exhibits natural color balance, with the rich golden tones of the chicken and potatoes complementing the bright red of the tomatoes and the fresh green of basil. A single fresh basil leaf garnishes the concasse. The composition is clean and professional, with appropriate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin, and standard flatware, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar
Pair with a light Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.

Cut potatoes into 1 cm x 1 cm x 6 cm batons. Toss with 2 tablespoons olive oil, chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crispy.
While potatoes roast, prepare the chicken. Pound each chicken breast to 1.5 cm thickness.
Set up a breading station: one plate with flour, one shallow dish with beaten eggs, and one plate with breadcrumbs mixed with grated Parmesan, salt, and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumb mixture, pressing to adhere.

Heat 4 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Pan-fry chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove from skillet and drain on paper towels.
For the tomato concasse: In a small bowl, combine diced tomatoes, chopped basil, minced garlic, 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Place a slice or two of fresh mozzarella on top of each hot chicken cutlet. Briefly return chicken to the warm skillet or a warm oven for 1-2 minutes until mozzarella is melted and gooey.
To serve, place a chicken cutlet on each plate. Spoon tomato concasse over the melted mozzarella. Arrange roasted potato batons neatly beside the chicken. Garnish with a fresh basil leaf.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For extra crispy chicken, ensure oil is hot enough before frying and do not overcrowd the pan.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Cashew Pea Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table surface. A generous single portion of creamy Cashew Pea Pasta fills the plate, featuring rigatoni or fusilli pasta perfectly coated in a vibrant, pale green sauce. The sauce is smooth and rich, clinging beautifully to the pasta, with the occasional whole or slightly crushed green pea visible, adding texture and bright color pops. A scattering of finely chopped fresh basil leaves and a few whole green peas garnish the top, providing a fresh green contrast. The pasta is arranged organically, creating a subtle mound in the center, allowing for moderate negative space around the edges of the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its creamy texture and fresh ingredients. A cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate, accompanied by standard silver flatware.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
A light green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Soak cashews in hot water for at least 30 minutes. Drain cashews.
Cook pasta according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, prepare sauce. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
In a high-speed blender, combine soaked cashews, vegetable broth, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Blend until completely smooth and creamy.

Pour cashew cream into the skillet with shallot and garlic. Stir well. Add most of the green peas, reserving a small handful for garnish. Simmer gently for 3-5 minutes, stirring often, until sauce thickens slightly.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat thoroughly. Add chopped fresh basil. Stir to combine.
Adjust seasoning. If sauce is too thick, add more reserved pasta water until desired consistency is reached.
Serve immediately.
notes: For a thinner sauce, add more reserved pasta water.
Cashews must be thoroughly blended for a smooth sauce.
Adjust nutritional yeast to taste for desired cheesiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato and Olive Bulgur Pilaf with Herbs
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. A generous, slightly mounded portion of golden-brown bulgur pilaf forms the centerpiece. The pilaf is loose and fluffy, revealing diced, tender onions, rehydrated dark red dried tomatoes, and glossy black olive halves mixed throughout. Vibrant green chopped parsley is gently folded into the pilaf, with more scattered over the top for freshness. A scattering of thinly sliced, pale pink quick-pickled red onions adds a bright pop of color and sharp contrast. The setting features a light, natural wood surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin rests beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the varied textures and natural colors of the ingredients. The background is clean and minimalist, allowing the dish to be the sole focus.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain yogurt (süzme yoğurt).
Accompany with a glass of traditional ayran (yogurt drink).
Offer an assortment of traditional Turkish pickled vegetables (turşu).

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.quantity: 1 large (diced, a small portion thinly sliced for pickling)

instructions: Rehydrate dried tomatoes in warm water for 15 minutes. Drain well.
Dice most of the large onion. Thinly slice a small portion of the onion for quick pickling.
To make quick-pickled onions: Combine sliced onion with 100 ml apple cider vinegar, 50 ml water, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of sugar. Let sit for at least 20 minutes.
In a large pot, melt beef fat over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in fermented tomato paste and red pepper flakes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add bulgur, rehydrated dried tomatoes, and halved black olives. Stir to combine.
Pour in water or vegetable broth. Season with salt and black pepper. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until bulgur is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let sit, covered, for 10 minutes to steam.
Fluff the bulgur pilaf with a fork. Stir in most of the chopped fresh parsley.
Serve warm, garnished with remaining fresh parsley, quick-pickled red onions, and a lemon wedge.
notes: Using homemade fermented tomato paste enhances authentic flavor and embodies zero-waste principles.
Leftover onion peels can be used to make vegetable broth for future recipes.
traditional_techniques: Salça Yapımı (Tomato Paste Making - referring to the use of fermented paste)

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Miso Tofu Pasta with Toasted Sesame
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy pasta is casually piled on a simple, round off-white ceramic plate, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The pasta, likely penne or spaghetti, is coated in a rich, pale yellow sauce. Scattered throughout are golden-brown 2 cm cubes of pan-fried tofu, some nestled within the pasta, others peeking out. Wilted deep green spinach leaves are gently folded into the dish, adding a pop of color. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of toasted white and black sesame seeds, providing visual texture and a subtle crunch. A single, simple fork is placed to the right. The lighting is warm and cozy, suggestive of a relaxed family kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Press tofu for 20 minutes to remove excess water. Cut tofu into 2 cm cubes.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Reserve 250 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Add onion to pan, cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic, cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tofu cubes to the pan. Brown lightly on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together miso paste, nutritional yeast, and vegetable broth until smooth.
Pour miso mixture into the pan with tofu and aromatics. Stir well to combine.
Add drained pasta and spinach to the pan. Toss to coat evenly. Cook until spinach wilts.
Add reserved pasta water gradually, 60 ml at a time, until desired creamy consistency is reached.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately.
Garnish each serving with toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Adjust the amount of reserved pasta water to achieve your preferred sauce thickness.

recipes.recipe_name: Sesame Miso Glazed Tofu Steaks
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sesame Miso Glazed Tofu Steaks is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a subtle, earthy rim. Two thick, golden-brown pan-seared tofu planks, each approximately 2cm thick, are arranged slightly overlapping in the center. The tofu is coated in a glossy, dark amber miso glaze, showing visible flecks of minced garlic and grated ginger. A generous sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds adheres to the glazed surface, adding a textural contrast. Alongside the tofu, a small, neat mound of fluffy white rice is positioned, touching the tofu. A few vibrant green, thinly sliced green onion batons are scattered over the tofu and rice for a fresh accent. The plate rests on a well-worn, light-colored wooden dining table, revealing natural grain and minor imperfections. A simple, silver fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, creating a cozy and approachable home-cooked atmosphere.
instructions: Press tofu for 30 minutes to remove excess water.
Slice tofu block into four equal 2 cm thick planks.
Lightly dust each tofu plank with cornstarch.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Sear tofu planks for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Remove from pan.
In the same pan, reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Whisk together miso paste, nutritional yeast, soy sauce, maple syrup, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and water in a small bowl.
Pour miso glaze into the pan. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened.
Return seared tofu planks to the pan. Turn to coat evenly with the glaze.
Cook for 1-2 minutes, allowing glaze to thicken and adhere to tofu.
Remove from heat. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Plant-Based Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of hearty Plant-Based Shepherd's Pie is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic ramekin on a well-used wooden dining table. The thick, golden-orange sweet potato topping, with its naturally swirled and slightly peaked surface, covers a rich, savory lentil and diced butternut squash filling. The filling, visible at the edges, features tender diced carrots, peas, and corn, creating a medley of earthy greens and oranges. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a touch of vibrant green to the topping. The ceramic ramekin has natural imperfections, reflecting a homely aesthetic. A simple, folded linen napkin and a silver fork are casually placed beside the ramekin. Warm, ambient kitchen lighting illuminates the dish, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere typical of a family meal.

ingredients.name: Butternut squash
ingredients.quantity: 700 g, peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Sweet potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 1 kg, peeled and cut into large chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Rinse lentils. Cook lentils in 600 ml water for 20-25 minutes until tender. Drain excess water.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add chopped onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced butternut squash, cooked lentils, vegetable broth, tomato paste, dried thyme, and dried rosemary. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until squash is tender.
Stir in frozen peas and corn. Cook for 2 minutes. Season filling with salt and pepper to taste. Set aside.
While filling cooks, boil sweet potato chunks in a large pot of salted water for 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain thoroughly.
Mash sweet potatoes with plant-based milk and plant-based butter until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Pour the vegetable and lentil filling into a 2-litre oven-safe baking dish or individual ramekins.
Spoon mashed sweet potato evenly over the filling. Spread to the edges. Create small peaks or swirls with the back of a spoon.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Herbs, Squash, and Sweet Potato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken with vegetables rests on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate, positioned on a well-used wooden kitchen table. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is the centerpiece. Around it are scattered generous, irregular thick chunks of vibrant orange sweet potato and pale yellow butternut squash, their edges slightly caramelized.
