Strain mixture. Pour the panna cotta mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl. This ensures a smooth texture.
Prepare molds. Lightly grease 6-9 small silicone molds or ramekins (approx. 50-60ml capacity each) with a tiny amount of neutral oil, or line with plastic wrap if using non-flexible molds.
Pour and chill. Divide the panna cotta mixture evenly among the molds. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or until firmly set.
Make berry coulis. In a small saucepan, combine mixed berries, 20g sugar, and lemon juice. Cook over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until berries soften and release juices.
Strain coulis. Press the berry mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds and skins. Chill the coulis.
Unmold panna cotta. To unmold, briefly dip the bottom of each mold in hot water (if using rigid molds) or gently peel away silicone/plastic wrap. Invert onto a serving platter.
Garnish and serve. Spoon a small amount of chilled berry coulis around each panna cotta. Garnish with a tiny fresh mint sprig. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe uses low-fat dairy products for a lighter, health-conscious dessert.

recipes.recipe_name: Low-Fat Lemon Yogurt Soufflé
recipes.visual_description: Two individual soufflés are presented in pristine white porcelain ramekins on a light wooden table surface. Each soufflé has risen significantly above its ramekin rim, forming a delicate, domed top with a golden-brown crust. The texture appears light and airy. A light dusting of powdered sugar graces the top of each soufflé, creating a subtle contrast. The overall color palette is warm, with the creamy white interior hinted at by the golden exterior. The plating is clean and minimalist, allowing the soufflé to be the focal point. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside one ramekin. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet inviting atmosphere, typical of a modern bistro setting. The background is simple and unobtrusive, ensuring the focus remains on the elegantly presented dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Place oven rack in lower third.
Butter two 200ml ramekins. Coat interior with granulated sugar. Tap out excess.
In a small saucepan, whisk together skim milk, 20g granulated sugar, and cornstarch. Heat over medium heat, whisking constantly, until mixture thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in low-fat yogurt, blended cottage cheese, lemon zest, and vanilla extract. Set aside.
In a clean, dry bowl, whip egg whites with remaining 40g granulated sugar until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Fold one-third of the whipped egg whites into the yogurt mixture to lighten it. Gently fold in remaining egg whites until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide soufflé mixture evenly between prepared ramekins. Fill to the rim.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until soufflés are well-risen and golden brown on top.
Serve immediately. Dust with powdered sugar.

recipes.recipe_name: Whipped Yogurt and Cottage Cheese Mousse with Berry Coulis
recipes.visual_description: Two individual servings of light, creamy whipped mousse are presented in clear, elegant glass ramekins on a clean white porcelain plate. The mousse, a pristine off-white, has a smooth, airy texture. A vibrant, deep red berry coulis is spooned gracefully over the top of each mousse, creating an appealing contrast of color. A delicate sprinkle of finely crushed, toasted pistachios adds a subtle green hue and textural interest on the coulis. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the balanced composition and appropriate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, all under natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Crushed toasted pistachios or slivered almonds

instructions: Bloom gelatin: Sprinkle gelatin powder over cold water in a small bowl. Let sit for 5 minutes until hydrated.

Prepare berry coulis: Combine mixed berries, 15g of sugar, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Simmer over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes. Berries should soften. Press through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds. Cool completely.
Process cottage cheese: Place cottage cheese in a food processor or blender. Process until completely smooth and creamy. Scrape down sides as needed.
Melt gelatin: Gently heat bloomed gelatin in a microwave for 10-15 seconds, or over a double boiler, until fully melted and clear. Do not boil.
Combine ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together the processed cottage cheese, yogurt, remaining 35g sugar, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Incorporate gelatin: Slowly drizzle the melted gelatin into the yogurt mixture while whisking continuously until fully incorporated.
Chill mousse: Divide the mixture evenly into two clear glass ramekins or small dessert bowls. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2-3 hours, or until set.
Serve: Spoon berry coulis over the set mousse. Garnish each serving with a sprinkle of crushed toasted pistachios or slivered almonds. Serve chilled.
notes: This recipe is designed to be low-fat. Ensure all dairy products used are low-fat versions.
For best results, ensure the cottage cheese is blended until absolutely smooth to avoid any grainy texture in the mousse.

recipes.recipe_name: Low-Fat Lemon Berry Yogurt Cheesecake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly cut slice of Low-Fat Lemon Berry Yogurt Cheesecake is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The cheesecake slice displays a pale yellow, creamy interior with a smooth, even surface. Its base reveals a thin, golden-brown biscuit crust. A small, glossy pool of vibrant mixed berry compote is artfully drizzled over the top of the slice, with some of the crimson and purple compote cascading onto the plate, showcasing visible whole and halved berries. A delicate sprig of fresh mint is placed beside the slice as a simple garnish. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a clean, inviting restaurant-style atmosphere with a minimal background to keep focus on the dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Grease and line a 15cm springform pan.
Crush digestive biscuits finely. Mix with melted butter until combined.
Press biscuit mixture firmly into the bottom of the prepared pan. Bake for 8 minutes. Remove and cool.
In a food processor, blend cottage cheese until completely smooth. Scrape down sides as needed.

In a large bowl, whisk together the blended cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, 75g granulated sugar, eggs, lemon zest, lemon juice, cornstarch, and vanilla extract until smooth. Add milk if mixture is too thick.
Pour the filling over the cooled crust in the springform pan.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until the edges are set and the center has a slight jiggle. Do not overbake.
Turn off the oven. Leave the cheesecake in the oven with the door slightly ajar for 30 minutes to cool gradually. This prevents cracking.
Remove from oven. Cool completely on a wire rack. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, before serving.

For the berry topping, combine mixed berries, 15g sugar, and 15ml water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until berries soften and sauce thickens slightly.
Let berry topping cool completely before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Cauliflower, Garlic and Roasted Pepper Salad
recipes.visual_description: Cauliflower florets, light cream in color from fermentation, intermingle with vibrant red roasted bell pepper pieces, diced ripe red tomatoes, and thinly sliced purple-red onion. Fresh green parsley leaves are scattered throughout. The salad is generously piled on a large, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural beige tone, leaving ample white space around the edges. The components are distinct, showcasing their natural colors and textures—crisp cauliflower, tender roasted pepper, juicy tomato, and crunchy onion. A subtle sheen from the olive oil dressing coats the vegetables. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige hue is folded neatly to one side. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with hints of natural elements, such as a blurred green plant. A small, unglazed clay bowl, reflecting traditional Turkish pottery, holds a side of dressing, and an olive wood serving spoon rests nearby. The presentation is unfussy, celebrating the pure beauty and sustainability of each ingredient.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a vibrant side dish (meze) alongside grilled meats or fish.
Accompany with fresh Turkish bread (pide) for scooping.
Pair with a glass of traditional ayran (yogurt drink).
instructions: Prepare cauliflower for light fermentation. Cut 500g cauliflower into small florets. Reserve stem and outer leaves for other culinary uses.
Make brine. Dissolve 15g salt in 500ml water.

Lightly ferment cauliflower. Place cauliflower florets in a clean glass jar. Pour brine over, ensuring cauliflower is fully submerged. Seal jar. Let ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours. Drain well before use.
Roast bell peppers. Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve 2 bell peppers, remove seeds. Place cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until skin is charred and flesh is tender.
Peel and dice peppers. Once cooled, peel skin from roasted peppers. Dice into 1.5 cm pieces.
Prepare other vegetables. Dice 3 tomatoes into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice 1 red onion. Mince 2 cloves garlic.
Make dressing. In a small bowl, whisk 60ml olive oil, 30ml fresh lemon juice, 5g sumac, salt, and black pepper.
Combine salad. In a large bowl, combine drained fermented cauliflower, diced roasted bell peppers, diced tomatoes, sliced red onion, and minced garlic.
Dress and serve. Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine. Garnish with fresh parsley or mint before serving.
notes: This recipe emphasizes sustainability by using seasonal vegetables, incorporating fermentation for preservation, and focusing on a plant-forward, zero-waste approach by suggesting the use of cauliflower stems and leaves in other dishes.
The light fermentation enhances flavor complexity and shelf life.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Yogurt Cottage Cheese Cake
recipes.visual_description: A perfectly portioned triangular slice of Lemon Yogurt Cottage Cheese Cake rests elegantly on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The cake reveals a smooth, creamy, pale-yellow interior contrasting with a thin, golden-brown biscuit crust. The texture is uniform and dense. Vibrant fresh raspberries and blueberries are scattered beside the slice, alongside a delicate sprig of fresh mint. A thin, translucent slice of candied lemon is placed gently on top. The plate is positioned slightly off-center, with moderate negative space. The presentation is clean and refined, showcasing balanced colors and inviting textures. In the subtle background, the remaining small, round cake sits on a minimalist cake stand. The setting is a simple wooden table, with a silver dessert fork and folded white cotton napkin, all bathed in soft, natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Crush biscuits finely. Mix with melted butter. Press mixture evenly into the bottom of a 15 cm springform pan. Bake for 8 minutes. Remove and cool.
In a food processor, blend cottage cheese until completely smooth and creamy. Scrape down sides as needed.
In a large bowl, whisk together blended cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, sugar, eggs, milk, lemon juice, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Sift flour and salt into the wet mixture. Add lemon zest. Gently fold until just combined. Do not overmix.

Pour filling over the cooled crust in the springform pan. Place the springform pan in a larger roasting pan. Pour hot water into the roasting pan to come halfway up the sides of the springform pan (water bath).
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until edges are set but the center still jiggles slightly.
Turn off oven. Leave cake in the oven with the door ajar for 1 hour. Remove from water bath. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, before serving.
Carefully remove cake from pan. Cut into slices. Garnish each slice with fresh berries, a mint sprig, and a thin lemon slice.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Yogurt Cake
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown loaf cake, slightly domed, sits on a simple wire cooling rack in the background. It is generously drizzled with a glistening lemon glaze, allowing it to drip down the sides. A thick, neat slice is taken from the cake, revealing a pale yellow, moist, tender crumb with visible specks of lemon zest. This single slice is placed on a simple, round white ceramic plate. The scene is set on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. A casual, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone is beside the plate. A simple silver fork rests on the napkin. The lighting is soft and warm, suggesting natural light from a kitchen window, creating a homely, inviting atmosphere for a comforting dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20x10 cm loaf tin.
Combine yogurt, caster sugar, egg, vegetable oil, and lemon zest in a mixing bowl. Whisk until smooth.
Fold in the self-raising flour until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared loaf tin.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in the tin for 10 minutes.
Invert cake onto a wire cooling rack.
While cake cools, whisk icing sugar and lemon juice together in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Pour the glaze evenly over the warm cake. Let glaze set before slicing.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Bell Pepper Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of wide, flat pappardelle pasta is gently coiled and tossed with a rich, deep red beef and bell pepper ragu. The slow-simmered ground beef, cooked until tender, is interspersed with small, soft pieces of finely diced red and yellow bell pepper, and translucent diced onion, creating a harmonious texture within the robust sauce. The thick, luscious ragu clings beautifully to each pappardelle strand, showcasing its hearty consistency. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese provides a creamy, salty contrast. A few fresh basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered on top, adding a pop of bright green and aromatic freshness. The dish is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl, allowing for moderate negative space, on a simple wooden surface. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting colors, with a cotton napkin placed beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Prepare vegetables. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Dice red and yellow bell peppers into 1 cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add ground beef. Brown beef, breaking it up with a spoon. Cook until no pink remains. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables soften.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste to the pot. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly until fragrant.
Pour in red wine (if using). Simmer for 3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Season with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of sugar.
Bring the ragu to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and cook for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally. The ragu should thicken considerably.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in a large pot of salted boiling water. Drain pasta, reserving 125ml of the pasta water.
Add the cooked pasta directly to the ragu in the pot. Toss gently to coat the pasta evenly. Add reserved pasta water if needed to achieve desired consistency.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese and a few torn fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Truffle & Pickled Radish Bites
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve elegant, bite-sized canapés are artfully arranged on a smooth, light beige handcrafted ceramic platter. Each canapé features an irregularly shaped, pale golden parsnip crisp as its base. A creamy, off-white dollop of smooth cashew cream is piped onto each crisp, topped with thin, translucent rounds of vibrant pink pickled radish. Delicate, paper-thin shavings of dark black truffle crown each canapé, their intricate patterns visible. A scattering of bright green microgreens provides a minimalist flourish. The presentation is clean and uncluttered, emphasizing natural shapes and textures with ample negative space. The platter rests on a light-toned reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin, bathed in soft, diffused natural light, highlighting the pure beauty of each ingredient against a clean, minimalist background.
instructions: Soak cashews in hot water for 30 minutes, or cold water overnight. Drain well.
Thinly slice radishes into rounds or half-moons. Set aside.

In a small saucepan, combine rice vinegar, sugar, 2.5g salt, and 100ml water. Heat until sugar dissolves. Pour hot brine over sliced radishes. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 150°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Peel parsnip. Using a mandoline, slice parsnip very thinly into rounds. Toss parsnip slices with olive oil and remaining 2.5g salt. Arrange in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake parsnip slices for 20-30 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Flip halfway through. Cool completely on a wire rack.
In a high-speed blender, combine drained cashews, 50ml water, lemon juice, and a pinch of black pepper. Blend until very smooth and creamy, scraping down sides as needed.
To assemble, spread a small dollop of cashew cream onto each parsnip crisp. Top with 2-3 slices of pickled radish.
Using a truffle shaver, shave thin slices of fresh black truffle over each canapé.
Garnish with finely chopped chives or microgreens. Arrange 8-12 pieces on a serving platter.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing the entire parsnip for crisps and promoting the use of seasonal radishes. Consider using any leftover radish greens as an additional garnish or in a small salad.
Soaking cashews overnight yields the creamiest texture for the cashew cream.
Ensure parsnip crisps are fully cooled and crisp before assembly to prevent sogginess.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto al Tartufo Nero con Capesante Scottate
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy, fluid Risotto al Tartufo Nero is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto has a pale, inviting color from the Parmigiano Reggiano and the subtle infusion of black truffle, with visible flecks of grated truffle. Three perfectly seared, golden-brown sea scallops are arranged artfully on top of the risotto, showcasing their caramelized crust. Delicate, thin shavings of fresh black truffle are elegantly draped over the scallops and risotto, adding a striking dark contrast. A light drizzle of high-quality extra virgin olive oil glistens on the surface. A small sprig of vibrant green Italian parsley provides a fresh, aromatic garnish. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space around the dish, highlighting the food. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table surface, a folded white cotton napkin positioned beside the plate, and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional yet inviting atmosphere, with a subtly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp, dry Italian white wine such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with extra virgin olive oil and lemon as a light accompaniment.
Provide additional freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano on the side for those who desire more.
instructions: Prepare broth: Heat vegetable broth in a saucepan. Keep it warm, just simmering.
Sauté shallots: In a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven, melt 20g butter with 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Do not brown.
Toast rice: Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges but opaque in the center.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.
Add broth: Begin adding warm broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Wait until each ladleful is almost completely absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
Grate truffle: After 10 minutes of adding broth, grate 10g of fresh black truffle directly into the risotto. Continue stirring and adding broth.
Check consistency: Risotto is done when it is creamy and fluid (al dente). The rice should have a slight bite.

Mantecare: Remove risotto from heat. Stir in remaining 40g butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Stir vigorously until butter and cheese are fully incorporated and risotto is very creamy. Cover and let rest 2 minutes.
Prepare scallops: While risotto rests, pat scallops very dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper.

Sear scallops: Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a separate heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering. Place scallops in the hot pan, ensuring they do not touch. Sear for 1.5-2 minutes per side until deeply golden brown and caramelized. Do not overcook.
Plate: Ladle risotto onto warm white plates. Place 3 seared scallops artfully on top of each risotto portion.
Garnish: Shave remaining 10g fresh black truffle generously over the scallops and risotto. Sprinkle with chopped Italian parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: The quality of the fresh black truffle is paramount for this dish's flavor and aroma.
Ensure the vegetable broth is always warm when adding to the risotto to maintain a consistent cooking temperature.
Risotto should be served immediately after preparation to enjoy its optimal creamy and fluid texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Red Onion & Chili Toast with Cured Beef Pastirma
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated starter portion on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. A thick-cut slice of golden-brown sourdough toast, lightly glistening with olive oil, forms the base. Centered on the toast is a vibrant mound of fermented red onion and chili relish, showcasing translucent red onion slices and bright red chili flecks. The relish has a slightly glossy, moist texture. Nestled atop the relish are several folded, thin slices of cured beef pastirma, their deep reddish-brown color contrasting with the relish. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped green parsley adds a pop of color. The plate features ample white space, emphasizing the dish's minimalistic nature. The scene is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin in natural beige and simple, traditional flatware to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting textures. A hint of natural green foliage is visible in the clean, blurred background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a meze spread alongside other small dishes.
Accompany with strong Turkish black tea or a glass of rakı.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.quantity: 1, thinly sliced (seeds removed for less heat)

instructions: Prepare the fermented relish: Combine thinly sliced red onions and chili in a clean glass jar. Dissolve salt in non-chlorinated water to create a brine. Pour brine over onions and chili, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Store in refrigerator after fermentation.
Drain fermented relish from brine before serving. Set aside.
Lightly toast sourdough bread slices until golden brown and crisp.
Drizzle each toasted sourdough slice with olive oil.
Spoon a generous amount of the fermented red onion and chili relish onto each toast.
Arrange thin slices of cured beef pastirma on top of the relish. Do not fan out.
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: The fermentation time for the relish can vary based on desired sourness and ambient temperature. A longer ferment (up to 7-10 days) will yield a deeper flavor.
Ensure onions and chili remain submerged during fermentation to prevent mold.
This recipe assumes the fermented relish is prepared in advance. Plan for 3-5 days for fermentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Tom Kha Gai
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tom Kha Gai is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. The creamy, off-white soup base is rich and inviting, with tender 2cm chicken cubes visible throughout. Halved straw mushrooms add a soft, earthy texture. The surface of the soup is garnished with vibrant green fresh cilantro leaves, a few thin slices of red bird's eye chili, and a small lime wedge resting on the rim of the bowl. The arrangement is natural and flowing, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, beside a small white rice bowl and a metal spoon. A folded cotton napkin is placed to the side. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable bistro atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the balanced composition without overcrowding.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed jasmine rice.
Offer extra fresh lime wedges and chilies for individual adjustment of flavor.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh
Lemongrass
ingredients.quantity: 2 stalks, bruised and cut into 5cm pieces

instructions: Prepare aromatics: Thinly slice galangal. Bruise lemongrass stalks with the back of a knife, then cut into 5cm pieces. Tear kaffir lime leaves.
Combine liquids: In a large pot, combine coconut milk and chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Infuse aromatics: Add sliced galangal, bruised lemongrass, and torn kaffir lime leaves to the simmering liquid. Simmer for 5-7 minutes to infuse flavors.

Add chicken and mushrooms: Add the cubed chicken to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and continue to simmer until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and mushrooms are tender.

Season the soup: Remove the pot from heat. Stir in fish sauce, fresh lime juice, palm sugar, and crushed bird's eye chilies. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed for a balance of sour, sweet, salty, and spicy.
Serve: Ladle the Tom Kha Gai into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro leaves and a few extra chili slices if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust the amount of chili to your preferred spice level.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the four fundamental Thai flavors (sour, sweet, salty, spicy)

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef and Lentil Comfort Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Spicy Beef and Lentil Comfort Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew is a rich, deep reddish-brown, showcasing tender, thick chunks of braised beef, plump brown lentils, and clearly visible diced carrots and onions. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a vibrant color contrast. The stew fills the bowl generously but not overflowing, creating an inviting, comforting appearance. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl on a casually draped cloth napkin. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Serve with a simple green salad
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 3 cm thick chunks. Season beef generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef chunks on all sides until well seared. Remove beef from the pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and diced carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables begin to soften.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return the browned beef to the pot. Stir in beef broth, hot sauce, Dijon mustard, and canned diced tomatoes.
Add brown lentils to the pot. Stir to combine all ingredients.
Bring the stew to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the beef is fork-tender and the lentils are cooked through. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Ensure the internal temperature of the beef reaches 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Taste the stew and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve the Spicy Beef and Lentil Comfort Stew hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust hot sauce quantity to your preferred spice level.
This stew freezes well for future meals.

recipes.recipe_name: Taro Entremet with Ginger Sponge and Kecap Manis Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, precisely cut square slice of Taro Entremet sits elegantly on a pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim. The cake reveals distinct, architectural layers: a tender, pale ginger sponge base, a thin, dark black sesame praline crunch, and a thick, smooth lavender-grey taro mousse. The entremet is encased in a deep, glossy kecap manis mirror glaze, reflecting light beautifully. A few delicate candied coriander seeds are artfully scattered around the base, with a single, shimmering edible gold leaf flake on top. The plate rests on a polished white marble surface, creating abundant negative space. A small, elegant silver dessert fork and a crisp white linen napkin are placed beside it. Dramatic lighting highlights the cake's refined textures and minimalist elegance. The background is clean, emphasizing the haute patisserie aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served best with a light, fragrant Indonesian tea, such as Jasmine or Green Tea, to complement the cake's subtle flavors.

ingredients.name: gelatin leaves (gold strength), bloomed in ice water
gelatin leaves (gold strength), bloomed in ice water

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 20x20 cm baking tray with parchment.
Whisk eggs and 60g sugar in a heatproof bowl over a bain-marie until warm and thick.
Remove from heat. Continue whisking until cool and pale.
Fold in grated ginger.
Sift 60g flour, baking powder, and salt. Gently fold into egg mixture.
Pour batter into prepared tray. Spread evenly.
Bake 10-12 minutes. Sponge is golden and springs back.
Cool completely on a wire rack. Cut into a 15x15 cm square. Set aside.
Melt 50g sugar in a saucepan over medium heat until golden caramel.
Stir in black sesame seeds and 5g butter. Mix quickly.
Pour onto a silicone mat. Spread thinly.
Cool completely. Break into small pieces. Process in a food processor to coarse crumbs. Do not over-process to a paste. Set aside.
Steam diced taro until very tender.
Combine steamed taro, 50ml milk, and 50ml cream in a blender. Blend until very smooth.
Press mixture through a fine-mesh sieve.
Heat strained taro puree with 50g sugar over low heat. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin (3 leaves). Stir into warm taro puree until dissolved.
Cool taro mixture to room temperature.
Whip 200ml cold heavy cream to soft peaks.
Gently fold whipped cream into cooled taro mixture in three additions.
Line a 16 cm square cake ring or mold with acetate film.
Place the 15 cm ginger sponge square inside the mold.
Spread an even layer of black sesame praline crunch over the sponge. Press lightly.
Pour taro mousse over the praline layer. Smooth the top.
Freeze entremet for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until completely solid.
Combine 100g sugar and 100ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Remove from heat.
Stir in kecap manis and rice vinegar.
Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin (6 leaves). Stir into warm glaze until dissolved.
Strain glaze through a fine-mesh sieve.
Cool glaze to 30-32°C.
Place frozen entremet on a wire rack over a baking tray.
Pour cooled glaze evenly over frozen entremet. Ensure full coverage.
Let excess glaze drip. Use an offset spatula to remove drips from bottom edge.
Carefully transfer entremet to a serving plate.
Refrigerate for 2-3 hours to thaw and set glaze.
Combine 10g coriander seeds, 20ml water, and 20g sugar in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil. Simmer until water evaporates and sugar crystallizes around seeds.
Remove from heat. Spread on parchment paper to cool.
Slice entremet into 4 equal portions.
Place one slice elegantly on each plate.
Scatter a few candied coriander seeds around the base of the cake.
Garnish with a small flake of edible gold leaf on top.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are at correct temperatures for optimal emulsion and setting.
For best results, use a high-quality kecap manis for the glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Pork Goulash
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Hungarian Pork Goulash is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl. Thick, succulent chunks of braised pork, rich with a reddish-brown hue, are nestled among tender, vibrant red and green bell pepper strips and softened diced onions. The dish is enveloped in a glossy, thick, deep reddish-brown paprika-infused sauce. A small, creamy dollop of bright white sour cream crowns the center, garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped vivid green parsley. The composition is naturally arranged, allowing the rich colors and textures of the stew to dominate. The bowl rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table, with a neatly folded white cotton napkin placed beside it. Lighting is soft, even, and natural, highlighting the warmth and depth of the dish. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere. A small, separate serving of traditional Hungarian nokedli (dumplings) or crusty bread is subtly visible beside the main bowl, completing the authentic presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with nokedli (Hungarian dumplings)
Serve with boiled potatoes
Serve with crusty bread
Garnish with a dollop of sour cream
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 4-5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onions to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, sweet paprika, smoked paprika, and crushed caraway seeds. Stir constantly for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not burn the paprika.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add bell pepper strips, crushed tomatoes, bay leaf, and beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2-2.5 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Uncover the pot for the last 30 minutes of cooking. This allows the sauce to thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Remove bay leaf before serving.
Serve hot, garnished with a dollop of sour cream and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Paprika Chicken and Noodle Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic portion of Creamy Paprika Chicken and Noodle Skillet is served in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl. Tender, seared chicken chunks with golden-brown edges are nestled among wide, flat egg noodles. The noodles and chicken are generously coated in a rich, creamy, orange-red paprika sauce. Visible chunks of diced red onion, vibrant green and red bell pepper strips, and small carrot rounds add color and texture. The dish is piled naturally, allowing the thick, comforting sauce to pool slightly at the bottom of the bowl. A sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and bright green chopped parsley garnish the top. The bowl sits on a well-worn, light wooden kitchen table. A simple, slightly textured off-white linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl, with a metal fork resting on it. Warm, diffused lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a homey kitchen counter, maintaining focus on the comforting meal.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2.5 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet; set aside. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Dice onion. Thinly slice bell peppers. Cut carrot into small rounds. Add onion, bell peppers, and carrot to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Mince garlic. Add paprika, curry powder, and minced garlic to the skillet. Stir and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
While sauce simmers, cook egg noodles according to package directions. Drain well.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in sour cream until well combined. Do not boil after adding sour cream to prevent curdling.
Add cooked noodles to the skillet with the chicken and sauce. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Grate Parmesan cheese. Serve hot, garnished with grated Parmesan and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken Paprika Noodles
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous portion of creamy, reddish-orange paprika-coated egg noodles. Tender, chunky pieces of chicken are nestled throughout the noodles. Vibrant red bell pepper strips and bright orange julienned carrots are visibly mixed in, adding color and texture. The rich, glossy sauce lightly coats all elements. A delicate swirl of lighter sour cream is visible on top, enhancing the creamy appearance. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped bright green parsley and a light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, standard flatware, and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a soft, restaurant-style background.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 4-5 cm chunks. Season with salt and black pepper.
Dice the onion. Slice the red bell pepper into thin strips. Julienne the carrot. Mince garlic cloves.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add sliced bell pepper and julienned carrot. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly softened.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in sweet Hungarian paprika and smoked paprika. Stir constantly for 30 seconds to toast spices, being careful not to burn them.
Return pot to heat. Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, cook egg noodles according to package directions in a separate pot of salted boiling water until al dente. Drain well.
Remove chicken from the pot. Stir sour cream into the sauce. Do not boil after adding sour cream. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Return chicken to the sauce. Add drained egg noodles to the pot with the chicken and sauce. Toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately. Garnish with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled King Prawns with Sambal Matah Foam, Blue Cheese Tuile, and Compressed Lemon Cucumber
recipes.visual_description: Four perfectly grilled king prawns, their shells exhibiting a vibrant orange hue with delicate char marks, are artfully arranged on a pristine, matte white bone china plate. The prawns are positioned organically, creating a subtle diagonal flow across the generous negative space. Beside them, a light, airy cloud of off-white Sambal Matah foam rises elegantly, flecked with minute specks of red chili and green lemongrass. Scattered precisely around the foam are a few translucent, vibrant green discs of compressed lemon cucumber, catching the light. A delicate, irregularly shaped blue cheese tuile, crisp and pale gold, is perched artfully near the prawns, adding a textural contrast. A subtle drizzle of glistening garlic-infused oil completes the composition. The setting features a polished grey marble surface, a precisely folded white linen napkin, and elegant, minimalist flatware, all under dramatic, directional lighting that casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's sophisticated simplicity and refined aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as a refined standalone course, honoring the dish's centerpiece status.
Traditionally, a small portion of steamed white rice might accompany such a dish in a separate, elegant ceramic bowl, though not essential for this refined presentation.

ingredients.name: King Prawns, peeled, deveined, tail on
Blue Cheese (e.g., Gorgonzola Dolce or Stilton)
Red Bird's Eye Chilies, thinly sliced
Lemongrass, white part only, thinly sliced

instructions: Prepare Compressed Lemon Cucumber: Peel cucumber. Slice into 5mm thick rounds. Using a small round cutter, create uniform discs. Zest and juice one lemon. In a vacuum seal bag, combine cucumber discs with lemon juice and zest. Vacuum seal. Chill for 30 minutes.

Prepare Blue Cheese Tuile: Preheat oven to 160°C. Crumble blue cheese. Mix blue cheese, flour, and water into a smooth paste. Spread a very thin layer onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Bake 8-10 minutes until crisp and golden brown. Cool on a wire rack. Break into irregular pieces.

Prepare Garlic-Infused Oil: Thinly slice garlic cloves. Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add garlic slices. Cook slowly until garlic is lightly golden and fragrant. Remove from heat. Strain garlic oil. Reserve crispy garlic for garnish or discard.

Prepare Sambal Matah Foam: In a bowl, combine thinly sliced shallots, red chilies, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and minced garlic. Add coconut milk, fish sauce, and sugar. Stir well. Add soy lecithin. Using an immersion blender, blend until smooth and frothy. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into a siphon bottle. Charge with N2O cartridge. Shake well. Keep warm in a water bath.

Prepare King Prawns: Pat prawns dry. Lightly brush with a small amount of garlic-infused oil. Season with salt and pepper. Heat a grill pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Grill prawns 2-3 minutes per side until opaque and slightly charred. Do not overcook.

Assemble Dish: Drain compressed cucumber. Arrange 4 grilled prawns artfully on each plate, leaving ample negative space. Dispense a cloud of Sambal Matah Foam alongside the prawns. Arrange a few pieces of compressed lemon cucumber around the foam. Place one or two irregular blue cheese tuile pieces on or near the prawns. Drizzle a small amount of garlic-infused oil around the plate for visual appeal and flavor. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the Sambal Matah foam is light and airy. The soy lecithin quantity is crucial for stability.
The blue cheese tuile should be very thin and crisp for delicate texture and subtle flavor.
Do not overcook the prawns; they should remain tender and succulent.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Thyme Mincemeat with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty mincemeat, seasoned with chili and thyme, is centrally mounded on a clean white porcelain plate. The mincemeat, a rich reddish-brown, has a slightly coarse, crumbly texture. Surrounding the base of the mincemeat are golden-brown roasted potato wedges and tender, slightly charred carrot chunks. These vegetables exhibit varied textures, from crispy edges to soft interiors. Bright green fresh thyme leaves are scattered over the mincemeat, with a small, vibrant red chili slice providing a pop of contrasting color. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, illuminated by soft, natural light, with moderate negative space on the plate to highlight the food. A plain white cotton napkin is placed neatly beside the plate, completing a refined yet approachable casual dining presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and cut potatoes into rustic wedges. Peel and cut carrots into thick chunks.
Toss potatoes and carrots with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden-brown. Turn halfway.
While vegetables roast, dice onions. Finely chop chilies. Mince garlic. Strip thyme leaves from sprigs.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add mincemeat to the pan. Break it apart with a spoon. Sear until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onions, chopped chilies, minced garlic, and thyme leaves to the pan with the mincemeat. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until onions soften.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens.
Season mincemeat with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve mincemeat hot, accompanied by roasted vegetables.
notes: Adjust chili quantity based on desired spice level.
Lamb mincemeat can be used as an alternative to beef.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora Rustico
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion of rustic Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks, approximately 4 cm, are nestled amongst vibrant strips of red, yellow, and orange bell peppers and tender diced onions. The ingredients are coated in a rich, deeply savory tomato-herb sauce, which gathers naturally around the components. Fresh basil leaves, torn or roughly chopped, are scattered over the dish, providing a contrasting green pop and aromatic appeal. The dish is centrally placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a slice of crusty artisan bread. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and inviting colors. The presentation is professional yet approachable, emphasizing the quality ingredients and traditional Italian comfort.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread for dipping in the sauce (fare la scarpetta).
Can be accompanied by a side of al dente pasta or creamy polenta.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Cut bell peppers into 2 cm wide strips. Dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the hot oil. Sear until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Do not overcrowd the pot; work in batches if necessary. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add bell pepper strips. Sauté for 7-8 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to loosen any browned bits. Reduce by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer.

Return the seared chicken chunks to the pot. Ensure chicken is submerged in the sauce. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Remove from heat. Stir in fresh basil leaves just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Ayam Consommé with Annatto & Forest Mushroom Essence
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Ayam Consommé is presented in a deep, wide, pristine white bone china bowl, featuring an elegant, flowing composition. The consommé itself is a brilliant, clear golden-amber, hinting at its rich, nuanced flavor. At the base, three to four perfectly poached chicken medallions, pristine white and cut into precise rounds, are artfully arranged. Alongside, two or three thinly sliced, lightly seared shiitake mushrooms are placed with intentional precision, offering a contrasting earthy tone. The surface of the consommé is adorned with a few small, vibrant green dots of coriander oil, creating a subtle color contrast. A few delicate, finely julienned red chili strips are meticulously placed as a final, precise garnish. The ample negative space in the bowl emphasizes the minimalist sophistication. The bowl rests on a premium grey veined marble surface, accompanied by a precisely folded white linen napkin and an elegant, modern stainless steel spoon. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish remains the sole focal point under dramatic, professional lighting with soft shadows.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Stock: Roughly chop chicken bones. Roast bones at 200°C for 30 minutes until golden. Place roasted bones, chopped onion, carrot, celery, and leek in a large pot. Add 3 litres of cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Skim impurities. Simmer gently for 3 hours, maintaining a low heat. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Chill stock.

Infuse Stock: In a small saucepan, toast annatto seeds over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant. Add annatto seeds, sliced ginger, and coriander roots/stems to the chilled chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer. Infuse for 30 minutes. Strain out aromatics and annatto seeds. The stock should have a golden-amber hue.

Clarify Consommé: In a bowl, whisk egg whites until frothy. Combine egg whites with the strained, infused chicken stock. Heat gently, stirring constantly until egg whites form a raft on top. Stop stirring. Simmer very gently for 20 minutes without disturbing the raft. Carefully ladle the clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Season consommé with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Mushroom Essence: Rehydrate dried shiitake mushrooms in 500 ml hot water for 30 minutes. Strain liquid, reserving mushrooms. Gently press mushrooms to extract more liquid. Reduce mushroom liquid over medium heat until intensely flavorful and concentrated (approx. 100 ml). Slice rehydrated mushrooms thinly. Sear mushroom slices lightly in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant.

Poach Chicken Medallions: Bring a small pot of salted water to a bare simmer. Add chicken breast. Poach gently for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Cool slightly. Slice chicken breast into thin, round medallions.

Prepare Coriander Oil: Blanch fresh coriander leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately plunge into ice water. Drain well. Blend blanched coriander with 50 ml neutral oil until smooth and vibrant green. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for clear oil.

Assemble and Serve: Place 3-4 chicken medallions in the center of each serving bowl. Artfully arrange a few seared mushroom slices around the chicken. Pour hot, clear consommé over the chicken and mushrooms. Drizzle small dots of vibrant coriander oil around the consommé. Garnish with a few delicate julienned red chili strips. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Prawns with Spicy Tomato Risotto and Basil Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant red-orange spicy tomato risotto is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The risotto is creamy and fluid, not dry, and forms a natural, appealing mound. Three to four plump, pan-seared prawns, their shells a delicate pink with caramelized edges, are artfully arranged on top of the risotto, showcasing their natural curvature. A bright green basil oil is drizzled sparingly over the prawns and around the risotto, providing a striking color contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers parts of the risotto and prawns. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with natural, even lighting highlighting the textures and colors. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate, and a silver fork and knife are placed to the right and left, respectively. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, allowing the dish to be the undisputed focal point.
instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves and minced red chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes until grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Stir until absorbed.
Add hot stock, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for liquid to be absorbed before adding more.
Continue adding stock and stirring for 18-20 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and rice al dente.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in 75 grams grated Parmesan and 20 grams butter. Cover and let rest for 2 minutes.
While risotto rests, prepare prawns. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat.
Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Cook for 30 seconds.
Add prawns. Cook for 2 minutes per side until pink and opaque.
Add soy sauce and vanilla extract to the pan. Cook for 30 seconds, coating prawns.
For basil oil, combine fresh basil leaves and 30 ml olive oil in a small blender. Blend until smooth. Season with a pinch of salt.
Season risotto with salt and pepper. Stir well.
Serve risotto immediately. Top with pan-seared prawns. Drizzle with basil oil. Garnish with remaining grated Parmesan and a few small basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Umami Tomato-Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, vibrant reddish-orange tomato sauce with visible flecks of red chili and green basil is generously spooned over and around the chicken, creating a rustic, flowing presentation. The sauce appears slightly chunky, showcasing the cooked down tomatoes. Fresh, verdant basil leaves, some torn and some whole, are artfully scattered over the chicken and sauce, adding a burst of color and freshness. A delicate dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese provides a contrasting white accent. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin placed beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and vibrant colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes to the skillet. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in soy sauce and 40 g of the grated Parmesan cheese. Simmer 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in vanilla extract and most of the fresh basil.
Return chicken to skillet, spooning sauce over each piece.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato-Basil Confit and Chili-Soy-Vanilla Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, cut into two or three thick, succulent medallions, is artfully positioned on a pristine white round plate. The chicken boasts a beautiful golden-brown crust, indicating a perfect sear. Adjacent to the chicken, a vibrant mound of tomato-basil confit presents a rustic yet refined cluster of ruby-red halved cherry tomatoes, softened garlic, and hints of green basil, glistening from olive oil. A rich, dark amber chili-soy-vanilla reduction is elegantly drizzled over the chicken and around the confit, adding a glossy sheen. A delicate, golden parmesan crisp stands upright beside the chicken, providing a textural contrast. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered thoughtfully as a final garnish, enhancing color and freshness. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and professional, set against a simple wooden table with natural, even lighting. A crisp white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate, completing the modern bistro aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Grate parmesan cheese. Form four small mounds on the baking sheet. Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Let cool and harden. These are parmesan crisps.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice 4 garlic cloves. Thinly slice red chili.

Combine halved tomatoes, sliced garlic, sliced chili, and half of the basil leaves (roughly torn) in a small oven-safe dish. Pour 80ml olive oil over. Season with salt and pepper. Bake for 25-30 minutes until tomatoes are soft and slightly caramelized. This is the tomato-basil confit.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes until golden brown crust forms. Flip chicken.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken, let rest on a cutting board.

While chicken rests, make reduction. Drain excess fat from skillet. Add chicken stock, soy sauce, and remaining 2 garlic cloves (smashed). Split vanilla bean lengthwise, scrape seeds into skillet, add pod. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce liquid by half, about 8-10 minutes, until slightly thickened. Remove garlic and vanilla pod. Stir in butter until melted and glossy. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick pieces or serve whole if small. Arrange chicken on plates. Spoon tomato-basil confit alongside. Drizzle generously with chili-soy-vanilla reduction. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and a parmesan crisp.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The vanilla bean adds a subtle, aromatic complexity to the reduction without being overtly sweet.
Adjust chili quantity to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Spicy Tomato-Soy Glaze and Garlic-Parmesan Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of pan-seared chicken breast rests on a bed of creamy, golden-yellow garlic-Parmesan polenta on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, golden-brown from searing, is placed slightly off-center. A rich, deep red spicy tomato-soy glaze is artfully drizzled over the chicken and around the polenta, creating a vibrant contrast. Fresh, bright green basil leaves, some whole, some roughly torn, are scattered over the chicken and polenta, adding a pop of color and freshness. The chicken breast is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its perfectly cooked texture. The polenta maintains a fluid, creamy consistency. The overall composition is balanced with appropriate negative space. The plate is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere with minimal distractions, focusing entirely on the culinary presentation.
instructions: Prepare polenta: Bring chicken stock to a simmer in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, until thickened and creamy, about 5-7 minutes for instant polenta. Stir in half of the minced garlic, Parmesan cheese, and butter. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a plate; tent with foil.

Make glaze: In the same skillet, add remaining minced garlic and chili flakes. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Stir in crushed tomatoes, soy sauce, and sugar. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla extract.

Plate the dish: Spoon a generous portion of creamy garlic-Parmesan polenta onto each plate. Place one seared chicken breast on top of the polenta. Drizzle the spicy tomato-soy glaze generously over the chicken and around the plate. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Chili-Tomato-Soy Glaze and Parmesan Basil Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is generously coated with a glossy, vibrant reddish-orange chili-tomato-soy glaze, showcasing small, tender pieces of cooked cherry tomato and flecks of red chili. A sprinkle of bright green basil and white grated Parmesan cheese forms a fresh, aromatic crumble over the chicken and glaze, adding textural contrast. The plate features moderate negative space, allowing the dish to be the focal point. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin placed neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish.

ingredients.name: Red chili, thinly sliced (seeds removed for less heat, optional)

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and sliced chili to the skillet. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add halved cherry tomatoes, soy sauce, chicken stock, and vanilla extract to the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, crushing tomatoes slightly, until sauce thickens slightly.

In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with cold water to create a slurry. Stir slurry into the simmering sauce. Cook 1-2 minutes, stirring, until glaze thickens to desired consistency. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Combine grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh basil in a small bowl.
To serve, place one chicken breast on each plate. Spoon generous amount of chili-tomato-soy glaze over chicken. Sprinkle Parmesan basil crumble evenly over the chicken and glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Tomato-Vanilla Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of long spaghetti pasta is neatly coiled on a round white porcelain plate, forming a modest mound in the center. The pasta is coated in a vibrant, rich red-orange tomato sauce, flecked with small pieces of red chili and dark green basil. The sauce has a glossy, slightly creamy texture. Three to four thick, golden-brown seared chicken chunks (not sliced or fanned) are placed atop the pasta. The chicken pieces show a distinct crust from searing. Fresh, whole green basil leaves are scattered generously over the chicken and pasta. A light dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese rests on top. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space around the pasta. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Standard flatware (fork and spoon) are positioned. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating subtle shadows. The background is a softly blurred, neutral-toned wall, keeping focus on the food.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the pan. Sauté diced onion 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sliced chili. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Stir in soy sauce and vanilla extract. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
While sauce simmers, cook spaghetti in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Add cooked spaghetti to the sauce. Add grated Parmesan. Toss well. Add reserved pasta water gradually to reach desired sauce consistency.
Slice chicken breasts into thick chunks. Divide pasta among 4 plates. Top each with sliced chicken. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Spicy Tomato-Basil Pan Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate set on a simple wooden table. A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, perfectly cooked, is placed slightly off-center. It is generously coated with a vibrant, reddish-orange tomato-basil pan sauce, rich with visible flecks of red chili and minced garlic. The sauce pools around the chicken, showcasing its smooth, slightly chunky texture. Fresh, bright green basil leaves, roughly chopped, are scattered over the chicken and sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. A delicate sprinkle of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese rests atop the chicken and sauce, adding subtle textural contrast. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. Adjacent to the plate, a crisp white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are neatly arranged. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and appealing textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
Pair with a dry red wine like Chianti.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken thighs to the hot skillet. Sear 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and chili flakes to the skillet. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in soy sauce and vanilla extract.
Simmer sauce 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Return chicken to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Stir in half of the fresh basil.
Serve chicken immediately, topped with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Adjust chili flakes for desired spice level.
Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Soy-Chili Glaze and Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and coated with a glossy, deep amber-brown soy-chili-vanilla glaze, rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented whole, with its plump, moist interior implied by its firm, seared exterior. Beside the chicken, a vibrant mound of roasted cherry tomatoes displays soft, slightly burst skins and bright red, tender pulp, intermingled with tender, golden-brown garlic slices. Fresh, verdant green torn basil leaves are artfully scattered over the tomatoes and chicken, providing a herbaceous contrast. Delicate, creamy white curls of shaved parmesan cascade over the dish, adding a refined touch. A sprinkle of bright green thinly sliced spring onions and a few vivid red chili rings add pops of fresh color and texture. The overall plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space, presented on a simple light wooden table surface. A folded light grey cotton napkin and standard silver flatware accompany the plate, under soft, natural, even lighting that suggests a modern bistro setting with a subtly blurred background.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.quantity: 2 (1-2 sliced for glaze, 1 thinly sliced for garnish)

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Prepare the glaze: Combine soy sauce, 4 minced garlic cloves, 1-2 sliced red chilies, vanilla extract, honey, and grated ginger in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Mix cornstarch with 30 ml water to create a slurry. Whisk slurry into simmering glaze. Cook, stirring, until glaze thickens. Remove from heat.
Roast tomatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C. On a baking tray, toss cherry tomatoes with 2 sliced garlic cloves, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast tomatoes for 15-20 minutes, until softened and slightly burst.
Sear chicken: Heat 15 ml neutral cooking oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Glaze chicken: During the last 2 minutes of cooking, brush chicken generously with the prepared glaze. Continue cooking briefly to allow glaze to caramelize onto chicken.
Plate: Place a chicken breast on each plate. Spoon roasted tomatoes next to the chicken.
Garnish: Scatter fresh torn basil, shaved parmesan, thinly sliced spring onions, and remaining thinly sliced red chili over the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Parmesan Chicken Risotto
recipes.visual_description: This dish presents as a vibrant, creamy Italian risotto, centered on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is fluid and spreads naturally on the plate, not molded. Golden-brown seared chicken pieces, approximately 2-3 cm chunks, are generously mixed throughout the creamy, pale ivory Arborio rice. Specks of finely minced garlic are visible within the rice. The surface is glistening from the heavy cream and melted Parmesan. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley leaves provides a fresh counterpoint of color and texture. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese sits atop the risotto. The overall impression is rich, comforting, and elegant. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware. A folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, with a softly blurred, casual bistro background. This is a single, refined restaurant portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to soak up the creamy risotto.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm pieces. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
In the same pan, melt 30g butter over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Cook until translucent, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.

Begin adding warm chicken broth, one ladle (approx. 125ml) at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for liquid to be almost fully absorbed before adding next ladle. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente and creamy.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30g butter, 100ml heavy cream, and 100g grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Stir vigorously until creamy.
Gently fold in cooked chicken pieces.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining Parmigiano Reggiano and fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken broth is warm before adding to risotto for even cooking.
Stir risotto continuously for best creamy texture.
Use freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano for superior flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Garlic Parmesan Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and moist, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is a whole piece, not sliced. It is generously coated and surrounded by a rich, ivory-colored creamy garlic parmesan sauce that glistens subtly. The sauce shows tiny flecks of minced garlic and melted cheese. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a contrasting pop of color on top of the chicken and sauce. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space around the dish. The scene features a simple wooden table surface, a folded white linen napkin beside the plate, and standard restaurant flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce
Accompany with a simple green salad with vinaigrette
instructions: Pound chicken breasts to an even 2 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. Whisk constantly until cheese melts and sauce thickens slightly.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Parmesan Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, is the focal point on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. It is generously coated with a creamy, pale ivory garlic Parmesan sauce, which pools invitingly around its base. The chicken displays a crisp, caramelized exterior from searing. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is scattered over the chicken and sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a light, natural wood table surface, with a folded off-white cotton napkin beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware is placed neatly alongside. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and warm tones. The arrangement is professional, balanced, and approachable, with moderate negative space on the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pasta, polenta, or crusty Italian bread to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt, pepper, and Italian herbs.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add shallot to skillet. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half.
Stir in heavy cream and Parmesan cheese. Whisk until smooth. Simmer 2-3 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Saltimbocca with Parmesan Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Saltimbocca with Parmesan Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table. The creamy, off-white Parmesan risotto forms a free-flowing base, exhibiting a soft, fluid consistency. A golden-brown, pan-seared chicken medallion, secured with a toothpick and showing a hint of prosciutto and sage, rests gracefully atop the risotto. Fresh green sage leaves are scattered around the chicken and risotto, adding vibrant color. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese completes the dish. The setting is a modern bistro, with a cotton napkin folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors. The background is softly blurred, maintaining focus on the food while suggesting a casual, refined dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of crisp Italian white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
Offer crusty Italian bread for soaking up any remaining sauce or risotto.
instructions: Prepare chicken: Pound chicken breasts to 1 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper. Lay two prosciutto slices on each chicken piece. Place two sage leaves on top of prosciutto.
Fold chicken: Fold each chicken piece in half, securing with a toothpick if needed.
Sear chicken: Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken. Keep warm.
Start risotto: In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil and 20g butter. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Toast rice: Add Arborio rice. Stir 2 minutes until translucent.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add broth: Add broth, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for each ladle to be absorbed before adding the next. Continue 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Finish risotto: Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 30g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute. Risotto should be fluid and creamy.
Plate dish: Ladle risotto onto plates. Place one chicken saltimbocca medallion on top of risotto. Garnish with fresh sage leaves and extra grated Parmesan.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the risotto remains creamy and fluid; it should not be dry or overly stiff. Add a little more hot broth if needed at the end.
