Use high-quality prosciutto for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Georgian Chicken and Suluguni Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Georgian Chicken and Suluguni Stew is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rich, reddish-brown stew features substantial, tender chicken chunks and soft, off-white potato pieces, coated in a savory tomato-based sauce. Melted suluguni cheese threads through the stew, adding a creamy, inviting texture. Vibrant green flecks of fresh chopped cilantro and parsley are scattered generously over the top. The stew has a comforting, hearty appearance with natural, flowing lines. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's warm colors and inviting textures. A small piece of traditional Georgian shotis puri bread rests on the table, completing the authentic cultural presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh Shotis Puri (Georgian bread) for dipping.
Accompany with a simple fresh cucumber and tomato salad.
Enjoy with a glass of dry red Georgian wine.
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender. Peel and cut into 2-3 cm chunks. Set aside.
Cut chicken breasts into 4-5 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer 20 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Add boiled potato chunks to the stew. Simmer uncovered 5 minutes to combine flavors.
Grate or thinly slice suluguni cheese. Add cheese to the stew, stirring gently until melted and incorporated.
Stir in chopped fresh cilantro and parsley. Adjust seasoning. Serve hot.
notes: For authentic Georgian flavor, add 5g Khmeli Suneli spice blend with the tomato paste.
Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Georgian Chicken and Potato Cheese Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, rustic Georgian Chicken and Potato Cheese Bake presented in a dark ceramic baking dish. Golden-brown, bubbly Suluguni cheese forms a delicious crust over tender chicken thighs and chunky roasted potatoes. The chicken pieces are whole, with crispy seared skin visible. Potatoes are thick, irregular chunks, soft and browned, coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato and onion sauce. Vibrant green flecks of fresh cilantro and parsley are scattered over the top. The dish is placed on a simple, worn wooden kitchen table. A single everyday ceramic plate holds a modest portion: melted cheese, a chicken piece, and potato chunks. A piece of fresh, crusty Georgian bread rests nearby, with a small bowl of pickled vegetables. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm Shotis Puri (Georgian bread) or other crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer a side of pickled vegetables (e.g., cucumber, cabbage) to balance the richness.
Serve with a small bowl of fresh chopped herbs (cilantro, parsley) for additional garnish at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add chopped onions to the same skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. If sauce is too thick, add 100 ml water or chicken broth.
Return seared chicken to the skillet, nestling it into the sauce.
While chicken sears, peel potatoes. Cut potatoes into thick chunks (approx. 3-4 cm). Boil potatoes in salted water until just tender, about 10-15 minutes. Drain well.
Add the par-boiled potato chunks around the chicken in the skillet. Gently mix potatoes with the sauce.
Cover the skillet or Dutch oven. Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove cover. Sprinkle grated Suluguni cheese evenly over the chicken and potatoes.
Return to oven, uncovered. Bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and cheese is melted and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and parsley. Serve directly from the skillet or transfer to serving plates.
notes: Suluguni cheese is a brined Georgian cheese with a slightly elastic texture that melts beautifully. If unavailable, use a blend of mozzarella and feta for a similar texture and salty tang.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
traditional_techniques: No specific named techniques beyond standard home cooking methods like searing and baking, which are common in Georgian family cooking. The emphasis is on fresh ingredients and robust flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Tomato Potato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Tomato Potato Pasta is presented in a round, off-white ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. Penne pasta is generously coated in a rich, matte, deep red tomato sauce. Diced potato cubes, approximately 1.5 cm, are interspersed throughout the pasta and sauce, some showing slightly softened edges. The dish has a hearty, comforting appearance. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered on top, providing a pop of color and freshness. A light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese covers parts of the dish. The bowl sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, cream-colored linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl, with a fork resting on it. Soft, warm, natural kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The background is minimal, hinting at a comfortable home dining area.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of red wine, if desired.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Dice into 1.5 cm cubes.
Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 125ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced potatoes. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
Add drained pasta to the sauce. Stir to combine. If sauce is too thick, add a splash of reserved pasta water.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure potatoes are tender but still hold their shape.
Adjust salt and pepper to your taste before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Asian Chicken & Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, hearty portion of Spicy Asian Chicken & Rice is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. Browned chicken chunks, coated in a glossy, dark reddish-brown sauce, are casually spooned over a fluffy mound of white jasmine rice. Visible within the sauce are softened diced onions, bright red chili slices, and tiny bits of minced garlic and ginger, clinging to the chicken. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of vibrant green sliced green onions and a scattering of white sesame seeds, adding color and texture contrast. The bowl sits on a warm-toned, well-used wooden kitchen table. A pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl on a small, unobtrusive ceramic chopstick rest. A casually crumpled linen napkin is nearby. The lighting is warm and inviting, suggesting a cozy, home-cooked meal in a lived-in kitchen environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple clear broth.
Accompany with a small dish of pickled daikon or kimchi.
Eat using chopsticks.
instructions: Cook 150g jasmine rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Cut 300g chicken thighs into 2 cm chunks.
In a small bowl, whisk together 30ml gluten-free soy sauce, 15ml sesame oil, 15ml rice vinegar, 10g brown sugar, 5g cornstarch, and 60ml water. Set aside.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the hot wok. Stir-fry until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok and set aside.
Add diced onion to the wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and sliced red chilies. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return cooked chicken to the wok.
Stir the prepared sauce mixture well. Pour into the wok.
Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens and coats the chicken.
Serve immediately over cooked jasmine rice. Garnish with sliced green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature for safety.
Adjust the quantity of red chilies to suit your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mushroom Risotto with Pan-Seared Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy mushroom risotto is centered on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto appears fluid and naturally spread, not constrained, showcasing its rich, pale golden hue and flecks of earthy brown, tender-looking sliced cremini mushrooms. Perched atop the risotto are two or three thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast medallions, their surfaces exhibiting a slight crispness from the searing, with no fanning. A scattering of bright green, finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and risotto, providing a vibrant contrast. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, even natural light, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the dish's inviting textures and colors. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Heat chicken stock in a saucepan. Keep it at a gentle simmer.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest for 5 minutes.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 grams butter to the same pan. Add finely diced shallots. Cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced cremini mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until tender and browned.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir 2 minutes to toast grains.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add one ladle of hot chicken stock to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding the next. This takes 18-20 minutes. Risotto should be creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 45 grams butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions.
Ladle risotto onto four warm plates. Place chicken medallions on top of risotto.
Garnish with finely chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Chipotle Chicken with Black Beans
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Smoky Chipotle Chicken with Black Beans is presented on a rustic terracotta-colored ceramic plate. Thick, irregular chicken chunks (3-4 cm) are nestled among dark black beans, all coated in a rich, glossy, reddish-brown chipotle sauce. The dish is garnished with vibrant green, chopped fresh coriander leaves and a few thinly sliced bright green pickled jalapeño rings, providing color contrast. Components naturally overlap, creating a comforting, unpretentious mound. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, under warm kitchen lighting. Beside it, a stack of warm corn tortillas on a simple plate, a quarter lime wedge, a casually folded cloth napkin, and a small Mexican hot sauce bottle complete the homely, lived-in kitchen scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer extra lime wedges for a fresh squeeze.
Provide a bottle of traditional Mexican hot sauce on the side.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 3-4 cm chunks
chipotle chiles in adobo sauce, minced
adobo sauce from the chipotle can
can black beans, rinsed and drained
fresh coriander, chopped, plus extra for garnish
lime, cut into wedges, for serving

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet or pot over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear chicken until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, minced chipotle chiles, adobo sauce, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Return chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Stir in rinsed black beans and chopped pickled jalapeños. Cook for 5 minutes, uncovered, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Stir in chopped fresh coriander. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with lime wedges.
notes: This dish is naturally gluten-free.
A perfect comfort food meal, simple to prepare yet full of rich, smoky flavor.
Adjust chipotle quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Asian-Inspired Chicken & Black Bean Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl with a rustic, slightly imperfect glaze, resting on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. A single, modest portion of the stir-fry fills the bowl. Diced chicken pieces, cooked to a light golden-brown, are mixed with dark, glossy black beans. The ingredients are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping. A vibrant scattering of fresh, chopped green coriander leaves adds a fresh contrast. A small pile of bright green pickled jalapeños sits casually on the side of the bowl, offering a pop of color and an inviting tang. The sauce, a rich, dark brown from tamari and chipotle, lightly coats all components, giving them a slight sheen. The texture is a mix of tender chicken, soft beans, and crisp coriander. The lighting is warm and natural, as if from a kitchen window, highlighting the dish's comforting, homemade appeal. A simple, plain cloth napkin is casually placed nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with plain steamed jasmine rice.
instructions: Combine tamari, rice vinegar, maple syrup, chipotle powder, hot sauce, and cornstarch slurry (cornstarch mixed with water) in a small bowl. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add minced garlic to the same pan. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add rinsed black beans to the pan. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return cooked chicken to the pan.
Pour in the sauce mixture. Stir constantly until sauce thickens and coats chicken and beans, about 1-2 minutes.
Stir in half of the fresh coriander.
Serve immediately over steamed rice. Garnish with remaining fresh coriander and pickled jalapeño slices on the side.
notes: Ensure all ingredients, especially hot sauce and tamari, are certified gluten-free.
Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Asian Chicken and Black Bean Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Asian Chicken and Black Bean Stir-fry is presented in a deep, simple white ceramic bowl, set on a rustic, well-used wooden kitchen table. Diced chicken chunks, coated in a glossy, dark reddish-brown sauce, are mixed with tender black beans and bright green chopped coriander. The chicken pieces are irregularly shaped, showcasing their home-cooked nature. A bed of fluffy white jasmine rice peeks out from beneath the stir-fry. Vibrant green coriander leaves are scattered generously over the top. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, emphasizing the dish's comforting appeal. A simple, slightly worn wooden chopstick rests casually on the bowl's rim. The background is minimal, showing a hint of a cloth napkin and the natural texture of the wooden table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a small side of quick-pickled cucumbers or daikon for a refreshing contrast.
instructions: Pat chicken breast dry. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Mince garlic cloves and ginger. Finely chop chipotle chile. Drain and rinse black beans.
In a small bowl, whisk together gluten-free tamari, rice vinegar, brown sugar, cornstarch, water, and hot sauce. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add sesame oil to the same skillet. Add minced garlic and ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add black beans, minced chipotle chile, and pickled jalapeno slices to the skillet. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Stir the sauce mixture again. Pour sauce over chicken and beans.
Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens and coats ingredients, about 1-2 minutes.
Roughly chop fresh coriander. Stir half of the chopped coriander into the skillet.
Serve immediately over steamed jasmine rice. Garnish with remaining fresh coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Garlic Chicken Pizza Bianca
recipes.special_requests: итальянская пицца на тонком тесте cuisine
recipes.visual_description: A single round pizza, approximately 25-30 cm in diameter, occupies the center of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The crust is thin, golden-brown, and slightly blistered, indicating a crisp texture. The surface is generously covered with melted, bubbly fresh mozzarella, showing slight browning in spots. Scattered across the cheese are irregular, rustic chunks of seared chicken, caramelized and golden-brown, interspersed with creamy dollops of white ricotta cheese. Specks of vibrant green fresh parsley and rosemary are sprinkled over the top, along with faint red pepper flakes, adding color and texture. The roasted garlic paste base creates a subtle, slightly darker hue beneath the cheese. The overall composition is organic and appealing, with moderate negative space around the pizza on the plate. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. Beside the plate, a neatly folded, light-colored cotton napkin is placed. Traditional Italian flatware (fork and knife) is positioned appropriately. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures and colors of the pizza. The background is softly blurred, showing a hint of a casual restaurant atmosphere, but remaining unobtrusive.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer extra red pepper flakes and grated Parmigiano Reggiano on the side.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white wine or sparkling water.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Slice off top quarter of garlic heads. Drizzle with olive oil. Wrap in foil. Roast 40-45 minutes until soft. Squeeze out cloves. Mash into a paste. Set aside.

In a large bowl, combine warm water and yeast. Let sit 5 minutes. Add flour, 10g salt, and 15ml olive oil. Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Knead on a floured surface 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place 1-2 hours, until doubled.
Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. In a bowl, toss chicken with 30ml olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 5-7 minutes until browned and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 220°C with a pizza stone or baking steel if available. Divide dough into 4 equal portions. On a lightly floured surface, stretch or roll each portion into a thin 25-30 cm circle.

Spread a thin layer of roasted garlic paste over each pizza base. Top with thinly sliced fresh mozzarella. Distribute cooked chicken chunks evenly. Dollop ricotta cheese over the pizza. Sprinkle with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
Carefully transfer pizzas to the preheated oven. Bake 10-15 minutes, or until crust is golden brown and cheese is bubbly.
Remove from oven. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil if desired. Slice and serve hot.
notes: For best results, use "00" flour for the pizza dough if available.
Allowing the dough to cold ferment in the refrigerator overnight can enhance flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Heritage Grain Fig & Yogurt Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single individual tartlet is the primary focus, approximately 10 cm in diameter, presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earth-tone (cream/beige) hue. The tartlet features a rustic, golden-brown crust made from heritage grain flour, showing subtle, natural flecks of wholemeal. The crust has a natural, slightly irregular edge, emphasizing its handcrafted quality. Inside, a generous mound of creamy, white strained Greek yogurt filling sits, its surface smooth. Artfully arranged on the yogurt are vibrant, plump fresh fig quarters, revealing their deep red-purple skin and contrasting pale pink flesh with tiny seeds. A scattering of roughly chopped green pistachios provides a pop of color and natural texture. A delicate drizzle of golden honey catches the soft, natural light. The overall presentation is minimalistic, with ample white space on the plate. The setting includes a light bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and simple, traditional Greek flatware placed beside the plate. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery visible, emphasizing the eco-conscious and organic theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with strong Greek coffee, such as a traditional Ellinikos kafes.
Offer a small glass of dessert wine, like a sweet Mavrodaphne.
instructions: Prepare Tartlet Dough: In a bowl, combine spelt flour, almond flour, and salt. Mix well. Add olive oil. Rub into flour until crumbly. Gradually add cold water, mixing until dough forms. Do not overmix. Wrap dough. Chill 30 minutes.

Bake Tartlet Shells: Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll dough thinly. Cut into four circles. Press into individual tartlet molds (approx. 10 cm diameter). Prick bottoms with a fork. Blind bake 15 minutes. Remove weights. Bake 5-7 more minutes until golden. Cool completely.
Prepare Yogurt Filling: In a bowl, whisk strained Greek yogurt, honey, vanilla extract, and lemon zest until smooth.
Prepare Figs: Wash figs gently. Quarter or slice figs. Reserve any trimmings for compost or a light syrup.
Assemble Tartlets: Spoon yogurt filling into cooled tartlet shells. Arrange fig quarters/slices decoratively on top of yogurt. Sprinkle with chopped pistachios. Drizzle with a little extra honey.
Chill: Refrigerate tartlets for at least 30 minutes before serving.
notes: For zero-waste, ensure all organic lemon parts are used for other purposes after zesting.
Any fig trimmings or bruised pieces can be simmered with a touch of water and honey to create a simple compote or syrup.
traditional_techniques: Use of strained yogurt for creamy textures
Baking with heritage grains like spelt

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Pizzaiola
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown seared bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, perfectly cooked, rests in a rich, vibrant red tomato and onion pizzaiola sauce. The sauce, glistening with olive oil, is studded with soft, translucent slices of caramelized onion and hints of minced garlic, showcasing its depth. Fresh green basil leaves, torn unevenly, are scattered artfully over the chicken and sauce, providing a pop of color and freshness. The chicken skin is crisp, offering a textural contrast to the tender meat and yielding sauce. The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, positioned on a simple wooden table surface. A cotton napkin and a slice of crusty Italian bread are placed beside the plate, completing a modern bistro setting with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Alternatively, serve over al dente spaghetti or creamy polenta.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette makes a good accompaniment.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and dried oregano. Bring sauce to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pan and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Uncover and continue to simmer for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh basil before serving.
notes: For a thicker sauce, simmer uncovered for longer.
The sauce benefits from resting for a few minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Asian Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Spicy Asian Chicken and Rice is presented in a deep, simple white ceramic bowl. Cooked jasmine rice forms a base. Generous chunks of golden-brown stir-fried chicken are nestled among vibrant red bell pepper pieces, translucent diced onion, and bright green slivers of chili and garlic. The chicken and vegetables are coated in a glossy, dark amber sauce that glistens. A sprinkle of fresh, thinly sliced green onions adds a pop of green on top. The dish shows natural, slightly overlapping components. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table. A pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl. Lighting is warm and cozy, reflecting a homely family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in individual rice bowls with chopsticks
Offer a side of kimchi or pickled daikon
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice. Cook rice with 300 ml water according to package directions.
In a bowl, combine chicken cubes, 5 ml gluten-free soy sauce, and 5 g cornstarch. Mix well.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together remaining gluten-free soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, remaining cornstarch, grated ginger, and 60 ml water. Set aside.

Heat 10 ml cooking oil in a large pan or wok over high heat. Add chicken. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 5 ml cooking oil to the pan. Add diced onion. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, sliced red chili, and bell pepper pieces. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until bell pepper is tender-crisp.
Return cooked chicken to the pan. Stir well.
Re-whisk sauce mixture. Pour sauce over chicken and vegetables. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately over cooked jasmine rice. Garnish with sliced green onions.
notes: This recipe is naturally gluten-free if using certified gluten-free soy sauce and cornstarch.
Adjust chili amount for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Rice & Cheddar Fritters with Quick Apple-Cherry Relish
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a minimalist arrangement of golden-brown, crispy rice and cheddar fritters on a clean, cream-toned ceramic plate. Each fritter is roughly circular, about 6 cm in diameter, exhibiting a rustic, slightly uneven edge and a visibly crisp, textured surface from frying. Scattered around the fritters, a vibrant quick apple-cherry relish adds bursts of red and pale yellow, showcasing finely diced apple and halved cherries. The relish appears glossy and slightly translucent, nestled naturally on the plate without being overly sauced. A few finely chopped chives are sprinkled over the fritters for a fresh green accent. The composition emphasizes natural shapes and textures, with ample white space on the plate. The entire plate is visible, placed on a light reclaimed wood surface. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the individual ingredients.

ingredients.name: medium apple, cored and finely diced

instructions: Prepare the Relish: In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add diced apple and halved cherries. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened but still retain shape. Remove from heat. Let cool completely.
Prepare Fritter Mixture: In a large bowl, combine cooked rice, grated cheddar, finely diced shallot, minced garlic, and chopped chives. Mix well.
Bind the Fritters: In a separate small bowl, whisk the egg and chicken stock. Pour into the rice mixture. Add flour. Mix thoroughly until just combined. Season with salt and pepper.
Form Fritters: Heat 2-3 cm of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Take spoonfuls of the rice mixture and gently flatten into small patties, about 5-6 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick.
Cook Fritters: Carefully place patties into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan. Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
Drain and Serve: Remove fritters from oil and place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve warm with the cooled Quick Apple-Cherry Relish on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Stroganoff with Creamy Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Stroganoff with Creamy Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy white rice forms a neat, slightly mounded base on one side of the plate. Alongside the rice, the rich, golden-brown chicken stroganoff is spooned, with tender chicken chunks and earthy sliced mushrooms visible within the smooth, pale yellow sauce. The seared chicken chunks show a distinct golden crust, contrasting with the creamy texture of the sauce. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped green dill garnishes the top of both the stroganoff and the rice, adding a pop of color. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. Standard silver flatware is placed beside the plate, with a neatly folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled cucumbers (solenye ogurtsy).
Offer dark rye bread (chernyy khleb) for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken in batches until golden brown. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add butter to the same pan. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until browned and moisture has evaporated, about 7-10 minutes.
Stir in all-purpose flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Slowly whisk in chicken broth until the mixture is smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pan. Stir in Dijon mustard. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, ensuring chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove pan from heat. Stir in sour cream. Do not boil the sauce after adding sour cream.
Adjust seasoning to taste.

Rinse long-grain rice. Combine rice with 600ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Serve chicken stroganoff generously over the creamy rice. Garnish with fresh chopped dill.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Do not boil the sauce after adding sour cream to prevent curdling.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef & Vegetable Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Hearty Beef & Vegetable Skillet is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. Thick chunks of seared beef, rich brown from cooking, are nestled among tender, sautéed cremini mushrooms, softened eggplant cubes, and translucent diced onions. The vegetables display varying shades of earthy browns and purplish-browns. Next to the skillet mixture, a modest portion of roasted cauliflower florets, golden-brown at the edges and creamy white within, adds a textural contrast. The components are casually arranged, naturally overlapping, filling the plate without overcrowding. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh accent. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. A standard metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. A casually folded, simple cloth napkin or a paper towel is nearby. Warm, inviting lighting, typical of a home kitchen, illuminates the dish, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a comfortable family kitchen setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet at the family table for a communal feel.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut cauliflower into florets. Toss with 10g beef fat, salt, and pepper. Spread on baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly browned.
Cut beef chuck into 3 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Slice mushrooms thickly. Cube eggplant into 2 cm pieces. Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat 10g beef fat in a large, heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until well browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove beef to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 10g beef fat to the skillet. Add diced onion and cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic, sliced mushrooms, and cubed eggplant to the skillet. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables are softened and lightly browned.
Stir in tomato paste, dried thyme, and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Return seared beef chunks to the skillet. Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Roughly chop fresh parsley.
Serve skillet mixture immediately, alongside the roasted cauliflower. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality beef chuck. Browning the beef properly adds depth.
Adjust the amount of beef broth for desired sauce consistency. For a thicker sauce, simmer uncovered for the last 10 minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: Porcini Risotto with Beef Fat Roasted Cauliflower and Eggplant
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of creamy Porcini Risotto is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a fluid, off-white base, is studded with dark, earthy specks of rehydrated porcini and various shades of brown from the sautéed fresh mushrooms. A natural, flowing mound of risotto fills the center of the bowl, allowing for moderate negative space around the edges. Artfully arranged on top are golden-brown roasted cauliflower florets and tender, slightly caramelized eggplant cubes, some partially nestled within the risotto. A vibrant scattering of freshly chopped green parsley provides a fresh contrast and garnish. The dish is set on a simple wooden table, part of a modern bistro setting, with a clean white cotton napkin and traditional flatware positioned beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating an inviting and approachable restaurant-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of dry Italian white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Vermentino.
Offer crusty Italian bread on the side for dipping.
Serve immediately, as risotto is best enjoyed fresh off the heat.
instructions: Place dried porcini mushrooms in a bowl. Pour 250 ml hot vegetable broth over them. Let soak for 20 minutes. Strain liquid through a fine-mesh sieve; reserve liquid. Chop rehydrated porcini.
Cut cauliflower into small florets. Cut eggplant into 2 cm cubes. Toss cauliflower and eggplant with 30g beef fat, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables in a preheated oven at 200°C for 20-25 minutes, until tender and lightly caramelized. Stir halfway through.
Heat remaining 30g beef fat in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced fresh mushrooms. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and brown slightly.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges. Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add the reserved porcini soaking liquid to the rice. Stir until absorbed. Begin adding hot vegetable broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring frequently.
Wait until most liquid is absorbed before adding the next ladle. Continue for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente. Stir in chopped rehydrated porcini.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and unsalted butter. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Let rest for 2 minutes.
Serve risotto immediately in shallow bowls. Top each serving with roasted cauliflower florets and eggplant cubes. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.
traditional_techniques: Manteca (finishing risotto with butter and cheese)

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Chicken Chasseur
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Classic Chicken Chasseur rests centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, unsliced, is nestled in a rich, glossy, reddish-brown tomato and herb sauce. Surrounding the chicken are tender, rustic chunks of vibrant red and yellow bell peppers, earthy quartered brown mushrooms, and translucent diced yellow onions. A generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The sauce pools invitingly around the ingredients, showcasing its smooth, comforting texture. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware placed neatly beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and inviting appeal, with a subtly blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with simple boiled potatoes or rice.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine.
instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken pieces skin-side down until deep golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pot. Add diced onion, bell pepper squares, and quartered mushrooms. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until vegetables soften and onions are translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine (if using). Scrape bottom of pot to release browned bits. Cook until wine reduces by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in chopped tomatoes, chicken broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in sauce. Cover pot.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Taste sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Beef and Bean Chili
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of hearty Spiced Beef and Bean Chili is presented in a deep, rustic white ceramic bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. The chili features substantial 2-3 cm chunks of dark-seared beef, nestled amongst plump kidney beans and vibrant 1 cm diced red and green bell peppers. Translucent 1 cm diced onions are visible within the rich, glossy, reddish-brown sauce. The chili's surface is adorned with a bright, contrasting dollop of white crema, gently swirled, and a generous sprinkling of fresh, roughly chopped green cilantro leaves. The texture appears thick and robust. A wooden spoon rests invitingly in the bowl. A folded cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and depth, with a minimalist bistro-style background ensuring the chili remains the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm cornbread
Serve with tortilla chips
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 2-3 cm cubes. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef cubes in batches. Sear until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Dice red and green bell peppers into 1 cm pieces. Dice yellow onion into 1 cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chili powder, ground cumin, smoked paprika, dried oregano, and cocoa powder. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add canned crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Stir well.
Drain and rinse kidney beans and black beans. Add to the pot.
Bring chili to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for at least 2 hours, or up to 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until beef is very tender.
Season chili with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle hot chili into serving bowls. Garnish with a dollop of crema or sour cream and fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: For extra depth, add a splash of dark beer or a chipotle pepper in adobo sauce during simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Poblano Peppers with Chihuahua Cheese
recipes.visual_description: The dish features roasted poblano peppers, each generously stuffed and presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The peppers are deep green with char marks, split lengthwise, and filled with a savory ground beef picadillo, showing diced red tomato and golden corn. A thick layer of melted, bubbly Chihuahua cheese, golden-brown in spots, covers the filling. Fresh chopped cilantro is sprinkled over the cheese for contrast. The plate rests on a simple wooden table. A white cotton napkin is beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. A small ceramic bowl of white crema and another with red salsa are subtly placed in the background, along with warm corn tortillas, suggesting traditional accompaniments. The presentation is clean, inviting, and authentically Mexican, without overcrowding.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer a side of Mexican crema or sour cream.
Provide a simple salsa roja or pico de gallo.
Accompany with traditional Mexican rice.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Roast poblano peppers directly over an open flame or under broiler until skin is charred and blistered.
Place roasted peppers in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap. Let steam for 10 minutes.
Peel skin from peppers. Make a slit down one side of each pepper. Carefully remove seeds and veins. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef to skillet. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned, drain excess fat.
Stir in diced tomatoes, corn kernels, ground cumin, chili powder, and dried oregano.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until liquid reduces and flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper.
Carefully stuff each poblano pepper with the ground beef mixture.
Place stuffed peppers in a baking dish. Top each pepper generously with shredded Chihuahua cheese.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and peppers are heated through.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.
notes: Wear gloves when handling poblano peppers to avoid skin irritation, especially if sensitive.
For extra heat, leave some veins and seeds inside the peppers.
Poblano peppers can vary in heat; taste a small piece before stuffing if concerned.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Bell Pepper Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and bell pepper risotto is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The Arborio rice is cooked to a fluid, flowing consistency, its creamy white base studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken chunks and vibrant, diced red and yellow bell peppers. The chicken pieces are irregularly shaped, showcasing their rustic preparation. Specks of green from freshly chopped basil and dried oregano are visible throughout, adding freshness. The dish is casually arranged, allowing components to naturally overlap. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen light. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl on a loosely folded, off-white cloth napkin. The setting evokes a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere, with minimal background elements to keep focus on the hearty comfort food.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2.5 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks.
Sear chicken until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Dice onion and bell pepper into 1 cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
If using, add white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add one ladle of hot chicken stock to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding stock, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each addition is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
After 15 minutes of adding stock, return seared chicken to the pan. Continue adding stock until rice is creamy and al dente. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove pan from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and creamy. This is 'mantecatura'.
Stir in chopped fresh basil.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately while hot and fluid.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish-Style Chicken and Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The saffron-infused golden bomba rice forms a slightly mounded base, interspersed with vibrant red and green diced bell peppers and bright green peas. Substantial, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled atop and within the rice. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a fresh green contrast. The plating is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and knife on a white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Cut chicken thighs into 4 cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and diced tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pot to deglaze. Cook until wine is almost evaporated.
Stir in the bomba rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the grains.
Add chicken broth and saffron (steeped in 30 ml warm broth). Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pot. Stir gently.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir during cooking.
Remove from heat. Stir in frozen peas. Cover and let rest for 5 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Check seasoning and adjust.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, use good quality smoked paprika and authentic saffron threads.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken and Rice Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, inviting portion of Homestyle Chicken and Rice Bake is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a rustic edge. A generous mound of moist white rice, studded with tender, diced red bell pepper and bright red diced tomatoes, forms the base. Resting atop the rice is a single, perfectly cooked, golden-brown chicken thigh. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley adds color. The plating is natural and unforced, as if served directly from a family meal. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and spoon are casually placed beside it, alongside a casually folded cloth napkin. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a comfortable kitchen environment with a softly blurred background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Dice onion and red bell pepper into 1cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Add onion and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.
Stir in rice, oregano, and basil. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes with their juice and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Nestle seared chicken thighs into the rice mixture. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover the pot tightly with a lid or foil. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish with parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Potato & Chickpea Bake with Fermented Aromatics
recipes.visual_description: The Greek Potato & Chickpea Bake is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a natural, earthy beige tone, set on a light, subtly textured reclaimed wood surface. The dish occupies the center, leaving generous white space around its edges. Hearty 3cm potato chunks, roasted to a tender finish, are nestled amongst plump, whole chickpeas, all coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce. The sauce is a deep, warm red, glossy from olive oil, with visible flecks of dried oregano. A scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh dill is sprinkled over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. A few golden-brown, irregularly shaped potato peel crisps are artfully placed on the side of the dish, adding a natural, zero-waste textural element. The composition is clean and unfussy, highlighting the wholesome ingredients. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige and minimal, traditional-style flatware (fork, spoon) rest beside the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the textures and warm colors of the food. The background is minimal, perhaps with a subtle out-of-focus hint of a green plant or a small terracotta pot, maintaining an organic and authentic Greek feel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Offer a wedge of lemon on the side for a fresh squeeze.
Traditionally accompanied by a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Wash reserved potato peels thoroughly. Pat dry. Toss with 5ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Bake 15-20 minutes, or until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Heat 60ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 8-10 minutes until translucent.
Stir in fermented garlic paste and fermented onion paste. Cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in sherry. Deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits. Cook 2 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Add crushed tomatoes, vegetable stock, dried oregano, and bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and black pepper.
Add 3cm potato chunks and drained chickpeas to the pot. Stir gently to combine. Ensure potatoes are mostly submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven. Bake 45-50 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and sauce has thickened.
Remove bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish each portion with fresh dill and potato peel crisps before serving.
notes: Fermented garlic and onion pastes add a complex, umami depth while utilizing preservation techniques. If unavailable, use fresh minced garlic and finely diced onion, but the flavor profile will differ slightly.
traditional_techniques: Slow stewing for tender vegetables and rich sauce

recipes.recipe_name: Warm Spinach and Tomato Salad with Poached Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is presented on an off-white, everyday ceramic plate, placed on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The dish features a natural, slightly asymmetrical arrangement. A bed of vibrant green, gently wilted spinach forms the base, topped with bright red cherry tomatoes, halved and slightly softened. A perfectly poached egg, with its firm white and invitingly runny golden yolk, rests centrally atop the vegetables. Thinly sliced bright green onion pieces are scattered over the egg and vegetables, adding a fresh accent. Shaved parmesan cheese curls are delicately placed, providing a subtle creamy texture. The colors are natural and appetizing: deep green, rich red, and creamy white and yellow. The texture contrast is inviting. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, with a casually placed cloth napkin beside the plate, emphasizing a homely, comfortable dining experience.
instructions: Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice green onion. Mince garlic.
Heat 10ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add spinach to the pan. Cook 1-2 minutes until wilted.
Add halved tomatoes to the pan. Cook 1 minute until slightly softened.
Season spinach and tomato with salt and pepper.
Transfer warm spinach and tomato mixture to a serving plate.
Poach egg: Bring a small pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add red wine vinegar. Crack egg into water. Cook 3-4 minutes for a runny yolk.
Carefully remove poached egg with a slotted spoon. Place on top of spinach and tomato mixture.
Drizzle with remaining 5ml olive oil.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onion and shaved parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Baked Eggs with Spinach and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Baked Eggs with Spinach and Tomato is presented in a well-loved, dark ceramic bowl, placed on a simple, worn wooden kitchen table. The rich, vibrant red tomato sauce forms the base, with tender, dark green wilted spinach leaves peeking through. Two perfectly baked eggs are nestled into the sauce; their whites are fully set and opaque, while the yolks are bright yellow and appear slightly soft, ready to burst. A generous sprinkle of golden-white grated Parmesan cheese melts gently over the eggs and sauce, creating small, savory pockets. Freshly chopped bright green onions are scattered over the top, providing a fresh contrast. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center, allowing for natural negative space. A piece of crusty, rustic bread, torn not sliced, rests casually beside the bowl. The scene is bathed in warm, soft kitchen lighting, evoking a cozy, lived-in family atmosphere with minimal, unobtrusive background elements. The overall presentation is homely and comforting, emphasizing natural textures and inviting warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet or individual bowls.
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping into the yolks and sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Add spinach to the skillet. Cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Season the tomato and spinach mixture with salt and black pepper to taste.
Create 8 small wells in the sauce. Carefully crack one egg into each well.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven.
Bake for 10-15 minutes, until egg whites are set and yolks are still slightly runny.
Remove skillet from oven. Sprinkle generously with grated Parmesan cheese and chopped green onions.
Serve immediately from the skillet.
notes: For a spicier kick, add a pinch of chili flakes with the garlic.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato and Spinach Orecchiette with Poached Egg
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tomato and Spinach Orecchiette is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, nestled on a simple wooden table surface. The orecchiette pasta is coated in a vibrant, creamy, reddish-orange sauce, rich with finely diced, softened tomatoes and tender, roughly chopped dark green spinach. The pasta is naturally swirled, creating a soft mound in the center of the bowl. Perched slightly off-center on top of the pasta is a perfectly poached egg, its delicate white set, hinting at a golden, runny yolk beneath. Thinly sliced bright green onion tops are scattered over the dish, along with a few fresh, whole basil leaves, providing a fragrant and colorful contrast. A generous dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly covers the egg and pasta. The background features a subtle, casual restaurant atmosphere. Beside the bowl, a neatly folded white cotton napkin and traditional Italian flatware (fork and spoon) are arranged. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the inviting textures and fresh colors. The plate is not overcrowded, maintaining appropriate negative space to emphasize the dish's refined simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a light red wine or sparkling water.
instructions: Cook orecchiette according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 150 ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic and white parts of green onions. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes to the pan. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and slightly broken down.
Stir in spinach. Cook 2-3 minutes until wilted.
Pour in heavy cream and vegetable broth (or reserved pasta water). Bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Add cooked orecchiette to the pan with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. Stir in 60 g grated Parmesan.

While pasta simmers briefly, poach eggs. Fill a pot with water, add white vinegar. Bring to a bare simmer. Crack each egg into a small bowl, then gently slide into simmering water. Cook 3-4 minutes until whites are set and yolks are runny. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Divide pasta among four bowls. Top each serving with one poached egg.
Garnish with remaining sliced green onions, fresh basil leaves, and additional grated Parmesan. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef Goulash
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a dark oak table. The focus is a hearty portion of Hungarian beef stew. The beef is cut into 3cm chunks, appearing dark red and tender. Vibrant orange carrots are cut into 2cm rounds. Potatoes are 2cm cubes, absorbing the deep red sauce. The sauce is thick and glossy, colored intensely by sweet paprika. Red bell peppers are cut into 2cm squares. A single dollop of white sour cream is placed on the side. A sprig of fresh parsley is the garnish. A side of crusty rye bread rests on a small ceramic plate next to the bowl. Natural light creates soft shadows and highlights the rich textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Galuska or Nokedli dumplings
Accompany with pickled cucumbers or fermented cabbage
Provide thick slices of fresh rye bread for dipping
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Finely dice onions and mince garlic.
Cut carrots into 2cm rounds and potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Dice tomatoes and cut bell pepper into 2cm squares.
Heat lard in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Sauté onions until translucent and golden.
Remove pot from heat and stir in paprika and caraway seeds.
Add beef chunks and return to heat.
Sear meat for 5 minutes until browned.
Add garlic, tomatoes, and bell pepper.
Pour in beef stock and add bay leaf.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots.
Simmer for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Do not boil the paprika over high heat to avoid bitterness.
The stew is even better when reheated the next day.
Ensure the beef is chuck or a similar braising cut for tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, golden-brown Creamy Chicken and Potato Bake is presented in a well-loved, rustic ceramic baking dish, slightly off-center on a warm, worn wooden kitchen table. The dish features tender, cubed chicken breast chunks and soft potato cubes, generously coated in a creamy, savory sauce, with vibrant green peas interspersed throughout. A thick, bubbly layer of golden-brown melted cheddar cheese forms a crisp crust over the top. The sauce peeks through in places, showing its rich, creamy texture. The overall appearance is hearty and inviting, with natural, modest portions. The setting is a homely family kitchen, bathed in warm, soft light from an overhead fixture. A simple, everyday ceramic plate with minor imperfections is placed nearby, ready for serving. A casually folded cloth napkin and basic flatware rest beside the dish. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in kitchen atmosphere with a natural, unpretentious feel, emphasizing the dish as the centerpiece of a satisfying home-cooked meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place in a pot of salted cold water. Bring to a boil. Cook 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain thoroughly.
Dice chicken breasts into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat an oven-safe baking dish or large skillet over medium heat. Melt butter. Add diced chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from dish.
Add chopped onion to the same dish. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Remove dish from heat.
Stir mayonnaise into the sauce until well combined. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Add seared chicken, drained potatoes, and frozen peas to the dish. Pour the creamy sauce over. Stir gently to coat all ingredients.
Sprinkle grated cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until bubbly and the cheese topping is golden brown. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Let the bake rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Paprika Chicken and Potato Casserole
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, comforting single portion of Paprika Chicken and Potato Casserole is presented on an off-white, everyday ceramic plate with a subtly irregular rim. The dish features generous, golden-brown chicken chunks, approximately 2-3 cm in size, nestled among soft, creamy 2 cm potato cubes. Diced onion pieces are visible, integrated into the rich, reddish-orange sauce, which has a smooth, thick consistency with visible flecks of paprika. A swirl of lighter, creamy sour cream is gently folded into the top. The casserole is generously garnished with vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley, adding a fresh contrast. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, filling the plate without overcrowding. The scene is set on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, illuminated by cozy, natural kitchen lighting. A simple, folded cream-colored cloth napkin and standard silver flatware (fork and knife) are casually placed beside the plate. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a lived-in, comfortable family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 800g, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden-brown on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Chicken does not need to be cooked through.
Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sweet paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add cubed potatoes and chicken broth. Stir well to combine. Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring mixture to a simmer. Cover the pot and transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for 30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Remove pot from oven. Stir in sour cream until well combined.
Return uncovered pot to oven. Bake for another 10-15 minutes, until casserole is bubbly and slightly thickened. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Remove from oven. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For extra richness, a handful of shredded cheddar cheese can be added during the last 10 minutes of baking.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Potato Casserole
recipes.visual_description: A generous, golden-brown portion of Creamy Chicken and Potato Casserole is presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate. The casserole features tender, roasted potato slices (thinly sliced rounds) and succulent chunks of cooked chicken breast (diced into 2 cm cubes), all enveloped in a rich, creamy, light-golden sauce. Scattered throughout are softened, translucent diced onions. The top layer of potatoes is slightly crisped and caramelized from baking, with visible bubbling sauce around the edges. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley adds a pop of color. The plate is positioned on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple silver fork and knife. A casually folded, light-colored cloth napkin rests beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, home-cooked meal. The background is slightly blurred, hinting at a comfortable family kitchen setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease a 2.5-liter baking dish.
Dice chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from skillet.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes into 0.5 cm rounds. Peel and dice onions into small pieces. Mince garlic.
In the same skillet, melt remaining 35 g butter over medium heat. Add diced onions. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth until smooth. Stir in sour cream. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer, stirring. Season sauce with salt, pepper, and dried thyme.
Layer half of the sliced potatoes in the prepared baking dish. Top with half of the seared chicken and half of the diced onions. Pour half of the sour cream sauce over.
Repeat layers with remaining potatoes, chicken, onions, and sauce.
Cover baking dish with foil. Bake for 45 minutes.
Remove foil. Bake for another 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Apple Terrine with Carrot Tuile and Olive Oil Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: A refined, minimalist sharing platter featuring golden-brown seared potato and apple terrine rectangles. Each terrine piece exhibits distinct, thinly layered potato and apple. Delicate, translucent orange-gold carrot tuile shards are artfully placed, some standing upright for visual height, others resting against the terrine. Glossy, pale green-yellow drops of olive oil emulsion are precisely dotted across the pristine white bone china platter, providing subtle visual contrast and sheen. A few vibrant green microgreens or finely snipped chives are strategically placed to add a final touch of color and freshness. The composition is clean, with abundant negative space. The setting features a premium white Carrara marble surface and a precisely folded white linen napkin, under dramatic, professional lighting that casts soft shadows, emphasizing the sophisticated simplicity and flawless execution of each component.

ingredients.name: Cold water or light vegetable stock

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a small terrine mold (approx. 15x8x5cm) with parchment paper, leaving overhang.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes and apples using a mandoline (1-2mm thick). Melt butter.
Layer potato and apple slices alternately in the prepared mold. Lightly season each layer with salt and pepper. Brush with melted butter. Press down firmly after every few layers to compact.
Cover the terrine with parchment paper and foil. Bake for 60-75 minutes, or until potatoes are tender when pierced.
Remove from oven. Place a weight on top of the terrine (e.g., another mold with cans). Chill completely for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.

For Carrot Tuiles: Peel and roughly chop carrots. Steam until very tender. Blend steamed carrots with 30ml water until perfectly smooth puree. Pass puree through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness.

Spread a very thin layer of carrot puree onto a silicone mat or parchment-lined baking sheet using an offset spatula. Bake at 130°C for 30-40 minutes, or until completely dry and crisp. Break into irregular shards.

For Olive Oil Emulsion: Combine 30ml olive oil, 30ml cold water (or stock), and a pinch of salt in a tall container. If using, add xanthan gum. Use an immersion blender to blend until a stable, slightly thickened emulsion forms. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Unmold the chilled terrine. Carefully trim edges. Cut terrine into precise 2x5cm rectangles (approx. 12-16 pieces).
Just before serving, heat a non-stick pan with a little olive oil. Sear terrine pieces on all sides until golden brown and crisp.
On a large, minimalist sharing platter, artfully arrange the seared potato-apple terrine rectangles. Place carrot tuile shards around and on top of some terrine pieces.
Dot the platter with small, precise drops or delicate swirls of the olive oil emulsion. Finish with a few tiny sprigs of microgreens or finely snipped chives, placed strategically.

recipes.recipe_name: Paprika Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, golden Paprika Chicken and Potato Bake fills a rustic, deep ceramic plate, showcasing a single, generous portion. Succulent chicken breast chunks, about 3 cm, are roasted to a tender, golden-brown. They are nestled among creamy, golden-orange potato cubes, roughly 2 cm, which are fork-tender. Diced, caramelized onions are visible throughout the rich, velvety paprika-infused sour cream sauce. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley adds a contrasting green garnish. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, set with an everyday, earthy-toned ceramic plate. A simple, casually placed cloth napkin and warm, cozy kitchen lighting complete the inviting, lived-in family meal atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer a side of pickled vegetables, such as gherkins.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onions to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in sweet paprika and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits.
Return chicken to the skillet. Add potato cubes. Stir to combine.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cover the skillet. Transfer to the preheated oven.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove cover. Stir gently. Continue baking for another 20-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove from oven. Let stand 5 minutes.
Stir in sour cream until well combined and creamy.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust paprika quantities to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Brined Roasted Chicken with Fermented Root Vegetables
recipes.special_requests: Healthy food cuisine, Fat-free meals, Not fried
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken breast, golden-brown and plump, is centered on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The chicken is presented whole, showcasing its moist, lean texture. Alongside, a vibrant medley of lacto-fermented vegetables is arranged naturally, not piled: bright orange carrot batons, pale parsnip chunks, and halved green Brussels sprouts are interspersed with finely shredded purple cabbage. A delicate drizzle of vibrant green herb stem pesto garnishes the chicken, adding a fresh contrast. The plating is minimalistic, with ample negative space. The setting features a light reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural elements or subtle plants, emphasizing a sustainable aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare chicken brine: Combine 1 litre water, 60g sea salt, bay leaves, 5g peppercorns, and 2 smashed garlic cloves in a large bowl. Stir until salt dissolves.
Brine chicken: Submerge chicken breasts in brine. Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Prepare vegetables for fermentation: Wash and peel carrots and parsnips. Cut carrots into 5 cm batons. Cut parsnips into 2 cm chunks. Halve Brussels sprouts. Shred green cabbage finely.
Prepare fermentation jars: Sterilize two 500 ml glass jars. Place 2 garlic cloves and 2 dill sprigs in the bottom of each jar.
Pack vegetables: Tightly pack prepared carrots, parsnips, Brussels sprouts, and shredded cabbage into the jars.
Prepare fermentation brine: Dissolve 15g sea salt in 750 ml non-chlorinated water.

Ferment vegetables: Pour salt brine over vegetables in jars, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small plastic bag filled with water to keep vegetables below the brine. Seal jars loosely. Place jars on a plate to catch overflow. Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 5-7 days, burping jars daily to release pressure. Fermentation is complete when vegetables are tangy and slightly softened. Refrigerate after fermentation.
Preheat oven: Preheat oven to 200°C.

Roast chicken: Remove chicken from brine. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels. Season lightly with black pepper. Place chicken breasts on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Make herb stem pesto: While chicken roasts, combine parsley stems, basil stems, 1 garlic clove, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, and 30 ml water in a small food processor. Blend until smooth. Add more water if needed for desired consistency.
Serve: Plate one roasted chicken breast. Arrange a generous portion of fermented vegetables alongside. Drizzle herb stem pesto over the chicken.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by using herb stems for pesto and seasonal root vegetables.
Lacto-fermentation enhances flavor and gut health.
Brining keeps chicken moist without added fat.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Cabbage and Apple Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared chicken breast, cut into thick, irregular chunks, is centered on a matte cream-beige ceramic plate. The chicken has a golden-brown crust, revealing tender white meat. Beside it, a vibrant mound of crisp fermented cabbage and apple slaw is neatly arranged. The slaw features pale green and white cabbage, red apple skin, and purple red onion, with bright green parsley flecks. A few golden-brown chicken skin crisps are scattered over the dish, adding texture. Ample white space highlights the clean composition.
