The setting is minimalistic: a light natural wood table, an undyed beige linen napkin, and soft natural lighting. The background is clean, with subtle plant greenery. The dish is presented as a refined individual portion, emphasizing sustainable ingredients and natural beauty.

ingredients.name: Seasonal apple, cored and thinly sliced

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Carefully remove chicken skin. Place skin on a cold pan. Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Place the pan with chicken skin over medium-low heat. Cook slowly until fat renders and skin is crispy. This takes 8-12 minutes. Remove crispy skin, set aside. Reserve rendered fat.

Increase heat to medium-high. Add 5 ml of rendered chicken fat or olive oil to the pan. Sear chicken breasts, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown. Flip chicken. Sear for another 5-7 minutes. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Rest for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, prepare slaw. In a large bowl, combine drained sauerkraut, thinly sliced apple, and thinly sliced red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, 10 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.
Pour dressing over slaw ingredients. Add chopped parsley. Toss gently to combine.

Slice rested chicken breasts into thick chunks. Arrange chicken chunks on individual plates. Place a generous mound of slaw beside the chicken. Crumble crispy chicken skin over the slaw and chicken. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Spiced Chicken with Herbed Couscous
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Moroccan Spiced Chicken with Herbed Couscous is presented on a simple, rustic ceramic plate with a slight rim, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The chicken, cut into thick, irregular chunks, is bathed in a rich, reddish-brown sauce flecked with diced tomatoes and herbs. The sauce clings to the chicken, showcasing its tender, braised texture. Beside it, a mound of fluffy, golden couscous, lightly tossed with chopped fresh parsley, forms a comforting base. A small, separate side bowl holds a vibrant, refreshing salad of crisp, bright green salad leaves and chunky diced cucumber, lightly dressed and garnished with fresh mint. Warm kitchen light illuminates the dish, highlighting earthy tones of chicken and couscous against fresh greens. A simple fork and knife are placed beside the plate on a casually draped cloth napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm flatbread or crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer harissa on the side for those who like more heat.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown chicken chunks on all sides for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, and cinnamon. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return chicken chunks to the pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, prepare couscous according to package directions using hot chicken broth or water. Fluff with a fork.
Dice the cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Roughly chop fresh parsley and mint.
In a large bowl, combine salad greens, diced cucumber, and chopped fresh mint. Dress with a squeeze of lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil. Toss gently.
Stir chopped parsley into the finished chicken stew. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve the Moroccan spiced chicken and sauce over fluffy herbed couscous. Serve the cucumber mint salad alongside.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Garlic Enoki Noodles with Crispy Tofu
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Spicy Garlic Enoki Noodles with Crispy Tofu is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple wooden table surface. The base of the dish is a tangle of thick, glossy udon noodles, coated in a rich, dark amber sauce. Piled atop the noodles are delicate clusters of pale, almost translucent enoki mushrooms, their slender stems artfully arranged to create volume and texture. Interspersed among the enoki and noodles are golden-brown, crispy tofu cubes, approximately 2cm, showcasing their perfectly seared exterior. A vibrant sprinkle of thinly sliced bright green green onions and a scattering of tiny, toasted sesame seeds provide a fresh contrast and visual interest. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. Beside the bowl, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks and a small ceramic spoon rest on a simple cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Press tofu. Cut into 2cm cubes. Toss tofu cubes with 15g cornstarch.
Heat 45ml neutral oil in large pan or wok over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes. Cook until golden and crispy on all sides. This takes 8-10 minutes. Remove tofu. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml neutral oil to the pan. Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and chili flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and vegetable broth to the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk remaining 15g cornstarch with 60ml water to make a slurry. Stir slurry into simmering sauce. Cook until sauce thickens slightly.
Add trimmed enoki mushrooms to the sauce. Cook for 2-3 minutes until tender.
Cook udon noodles according to package directions. Drain well.
Add cooked noodles to the sauce with enoki. Toss to coat.
Gently fold in crispy tofu cubes.
Serve immediately in individual bowls. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds.
notes: This recipe can be adjusted for spice level.
Ensure tofu is well-pressed for optimal crispiness.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Roasted Vegetable Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Spicy Roasted Vegetable Pasta is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. Al dente penne pasta is coated in a rustic tomato sauce, interwoven with tender, roasted 2cm diced eggplant, sweet 2cm diced red bell pepper, and vibrant 3cm pieces of asparagus. Finely chopped red chili and sliced garlic are visible throughout. The dish showcases natural colors: deep reds, rich purples, and bright greens. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly melts over the top, adding creamy white contrast. A few fresh basil leaves are casually scattered. The presentation is homely and comforting, with components naturally overlapping, suggesting a casual, family-style meal. Warm, soft light illuminates the dish. A simple fork and linen napkin are casually placed beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
On a large baking tray, toss diced eggplant, bell pepper, asparagus, 2 sliced garlic cloves, and half of the chopped chili with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, stirring halfway, until vegetables are tender and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente.
In a large pan, heat remaining 30ml olive oil over medium heat. Add 2 minced garlic cloves and remaining chopped chili. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper.
Add roasted vegetables to the tomato sauce. Stir to combine.
Drain cooked pasta. Add pasta directly to the pan with the sauce and vegetables. Toss well to coat.
Serve immediately. Top each portion with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh basil or parsley.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to desired spice level.
Any short pasta shape like fusilli or rigatoni works well.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta alla Norma
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni pasta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Each tube of pasta is evenly coated in a vibrant, glossy tomato sauce. Large 2cm cubes of eggplant, fried to a rich golden-brown with visible caramelized edges, are distributed throughout the dish. A central mound of snow-white Ricotta Salata is coarsely grated over the top, providing a sharp textural contrast. Three fresh, deep green basil leaves are placed intentionally off-center. The bowl sits on a dark walnut wood table under soft, natural side lighting. A neutral grey cotton napkin and a polished silver fork rest beside the bowl. The arrangement is clean, focusing on the vivid red, white, and green colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Nero d'Avola red wine
Present with extra Ricotta Salata on the side
Provide crusty bread to clean the sauce
instructions: Cut eggplant into 2cm cubes.
Sprinkle cubes with salt. Let sit for 30 minutes.
Rinse eggplant and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat 200ml olive oil in a pan. Fry eggplant cubes until golden brown.
Drain eggplant on paper towels. Set aside.
Mince garlic cloves.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet. Sauté garlic for 1 minute.
Add tomato passata. Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Boil 4 liters of salted water. Cook rigatoni until al dente.
Drain pasta. Reserve 50ml pasta water.
Add pasta and half the eggplant to the sauce.
Toss over heat for 1 minute. Add pasta water if dry.
Plate pasta. Top with remaining eggplant.
Grate ricotta salata over the top. Garnish with basil.
notes: Ensure eggplant is dried thoroughly before frying to achieve a crisp texture.
Use aged Ricotta Salata, not fresh ricotta, for the authentic salty flavor profile.
Do not overcook the pasta; it must maintain a firm bite.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Tomato & Thyme Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of clear, reddish-orange broth fills a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic bowl. The broth, derived from fermented tomatoes and onions, shimmers with a subtle swirl of golden extra virgin olive oil on its surface. Finely diced, vibrant red fermented tomato pulp (approximately 5mm cubes) is sparsely scattered within the broth, alongside a fresh, small sprig of green thyme. A thin, translucent slice of fresh ginger rests near the bowl's rim. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a simple, undyed linen napkin and a plain, traditional Greek-style spoon. The background is clean and minimalist, allowing the natural colors and textures of the dish to be the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread (psomi) for dipping.
Offer a small side dish of Kalamata olives.
Accompany with a sprinkle of crumbled feta cheese on the side, if desired.

ingredients.name: Vegetable Scraps (e.g., carrot peels, onion skins, celery ends)

instructions: Prepare vegetable scrap broth. Combine 1.5 litres water and 200 g vegetable scraps in a pot. Simmer 30 minutes. Strain broth. Discard solids.
Combine strained broth, 200 ml fermented tomato brine and pulp, 100 ml fermented onion brine and pulp, sliced ginger, and 4 sprigs of thyme in a clean pot.
Bring mixture to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Strain the soup. Discard ginger and cooked thyme sprigs.
Return the clear liquid to the pot. Season with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Stir in the juice from 1 lemon and 30 ml extra virgin olive oil.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with a few finely diced pieces of the fermented tomato pulp and a fresh thyme sprig.
notes: To prepare fermented tomatoes and onions: Roughly chop ripe tomatoes and onions. Place in a clean jar. Cover with a 2% brine solution (20g sea salt per litre of filtered water). Ensure vegetables are fully submerged. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermentation. This recipe assumes pre-prepared fermented ingredients.
This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing vegetable scraps for broth and incorporating fermented elements for preservation and flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Jerk Chicken with Rice and Peas
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly cooked jerk chicken thigh, exhibiting a deep, mahogany-brown, crispy skin, rests beside a neat, rounded mound of creamy Rice and Peas on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its succulent texture. The Rice and Peas display individual, tender rice grains interspersed with soft, dark red kidney beans, infused with coconut milk. Freshly chopped bright green scallions are sprinkled over the Rice and Peas, providing a vibrant contrast. A small lime wedge is placed beside the chicken. The dish is set on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the rich colors and textures, creating an inviting, authentic Caribbean presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fried ripe plantains.
Offer a small bowl of refreshing coleslaw.
Include a bottle of traditional Jamaican hot sauce for an authentic spicy kick.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Score chicken skin deeply a few times. Season with salt and pepper.

For jerk marinade: finely chop 2 scallions, 2 thyme sprigs, 4 garlic cloves, ginger, and scotch bonnet (if using). Crush allspice berries. Combine with brown sugar, soy sauce, and juice of half a lime. Mix well.
Rub marinade all over chicken thighs. Cover. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Drain and rinse kidney beans. Set aside.
For rice and peas: Finely dice the remaining onion. Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add rinsed rice, drained kidney beans, remaining 4 thyme sprigs, coconut milk, and 300ml water to the pot. Season with salt.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid during cooking. Fluff with a fork.
While rice cooks, cook chicken. Heat remaining 15ml vegetable oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F). Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve chicken with a generous portion of rice and peas. Garnish with chopped fresh scallions and a lime wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Keto Thai Green Curry Cod with Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of vibrant Thai green curry with cod and roasted vegetables is presented in a simple, rustic ceramic bowl with subtle imperfections. A whole, flaky cod fillet is positioned slightly off-center within the thick, creamy, pale green curry sauce. Alongside the cod, tender, roasted cauliflower florets and diced butternut squash, in shades of creamy white and soft orange, exhibit slight caramelization on their edges. The dish is topped with a scattering of fresh, deep green Thai basil leaves. Components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, inviting mound. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden dining table. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks and a small ceramic spoon are placed casually beside the bowl. Lighting is warm and inviting, highlighting the dish's natural colors. A simple white cloth napkin is folded nearby, enhancing the homely kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.
Traditionally served with jasmine rice, but for Keto, enjoy as is.
Offer extra fish sauce or lime wedges on the side for personal seasoning.

ingredients.name: Butternut Squash
ingredients.quantity: 1 small, peeled and diced into 2cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss cauliflower florets and diced squash with 1 tablespoon avocado oil, salt, and pepper. Spread vegetables in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes. Vegetables should be tender and lightly browned.
Heat remaining 1 tablespoon avocado oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add green curry paste to the pot. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in coconut milk. Stir well to combine with the paste. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in fish sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Gently place cod fillets into the simmering curry sauce. Ensure fish is mostly submerged.
Simmer cod for 8-10 minutes, or until cooked through and flakes easily.
Carefully add roasted cauliflower and squash to the pot. Stir gently to combine all ingredients.
Remove from heat. Stir in fresh Thai basil leaves.
Squeeze fresh lime juice over the curry before serving.
notes: Adjust green curry paste quantity to desired spice level.
Ensure green curry paste is Keto-friendly by checking ingredients for added sugar or starches.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Cod with Garlic-Lime Thai Basil Butter
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared cod fillet rests centrally on an off-white ceramic plate on a well-used wooden dining table. The cod presents a beautiful golden-brown sear on its surface, contrasting with its flaky, tender white interior. A generous spooning of the glossy, light green garlic-lime Thai basil butter sauce cascades over the fish, showcasing vibrant green pieces of roughly chopped Thai basil leaves and tiny flecks of minced garlic. Beside the cod, bright green steamed broccoli florets are naturally arranged. The overall presentation is homely and inviting, with natural, unforced portions. The setting features simple metal flatware and a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, emphasizing the comforting appeal of the dish in a lived-in family dining area.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed low-carb vegetables like broccoli or green beans.
instructions: Pat cod fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place cod fillets in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until golden brown and cooked through. Remove cod from pan and set aside on a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Once melted, add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in lime juice and fish sauce. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer for 1 minute.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in the roughly chopped fresh Thai basil leaves.
Spoon the butter-lime-basil sauce generously over the seared cod fillets.
Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe is naturally Keto-friendly.
Ensure cod is cooked to an internal temperature of 63°C (145°F) for safety and optimal flakiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Cod, Thai Basil Velouté, Forbidden Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely plated portion of Pan-Seared Cod rests on a pristine, subtly patterned bone china plate. The golden-brown seared cod fillet, its flesh flaking tenderly, is positioned slightly off-center. Beneath and around it, a flowing, organic pool of vibrant, silky Thai basil velouté spreads, its creamy light green hue contrasting with the dark fish. Beside the cod, a small, perfectly formed quenelle of deep purple-black forbidden rice adds a striking textural and color element. Two or three crisp-green asparagus tips, precisely blanched, are arranged artfully, adding a final touch of verdant freshness. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the architectural precision of the arrangement. The dish is presented on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, with a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish as the sole focal point against an ultra-minimalist background, ensuring maximum visual impact.
instructions: Rinse forbidden rice. Combine rice with 400ml cold water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Keep warm.
For the Thai Basil Velouté: Melt 30g butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add shallots, garlic, and ginger. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Stir in flour to create a roux. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in fish stock and coconut milk until smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring. Cook for 5 minutes until thickened. Season with salt and pepper.

Remove velouté from heat. Add 50g fresh Thai basil leaves. Blend with an immersion blender until very smooth and vibrant green. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky texture. Stir in lime juice and zest. Keep warm.

Prepare asparagus tips: Trim woody ends from asparagus. Blanch the top 5cm of each stalk in boiling salted water for 1-2 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Season cod fillets generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil and remaining 30g butter in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place cod fillets skin-side down (if skin-on). Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip cod fillets. Cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C and fish flakes easily. Rest briefly.

To plate: Spoon a generous pool of Thai basil velouté onto the center of each plate. Place a seared cod fillet on top of the velouté. Form a small, neat quenelle of forbidden rice beside the cod. Arrange 2-3 blanched asparagus tips artfully on the plate. Garnish with a small, fresh Thai basil leaf.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Garlic Chicken with Root Puree and Pickled Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown with crispy skin, rests prominently on a matte, light grey ceramic plate. It is unsliced. Beside it, a smooth, creamy swirl of light orange root vegetable puree provides a comforting base. A small, vibrant cluster of bright green, quick-pickled kale leaves, slightly crinkled, adds a pop of contrasting color and texture. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped chives. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. The plate sits on a light reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a natural beige linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural textures and colors of the sustainable ingredients.

ingredients.name: Kale or Swiss chard, tough stems removed
Fresh chives or parsley, finely chopped

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Crush fermented garlic cloves into a paste. Mix with honey and 15 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub chicken with garlic-honey mixture. Place skin-side up on a baking sheet.
Roast chicken for 30-40 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Skin should be golden and crispy. Let rest 5 minutes.
While chicken roasts, boil carrots and parsnips in salted water until very tender. Drain well.
Mash cooked root vegetables. Add chicken stock and remaining 15 ml olive oil. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For quick pickled greens, bring apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and mustard seeds to a boil. Simmer until sugar dissolves.
Add kale or Swiss chard to the hot brine. Stir until wilted, about 1-2 minutes. Remove from heat immediately.

Plate each portion: Spoon root vegetable puree onto a light ceramic plate. Place one roasted chicken thigh beside the puree. Arrange a small pile of quick-pickled greens next to the chicken. Garnish with chopped fresh chives or parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: For zero-waste, save chicken bones to make homemade chicken stock for future recipes.
Vegetable trimmings from carrots and parsnips can be added to your compost or used for vegetable stock.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Lemon Cottage Cheese Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A modest square piece of Baked Lemon Cottage Cheese Pudding sits on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The pudding has a lightly golden, slightly crinkled top and a creamy, pale yellow interior, showing the subtle texture of cottage cheese. A small cluster of vibrant red raspberries is artfully placed beside the pudding. The plate rests on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple silver fork lies casually to the right. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. A casually folded cloth napkin is visible in the background, adding to the homely feel.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Lightly grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, eggs, erythritol, lemon zest, lemon juice, vanilla extract, cornstarch, and salt.
Mix well until smooth. A hand blender can be used for a creamier texture, or a whisk for a slightly coarser texture.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish.
Bake for 35-45 minutes. The pudding should be set and lightly golden on top.
Remove from oven. Let it cool completely in the dish.
Cut into 4 modest square pieces. Serve chilled, topped with fresh raspberries.
notes: This recipe uses a sugar substitute and is suitable for a diabetic diet. Adjust sweetener to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Cottage Cheese Custard with Roasted Root Vegetables and Fermented Carrot Top Pesto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of savory cottage cheese custard, gently inverted from its ramekin, presents a smooth, pale, slightly domed form centrally on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. Surrounding it, in a natural, unforced arrangement, are roasted root vegetables: vibrant orange carrots, earthy purple beets, and pale yellow parsnips, cut into irregular, rustic chunks and wedges, showing caramelized edges. A vibrant dollop of bright green fermented carrot top pesto rests beside the custard, its textured surface contrasting. A few delicate sprigs of fresh dill or microgreens are thoughtfully placed for natural color. The plate, with ample negative space, sits on a light, reclaimed wood surface. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting textures. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige completes the clean, ingredient-focused composition.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).

Prepare root vegetables: Wash carrots, parsnips, and beets. Reserve carrot tops for pesto. Cut carrots, parsnips, and beets into irregular, rustic chunks and wedges. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 25-35 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized. Turn halfway through.

Prepare fermented carrot top pesto: Thoroughly wash and dry carrot tops. In a food processor, combine carrot tops, garlic, walnuts or sunflower seeds, 15 ml olive oil, 5 g salt, and 15 ml water. Blend until mostly smooth. For immediate use, it is ready. For enhanced fermentation, transfer to a clean jar, press down to remove air bubbles, cover loosely, and let sit at room temperature for 1-3 days. Refrigerate after desired fermentation.
Prepare custard: In a blender or food processor, combine cottage cheese, milk, eggs, nutritional yeast, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Blend until very smooth. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Pour custard mixture into four individual oven-safe ramekins (approximately 150 ml capacity each) or a small oven-safe dish.
Place ramekins in a larger baking dish. Pour hot water into the larger dish, reaching halfway up the sides of the ramekins. This creates a water bath.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the custard is set but still slightly wobbly in the center. A knife inserted near the center should come out clean.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly. Invert each custard onto a serving plate.
Plate: Arrange roasted root vegetables naturally around the custard. Place a dollop of fermented carrot top pesto beside the custard. Garnish with fresh dill or microgreens. Serve immediately.
notes: The fermented carrot top pesto can be made up to a week in advance and stored in the refrigerator.
Adjust root vegetables based on seasonal availability (e.g., sweet potatoes, celeriac, turnips).

recipes.recipe_name: Cultured Cottage Fritters with Seasonal Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A single portion features three golden-brown, pan-fried cottage cheese fritters, irregularly shaped, arranged organically on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream tone. The fritters are soft and slightly textured, flecked with finely chopped chives. Beside them, a vibrant mound of lacto-fermented root vegetable slaw provides striking contrast. The slaw showcases finely shredded red cabbage, bright orange julienned carrots, and translucent white julienned daikon radish. The plating is clean and minimalist, with ample white space, emphasizing natural beauty and sustainability. The table surface is light reclaimed wood. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige sits subtly. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean with a hint of natural greenery.
instructions: Prepare the fermented slaw. In a large bowl, combine shredded red cabbage, julienned carrots, and julienned daikon.

Dissolve 15g sea salt in 500ml water to make brine. Pour brine over vegetables. Ensure vegetables are fully submerged. Place a plate or weight on top to keep vegetables under brine. Let ferment at room temperature for 12-24 hours for a quick ferment, or longer for more tang. Drain well before serving.
Prepare the fritter batter. In a separate bowl, combine cottage cheese, eggs, and milk. Mix well.
Add chickpea flour, finely chopped chives, 5g sea salt, and black pepper. Stir until just combined. Do not overmix.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Add a little olive oil.
Spoon about 50ml of batter per fritter into the hot pan. Flatten slightly with the back of the spoon.
Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Repeat with remaining batter.
To serve, arrange cooked fritters on plates. Place a generous portion of fermented slaw alongside. Garnish with a few fresh chive sprigs or edible flower petals.
notes: This recipe embraces zero-waste principles by utilizing seasonal vegetables and promoting fermentation as a preservation method.
Vegetable trimmings from the slaw ingredients can be saved to make a flavorful vegetable broth for future meals.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Tvorozhniki with Quick-Pickled Cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion features two golden-brown, lightly irregular round tvorozhniki (cottage cheese patties) centered on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a creamy beige tone. Their cooked exterior offers a subtle crispness, contrasting with the soft, creamy interior. Adjacent, a compact mound of vibrant quick-pickled cabbage and julienned carrots provides a sharp, fresh counterpoint, showcasing crisp textures and bright green and orange hues. A few delicate sprigs of fresh dill are naturally scattered over the tvorozhniki and beside the vegetables. Ample negative space surrounds the components, highlighting their pure beauty. The plate rests on a light, natural bamboo surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige sits beside it. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, with a minimalist, out-of-focus green plant in the background, reinforcing an eco-conscious aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally, tvorozhniki are often served with a dollop of smetana (sour cream). For a lighter, sustainable option, a thin cultured cream can be used.
Serve with a simple, crusty whole-grain bread.
instructions: Prepare the Quick-Pickled Cabbage: Thinly slice the white cabbage. Julienne the carrot.
In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, 5g salt, mustard seeds, and black peppercorns. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat.
Tightly pack the sliced cabbage and julienned carrot into a clean, heat-proof glass jar. Pour the hot brine over the vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal the jar.
Allow to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 24 hours before serving. This allows flavors to develop.
Prepare the Savory Tvorozhniki: In a medium bowl, mash the cottage cheese until smooth.
Add the egg, milk, chopped fresh dill, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper to the mashed cottage cheese. Mix well to combine.
Gradually add the all-purpose flour to the mixture. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into 8-10 flat, round patties, approximately 2 cm thick.
Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Carefully place the tvorozhniki patties in the hot pan. Cook for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
To serve, arrange two tvorozhniki per plate. Serve alongside a generous portion of the quick-pickled cabbage.
Garnish with a few fresh dill sprigs.
notes: To enhance zero-waste efforts, use outer cabbage leaves and dill stems to make a vegetable stock.
Ensure cottage cheese is well-drained for best tvorozhniki texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Savory Syrniki with Fermented Cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of 'Sustainable Savory Syrniki with Fermented Cabbage' is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate with a wide rim, resting on a light reclaimed wood surface. Three golden-brown, pan-fried syrniki discs, each approximately 6-7 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick, are arranged slightly overlapping in a loose arc on the plate. Their surfaces show a light, crisp crust with subtle variations in texture. Adjacent to the syrniki is a smooth, off-white mound of root vegetable puree, its creamy texture visible. A vibrant, finely shredded fermented cabbage and carrot relish, displaying shades of pale green and bright orange, is placed as a distinct, slightly mounded element, providing a textural and color contrast. The entire composition embraces natural forms and negative space, allowing each component to breathe. A few fresh, feathery sprigs of bright green dill are placed artfully on top of the syrniki and puree, adding a pop of natural color. The setting includes an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone to one side, and a simple glass of water. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft, natural light illuminating the scene, hinting at a natural element like a green plant just out of focus. The focus is sharp on the food, showcasing its pure, unadorned beauty and natural textures. The overall impression is one of clean, sustainable elegance and honest ingredients.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Cabbage Relish: Finely shred green cabbage and carrot. Combine with 10g salt. Massage vigorously until liquid releases. Pack tightly into a clean jar. Ensure vegetables are submerged in their brine. Seal loosely to allow gas release. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Refrigerate once desired tanginess is reached. Reserve brine.

Prepare Syrniki: In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, egg, 60g flour, 5g salt, and pepper. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix. Form mixture into 12 small discs, approximately 2 cm thick. Dust lightly with extra flour if needed.

Cook Syrniki: Heat neutral oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Fry syrniki for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove and drain on a wire rack.

Prepare Root Vegetable Puree: Wash and peel potato, parsnip, and celeriac. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Place in a pot. Cover with vegetable stock and 50 ml milk. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain most liquid, reserving a small amount. Mash or blend vegetables until smooth. Add reserved cooking liquid or more milk as needed for desired creamy consistency. Season with salt to taste.

Assemble Dish: Place a generous dollop of root vegetable puree on one side of each plate. Arrange three syrniki next to the puree. Place a small mound of fermented cabbage relish beside the syrniki. Garnish with fresh dill sprigs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Vegetable & Cottage Cheese Fritters
recipes.visual_description: Three golden-brown, round Fermented Vegetable & Cottage Cheese Fritters are arranged naturally on one side of a cream-colored, handcrafted ceramic plate. Visible within the fritters are flecks of vibrant green spinach, bright orange grated carrot, and subtle zucchini. A small, artful cluster of translucent, vibrant pink quick-pickled red onion slices rests beside the fritters, adding a sharp color contrast. A delicate swirl of pale green dill yogurt sauce is artfully drizzled across the plate, connecting the elements. The presentation is clean and unforced, emphasizing natural textures and earthy tones. A few fresh dill sprigs are casually placed as a natural garnish. The setting features a light bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin, and a minimalist background with soft, natural light.

ingredients.name: Medium zucchini, grated, excess water squeezed

instructions: Prepare Quick-Pickled Onions: Combine white vinegar, water, granulated sugar, and 2 g sea salt in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Place thinly sliced red onion in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over onions. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Prepare Fritter Batter: In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, eggs, and milk. Mix well. Add whole wheat flour, grated zucchini (squeezed dry), grated carrot, chopped spinach, 30 g chopped dill, 20 g chopped chives, 5 g sea salt, and 2 g black pepper. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.

Cook Fritters: Heat olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Spoon 60 ml (about 1/4 cup) of batter per fritter into the hot pan, flattening slightly. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Repeat with remaining batter. Yields 12-16 fritters.
Prepare Dill Yogurt Sauce: In a small bowl, combine yogurt, 10 g finely chopped dill, 5 g finely chopped chives, 1 g sea salt, and 0.5 g black pepper. Stir well.
Serve: Arrange 3-4 fritters per plate. Garnish with a spoonful of dill yogurt sauce and a small mound of quick-pickled red onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fromage Blanc Gnudi with Forest Mushrooms and Herb Milk Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving of Fromage Blanc Gnudi is elegantly arranged on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, organic rim. Three to four delicate, cloud-like gnudi, approximately 3cm in length, are clustered organically on one side of the plate. Their surface is smooth and creamy white. Adjacent to the gnudi, a small, artful mound of seared forest mushrooms, including quartered shiitake and whole cremini, exhibits a rich, earthy brown hue and tender texture. A luminous, frothy herb milk emulsion, a soft, off-white color, pools delicately around the base of the gnudi and mushrooms, creating a subtle visual flow. The dish is meticulously garnished with a scattering of vibrant green, finely minced chives and a few fresh, slender pea shoots, adding a pop of fresh color and delicate height. The presentation emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the purity and precision of each component. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. Dramatic, directional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures and creating depth. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits to the side, maintaining the ultra-minimalist, high-end aesthetic.
instructions: Line a fine-mesh sieve with cheesecloth. Place cottage cheese in sieve. Set over a bowl. Refrigerate 4 hours or overnight to drain excess liquid.
Transfer drained cottage cheese to a food processor. Add egg yolks, semolina flour, nutmeg, salt, and white pepper. Process until smooth and combined, scraping sides as needed.
Transfer mixture to a piping bag or a bowl. Chill for 30 minutes. This makes the dough easier to handle.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously.

Carefully spoon or pipe small quenelles (oval shapes) of the cottage cheese mixture directly into the simmering water. Do not overcrowd the pot. Cook gnudi for 3-4 minutes, or until they float to the surface and are cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon. Transfer to a plate. Lightly drizzle with olive oil to prevent sticking.

In a small saucepan, combine milk, thyme sprigs, and smashed garlic clove. Heat gently over medium-low heat until just simmering. Remove from heat. Let steep for 10 minutes. Strain out thyme and garlic. Season milk with salt and white pepper. Reheat gently. Use an immersion blender or whisk vigorously to create a light foam or emulsion.

Clean mushrooms. For larger mushrooms, quarter them. Heat butter in a medium skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms. Sear until golden brown and tender, about 4-6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate, arrange 3-4 gnudi in an organic, slightly asymmetrical cluster on one side of a deep, warm plate. Place a small pile of seared mushrooms next to the gnudi. Spoon a generous amount of the warm herb milk emulsion around the gnudi and mushrooms. Garnish with minced chives and a few microgreens. Finish with a small drizzle of high-quality olive oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Cottage Cheese & Herb Bake with Roasted Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: An individual, golden-brown savory cottage cheese and herb bake is presented in a white ceramic oval ramekin, positioned slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The bake's top is lightly browned, indicating a tender, custardy interior. Freshly chopped chives are sprinkled over the bake for a vibrant green garnish. Alongside the ramekin, a neat pile of bright green roasted asparagus spears is arranged, retaining a slight crispness. A few whole, slightly blistered red cherry tomatoes add bursts of color. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, with standard polished silver flatware placed neatly to the right of the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred background of a modern bistro.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease four individual oven-safe ramekins or baking dishes with butter. Dust with breadcrumbs.
Finely dice the onion. Mince the garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil and butter in a medium skillet over medium heat. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, milk, eggs, and flour. Whisk until smooth.
Stir in sautéed onion and garlic mixture, chopped chives, chopped parsley, grated Parmesan cheese, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Divide the mixture evenly among the prepared ramekins. Place ramekins on a baking sheet.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the bakes are puffed, golden brown, and set in the center.
While bakes cook, prepare asparagus. Trim the woody ends from asparagus spears. Toss asparagus with remaining 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.

Spread asparagus and whole cherry tomatoes on a separate baking sheet. Roast in the same oven during the last 15-20 minutes of the bake's cooking time, or until asparagus is tender-crisp and tomatoes are slightly burst.
Remove bakes from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve each savory bake directly in its ramekin or carefully invert onto a plate. Arrange roasted asparagus spears and cherry tomatoes alongside.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Cottage Cheese Soufflé
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly risen Sweet Cottage Cheese Soufflé is presented in a white ceramic ramekin. The soufflé has a golden-brown, slightly cracked top, showing its light and airy texture. It stands tall above the ramekin rim, indicating a successful rise. A delicate dusting of white powdered sugar covers the top. The ramekin sits directly on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. The setting is simple and homely, with a crumpled, light-colored cloth napkin placed casually beside the ramekin. Lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen. The scene feels natural, as if just placed for a family dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Generously butter four 200 ml ramekins. Dust with sugar or flour. Tap out excess.
Separate egg yolks and whites. Place whites in a clean, large bowl.
In a blender, combine cottage cheese, milk, egg yolks, 50g granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and flour. Blend until smooth.
Add a pinch of salt to egg whites. Beat egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add remaining 25g granulated sugar. Beat until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Gently fold one-third of beaten egg whites into the cottage cheese mixture to lighten it.
Fold in remaining egg whites in two additions until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide mixture evenly among prepared ramekins. Fill almost to the top.
Place ramekins on a baking sheet. Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until soufflés are puffed and golden brown.
Serve immediately. Dust with powdered sugar.
notes: Serve soufflés immediately after baking for best texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Poached Pear with Cultured Butter Crème and Cherry Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single poached pear, upright and slightly off-center, rests on a round, handcrafted cream-colored ceramic plate. Beside it, an organic dollop of light cultured butter crème. A vibrant, glossy ruby cherry reduction flows naturally across the plate, pooling beneath the pear and subtly touching the crème. The pear's pale golden hue contrasts with the creamy white crème and deep red reduction. Textures are smooth and inviting. Garnish is minimal: a delicate curl of lime zest atop the crème, and a single tiny lemon verbena leaf for a hint of green. The plate sits on a light reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by simple, elegant French flatware. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, with a blurred natural plant element in the background, creating a clean, understated, and eco-conscious presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light, elegant dessert, often accompanied by a small espresso or digestif.
instructions: Peel pears carefully. Leave stems intact. Set aside.
Combine water, sugar, vanilla bean, lime juice, and zest of one lime in a medium saucepan. Bring liquid to a gentle simmer over medium heat.

Add peeled pears to the simmering liquid. Ensure pears are submerged. Cover with a parchment paper circle if needed. Simmer gently for 15-25 minutes, or until pears are tender when pierced. Do not overcook.
Remove pears from liquid. Let cool completely. Strain poaching liquid and reduce by half over medium heat until slightly syrupy. Reserve.

For the cherry reduction: Combine pitted cherries and a splash of water in a small saucepan. Simmer over low heat for 10-15 minutes until cherries soften and break down. Mash lightly with a fork. Continue to simmer until liquid reduces to a syrupy consistency. Strain for a smoother sauce if desired, discarding solids.
For the cultured butter crème: In a bowl, whip softened cultured butter with heavy cream until light and fluffy. Add a tiny pinch of salt and the zest of the remaining lime. Mix until just combined.

To plate: Place one cooled poached pear upright on a serving plate. Spoon a dollop of cultured butter crème beside the pear. Drizzle the cherry reduction artfully around and under the pear and crème. Garnish with a delicate lime zest curl or a small lemon verbena leaf.
notes: This recipe emphasizes sustainable practices: using seasonal fruits, minimizing waste by utilizing lime zest and reducing poaching liquid, and incorporating a fermented element through cultured butter.
Adjust sugar in poaching liquid based on pear sweetness. The reduced poaching liquid can be used as a natural syrup for other desserts.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Soufflé Cottage Cheese Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Lemon Soufflé Cottage Cheese Cake rests on a clean white porcelain plate. The cake has a delicate, airy, and slightly moist texture, exhibiting a pale cream to light yellow hue. Its top is a subtle golden-brown, with a characteristic slight dip in the center and fine, natural cracks indicative of its soufflé-like structure. A light dusting of powdered sugar gently covers the top surface of the slice. Beside the cake, a vibrant, thin lemon curl provides a pop of bright yellow, and a few fresh, plump raspberries are artfully placed for a touch of natural color and freshness. The overall presentation is clean and refined, with balanced negative space around the cake slice. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable aesthetic, highlighting the cake as the focal point.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Prepare a 20 cm round springform pan. Line bottom with parchment paper. Do not grease.
Process cottage cheese in a food processor until completely smooth. Scrape down sides as needed.
In a large bowl, whisk together the smooth cottage cheese, egg yolks, 70 g sugar, lemon zest, lemon juice, cornstarch, and vanilla extract until well combined.

In a separate clean bowl, whisk egg whites with a pinch of salt using an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Gradually add the remaining 30 g sugar and continue whisking until stiff, glossy peaks form.

Gently fold one-third of the whipped egg whites into the cottage cheese mixture to lighten it. Then, carefully fold in the remaining egg whites until just combined, being careful not to deflate the mixture.
Pour the batter into the prepared springform pan. Smooth the top.
Place the springform pan into a larger roasting pan. Pour hot water into the roasting pan to come halfway up the sides of the springform pan.
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until the cake is puffed and golden brown, and a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. The cake will puff significantly and may crack slightly on top.
Turn off the oven. Leave the cake in the oven with the door ajar for 15 minutes to cool gradually.
Remove from oven and water bath. Let cool completely on a wire rack.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, before serving.
notes: This cake is naturally very light and airy, similar to a Japanese cheesecake or a very light soufflé. It is designed to be extremely low in fat, focusing on natural sweetness and citrus notes. The texture is delicate and moist when chilled. It relies on the natural fat in egg yolks and fat-free cottage cheese, with no added fats.

recipes.recipe_name: Orange Blossom Cottage Cheese Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly cut wedge of Orange Blossom Cottage Cheese Cake is presented on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The cake slice reveals a light, airy crumb with a pale, creamy hue, subtly flecked with bright yellow lemon zest. A delicate, almost translucent lemon-orange blossom glaze cascades gently over the top and edges of the slice, catching the light. Garnished minimally with a fine strand of candied orange peel, curled delicately beside the cake. In the background, the whole small, round cake sits on a simple white ceramic cake stand. The setting is a modern bistro: a clean, light wooden table surface, a folded grey cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the cake's refined texture and understated elegance, with ample negative space on the plate for a professional, approachable look.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake tin.
Blend cottage cheese in a food processor until completely smooth and creamy. Set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Gently fold in the blended cottage cheese, lemon zest, and 1 teaspoon orange blossom water into the egg mixture.
Sift self-raising flour and salt over the mixture. Fold gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared cake tin. Smooth the top.
Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. The cake will be lightly golden.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze, whisk icing sugar, lemon juice, and 1/2 teaspoon orange blossom water in a small bowl until smooth.
Once cake is completely cool, pour the glaze evenly over the top. Let glaze set before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Lemon Cottage Cheese Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Baked Lemon Cottage Cheese Cake is precisely plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The slice reveals a smooth, creamy, off-white interior with a faint golden-brown top crust. The cake slice is tall and holds its shape perfectly, indicating a refined texture. A light, even dusting of white icing sugar covers the top of the slice. Beside the cake, a small cluster of vibrant red raspberries and deep blue blueberries provides a pop of color and freshness. A delicate, thinly coiled lemon curl rests alongside the berries. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, reflecting a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The overall scene is clean and uncluttered, with natural, even lighting highlighting the cake's texture and colors. In the softly blurred background, the remaining whole cake, still in its springform pan or on a simple cake stand, offers a sense of abundance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F). Grease and line an 18cm springform pan. Wrap the bottom of the pan securely with aluminum foil for a water bath.
Crush digestive biscuits finely. Mix with melted butter until combined. Press mixture evenly into the base of the prepared pan. Chill in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.
Place cottage cheese in a food processor or blender. Process until completely smooth and creamy, with no lumps.
In a large bowl, whisk together granulated sugar, eggs, sour cream, cornstarch, lemon zest, lemon juice, and vanilla extract until well combined.
Add the blended cottage cheese to the egg mixture. Whisk gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour the cottage cheese filling over the chilled biscuit base in the springform pan.
Place the springform pan into a larger roasting pan. Carefully pour hot water into the roasting pan until it reaches halfway up the sides of the springform pan.
Bake for 60-70 minutes, or until the edges are set and the center jiggles slightly when gently shaken. Turn off the oven, leave the cake inside with the door ajar for 30 minutes.
Remove cake from the oven and water bath. Let cool completely on a wire rack. Once cool, refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, before serving.
To serve, carefully remove the cake from the pan. Dust a single slice with icing sugar. Arrange a few fresh berries and a delicate lemon curl on the plate beside the slice.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Sausage and Tomato Ragu
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Orecchiette with Sausage and Tomato Ragu is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with subtle imperfections, set upon a warm, well-used wooden dining table. The small, ear-shaped pasta is coated in a rich, rustic, reddish-brown tomato ragu, with visible crumbles of browned Italian sausage and small diced onion pieces interspersed throughout. A few vibrant green, whole fresh basil leaves are scattered on top, along with a light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano, creating a natural and inviting contrast. The dish looks hearty and comforting, with components naturally overlapping. A plain cloth napkin and standard metal fork are casually placed beside the plate. Warm, soft light from an unseen kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for 'scarpetta' (sopping up the sauce).
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Break into small crumbles.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add sausage crumbles. Brown well, breaking up with a spoon. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from pot.
Dice the onion. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Mince garlic cloves. Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine mostly evaporates.
Return sausage to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, salt, pepper, and a pinch of sugar. Stir well.
Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 30 minutes, or up to 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Ensure sausage reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
While sauce simmers, bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add orecchiette pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving about 120 ml of pasta cooking water.
Add drained pasta to the sauce. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce. Toss to coat pasta evenly.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir most basil into the pasta. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
notes: For best flavor, use high-quality canned crushed tomatoes.
Adjust salt and pepper to your preference before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Bacon Mushroom Cottage Cheese Bake
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, bubbling Bacon Mushroom Cottage Cheese Bake is presented in a clean white porcelain ramekin. The gratin's surface is a rich, caramelized golden from the melted Parmesan, revealing hints of crisp, diced bacon and tender, earthy brown mushroom slices peeking through. Below the bubbly cheese, the creamy white cottage cheese base is flecked with vibrant red diced tomatoes and fresh green parsley. The bake is served as a single, generous portion, maintaining its structured layers. The ramekin sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth against a subtly blurred, casual bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Dice bacon into 1 cm pieces. Cook bacon in a large pan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve 15 ml bacon fat in the pan.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Dice tomatoes into 1 cm cubes.

Add sliced mushrooms and diced onion to the pan with reserved bacon fat. Sauté 8-10 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more until fragrant. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, diced tomatoes, chopped fresh parsley, salt, and black pepper. Mix well.
Lightly grease a 20x20 cm baking dish or four individual gratin dishes.
Spread half of the sautéed mushroom and onion mixture evenly in the bottom of the dish(es).
Layer half of the cottage cheese mixture over the mushrooms.
Sprinkle half of the crispy bacon over the cottage cheese layer.
Repeat layers with remaining mushroom mixture, cottage cheese mixture, and bacon.
Top generously with grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and bubbly.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Serve hot. Pairs well with crusty bread or a simple green salad.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Supreme, Fondant Potato, Broccoli Stem Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of an ultra-sophisticated main course is presented on an expansive white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim. The plate rests on a cool, grey-veined Carrara marble surface. A single golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken supreme, precisely cut into two thick, succulent pieces, anchors the composition. Adjacent to the chicken sits a perfectly formed, cylindrical fondant potato, its top a rich, caramelized brown, hinting at its tender, buttery interior. Beside these elements, a small, vibrant green quenelle of velvety smooth broccoli stem puree adds a striking color contrast and elegant form. A few delicate, charred broccoli florets are strategically placed for textural intrigue. A small, glistening pool of dark, rich chicken jus subtly enhances the plate, complementing the main components without overpowering them. The composition is artfully asymmetrical, with abundant negative space emphasizing the purity and precision of each element. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and vibrant colors. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests to the side, completing the minimalist and luxurious setting.

ingredients.name: Large Desiree or Maris Piper potatoes

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Prepare chicken supremes. Pat dry thoroughly. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 5cm thick cylinders or rectangular blocks. Aim for even shapes.

Heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear potato blocks on all sides until golden brown. Add smashed garlic and 2 thyme sprigs. Pour in 250ml chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and liquid is absorbed. Baste occasionally. Remove from oven and set aside.

Separate broccoli florets from stems. Peel tough outer layer from stems. Cut stems into 2cm pieces. Blanch stems in boiling salted water for 5 minutes. Drain well. Transfer blanched stems to a blender. Add 30g butter and cream. Blend until completely smooth. Pass puree through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Blanch small broccoli florets in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain immediately. Plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain again. Pat very dry. Heat 15ml olive oil in a small pan over high heat. Fry florets until slightly charred and crisp. Season lightly with salt. Set aside.

For the jus: Combine remaining 250ml chicken stock with chicken trimmings (if available) and remaining 2 thyme sprigs in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer until liquid is reduced by half and thickened slightly. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add 15ml olive oil. Place chicken supremes skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Add remaining 50g butter and garlic/thyme (from potatoes, or fresh). Baste chicken continuously for 5-7 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

To plate: Place one fondant potato centrally on a warm plate. Spoon a dollop of broccoli stem puree beside it. Slice chicken supreme into 2-3 thick chunks. Arrange chicken next to potato. Garnish with a few crispy broccoli florets. Drizzle a small pool of chicken jus around the components. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Roulade, Fermented Onion, Crab Mousseline
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white or light cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate serves as the canvas, showcasing a single, elegantly presented individual portion. At the center, a generous, organic-shaped dollop of pale, creamy Fermented Onion Purée provides a soft, earthy base. Resting gently on the purée are two to three thick, round medallions of Beef Roulade, revealing a tightly wound spiral of deep brown seared beef, contrasting with the lighter, creamy chicken and crab mousseline filling, and specks of darker mushroom duxelles interspersed with hints of melted Comté cheese. The beef is cooked to a rich, uniform brown on the exterior, with the interior showcasing the distinct layers. Beside the roulade, a small cluster of vibrant, tender-crisp seasonal vegetables—such as bright green asparagus spears or small, orange baby carrots—are arranged naturally, their natural textures and colors highlighted. A glossy, reduced pan sauce, deep amber in hue, is lightly drizzled over the beef and vegetables, adding a subtle sheen. The plating emphasizes negative space, allowing each element to breathe. The background features a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, with an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the natural colors and textures. A minimal, clean background with subtle hints of natural elements or plants completes the eco-conscious setup.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a light, crisp French white wine.
Offer crusty baguette to sop up the sauce.
Present as a refined main course in a multi-course French meal.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Onion Purée (needs prep time): Slice 2 large onions thinly. Place in a clean jar. Add 2% brine (20g salt per 1 liter water) to cover onions. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly tangy. Drain onions. Blend with a splash of the brine until smooth purée. Set aside.

Prepare Mushroom Duxelles: Finely chop 300g mushrooms and 1 small onion. Heat 20g butter and 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add chopped mushrooms and onion. Cook until all moisture evaporates and mixture is golden and fragrant, about 10-12 minutes. Stir in chopped parsley and 30g finely grated Comté or Gruyère cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside to cool.

Prepare Chicken & Crab Mousseline: Cut chilled chicken breast into small cubes. Blend chicken cubes in a food processor until smooth paste. Gradually add 100ml chilled heavy cream while blending until light and fluffy. Gently fold in fresh crab meat. Season with salt and pepper. Keep chilled.

Assemble Beef Roulades: Lay pounded beef pieces flat. Season with salt and pepper. Spread a thin, even layer of mushroom duxelles over each beef piece. Spoon a line of chicken and crab mousseline along one edge of each beef piece. Carefully roll up each beef piece tightly. Secure with kitchen twine or toothpicks.

Cook Beef Roulades: Heat 15g butter and 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear roulades on all sides until golden brown. Add white wine and beef stock to the pan. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cover pan. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 25-30 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) to ensure chicken safety. Remove roulades from pan. Rest 5 minutes. Remove twine/toothpicks. Reduce pan sauce over high heat until slightly thickened.
Prepare Seasonal Vegetables: Blanch baby carrots or asparagus until tender-crisp. Lightly roast or sauté with a touch of olive oil and salt.

Plate the Dish: Spoon a generous dollop of Fermented Onion Purée onto each plate. Slice each beef roulade into 2-3 thick medallions. Place 2-3 medallions neatly on the purée. Arrange blanched and roasted seasonal vegetables beside the roulade. Drizzle with the reduced pan sauce.
notes: The Fermented Onion Purée can be prepared several days in advance for deeper flavor.
Using beef trimmings and mushroom stems to make a rich stock for the sauce enhances sustainability.
Adjust cooking time for roulades based on thickness and desired beef doneness, ensuring chicken reaches safe temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Mozzarella Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, single portion of Baked Chicken and Mozzarella Pasta is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The dish features al dente penne pasta, tender 2 cm cubed chicken pieces, and a rich red tomato sauce, all generously covered with melted, bubbly mozzarella and golden-brown Parmesan cheese. Scattered fresh green basil leaves provide a vibrant contrast. The pasta and chicken are naturally mixed, showcasing the textures and colors of the ingredients. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen setting. Beside the bowl, a simple white ceramic side plate holds a slice of crusty Italian bread, accompanied by a casual fork and spoon. A subtly crumpled, plain cloth napkin adds to the relaxed atmosphere. Warm, cozy lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the inviting, hearty nature of the meal. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space around the modest, home-style portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of warm, crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Mince garlic. Dice onion.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or pot over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet; set aside.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Stir in dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While sauce simmers, cook penne pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Return cooked chicken to the sauce. Stir in cooked pasta.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Sprinkle shredded mozzarella and grated Parmesan evenly over the pasta and chicken mixture in the skillet.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for a few minutes.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Roasted Garlic Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a refined single serving of Chicken and Roasted Garlic Tomato Pasta on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. A bed of al dente penne pasta forms the base. Tender, pan-seared chicken breast medallions, golden-brown from searing, rest atop the pasta. A rich, vibrant red tomato sauce, infused with roasted garlic and finely diced onion, generously coats the pasta and chicken. Torn pieces of fresh mozzarella are melted gently over the chicken and sauce, creating soft, creamy pockets. The dish is garnished with fresh, whole basil leaves, providing a bright green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese completes the presentation. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. The composition is clean, balanced, and inviting, with appropriate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice the top off 2 garlic cloves. Drizzle with 5ml olive oil. Roast for 15 minutes until soft.
Boil 1 litre salted water. Add 80g penne pasta. Cook al dente according to package directions. Drain pasta. Reserve 50ml pasta water.

Season 150g chicken breast with salt and pepper. Heat 5ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest for 5 minutes. Slice into medallions.
In the same pan, add remaining 5ml olive oil. Sauté 30g diced onion until soft. Add 1 minced garlic clove and 2g red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Squeeze roasted garlic from skins into the pan. Add 200g crushed tomatoes and 50ml chicken broth. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add drained pasta to the sauce in the pan. Stir to coat thoroughly. Add sliced chicken medallions. Toss gently to combine. If the sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually.

Transfer the pasta and chicken to a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. Scatter 60g torn fresh mozzarella over the hot dish. Garnish with 10-15g fresh basil leaves and 20g grated Parmesan cheese. Serve immediately.
notes: Using fresh, quality ingredients will significantly enhance the flavor of this dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Skillet Chicken with Mushrooms and Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Rustic Skillet Chicken is presented on an everyday, off-white ceramic plate. Tender, seared chicken chunks are nestled among earthy sliced cremini mushrooms and vibrant diced red bell peppers, all coated in a rich, rustic tomato-herb sauce. The chicken exhibits a golden-brown crust, while vegetables appear soft and slightly caramelized. Fresh, torn basil leaves are scattered over the top, adding a pop of green and fragrant contrast. The dish is casually arranged, with components naturally overlapping, showcasing its homely comfort. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy family dining atmosphere. A simple cloth napkin is casually draped nearby. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the food, highlighting its inviting, unpretentious appeal.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut into large 3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice the yellow onion. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Slice the cremini mushrooms. Dice the red bell pepper into 2 cm pieces. Mince the garlic cloves.
Add sliced mushrooms, diced bell pepper, and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 7-8 minutes until vegetables soften.
Stir in dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in canned diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Return seared chicken chunks to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the skillet. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is cooked through.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir most of the basil into the skillet. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with remaining fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken with Saffron Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh rests on a bed of vibrant saffron-infused brown rice. The chicken skin is visibly crisp, showcasing its rich, deep golden hue. The rice is fluffy, with an appealing orange-yellow color from the saffron, and individual grains are distinct. A bright yellow lemon wedge is placed beside the chicken, along with a small sprig of fresh rosemary and thyme. The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a rustic wooden table surface. A neatly folded light-colored cotton napkin is beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a subtly blurred, modern bistro-style background, suggesting a casual yet refined dining atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden and crisp. Flip and sear for 2 minutes.
Transfer skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken roasts, prepare the rice. Dice the small onion. Mince the garlic cloves.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and brown rice to the saucepan. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Squeeze lemon juice over chicken. Garnish with fresh rosemary, thyme, and chopped parsley.
Plate a portion of saffron brown rice. Place one roasted chicken thigh beside the rice. Add a lemon wedge and a fresh herb sprig.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Champignon & Romarin Rillettes, Moutarde Fermentée
recipes.visual_description: A small individual starter portion of a rustic French mushroom rillette is elegantly presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The rillette, a rough, chunky mound of earthy brown mushrooms, is positioned slightly off-center. A glossy, dark red wine reduction is drizzled artfully over and around the rillette, creating a rich contrast. Beside it, a small pile of vibrant green, slightly translucent fermented mustard greens adds a bright, tangy counterpoint. The plate itself is minimalistic, with ample negative space. The background features a light reclaimed wood surface. A few toasted, irregular slices of sourdough baguette are placed beside the rillette. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, highlighting the varied textures: the soft rillette, the shiny reduction, and the crisp baguette. The scene is clean, uncluttered, and highlights the natural beauty of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh, crusty baguette.
Offer a glass of dry red wine, such as a light Pinot Noir or Beaujolais.
Present as part of a multi-course meal, typically after an aperitif and before the main course.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Mustard Greens: Wash mustard greens. Coarsely chop. Combine greens, 2g sea salt, and red pepper flakes in a clean jar. Massage until liquid is released. Press greens down. Ensure liquid covers greens. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Refrigerate when desired tang is reached.

Make Mushroom Rillettes: Clean mushrooms. Roughly chop. Melt 30g butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced shallots. Cook until softened, 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute. Add chopped mushrooms. Cook until softened and browned, 8-10 minutes.
