Pour 100ml red wine into the pan. Deglaze. Cook until wine reduces by half. Add beef stock and finely chopped rosemary (from 2 sprigs). Simmer until liquid is almost absorbed. Stir in heavy cream. Cook until cream thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer mushroom mixture to a food processor. Pulse until chunky but spreadable. Do not over-process. Adjust seasoning.
Press rillette into a small terrine or ramekins. Cover surface directly with plastic wrap. Chill for at least 2 hours.

Prepare Red Wine Reduction: Combine 150ml red wine and remaining 1 sprig rosemary in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Reduce until syrupy, 10-15 minutes. Remove rosemary. Stir in 10g butter until melted and glossy. Keep warm.
Assemble: Spoon mushroom rillette onto small plates. Drizzle with red wine reduction. Place fermented mustard greens alongside. Serve with toasted sourdough baguette slices.
notes: The mushroom rillette can be prepared up to 3 days in advance and stored in the refrigerator, covered tightly.
The fermented mustard greens can be made a week or more in advance. Adjust fermentation time to personal preference for tanginess.
Use any mushroom stems or tough parts to make a vegetable stock for other dishes, reducing waste.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pan Roasted Chicken and Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty One-Pan Roasted Chicken and Bell Peppers rests on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. Two golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thighs are the centerpiece, nestled among vibrant, tender-crisp bell pepper chunks in red, yellow, and orange hues. Whole, softened cloves of roasted garlic are scattered throughout. A light sheen of savory pan juices coats the ingredients. The dish is casually arranged, components slightly overlapping, filling the plate naturally. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley adds a touch of green. The plate sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, accompanied by a simple metal fork and knife. A casually placed, folded cloth napkin and warm, cozy kitchen lighting complete the inviting, homely scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Cut bell peppers into thick chunks. Separate garlic cloves from the head; peel if desired, or leave unpeeled for a milder flavor.
In a large roasting pan, combine chicken thighs, bell pepper chunks, and garlic cloves.
Drizzle olive oil over all ingredients. Sprinkle with dried oregano and dried thyme.
Toss everything gently to coat evenly.
Pour chicken broth into the bottom of the pan.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and skin is golden and crispy. Vegetables should be tender and slightly caramelized.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken and vegetables with pan juices. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti al Pomodoro e Basilico
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spaghetti al Pomodoro e Basilico is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The spaghetti is twirled into a neat mound, centrally placed, coated in a vibrant, rich red tomato sauce. The sauce appears slightly chunky from crushed tomatoes, clinging perfectly to the al dente pasta strands. Scattered generously over the spaghetti are fresh, bright green basil leaves, some whole, some gently torn, providing a beautiful color contrast and aromatic highlight. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the dish. The scene is set on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing the fresh ingredients and inviting texture. The background is minimal, allowing the dish to be the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread, such as Ciabatta, for dipping in the sauce.
Offer freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table for individual preference.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with extra virgin olive oil and red wine vinegar.

ingredients.name: Canned whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes

instructions: Dice the onion into small cubes. Mince the garlic.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large, deep pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Pour in 800g whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes. Crush tomatoes with a spoon or your hands. Add a pinch of sugar. Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally. Sauce should thicken slightly.
While sauce simmers, bring 4 litres of generously salted water to a rolling boil in a large pot. Add 400g spaghetti. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Before draining, reserve 250ml of the pasta cooking water.
Drain spaghetti. Transfer spaghetti directly to the pan with the tomato sauce.
Add 120ml of the reserved pasta water to the pan. Toss pasta vigorously with the sauce until well coated and slightly emulsified. Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Tear half of the fresh basil leaves. Stir them into the pasta.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining fresh basil leaves.
notes: Using high-quality San Marzano tomatoes is crucial for the authentic flavor of this simple sauce.
Adjust the amount of pasta water to achieve your preferred sauce consistency; it should be fluid and coat the pasta well.
traditional_techniques: Soffritto (base of sautéed onion and garlic)

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken and Vegetable Medley
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown roasted chicken thigh rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Its skin is crisp and slightly blistered. Beside the chicken, vibrant green broccoli florets and tender-crisp green beans are artfully arranged, some exhibiting delicate charring from roasting. Scattered among the vegetables are plump, ruby-red cherry tomatoes, some slightly burst and caramelized. A light drizzle of pan juices glazes the ingredients, adding a subtle sheen. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. A fresh sprig of oregano and a bright yellow lemon wedge garnish the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's colors and textures. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful pan juices.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and dried oregano.
Trim green beans. Cut broccoli into florets. Halve cherry tomatoes if desired, or leave whole.
In a large bowl, toss broccoli florets, green beans, and cherry tomatoes with olive oil, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper.
Arrange seasoned chicken thighs on a large baking sheet. Distribute the seasoned vegetables around the chicken.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip chicken thighs once.
Continue roasting for 10-15 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C. Vegetables should be tender-crisp with some charred edges.
Remove baking sheet from oven. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the entire dish.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust roasting time based on chicken thigh size and oven calibration.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom, Fermented Onion, and Sourdough Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a rustic white or light beige handcrafted ceramic plate. Mixed seasonal greens form a natural base. Scattered artfully over the greens are tender pickled mushroom quarters, vibrant pink fermented red onion slices, and golden-brown sourdough croutons. Seared chicken chunks, golden and moist, are placed amongst the vegetables, avoiding any fanned arrangement. A light, glistening drizzle of golden ginger-mustard vinaigrette coats the ingredients, highlighting their textures. The plate is garnished simply with finely chopped fresh chives. The setting is a light reclaimed wood table, with an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, with a minimalist background featuring subtle green plants, emphasizing a sustainable, ingredient-focused aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette on the side.
Enjoy as a light lunch or an elegant starter.

ingredients.name: Stale sourdough bread, cut into 2 cm cubes
Chicken breast, cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: To pickle mushrooms: In a saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, 250 ml water, 10 g salt, sugar, thyme, and peppercorns. Bring to a boil. Add quartered mushrooms. Reduce heat, simmer 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool completely in liquid. Store in airtight jar.

To ferment onions: Dissolve non-iodized salt in 500 ml non-chlorinated water to make brine. Place thinly sliced red onions in a clean jar. Pour brine over onions, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess. Burp daily.
To prepare croutons: Preheat oven to 180°C. Toss sourdough cubes with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake 10-15 minutes, or until golden and crisp.

To sear chicken: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Set aside.

To make vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together verjus, Dijon mustard, and grated ginger. Slowly drizzle in 120 ml extra virgin olive oil while whisking constantly until emulsified. Season with salt and pepper.
To assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, pickled mushrooms, fermented onions (drained), and sourdough croutons. Add seared chicken chunks if using.
To dress and serve: Pour vinaigrette over the salad. Toss gently to combine. Garnish with fresh chives. Serve immediately.
notes: The pickled mushrooms and fermented onions can be prepared days or weeks in advance, enhancing flavor and reducing food waste.
Adjust the fermentation time for onions based on desired tanginess and personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Jalapeño-Lime Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast rests slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain plate. A generous pool of creamy, pale green jalapeño-lime sauce elegantly embraces the chicken, its smooth texture contrasting the seared exterior. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of dark, tender cilantro-lime black beans, cooked with finely diced onion and garlic, adds depth. The dish is garnished with fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves and a few paper-thin slices of fresh jalapeño on the sauce for color. A bright lime wedge is placed alongside. The plating is clean, balanced, with moderate negative space. The scene is on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro setting. Traditional flatware is beside the plate. A single warm corn tortilla is casually placed nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer a side of simple salsa roja or pico de gallo.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.
In the same skillet, reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Add 1/4 finely diced white onion and 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Seed and finely dice 1 jalapeño. Add to skillet. Sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, until sauce thickens slightly. Stir in juice from 1 lime and 30g chopped cilantro. Season sauce with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For the black beans: In a separate small saucepan, sauté remaining 1/4 finely diced white onion and 1 minced garlic clove until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add rinsed black beans and 5g ground cumin. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add juice from 1 lime and remaining 20g chopped cilantro. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice remaining 1 jalapeño into very thin rounds for garnish. Cut remaining lime into wedges.

To serve: Spoon creamy jalapeño-lime sauce onto the center of each plate. Place one pan-seared chicken breast on top of the sauce. Spoon a side portion of cilantro-lime black beans next to the chicken. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and thin jalapeño slices. Serve with a lime wedge and warm corn tortilla.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Lentil Pilaf with Roasted Cherries and Peanut Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spiced Lentil Pilaf with Roasted Cherries and Peanut Gremolata is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A neat, mounded portion of earthy brown lentil pilaf forms the base. Whole, glistening roasted cherries, deep maroon in color, are artfully scattered over and around the pilaf. A generous sprinkling of vibrant green and golden peanut gremolata crowns the dish, with finely chopped parsley, bright lemon zest, and coarsely chopped roasted peanuts adding delightful texture. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors, with a soft, blurred background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss pitted cherries with 5ml olive oil. Spread on baking sheet. Roast 15-20 minutes until slightly softened and caramelized. Set aside.
Rinse lentils thoroughly.
Heat 15ml olive oil in large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté 5-7 minutes until translucent.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in cumin, coriander, and turmeric powders. Cook 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add rinsed lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender and broth absorbed. Season with salt and pepper.
While lentils cook, prepare gremolata. Coarsely chop roasted peanuts.
In small bowl, combine chopped peanuts, finely chopped parsley, and lemon zest.
Stir in 10ml olive oil and 15ml lemon juice. Mix well. Season with pinch of salt.
Fluff cooked lentil pilaf with fork. Stir in roasted cherries.
Serve warm pilaf. Top each portion with generous spoon of peanut gremolata.

recipes.recipe_name: Warm Roasted Cherry and Lentil Bowl with Spicy Peanut Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant plant-based bowl is presented in a clean, white ceramic bowl on a simple wooden table. The base consists of fresh, bright green baby spinach. Over this, a generous portion of earthy, cooked green lentils forms a comforting layer. Scattered on top are tender, orange cubes of roasted sweet potato, softened red onion wedges, and glistening, deep red roasted cherries, some slightly burst and caramelized. A creamy, rich brown spicy peanut dressing is drizzled artfully over the ingredients, creating inviting swirls. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of coarsely chopped, light brown roasted peanuts, adding a textural contrast. The overall presentation is fresh and inviting, with a balanced composition of colors and textures. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a minimalist background to keep focus on the food. A simple cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl.
instructions: Rinse lentils thoroughly. Cook lentils in 700 ml water for 20-25 minutes. They should be tender but not mushy. Drain excess water. Season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Pit cherries. Peel and dice sweet potato into 2 cm cubes. Cut red onion into thick wedges.
Toss sweet potato and red onion with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 20 minutes.
Add pitted cherries to the baking tray with vegetables. Roast for another 10-15 minutes, until sweet potato is tender and cherries are slightly caramelized.

For the dressing, combine peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, maple syrup, grated ginger, minced garlic, chili flakes, lime juice, and water in a bowl. Whisk until smooth. Adjust consistency with more water if needed.
Divide baby spinach among four serving bowls. Top with cooked lentils.
Arrange roasted sweet potato, red onion, and cherries over the lentils and spinach.
Drizzle generously with the spicy peanut dressing. Coarsely chop roasted peanuts. Sprinkle chopped peanuts over each bowl. Serve warm.
notes: Ensure lentils are cooked al dente for best texture.
Adjust chili flakes in the dressing to your preferred spice level.
Fresh cherries are essential for the desired flavor and visual appeal.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken & Beef Savory Bites
recipes.visual_description: The Homestyle Chicken & Beef Savory Bites are presented casually on a simple, round, cream-colored ceramic platter, which sits on a well-used, light wooden kitchen table. Ten golden-brown, puffed pastry bites, cut into approximate 7x7 cm squares and folded into small parcels, are arranged in a loose, natural cluster, some slightly overlapping. The pastry is light and flaky, with a rich, golden-brown crust. A few bites are gently split open, revealing the hearty, dark brown filling of minced beef and chicken, mixed with visible specks of finely diced orange carrot and green parsley. The overall appearance is comforting and inviting. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley lightly garnishes the tops of some bites. The scene is bathed in warm, natural light, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. A simple, folded checkered cloth napkin rests casually beside the platter.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and carrot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef and ground chicken to the pan. Break up meat with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer. Cook until liquid reduces and mixture thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat. Let filling cool completely.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Unroll puff pastry. Cut into 8-12 equal squares or rectangles, approximately 7x7 cm.
Place a tablespoon of cooled filling onto one half of each pastry piece.
Fold the other half of the pastry over the filling to create a small parcel. Press edges to seal. Use a fork to crimp the edges.
Arrange savory bites on the prepared baking sheet. Brush tops with beaten egg.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown and puffed. Ensure internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Let cool slightly before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Danpat Juk with Goat Cheese Cream and Chili-Port Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A creamy, light brown Danpat Juk (sweet brown rice and kidney bean porridge) is served warm in a small, clean white ceramic bowl, characteristic of Korean individual serving dishes. The porridge is smooth with subtle texture from the brown rice grains. Centered atop the juk is a pristine, soft quenelle of whipped goat cheese cream, its off-white color contrasting gently with the porridge. A glossy, deep amber Chili-Port Glaze is artfully drizzled over the goat cheese and around the porridge, creating delicate ribbons of dark color. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a traditional long-handled Korean spoon placed neatly beside the bowl. The setting is clean and uncluttered, with natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's refined appearance and balanced composition. No other distracting elements are present, focusing entirely on the elegant single portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served in individual small ceramic bowls with a long-handled Korean spoon.
instructions: Rinse dried kidney beans. Soak in cold water overnight, or at least 8 hours. Drain.
Place soaked beans in a pot, cover with fresh water, bring to a boil. Reduce heat, simmer 1 hour, or until very tender. Drain.
Rinse brown rice. In a separate pot, combine rice with 300ml water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover. Simmer 40 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Transfer cooked kidney beans to a food processor or use a potato masher. Add 50g sugar and a pinch of salt. Process or mash until a coarse paste forms. Do not make it too smooth.

In a large pot, combine cooked brown rice, bean paste, and 1 litre of water. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer, stirring frequently, for 20-30 minutes until thickened to a porridge consistency. Add more water if too thick.

Peel and thinly slice shallots and onion. In a small saucepan, add sliced shallots and onion. Cook over very low heat for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized, soft, and very sweet. They should be dark brown and jam-like.
In a separate small saucepan, combine white port, 50g sugar, 1 tablespoon of the deeply caramelized shallot/onion, and the small piece of dried chili. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat and cook slowly until the liquid has reduced by half and is syrupy. Strain the glaze through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing on the solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
In a small bowl, combine goat cheese, 50g sugar, and optional 50ml heavy cream. Whisk until smooth and light.
Divide warm Danpat Juk among 4 individual serving bowls. Place a dollop or quenelle of goat cheese cream on top of each serving. Drizzle generously with the Chili-Port Glaze. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Tomato and Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken with roasted tomato and mozzarella is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A golden-brown, whole chicken breast, unsliced, forms the centerpiece. Melted, gooey fresh mozzarella drapes over the chicken, exhibiting a slight golden char. Around the chicken, vibrant red halved roasted cherry tomatoes, softened purple onion wedges, and golden-brown smashed garlic cloves are artfully arranged. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered over the dish, providing a pop of color and freshness. The textures are varied: crispy chicken exterior, juicy interior, tender roasted vegetables, and creamy cheese. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a rustic piece of crusty Italian bread and a cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread like Pane di Altamura to soak up the juices.
A simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar complements the richness.
Pair with a glass of light-bodied red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Cut red onion into 1.5 cm thick wedges. Smash garlic cloves lightly.
Toss tomatoes, onion wedges, and smashed garlic with 30ml olive oil, dried oregano, salt, and pepper on a baking tray.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove skillet from heat. Arrange roasted tomatoes, onions, and garlic around chicken in the skillet.
Slice fresh mozzarella into 0.5 cm thick rounds. Place mozzarella slices over each chicken breast.
Return skillet to the oven for 5-7 minutes, until mozzarella is melted and bubbly.
Remove skillet from oven. Garnish generously with fresh basil leaves.
Serve immediately from the skillet or transfer to individual plates.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.
Using fresh, quality mozzarella is key for the best melt and flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Spicy Creamy Pork & Bean Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Korean Spicy Creamy Pork & Bean Rice Bowl is presented in a deep, wide, off-white ceramic bowl, centered on a simple light wooden table. The base is a mound of perfectly steamed short-grain white rice. Spooned over the rice is a rich, reddish-brown creamy mixture of ground pork and black beans, with some of the white rice peeking through the edges. The sauce has a glossy, thick texture, coating the dark beans and ground pork chunks. Garnishes are meticulously placed: vibrant green diagonal slices of fresh green onions are scattered across the top, complemented by a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. A few thin, bright red rounds of fresh chili are artfully arranged for a pop of color. The setting features a clean white porcelain dinner plate, and metal Korean chopsticks rest beside the bowl. A small, subtly blurred ceramic dish of red kimchi sits in the background. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an approachable yet refined restaurant-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot as a main course.
Traditionally enjoyed with various banchan (side dishes) like kimchi and pickled radishes.
A side of clear soup often accompanies this type of hearty rice dish.

ingredients.name: Canned black beans, drained and rinsed
Fresh red chili, thinly sliced (optional, for extra heat)

instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package instructions. Keep warm.
Heat cooking oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat.
Add ground pork. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, and sugar to the pan. Stir well to combine with the pork and onion mixture.
Stir in drained black beans. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in evaporated milk and water or chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until the sauce slightly thickens.
Remove from heat. Stir in toasted sesame oil.
Spoon the spicy creamy pork and bean mixture generously over individual portions of cooked rice.
Garnish with diagonally sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Add fresh red chili slices if desired.
notes: This recipe incorporates evaporated milk for a unique creamy texture, offering a modern interpretation of Korean flavors. It is not a traditional Korean dish but uses authentic Korean spices and ingredients.
Cayenne pepper from the prompt is substituted with gochugaru for authentic Korean chili flavor; extra fresh red chili can be added for more heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Taro Coconut Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Sweet Taro Coconut Soup is presented in a deep, simple ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The creamy, off-white coconut milk base fills the bowl, studded with soft, light purple and off-white taro cubes, approximately 2cm in size. Some taro pieces show their slightly darker, fibrous edges. The soup has a gentle sheen from the coconut milk, and the taro cubes are tender, some slightly breaking down to naturally thicken the soup. The overall color palette is muted, focusing on natural creamy white and soft purple hues. The bowl is placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl, and a folded, plain cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, comforting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a comforting dessert.
instructions: Peel taro. Cut taro into 2cm cubes.
Rinse taro cubes to remove excess starch.
In a medium pot, combine taro cubes, water, and pandan leaf (if using).
Bring mixture to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer until taro is tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Add coconut milk, sugar, and salt to the pot. Stir gently to combine.
Continue to simmer for another 5-7 minutes. Do not boil vigorously.
Remove and discard the pandan leaf.
Serve the sweet taro coconut soup warm.
notes: Wear gloves when peeling raw taro, as it can cause skin irritation for some individuals.
Adjust the amount of sugar to suit your preferred level of sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Vanilla Milk Cake with Cherry Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A pristine slice of Vanilla Milk Cake sits elegantly on a clean white porcelain dessert plate. The cake is moist and light, a pale ivory color, generously soaked with milk. A vibrant, glossy ruby-red cherry glaze cascades over the top and gently drips down the sides of the slice. Small, plump, whole cherries are suspended within the glaze, adding texture and color. The cake slice reveals its soft, porous crumb. Beside the slice, a silver dessert fork rests. In the soft-focused background, the remaining whole 20 cm round cake, also adorned with the rich cherry glaze, sits on a simple white cake stand. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface and natural, even lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake pan.
In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, incorporating each fully before adding the next. Stir in vanilla extract.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with whole milk. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared cake pan. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in pan for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
In a medium bowl, whisk together evaporated milk, condensed milk, whole milk, and vanilla extract.
Once cake is completely cool, place it back into the clean cake pan or a shallow dish. Pierce the top of the cake all over with a fork.
Slowly pour the milk soak evenly over the cake. Allow cake to absorb the milk for at least 1 hour, or preferably overnight in the refrigerator.
In a saucepan, combine pitted cherries, sugar, and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until cherries soften.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry. Cook, stirring constantly, until glaze thickens, about 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat. Let cool completely. The glaze will thicken further as it cools.
Once cake has absorbed the milk soak and glaze is cool, carefully transfer the cake to a serving plate.
Pour the cherry glaze evenly over the top of the cake, allowing it to drip down the sides.
Slice and serve.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Savory Chocolate Sauce and Strawberry-Basil Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared duck breast is centrally plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Thick, tender duck medallions, with perfectly rendered, crispy golden-brown skin, are arranged naturally on a generous pool of rich, dark, glossy savory chocolate sauce. Beside the duck, a vibrant mound of fresh strawberry-basil salsa provides a striking color contrast, featuring bright red diced strawberries, specks of green basil, and finely diced red onion. Golden-brown, irregularly cubed brioche croutons are scattered artfully around the dish, adding textural crunch. The composition is balanced and inviting, with appropriate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: the plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its varied textures and appealing colors, creating an inviting, professional yet approachable presentation.

ingredients.name: Unsweetened dark chocolate (70% cacao or higher)

instructions: Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Do not cut into meat. Season duck with salt and pepper.
Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold pan. Cook over medium heat for 10-12 minutes. Render fat. Skin should be crispy and golden.
Flip duck breasts. Cook for 3-5 minutes for medium-rare, or until internal temperature reaches desired doneness. Rest duck on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
For the sauce: Drain most duck fat from pan, leave 15 ml. Add diced shallot. Sauté 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, oregano, and tomato paste. Cook 1 minute. Deglaze pan with red wine. Scrape up browned bits.
Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat. Simmer 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For the strawberry-basil salsa: In a bowl, combine diced strawberries, chopped basil, finely diced red onion. Add lime juice and 15 ml olive oil. Gently mix. Season with salt.
For the brioche croutons: Preheat oven to 180°C. Toss brioche cubes with 15 ml olive oil, garlic powder, and dried herbs. Spread on a baking sheet.
Bake 8-10 minutes. Croutons should be golden and crispy.
Slice rested duck breasts into thick 2 cm medallions. Do not fan out.

Spoon a pool of warm chocolate sauce onto each plate. Arrange duck medallions on top of the sauce. Place a generous spoonful of strawberry-basil salsa beside the duck. Scatter brioche croutons around the plate. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Bell Pepper Salad with Marinated Beef
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table. A bed of vibrant mixed greens forms the base. Artfully arranged on top are tender, earthy brown sliced cremini mushrooms and brightly colored thin slices of red and yellow bell peppers, showcasing their natural shapes and textures. Interspersed among the vegetables are small, irregular chunks of thinly sliced, glazed marinated beef, cooked to a rich brown, clearly visible but not dominating the vegetable components. A light sheen of the Korean-inspired dressing coats all ingredients, integrating them visually. The salad is garnished with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds for textural contrast and thinly sliced fresh green onion for a pop of bright green. The overall presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space. The setting includes a folded cotton napkin beside the plate and traditional Korean metal chopsticks, with small banchan-style bowls subtly in the background. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the fresh ingredients and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refreshing side dish (banchan) alongside a main meal of rice and other Korean dishes.
Offer individual small bowls of rice to accompany the salad.
instructions: Combine beef, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, mirin, brown sugar, 1 tsp minced garlic, grated ginger, and black pepper in a bowl. Marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Heat a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of cooking oil.
Add the marinated beef to the hot pan. Stir-fry quickly until beef is cooked through, about 2-3 minutes. Remove beef from pan and set aside.
In the same pan, add sliced mushrooms and bell peppers. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Add remaining minced garlic and sliced onion; cook for 2 more minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together 3 tbsp soy sauce, rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, honey or sugar, gochugaru (if using), and 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds for the dressing.
In a large mixing bowl, combine mixed greens, sautéed mushrooms, bell peppers, and onion. Add the cooked beef.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to coat all components evenly.
Divide the salad among four plates. Garnish with remaining toasted sesame seeds and fresh green onion.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cherry & Chestnut Verjus Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of Fermented Cherry & Chestnut Verjus Cake rests centrally on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a warm cream hue. The cake displays a rich, earthy brown crumb from the chestnut flour, flecked with tiny specks of vanilla bean. Its texture appears moist and dense. A small, natural pool of glistening fermented cherry compote, a deep ruby red with whole and halved cherries, is spooned beside the cake slice. A whisper of finely grated lemon zest is scattered over the cake. The plate is positioned on a light, reclaimed wood table. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the cake's natural textures. A simple, undyed linen napkin is folded loosely nearby. The background is clean and uncluttered, hinting at a natural setting. The composition is minimalistic, emphasizing the cake's wholesome, rustic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of strong black coffee or espresso
Pair with a glass of light dessert wine
instructions: To ferment cherries: Wash and pit cherries. Place in a clean, airtight jar. Dissolve 20g sugar in 50ml water. Pour over cherries. Seal jar loosely. Let stand at room temperature for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Refrigerate when desired tang is reached.
Preheat oven to 170°C. Grease and flour a 18 cm round cake tin.
Cream softened butter and 100g caster sugar in a bowl until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix well after each addition.
Stir in verjus, vanilla extract, and lemon zest.
In a separate bowl, whisk together chestnut flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared cake tin. Smooth the top.
Bake for 35-40 minutes. Cake is done when a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in tin for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Serve a slice of cake with a spoonful of fermented cherry compote. Garnish with fresh mint if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Red Wine Beef Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of slow-cooked red wine beef stew is served in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The stew features large, tender beef bolar chunks, along with substantial pieces of soft, earthy carrots and potatoes. A few bright green celery pieces and specks of minced parsley provide contrasting color. The rich, dark red-brown sauce coats all ingredients, creating a comforting, slightly glossy texture. The components are naturally piled in the bowl, some overlapping, others peeking out from the sauce. No fanned meat slices. The bowl rests directly on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. A simple, off-white linen or cotton napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. A single piece of crusty, artisanal bread with a torn edge is placed nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, soft, natural light, reminiscent of a cozy kitchen. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen, perhaps with a blurred, warm-toned wall.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Serve over mashed potatoes or buttered noodles
instructions: Cut beef bolar into 3-4 cm cubes. Pat beef dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown beef cubes in batches until seared on all sides. Transfer seared beef to slow cooker.
Dice onion, carrots, and celery into 2 cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the frying pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Deglaze pan with red wine, scraping up browned bits. Bring to a simmer.
Pour wine mixture over beef in slow cooker. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves.
Cover slow cooker. Cook on low for 6-8 hours, or on high for 3-4 hours, until beef is very tender.
Cut potatoes into 3 cm chunks. Add to slow cooker during the last 1.5-2 hours of cooking on low, or 1 hour on high.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Bolar beef is ideal for slow cooking as it becomes incredibly tender.
Cooking time may vary based on your slow cooker model.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Rôti, Légumes Racines et Condiments Maison
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in muted cream. A single, whole roasted chicken breast, skin golden and crisp, is the focal point. Rustic potato wedges, thick carrot batons, and tender onion wedges are arranged organically around it, showcasing earthy colors and roasted textures. Halved roasted cremini mushrooms are interspersed. A vibrant contrast is provided by a small cluster of thinly sliced, quick-pickled cucumber rounds and delicate pale purple pickled onion slices. A light drizzle of shimmering verjus-thyme pan sauce subtly coats the chicken and vegetables. Garnish is sparse: fresh thyme leaves and a whisper of finely grated Comté cheese. The composition is clean, celebrating ingredient beauty. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood table with simple French flatware and an undyed linen napkin, creating an eco-conscious, minimalist aesthetic under soft natural light, with subtle greenery in background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a centerpiece main course.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer a crusty baguette to sop up the delicious pan sauce.
Pair with a dry white wine, such as a Sancerre or Pouilly-Fumé.

ingredients.name: Potato
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium (approx. 600g), peeled, cut into rustic wedges

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium (approx. 300g), peeled, cut into thick batons

ingredients.name: Cucumber
ingredients.quantity: 1 large (approx. 250g), thinly sliced into rounds or ribbons

instructions: Prepare Pickled Cucumber and Onion: In a small saucepan, combine 200ml water, 100ml white wine vinegar, 10g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. Place thinly sliced cucumber and small onion in separate heatproof jars. Pour hot brine over them. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Prepare Vegetables for Roasting: Preheat oven to 200°C. In a large bowl, toss potato wedges, carrot batons, large onion wedges, and halved mushrooms with 40ml olive oil, salt, pepper, and 4 sprigs of thyme. Spread in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast Vegetables: Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned. Turn vegetables halfway through cooking.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season skin generously with salt and pepper.
Sear Chicken: Heat remaining 20ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy.

Finish Chicken in Oven: Flip chicken breasts. Add 2 sprigs of thyme to the skillet. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven with the vegetables. Roast for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Make Verjus Sauce: While chicken rests, place skillet with pan drippings over medium heat. Add verjus and butter. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced and emulsified. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Plate Dish: Place a roasted chicken breast on each plate. Arrange roasted potato wedges, carrot batons, onion wedges, and mushrooms around the chicken. Drain pickled cucumber and onion. Place a small, artful mound of pickled cucumber and a few pickled onion slices next to the roasted vegetables. Drizzle verjus sauce over the chicken and roasted vegetables. Garnish with a few fresh thyme leaves and a very light grating of Comté cheese, if using.
notes: To embrace zero-waste, save vegetable peels and trimmings to make a flavorful vegetable stock for future recipes.
Source chicken and vegetables from local, seasonal producers when possible to reduce environmental impact.
The quick-pickled elements offer a nod to traditional preservation techniques, adding a refreshing, acidic counterpoint to the rich roasted flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Roasted Chicken with Lemon and Oregano
recipes.visual_description: Crispy, golden-brown roasted chicken thighs, cooked to tender perfection, are the centerpiece. They are arranged naturally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Surrounding the chicken are caramelized red onion wedges, soft roasted potato wedges, and vibrant bell pepper chunks. Smashed garlic cloves are interspersed among the vegetables. Fresh lemon slices and a sprinkle of dried oregano garnish the dish, adding bright color and aroma. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, showcasing the rustic beauty of the roasted ingredients. The entire plate is visible on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a cotton napkin and traditional flatware, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting with a nod to Mediterranean warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of tzatziki or a simple Greek salad.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the pan juices.

ingredients.name: Bell pepper
ingredients.quantity: 1 large, any color, cut into chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Combine chicken thighs, potato wedges, onion wedges, smashed garlic, and bell pepper chunks in a large bowl.
Add olive oil, fresh lemon juice, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper. Toss thoroughly to coat all ingredients.
Arrange the mixture in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Garnish with fresh lemon wedges before serving.
notes: For best flavor, marinate chicken and vegetables for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours, before roasting.

recipes.recipe_name: Honey Oat Milk Buns with Fermented Honey Butter and Crisped Oat Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated, minimalist composition featuring three perfectly round, small Honey Oat Milk Buns, each sliced horizontally. They are arranged casually on a sleek, matte grey ceramic sharing plate. On the bottom half of each bun, a perfectly formed quenelle of creamy, pale yellow Fermented Honey Butter is nestled. The top halves of the buns rest gently atop the butter. Around the buns, a scattering of glistening, deep golden Candied Oats provides texture and visual interest. Three delicate, irregular-shaped Crisped Oat Tuiles, translucent and light golden, are artfully placed, leaning against the buns or subtly overlapping. The overall color palette is warm, natural, and harmonious. The plate is positioned on a premium beige travertine surface. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft, intentional shadows, highlighting the textures and forms. The background is ultra-minimalist, creating abundant negative space. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle, rests to the side of the plate.
instructions: For the Honey Oat Milk Buns: Grind 30g rolled oats into fine flour. In a large bowl, combine bread flour, ground oat flour, salt. Whisk to combine.
In a separate bowl, whisk warm milk, yeast, and 20g honey. Let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Add wet ingredients to dry. Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Cover and rest 15 minutes (autolyse).
Add softened butter to dough. Knead dough on a lightly floured surface for 10-12 minutes. Dough should be smooth and elastic.
Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl. Cover and proof in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours, or until doubled in size.
Gently punch down dough. Divide into 8 equal pieces (approx. 60g each). Shape each piece into a tight, round bun.
Place buns on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Cover loosely and proof for another 45-60 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Bake buns for 15-18 minutes, until golden brown. Cool on a wire rack.
For the Fermented Honey Butter: Cut 200g high-quality unsalted butter into cubes. Soften at room temperature.
In a bowl, combine softened butter, 15ml buttermilk, 10g honey, and a pinch of salt. Mix well.
Cover bowl loosely. Let butter ferment at room temperature (20-22°C) for 24-48 hours. Taste periodically for desired tanginess.
Once fermented, chill butter for 30 minutes. Whip with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Refrigerate until use.
For the Crisped Oat Tuile: Grind remaining 20g rolled oats into fine flour. In a bowl, whisk egg white, 30g honey, and granulated sugar until combined.
Stir in ground oat flour and 10g melted unsalted butter. Mix until smooth.
Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat.
Spoon small amounts of batter onto the prepared sheet. Spread very thinly with an offset spatula into irregular, delicate shapes.
Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely on the baking sheet.
For the Candied Oats: In a small pan, toast 20g rolled oats over medium heat until fragrant and lightly golden.
Add 5g honey to the pan. Stir continuously until oats are evenly coated and honey caramelizes slightly. Spread on parchment paper to cool and crisp.
To Assemble: Slice each cooled Honey Oat Milk Bun horizontally. Pipe or quenelle a generous amount of Fermented Honey Butter onto the bottom half of each bun.
Place the top half of the bun back on. Arrange 3-4 prepared buns on a modern sharing plate or small wooden board.
Scatter Candied Oats artfully around the buns. Garnish with delicate Crisped Oat Tuiles, leaning against the buns or scattered on the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Honey Oat Focaccia with Caramelized Onion and Roasted Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A single rectangular portion of golden-brown Savory Honey Oat Focaccia rests on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The focaccia exhibits a crisp, dimpled crust with visible golden-brown rolled oats and dark roasted garlic cloves. Deeply caramelized onion strands are interspersed across its surface, alongside vibrant green sprigs of fresh rosemary and shimmering flakes of sea salt. The interior, visible from the cut edge, is airy, soft, and light-colored, showcasing a perfectly baked crumb. The overall color palette is warm, with shades of golden-brown, amber from the onions, and green from the herbs. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, reflecting a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded light-colored cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the focaccia's texture and color, creating a professional yet inviting presentation. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.

ingredients.name: Garlic head, cloves separated and peeled

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Toss garlic cloves with 5 ml olive oil. Roast for 15-20 minutes until soft and lightly golden. Set aside.
In a large pan, heat 10 ml olive oil over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onions. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine bread flour, rolled oats, and instant dry yeast. Whisk to combine.
In a separate bowl, dissolve honey in warm water. Add 30 ml olive oil and fine sea salt. Stir well.

Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough will be sticky.
Lightly oil a clean bowl. Place dough in bowl, turning to coat. Cover with a damp cloth or plastic wrap. Let rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.

Lightly oil a 20x30 cm baking tray. Gently transfer the risen dough to the tray. Use oiled fingertips to gently stretch and press the dough to fill the tray. Create dimples all over the surface with your fingers.
Evenly scatter the caramelized onions and roasted garlic cloves over the dough. Sprinkle with chopped fresh rosemary and flaky sea salt.
Cover the tray with a damp cloth. Let rise again for 30-45 minutes until slightly puffy.
Preheat oven to 200°C (fan-assisted 180°C). Drizzle generously with olive oil over the focaccia. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until golden brown on top and cooked through.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly in the tray before transferring to a wire rack. Cut into 4 equal portions. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Pork Shoulder with Pickled Apple and Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of slow-cooked pork shoulder is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The pork is a generous, naturally shaped chunk, exhibiting a deep, caramelized crust from searing and a tender, moist interior. Alongside the pork, a small, organic cluster of thinly sliced pickled red onion and apple wedges provides a vibrant counterpoint, their pale pinks and light yellows contrasting with the pork's rich brown. A small pool of smooth, amber-hued pear jus gently pools beside the pork, reflecting light. The plating is minimalistic, with ample white space on the round plate, emphasizing the natural textures of each ingredient. No ornate garnishes are used, preserving a clean aesthetic. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually draped beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the food's natural beauty. The background is clean and uncluttered, with subtle hints of green from a potted plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Pat pork shoulder dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork shoulder on all sides until deeply browned. Remove pork.
Add 2 medium chopped onions and 4 crushed garlic cloves to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Return pork to the pot. Add vegetable stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C. Cook for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is very tender and easily pulled apart.
While pork cooks, prepare pickled apple and onion. Slice 1 small red onion and 2 apples into thin wedges. Place in a heatproof jar.

In a small saucepan, combine 100ml apple cider vinegar, 100ml water, and 50g sugar. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Pour hot pickling liquid over apples and red onion. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until serving.
Once pork is cooked, remove from pot. Strain cooking liquid into a clean saucepan, discarding solids. Skim any excess fat from the liquid.

Add 2 roughly chopped pears and 50ml apple cider vinegar to the strained liquid. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half, until slightly thickened and flavorful. Remove thyme stems and bay leaf. Blend the pear jus with an immersion blender until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Cut pork shoulder into thick, rustic chunks or pull apart into large pieces. Serve warm with pickled apple and onion, drizzled with pear jus.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Broccoli Rice with Savory Tomato Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Chicken and Broccoli Rice with Savory Tomato Cream is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A whole, golden-brown baked chicken breast, coated in a lightly browned, creamy tomato-mayo sauce, rests atop a bed of fluffy white long-grain rice. Visible within the sauce are small, tender pieces of diced red tomato. Around the chicken and rice, vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets are neatly arranged. The overall composition is balanced and inviting. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface with a white cotton napkin placed beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant-style presentation with a minimal background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Season chicken breasts generously with salt, pepper, and 2g paprika.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe baking dish or large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion to the dish. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Carefully place seasoned chicken breasts on top of the rice mixture.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, diced tomatoes, remaining 3g paprika, dried oregano, 2g salt, and 2g black pepper. Mix well.
Spread the tomato-mayo mixture evenly over each chicken breast.
Bake uncovered for 20 minutes.
Remove dish from oven. Arrange broccoli florets around the chicken and rice.
Return to oven. Bake an additional 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and rice is tender.
Let dish rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Hake Velouté with Fermented Tatsoi and Verjus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Hake Velouté is presented in a deep, handcrafted ceramic bowl with a natural off-white glaze. The pale, free-flowing soup cradles a perfectly poached, thick hake fillet, its natural flaky texture visible. A few vibrant green fermented tatsoi leaves are artfully arranged atop the hake and soup, offering a bright textural contrast. Fresh, tender tatsoi leaves add another layer of green. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing the natural beauty of the ingredients to shine. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin and simple, elegant French flatware accompany the dish. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, with a subtle, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette for dipping.
Enjoy as a light main course or a sophisticated starter.
instructions: Make fish stock. Combine hake bones, trimmings, onion, garlic, bay leaf, thyme, and 1 litre cold water in a pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook 30 minutes. Skim impurities. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Set aside.

Prepare fermented tatsoi. Reserve 50g tatsoi leaves whole for garnish. Thinly slice remaining 100g tatsoi leaves and stems. Place in a clean jar. Add 20ml verjus and a pinch of salt. Press down to submerge. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for 1-2 days, or until desired tanginess. Refrigerate.
Poach hake. Gently lower hake fillets into a shallow pan with enough hot fish stock to cover halfway. Cook 5-7 minutes until opaque and flaky. Do not boil. Remove hake. Keep warm.

Make velouté. Melt butter in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour to make a roux. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Gradually whisk in 750ml warm fish stock until smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.

Prepare liaison. In a small bowl, whisk egg yolk with heavy cream. Slowly whisk 100ml hot velouté into the liaison mixture to temper it. Pour liaison back into the vel velouté in the saucepan. Stir constantly. Do not boil after adding liaison.
Finish soup. Stir in remaining 30ml verjus and yogurt. Season with salt and white pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with more stock if needed.

Serve. Ladle hot velouté into individual deep bowls. Place one poached hake fillet in each bowl. Garnish with the prepared fermented tatsoi and the reserved fresh whole tatsoi leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing hake bones for stock and fermenting tatsoi for preservation.
The fermentation time for tatsoi can be adjusted based on desired tanginess. A quick verjus pickle works in 30 minutes, or a longer lacto-fermentation over 1-2 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Heirloom Tomato and Forbidden Rice Salad with Seared Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A Michelin-starred presentation on a pristine white bone china plate, set on white Carrara marble. The vibrant composition features ample negative space. Compressed heirloom tomato wedges, in red, orange, and yellow, are artfully arranged, showcasing translucent texture. Two to three perfectly seared, golden-brown chicken breast chunks are nestled among the tomatoes. A deep purple forbidden black rice tuile shard stands elegantly upright, adding height and crisp texture. A vibrant red roasted bell pepper coulis is subtly swiped or dotted. Glossy, marinated cannellini beans add subtle contrast. Delicate green microgreens garnish the dish. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the minimalist aesthetic. A crisp white linen napkin, precisely folded, completes the elegant setting. The impression is sophisticated simplicity and exquisite precision.
instructions: Prepare Compressed Heirloom Tomatoes: Slice heirloom tomatoes into 1 cm thick disks or wedges. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Arrange in a single layer in a vacuum seal bag. Add 15 ml olive oil and 15 ml white balsamic vinegar. Vacuum seal. Chill for 30 minutes. If no vacuum sealer, gently press between two plates with a light weight for 30 minutes.

Cook Forbidden Rice: Rinse forbidden black rice. Cook according to package directions until tender but still firm, about 25-30 minutes. Drain any excess water. Spread rice on a tray to cool completely. For rice crisps: Once cooled, blend a small portion of cooked rice with a tablespoon of water to a paste. Spread very thinly on a silicone mat. Bake at 150°C until crisp and dry, about 45-60 minutes. Break into shards.

Prepare Roasted Red Pepper Coulis: Roast red bell pepper whole at 200°C until skin is blistered and charred, about 20-25 minutes. Transfer to a bowl, cover with plastic wrap for 10 minutes. Peel, deseed, and roughly chop. Blend roasted pepper with 15 ml olive oil, 5 ml white balsamic vinegar, a small pinch of salt, and pepper until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky coulis. Set aside.

Cook Chicken Breast: Pat chicken breast dry. Season with salt, pepper, and a few thyme leaves. Heat 15 ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breast for 4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to preheated 180°C oven. Roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C, about 10-12 minutes. Rest chicken for 5 minutes. Cut into 2-3 precise 2-3 cm thick chunks.

Prepare Marinated Cannellini Beans: Rinse and drain cooked cannellini beans. In a small bowl, toss beans with remaining 15 ml olive oil, 5 ml white balsamic vinegar, minced garlic, finely chopped basil, salt, and pepper. Let marinate for 10 minutes.

Assemble the Salad: On each plate, create a subtle swipe or a few dots of red pepper coulis. Arrange compressed heirloom tomato pieces artistically on the plate, leaving ample negative space. Place 1-2 pieces of seared chicken alongside the tomatoes. Scatter a small amount of marinated cannellini beans. Arrange a few forbidden rice crisps. Garnish with fresh microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Apple Relish with Savory Beef & Sausage Crumble
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone, showcasing its raw, earthy texture. A generous dollop of the Fermented Tomato & Apple Relish forms the base, its vibrant, mottled red and pale green hues from the diced tomatoes and apples creating a natural, organic shape. The relish has a slightly chunky, rustic texture, reflecting its homemade, preserved nature. Scattered generously over the relish is the Savory Beef & Sausage Crumble. The crumble consists of irregular, small, dark brown pieces of crispy beef and sausage, providing a stark textural and color contrast. A few small, bright green flecks of finely chopped fresh parsley are sparsely sprinkled on top, adding a fresh accent without overwhelming the natural aesthetic. The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample white space around the dish on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the individual textures and natural colors of the ingredients. No ornate garnishes or elaborate arrangements are present; the focus is solely on the honest beauty of the sustainable ingredients.

ingredients.name: Whey or brine from previous fermentation
Beef trimmings or lean ground beef

instructions: Combine diced tomatoes, diced apples, minced onion, minced garlic, grated ginger, salt, and whey (or brine) in a clean bowl. Mix thoroughly.
Transfer mixture to a clean glass jar. Press down firmly to remove air pockets. Ensure all solids are submerged.
Cover jar with an airlock lid or cloth. Secure with a rubber band.
Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 3-5 days. Ferment until desired tanginess. Burp daily if using cloth.
Store fermented relish in the refrigerator.
Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Add crumbled sausage meat.
Cook sausage until deeply browned and crispy. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon. Reserve excess fat.
Add minced beef to the same pan. Use a small amount of reserved sausage fat if needed. Cook until beef is browned and crispy.
Return crispy sausage to the pan with the beef. Add reduced chicken stock and dried herbs. Stir until liquid evaporates and coats meat.
Season meat crumble with black pepper.
Spoon Fermented Tomato & Apple Relish onto a plate.
Sprinkle Savory Beef & Sausage Crumble over the relish.
Garnish with finely chopped fresh parsley or chives.
notes: Emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing beef trimmings and promoting fermentation.
Seasonal and local ingredients are key for optimal flavor and sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Salada de Frutas Tropical
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely portion of vibrant fruit salad fills a rustic, slightly imperfect ceramic bowl, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. Diced peaches, quartered strawberries, whole raspberries, and 1 cm thick banana slices are naturally mixed and piled high, showcasing their juicy textures and bright, natural colors—reds, yellows, and oranges. A few fresh green mint leaves are casually scattered on top for a pop of freshness. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, reflecting a comfortable, lived-in family dining area. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl, with a casually placed, slightly crumpled cloth napkin completing the unpretentious, comforting tableau.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a refreshing dessert or a light breakfast.
Enjoy simply with a spoon.
Optionally, serve with a side of condensed milk (leite condensado) for a richer, more traditional Brazilian touch.
instructions: Prepare peaches: Peel, pit, and dice peaches into 2 cm cubes.
Prepare strawberries: Hull strawberries. Quarter larger ones. Leave smaller ones whole.
Prepare bananas: Slice bananas into 1 cm thick rounds.
Combine fruits: Gently place diced peaches, quartered strawberries, whole raspberries, and sliced bananas in a large mixing bowl.
Make dressing: In a separate small bowl, whisk together orange juice, lime juice, and sugar until sugar is dissolved.
Dress fruit: Pour the juice dressing over the mixed fruits. Gently toss to coat all fruit evenly.
Chill: Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld and fruit to chill.
Serve: Spoon generous portions of chilled fruit salad into individual serving bowls. Garnish each portion with a few fresh mint leaves before serving.
notes: Use ripe but firm fruits for best texture.
Chilling the salad before serving enhances its refreshing quality and allows the flavors to deepen.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Tomato Risotto and Crispy Potato Rosti
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, professionally plated dish. A pan-seared salmon fillet, with crispy golden skin and tender pink flesh, rests on creamy, al dente tomato risotto. The risotto, rich orange-red from crushed tomatoes, is flecked with grated Parmesan and green parsley. Beside it, a perfectly round, golden-brown crispy potato rosti stands tall, showcasing its finely grated texture. Fresh chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a vibrant green contrast. The clean white porcelain plate is centered on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware complete the modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the food, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a casual restaurant ambiance.
instructions: Potato Rosti:
Peel russet potatoes. Grate coarsely.
Rinse grated potatoes in cold water. Squeeze out excess water thoroughly with a clean cloth.
Season potatoes with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Press potato mixture into 4 compact rounds in the pan. Do not overcrowd.
Cook rostis 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer rostis to a wire rack. Keep warm in a low oven (80°C).
Tomato Risotto:
Heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add finely diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Toast rice 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir to combine.
Add stock one ladle at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for liquid to be absorbed before adding more.
Continue adding stock and stirring for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 20g butter and grated Parmesan.
Season with salt and pepper. Cover. Let rest 2 minutes.
Pan-Seared Salmon:
Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season skin and flesh with salt and pepper.
Heat a large non-stick or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add 15ml olive oil.
Place salmon skin-side down in hot skillet. Sear 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip salmon. Cook 3-4 minutes on flesh side until internal temperature reaches 60°C.
Remove salmon from pan. Rest 2 minutes.
Plating:
Spoon a portion of creamy tomato risotto onto the center of each plate.
Place one crispy potato rosti beside the risotto.
Gently place a pan-seared salmon fillet on top of the risotto or beside it, slightly overlapping.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Brigadeiros de Limão
recipes.visual_description: The finished Brigadeiros de Limão are presented as small, uniform, spherical sweets, each approximately 2-3 cm in diameter. Their color is a delicate, creamy pale yellow, with a slightly textured surface from a light coating of granulated sugar. They are arranged artfully, but naturally, in a cluster of 6-9 pieces on a simple, elegant white ceramic serving platter. The arrangement allows for appropriate negative space, highlighting the individual perfect spheres. The texture is firm yet yielding, suggesting a rich, fudgy interior. The platter sits on a well-used wooden dining table in a homely family kitchen. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene. A casually placed cloth napkin and a small bowl of fresh lemon wedges are subtly visible in the background, adding to the authentic, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served on small paper cups (forminhas de brigadeiro) at celebrations.
Often presented on decorative platters with other small sweets (docinhos).
instructions: Combine condensed milk, butter, lemon juice, lemon zest, and vanilla extract in a medium non-stick saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon.
Continue stirring until the mixture thickens significantly and pulls away from the bottom and sides of the pan (ponto de brigadeiro). This takes 10-15 minutes.
Remove from heat. Transfer the mixture to a greased plate or shallow dish. Spread evenly.
Allow the mixture to cool completely at room temperature, or chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
Lightly grease your hands with butter. Scoop small portions of the cooled mixture.
Roll each portion into a uniform sphere, approximately 2-3 cm in diameter.
Roll each brigadeiro in granulated sugar to coat evenly.
Place finished brigadeiros into small paper cups (forminhas de brigadeiro) if desired, or arrange directly on a serving platter.
notes: Ensure the mixture cools completely before rolling; this makes handling much easier.
Adjust lemon juice and zest to your preferred level of tartness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with "Confetti" Quinoa
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a refined casual dining aesthetic. A mound of fluffy quinoa, subtly integrated with finely diced red, yellow, and green bell peppers and chives, forms a vibrant base. Beside it rests a perfectly seared chicken breast, its golden-brown crust contrasting with the tender, moist interior. The chicken is whole, unsliced. A light sheen from the lemon-butter pan sauce glistens on the chicken surface. The entire composition is generously sprinkled with a "confetti" of vibrant, finely diced bell peppers, bright green chives, and scattered toasted pumpkin seeds, creating a playful yet elegant visual texture resembling "100s and 1000s." Colors are natural and appealing. Moderate negative space surrounds the elements. A cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting. A single individual portion is displayed.
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly under cold water. Combine quinoa and chicken stock in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Or cook until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
While quinoa cooks, finely dice red, yellow, and green bell peppers. Finely chop chives. Toast pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 2-3 minutes. Set aside.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-6 minutes per side until golden brown.

Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Add butter and lemon juice to the skillet, basting the chicken. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Gently fold half of the diced bell peppers and chives into the cooked quinoa.
Spoon a generous portion of "confetti" quinoa onto each plate. Place one seared chicken breast beside the quinoa.
Sprinkle the remaining diced bell peppers, chives, and toasted pumpkin seeds over the chicken and quinoa.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Sun-Dried Tomato Fettuccine
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Chicken and Sun-Dried Tomato Fettuccine is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The fettuccine, coated generously in a rich, creamy off-white sauce, is coiled naturally in the center. Scattered among the pasta are golden-brown seared chicken chunks, approximately 2-3 cm in size, exhibiting a slight crisp exterior. Vibrant red slices of sun-dried tomatoes and deep green wilted spinach leaves provide pops of color and texture. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the dish. Fresh green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the top as a garnish. The plate rests on a simple rustic wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork are placed neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows. The background is a subtly blurred, casual restaurant setting, enhancing the approachable bistro atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space around the edges.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing sauce to slightly thicken.
Meanwhile, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
