recipes.recipe_name: Velouté of Bitter Greens, Crispy Radicchio, Sherry Reduction
recipes.visual_description: The Velouté of Bitter Greens is presented in a deep, elegant bone china bowl with abundant white space. The soup itself is a vibrant, verdant green, perfectly smooth and glistening, poured to fill about one-third of the bowl's volume, leaving ample pristine white rim. In the center, a cluster of small, pale green endive leaves are delicately arranged, their crisp texture providing a subtle contrast. Around this central arrangement, a precise drizzle of dark, glossy sherry reduction forms abstract lines. A scattering of finely julienned, golden-crisp radicchio pieces adds a touch of warmth and textural interest. A few bright green micro-arugula leaves are meticulously placed as a final, fresh garnish. The composition is minimalist yet rich in color and texture, with each element purposefully placed for visual harmony. The bowl rests on a polished white Carrara marble surface, accompanied by a single, meticulously folded white linen napkin and a minimalist silver spoon, all under dramatic professional lighting creating soft shadows.

ingredients.name: Mixed salad greens (e.g., frisée, baby spinach)

instructions: Remove outer leaves from radicchio. Cut radicchio into very thin julienne strips.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Fry radicchio strips until crisp. Drain on paper towel. Season lightly with salt. Set aside.
In a small saucepan, combine sherry wine vinegar and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Reduce until syrupy, about 15ml. Set aside.
Peel and finely dice shallots. Peel and thinly slice garlic.
In a large pot, melt 30g butter with 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced shallots and sliced garlic. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes. Do not brown.
Wash all salad greens, arugula, watercress, and leaves from one head of endive. Add them to the pot with shallots and garlic. Cook, stirring, until wilted, about 3-5 minutes.
Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Carefully transfer soup mixture to a high-speed blender. Blend until very smooth. Pass soup through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. Discard solids.
Return sieved soup to low heat. Stir in heavy cream. Whisk in remaining 20g butter until melted and emulsified. Season with salt and white pepper to taste. Keep warm. Do not boil after adding cream.
Separate remaining endive head. Select small, pristine inner leaves for garnish.

Ladle warm velouté into each of four warm soup bowls. Arrange a few small endive leaves delicately in the center. Drizzle a few drops of the sherry reduction around the endive leaves. Scatter a small amount of crispy radicchio over and around the endive. Garnish with a few micro-greens. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure all greens are thoroughly washed and dried before cooking to prevent excess water dilution.
Blending and sieving are crucial for a silky-smooth velouté.
Adjust sherry reduction sweetness and acidity to balance the bitterness of the greens.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Radicchio & Roasted Root Vegetable Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, minimalistic bowl showcases sustainable ingredients. A bed of earthy green lentils forms the base. Arranged artfully are tender, roasted root vegetable chunks—orange carrots, pale parsnips, ruby beetroot—each lightly caramelized. Bright, tangy strips of fermented radicchio nestle among them, their deep purple contrasting lighter elements. Crisp fresh leaves of arugula, watercress, and individual endive spears are delicately placed, adding varied greens and a peppery bite. The dish is lightly dressed with a golden sherry vinaigrette. A scattering of toasted pumpkin seeds provides textural crunch. The clean, unfussy presentation highlights natural beauty and distinct textures. It rests in a handcrafted ceramic bowl on a light reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin and simple, modern flatware complete the eco-conscious setting under soft natural light.
instructions: Clean radicchio. Cut into 2 cm strips. Pack into a clean jar. Dissolve 15 g salt in 500 ml water for brine. Pour brine over radicchio. Ensure radicchio is submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature 5-7 days. Burp daily. Store in refrigerator.
Collect root vegetable peelings, onion ends, herb stems. Simmer in 1 litre water for 30 minutes. Strain broth.

Rinse lentils. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pot. Sauté diced onion until translucent. Add lentils, 800 ml broth, bay leaf, thyme, smashed garlic. Bring to boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 20-25 minutes until tender. Remove bay leaf, thyme, garlic. Season with 3 g salt and 1 g pepper.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut carrots, parsnips, and beetroot into 2 cm chunks. Toss root vegetable chunks with 30 ml olive oil, 5 g salt, 2 g pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast 25-35 minutes until tender and caramelized.
Whisk 60 ml sherry wine vinegar, 5 ml Dijon mustard, 5 ml maple syrup, 2 g salt, 1 g pepper. Slowly whisk in 120 ml olive oil until emulsified.

Divide cooked lentils among 4 bowls. Arrange roasted root vegetables alongside. Drain fermented radicchio; add to bowls. Arrange fresh arugula, watercress, endive leaves, and mixed salad greens. Drizzle with sherry vinaigrette. Garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds and chopped parsley.
notes: Fermentation time for radicchio can vary based on desired tanginess and room temperature. Taste after 5 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Medallions with Sherry-Glazed Radicchio and Bitter Greens
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of pan-seared pork medallions, showing a golden-brown crust and moist interior, rests beside vibrant, tender, sherry-glazed radicchio wedges. The radicchio displays its characteristic deep red and white hues. A fresh, slightly mounded mix of crisp green arugula, pale yellow-green endive leaves, and bright green watercress is casually placed adjacent, providing a textural and color contrast. The dish is presented on a simple, well-used ceramic plate with natural imperfections, set on a warm wooden dining table. A simple cloth napkin and everyday flatware are casually arranged nearby. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, enhancing the natural colors of the food. The pork is presented as whole medallions, not sliced or fanned.
instructions: Trim silver skin from pork tenderloin. Cut into 2.5 cm thick medallions. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork medallions 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). Remove pork from skillet. Set aside, tent with foil.
Halve radicchio, remove core. Cut into 2 cm wide wedges.
In the same skillet, add remaining 15 ml olive oil. Add diced shallot and minced garlic. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add radicchio wedges to skillet. Cook 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until slightly softened.
Pour in sherry wine vinegar. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of skillet. Add chicken broth and sugar. Bring to a simmer.

Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and cook 8-10 minutes until radicchio is tender. Remove lid. Increase heat to medium. Cook 2-3 minutes more to reduce liquid to a light glaze. Stir in butter until melted. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine arugula, endive, and watercress.
Arrange braised radicchio on plates. Place pork medallions alongside. Top with fresh bitter greens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Chicken and Bitter Greens Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, inviting individual portion of Grilled Chicken and Bitter Greens Salad rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The plate is not overcrowded, showcasing a balanced composition with moderate negative space. Succulent grilled chicken breast pieces, sliced crosswise into 1.5 cm thick chunks, are arranged naturally atop a bed of mixed bitter greens – crisp green arugula and watercress, pale yellow and white endive wedges, and deep purple radicchio ribbons. The chicken exhibits char marks and a golden-brown exterior, contrasting with its tender, juicy interior. A light, glossy sherry vinaigrette subtly coats the leaves, enhancing their natural colors. Toasted walnut halves add textural contrast and warm brown tones. Crumbled white goat cheese provides creamy accents. The presentation is clean, professional, and approachable. A folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's freshness and textures.
instructions: Prepare vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together sherry wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, minced shallot, salt, and pepper. Slowly drizzle in olive oil while whisking constantly until emulsified. Set aside.
Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Lightly brush with olive oil. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Grill chicken: Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts on the grill. Cook for 6-8 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from grill. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Slice chicken: Slice rested chicken breasts crosswise into 1.5 cm thick pieces. Do not fan out.
Prepare greens: Wash and thoroughly dry arugula, watercress, endive, and radicchio.
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine arugula, watercress, endive, and radicchio. Drizzle half of the vinaigrette over greens. Gently toss to coat.
Plate: Divide dressed greens among four individual plates. Arrange sliced grilled chicken pieces on top of the greens.
Finish: Scatter toasted walnuts and crumbled goat cheese over each salad. Drizzle remaining vinaigrette over chicken and salad. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Scallops with Bitter Green Essence and Sherry Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared scallops sits gracefully on a large, pristine white bone china plate. Four plump, perfectly seared scallops display a deep golden-brown crust and tender, white interiors. A vibrant green essence, derived from watercress and arugula, is artfully dotted around the scallops, its intense color contrasting with their golden hue. A delicate drizzle of glossy, amber sherry gastrique weaves elegantly across the plate. Scattered sparingly are a few irregularly shaped, ultra-crisp radicchio chips, offering deep burgundy color and textural crunch. Two small, pale green endive leaves are precisely placed, adding architectural structure. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space highlighting the perfection of each element. The setting is a white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin and elegant silver flatware complete the luxurious, understated scene.
instructions: Prepare Sherry Gastrique: Combine 100ml sherry wine vinegar and 50g granulated sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until syrupy and coats the back of a spoon, approximately 15ml-20ml. Set aside.

Prepare Bitter Green Essence: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath. Blanch 100g watercress and 50g arugula for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain greens well; squeeze out excess water.

Blend blanched greens with 50ml ice water until very smooth. Pass the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing firmly to extract liquid. Discard solids. Whisk in 10g unsalted butter until emulsified. Season with salt. Keep warm gently.

Prepare Crispy Radicchio: Remove outer leaves of 1 small radicchio head. Slice leaves paper-thin into irregular chips using a mandoline. Heat 20ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Fry radicchio chips in batches until crisp. Drain on paper towel. Season with flaky sea salt.
Prepare Endive: Separate individual leaves from 2 endive heads. Select 1-2 small, perfect inner leaves per serving.

Sear Scallops: Pat scallops very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides. Heat remaining 20ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering. Add scallops in a single layer; do not overcrowd. Cook undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until a deep golden-brown crust forms.

Flip scallops. Add remaining 40g unsalted butter to the pan. Baste scallops with melted butter for another 1-2 minutes until cooked through but still tender in the center. Transfer scallops to a plate.

Plate the dish: Arrange 3-4 seared scallops off-center on a large white bone china plate. Drizzle a fine line or small pool of sherry gastrique near the scallops. Place a few dots or a small quenelle of the vibrant green essence on the plate. Scatter 2-3 crispy radicchio chips artfully around the scallops. Place 1-2 small endive leaves as an accent.

recipes.recipe_name: Radicchio & Root Vegetable Salad with Sherry Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist presentation on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone (e.g., matte cream). A vibrant base of mixed salad greens, arugula, and watercress supports thinly sliced fresh radicchio and endive, providing sharp color and textural contrast. Vibrant orange roasted carrot rounds, cut into 1 cm thick, are artfully distributed. Magenta quick-pickled radicchio pieces, thinly sliced, add bright pops of color. Toasted pumpkin seeds are sparingly sprinkled. The sherry vinaigrette lightly coats the leaves. The scene is set on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh, sustainable ingredients against a clean, minimalist background with subtle greenery.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled and cut into 1 cm thick rounds or half-moons

instructions: Prepare Pickled Radicchio: In a small saucepan, combine water, sherry wine vinegar, 15 ml honey, and 5g sea salt. Bring to a simmer. Stir until salt and honey dissolve. Remove from heat. Place thinly sliced radicchio in a heatproof jar. Pour hot brine over radicchio. Ensure radicchio is submerged. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Roast Carrots: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss carrot rounds with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet in a single layer. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool.

Make Vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together 45 ml sherry wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, 5g honey, a pinch of sea salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Slowly drizzle in 90 ml extra virgin olive oil while whisking continuously until emulsified.
Assemble Salad: In a large bowl, combine mixed salad greens, fresh endive slices, fresh arugula, fresh watercress, and fresh radicchio slices. Add cooled roasted carrots.

Dress and Serve: Drain about half of the pickled radicchio. Add drained pickled radicchio to the salad bowl. Pour vinaigrette over the salad. Toss gently to combine. Divide salad among four plates. Garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Radicchio and Mixed Greens Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Radicchio and Mixed Greens Salad is presented in a simple, deep white ceramic bowl, resting on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The radicchio is thinly sliced, showcasing its deep red-purple hue and crisp texture. It is casually tossed with roughly chopped endive, bright green arugula, and delicate watercress, creating a harmonious blend of colors and leafy forms. A light, glossy sherry vinaigrette evenly coats the fresh leaves, enhancing their natural sheen. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, with leaves slightly overlapping, creating a visually appealing yet homely portion. A simple, everyday fork rests casually beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin. Warm, natural light from a nearby window illuminates the fresh ingredients, emphasizing their natural vibrancy and inviting texture.

ingredients.name: Salad green (e.g., Romaine or Butter lettuce)

instructions: Thoroughly wash and dry all salad greens.
Thinly slice the radicchio.
Roughly chop the endive and the additional salad green.
Combine sliced radicchio, chopped endive, arugula, and watercress in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together sherry wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper.
Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while continuously whisking until the dressing is emulsified.
Pour the dressing over the mixed greens.
Toss gently until all greens are evenly coated.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure greens are very dry for best dressing adherence.

recipes.recipe_name: Radicchio and Mixed Green Salad with Toasted Walnuts
recipes.visual_description: The Radicchio and Mixed Green Salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Shredded crimson radicchio provides a vibrant base, intertwined with bright green arugula, deep green watercress, and lighter mixed salad greens. Thinly sliced white endive pieces are artfully distributed throughout, adding textural contrast. The ingredients are moderately tossed, creating an organic, yet professional, arrangement with visible pockets of color and texture. A light sheen of sherry vinaigrette glistens on the leaves. Roughly chopped toasted walnuts are scattered generously over the top. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface and a folded cotton napkin positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its freshness and vibrant colors. No overcrowding, just a clean, approachable presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Spread walnuts on a baking sheet. Toast 8-10 minutes until fragrant. Let cool. Roughly chop.
Core radicchio. Shred finely. Place in a large bowl.
Trim endive. Thinly slice lengthwise. Add to the bowl.
Add arugula, watercress, and mixed salad greens to the bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, sherry wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper until emulsified.
Pour vinaigrette over the greens. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Divide salad among four plates. Sprinkle toasted walnuts over each serving. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Radicchio and Endive Salad with Toasted Walnuts and Sherry Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine, oversized round bone china plate with abundant white space. A central, artfully composed mound of vibrant greens forms the focal point. Finely shredded ruby-red radicchio contrasts with pale, crisp julienned endive, dark green arugula, and bright watercress. Each leaf is distinct, lightly coated with a shimmering, golden sherry vinaigrette. Scattered precisely over and around the greens are irregularly shaped pieces of golden-brown toasted walnuts, adding a textural counterpoint. The composition is organic and flowing. The plate rests on a premium grey veined marble surface. A perfectly folded white linen napkin sits beside it. Dramatic, focused lighting creates soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's contours and fresh textures. The background is minimalist, ensuring the salad's sophisticated simplicity is paramount.
instructions: Wash and thoroughly dry all salad greens.
Finely shred the radicchio. Separate endive leaves, reserving a few small whole leaves. Julienne the remaining endive.
Gently toast walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant. Cool, then roughly chop.
For the vinaigrette, finely mince the shallot. In a small bowl, whisk together minced shallot, Dijon mustard, sherry wine vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Slowly drizzle in extra virgin olive oil while continuously whisking until the dressing is emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine shredded radicchio, julienned endive, arugula, and watercress.
Add a small amount of vinaigrette to the greens. Gently toss to lightly coat.
On each plate, create an artful, minimalist mound of dressed greens. Arrange a few reserved whole endive leaves around the base for visual structure.
Sprinkle toasted walnuts over and around the greens. If using, delicately place a few very thin shavings of Pecorino cheese on top.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli & Crab Garden with Onion Soubise
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, artfully composed salad on a pristine white bone china plate. A delicate, creamy swirl of pale ivory Onion Soubise forms the base. Arranged organically atop and around the soubise are vibrant, precisely cut vegetable components: tiny, tender-crisp blanched broccoli florets, bright green peas, sweet yellow corn kernels, and small, subtly caramelized cubes of roasted carrot and potato. Interspersed among the vegetables are 2-3 pristine, delicate mounds of flaky white crab meat, gently warmed. A scattering of golden-brown, crispy broccoli stem crumble adds texture. The dish is finished with precise dots of a vivid green garlic-herb oil and a few sprigs of delicate microgreens, providing subtle height and color contrast. Abundant white space surrounds the composition, emphasizing the architectural precision and sophisticated simplicity. The setting features a superpremium wooden table, a crisply folded white linen napkin, and dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows, highlighting the dish's exquisite details.
instructions: Prepare Onion Soubise: Thinly slice onions. Melt 20g butter in a saucepan over low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly for 20-25 minutes until very tender and translucent, without browning. Add cream. Simmer for 5 minutes. Season with salt and white pepper. Blend until perfectly smooth. Pass through a fine mesh sieve. Keep warm.

Prepare Roasted Vegetables: Peel carrots and potatoes. Cut into precise 3mm brunoise (tiny cubes). Toss with 15ml olive oil and salt. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast at 180°C for 15-20 minutes until tender and lightly caramelized. Do not overcook. Set aside.

Prepare Blanched Vegetables: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath. Blanch broccoli florets for 2 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Repeat with green peas and corn kernels, blanching for 1 minute each. Drain all blanched vegetables very well. Set aside.

Prepare Broccoli Stem Crumble: Peel broccoli stems. Grate or finely mince the peeled stems. Toss with 5ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread thinly on a baking sheet. Roast at 140°C for 30-40 minutes until completely dry and crisp, stirring occasionally. Alternatively, use a dehydrator followed by a light toast. Set aside.
Prepare Crab Meat: Gently warm the crab meat in 20g butter over very low heat for 1-2 minutes. Do not cook. Season lightly with salt. Mix in half of the finely minced chives.

Prepare Garlic-Herb Oil: Gently confit peeled garlic cloves in neutral oil over very low heat for 15 minutes. Let cool slightly. Blend the garlic-infused oil with fresh parsley and remaining chives until vibrant green and smooth. Strain through a fine sieve for a clear oil. Season with salt.

Plate the dish: Ladle a delicate swirl of warm Onion Soubise onto the center of each plate. Artistically arrange small, distinct clusters of roasted carrot brunoise, roasted potato brunoise, blanched broccoli florets, green peas, and corn kernels around and on the soubise. Place 2-3 small, pristine pieces of warmed crab meat among the vegetables. Sprinkle the crisp broccoli stem crumble sparingly for texture. Drizzle precise dots or a fine line of the Garlic-Herb Oil around the composition. Garnish with a few microgreens for elevation and fresh color. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot, Pea, and Crab Salad with Crispy Potato and Garlic-Herb Oil
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a pristine white bone china plate with a wide rim, set on a premium white Carrara marble surface. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's texture and form, while maintaining an ultra-minimalist background with abundant negative space. The composition is an organic, flowing arrangement, avoiding any geometric shapes. A vibrant, smooth swipe of emerald green pea puree forms a base, upon which the other components are artfully arranged. Golden-orange roasted carrot batons and rounds are interspersed with delicate, small blanched broccoli florets and precisely pan-fried 1 cm crispy potato cubes. Small, pristine white chunks of lump crab meat are strategically placed among the vegetables, ensuring a 4:1 vegetable-to-meat visual ratio. The entire ensemble is glistening with a light drizzle of golden garlic-herb oil, enhancing its visual appeal. The colors are sophisticated: vibrant green, earthy orange, and pristine white, creating a harmonious contrast. A single, delicate sprig of fresh dill or a fine lemon zest curl serves as a precise garnish, adding a final touch of elegance. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests beside the plate.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Peel carrots. Cut 200g into 5 cm batons. Cut remaining 200g into 0.5 cm thick rounds.
Toss carrot batons and rounds with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp.
Peel and dice potatoes into 1 cm cubes. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Pan-fry potato cubes until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Season with salt. Drain on paper towels.
Separate broccoli into very small florets. Blanch broccoli florets in boiling salted water for 1 minute. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Blanch green peas in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Reserve 50g whole peas for garnish. Drain remaining peas.

Blend drained peas with 15 ml olive oil, a squeeze of lemon juice, and a pinch of salt until very smooth. Adjust consistency with a tablespoon of water if needed. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a refined puree.

Peel and thinly slice garlic cloves. Combine garlic with 50 ml olive oil in a small saucepan. Cook over very low heat for 15-20 minutes until garlic is soft and golden, not browned. Strain the garlic confit oil, reserving the oil. Discard solids.
Finely mince red onion. Mince fresh dill and chives.
In a small bowl, whisk together garlic confit oil, white wine vinegar, juice of half a lemon, minced red onion, dill, and chives. Season with salt and pepper.
Gently pick through crab meat to remove any shell fragments. Keep crab meat cold.

To assemble, gently combine roasted carrots, crispy potato cubes, blanched broccoli florets, and reserved whole green peas. Add 2-3 small pieces of lump crab meat per serving. Lightly dress with a portion of the vinaigrette.

Spoon a generous artistic swipe or two of pea puree onto each plate. Artfully arrange the salad mixture on top of and around the pea puree, creating an organic, flowing composition. Ensure all components are visible.
Drizzle the remaining vinaigrette over the salad. Garnish with a few micro-herbs or a very thin lemon zest curl for a final touch.

recipes.recipe_name: Apel Pisang Pai Kelapa
recipes.visual_description: A single, rustic Apel Pisang Pai Kelapa is presented on a simple, slightly chipped ceramic plate, set on a well-used wooden dining table. The tartlet features a golden-brown, flaky shortcrust pastry with natural imperfections. The filling, a rich, caramelized blend of diced apples and thinly sliced bananas, peeks through the top, showing soft textures and deep brown hues from the gula aren. A generous sprinkle of golden-brown toasted shredded coconut covers the top, adding a textural contrast. The plate is positioned casually off-center, with a folded, slightly worn batik-patterned cloth napkin beside it. Warm, natural light streams from a nearby window, casting soft shadows. The overall scene is homely and inviting, reflecting a relaxed Indonesian family kitchen atmosphere. No decorative elements distract from the food itself; the focus is on the comforting, natural appearance of the dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a glass of teh tawar (plain hot tea).
Can be accompanied by a small dollop of santan (coconut milk) cream.

ingredients.name: Apples, peeled, cored, diced into 1 cm cubes
Firm ripe bananas, sliced 0.5 cm thick
Gula aren (palm sugar), grated or finely chopped
Egg wash (1 egg yolk + 1 tbsp water)

instructions: Combine flour and salt in a large bowl. Add cold butter. Rub butter into flour using fingertips until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add iced water, mixing until dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form into a disc, wrap in plastic, and chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease four 10 cm tartlet molds.
Melt 10 g butter in a pan over medium heat. Add diced apples. Cook for 5 minutes until slightly softened.
Add sliced bananas, gula aren, cinnamon, and lime juice to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fruit is tender and sugar is dissolved. Set aside to cool slightly.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out chilled dough to 3 mm thickness. Cut out four circles large enough to fit the tartlet molds.
Press dough circles into molds. Trim excess dough. Fill each tartlet shell evenly with the fruit mixture.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until crust is golden brown and filling is bubbling. If crust browns too quickly, cover edges with foil.
While tartlets bake, toast shredded coconut in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 3-5 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden brown and fragrant. Set aside.
Remove tartlets from oven. Let cool in molds for 5 minutes, then carefully transfer to a wire rack.
Brush tartlet crusts with egg wash for a golden sheen (optional, for visual appeal).
Garnish each warm tartlet with toasted shredded coconut before serving.
notes: Ensure bananas are firm-ripe, not overripe, to maintain some texture.
Gula aren (palm sugar) provides a distinct caramel-like flavor unique to Indonesian sweets.
traditional_techniques: Using gula aren as a primary sweetener

recipes.recipe_name: Bolinhos de Carne e Arroz com Legumes
recipes.visual_description: A casual, inviting image of golden-brown Bolinhos de Carne e Arroz with Legumes arranged on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The croquettes are irregularly shaped, showcasing their homemade nature, with visible flecks of green parsley, red tomato, and dark mushroom against the light brown crust. Some are stacked gently, others are scattered naturally on the plate, allowing generous negative space. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, small ceramic bowl with a rich, red tomato dipping sauce sits beside the croquettes. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere. A casually draped, textured linen napkin in a neutral tone completes the homely, unpretentious scene. The entire plate is visible, highlighting its generous, comforting portion size.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as 'petiscos' (Portuguese tapas) with other small plates.
Accompany with a simple 'molho de tomate' (tomato sauce) for dipping.
Offer a wedge of lemon for a fresh squeeze.
Serve alongside a glass of vinho verde or a light beer.
instructions: Cook brown rice according to package directions. Set aside to cool.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef to the pan. Break it apart. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Drain any excess fat from the beef.
Stir in diced tomatoes, diced mushrooms, and finely chopped broccoli. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften.
Transfer cooked beef and vegetable mixture to a large bowl. Add cooled brown rice.
Add chopped parsley, egg, salt, and pepper to the mixture. Mix well to combine.
If using, add piri-piri sauce to taste. Mix again.
Take small portions of the mixture. Form into oval or round croquettes, about 5 cm long.
Place breadcrumbs in a shallow dish. Roll each croquette in breadcrumbs, coating evenly.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat.
Fry croquettes in batches. Cook until golden brown and crisp on all sides, about 4-6 minutes per batch.
Ensure beef is cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 71°C (160°F).
Remove croquettes. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve warm.
notes: Ensure the beef and rice mixture is cooled before adding the egg to prevent the egg from cooking prematurely.
For extra flavor, a pinch of smoked paprika can be added to the beef mixture.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Acorn Squash with Garlic Shrimp and Crab Stuffing
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted acorn squash half, golden-brown and tender, rests on a pristine white porcelain plate. Its cavity is generously filled with a vibrant, mounded medley of ingredients. Succulent pink shrimp are interspersed with delicate white flakes of lump crab meat. Earthy brown cremini mushrooms and bright red diced bell peppers add color and texture. The mixture glistens from a light lemon-garlic sauce. Fresh green chopped parsley is scattered over the top, providing a pop of freshness. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, showcasing the natural beauty of the ingredients. The plate sits on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin beside it, under soft, natural lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut each acorn squash in half lengthwise. Scoop out seeds.
Drizzle squash halves with 15ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Place squash cut-side down on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-40 minutes until tender.
While squash roasts, heat remaining 15ml olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced bell pepper and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add shrimp to the pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Remove pan from heat. Gently fold in lump crab meat, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
Season filling with salt and pepper to taste.
Once squash is roasted, turn cut-side up.
Spoon the seafood and vegetable filling generously into each squash half.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Confit Chicken and Crispy Potato Pavé Bites
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a large, rectangular, white bone china sharing platter, centered on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, creating an architectural and minimalist composition. Eight to twelve perfectly golden-brown, rectangular potato pavé blocks are arranged organically across the platter, each showcasing a crisp exterior and distinct layers. A small, artfully formed quenelle of shredded, tender confit chicken rests atop each pavé, its golden-brown hues contrasting with the pale potato. Adjacent to the chicken, a precise dot or delicate swirl of a pale yellow lemon-thyme emulsion adds a vibrant accent. Each bite is meticulously garnished with a few translucent, thinly sliced gherkin discs and a tiny, fresh sprig of bright green parsley or chervil, adding precise color and texture. The overall presentation is elegant and restrained, emphasizing the quality of ingredients and precise execution. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and texture. A precisely folded white linen napkin is positioned unobtrusively in the background on the marble surface.

ingredients.name: Duck fat or light olive oil

instructions: Pre-salt chicken thighs: Rub chicken thighs with 10g sea salt and peppercorns. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.

Prepare chicken confit: Preheat oven to 140°C. Rinse chicken thighs and pat dry. Place chicken, garlic, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf in an oven-safe pot. Cover completely with duck fat or olive oil. Cook in oven for 2.5 to 3 hours, until very tender and meat easily pulls from bone. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Cool and shred chicken: Remove chicken from fat. Discard skin and bones. Shred chicken meat into fine pieces. Reserve warm for assembly.

Prepare potato pavé: Preheat oven to 180°C. Peel potatoes and slice very thinly (1-2 mm) using a mandoline. In a bowl, toss potato slices with cream, melted butter, 5g salt, 2g white pepper, and 5g fresh thyme leaves. Arrange layers of potato tightly in a parchment-lined 15x15 cm baking dish. Bake for 60-70 minutes, until tender. Place a weighted flat surface on top of the pavé while still warm. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until firm.

Crisp potato pavé: Once chilled, remove pavé from dish. Cut into 8-12 uniform rectangular blocks (approx. 3x5 cm). Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat with a little olive oil. Sear pavé blocks on all sides until golden brown and crispy.

Make lemon-thyme emulsion: In a tall, narrow container, combine egg yolk, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, 2g salt, 1g white pepper, and 5g fresh thyme leaves. Using an immersion blender, slowly drizzle in the 150ml olive oil while blending continuously until a thick emulsion forms.
Prepare gherkins: Thinly slice gherkins into small discs or julienne.

Assemble and serve: On a large sharing platter, arrange the crispy potato pavé blocks. Top each pavé with a small quenelle of shredded confit chicken. Place a precise dot or swirl of lemon-thyme emulsion next to the chicken. Garnish each bite with a few thinly sliced gherkin discs and a tiny sprig of fresh parsley or chervil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Loin with Roasted Apples and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A professional food photograph of a single portion on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. The focal point is the pan-seared pork loin, presented as thick, golden-brown medallions, with a glistening caramelized crust. Alongside, roasted potato wedges, golden-edged and tender, are arranged with soft, caramelized apple chunks and sweet, charred onion slices. A rich, creamy pan sauce, made from pan drippings, vegetable stock, and cream, is lightly drizzled over the pork and vegetables. The color palette is warm: deep browns of pork, golden potatoes and apples, hints of green from fresh thyme sprigs. Textures are inviting: crisp exteriors, tender interiors. The plate has moderate negative space. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting textures.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into 2cm wedges.
Core and cut apples into 2cm chunks. Do not peel.
Slice onion into thick rings. Smash garlic cloves.
On a large baking sheet, toss potatoes, apples, onion, garlic, and 4 thyme sprigs with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned. Flip halfway.
Pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork loin on all sides until golden brown, about 3-4 minutes per side.
If pork loin is thick, transfer skillet to preheated oven. Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 70°C.
Remove pork from skillet. Let rest on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes. Internal temperature will rise to 75°C.
While pork rests, place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add butter.
Deglaze skillet with vegetable stock, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in cream. Simmer until slightly thickened, about 1-2 minutes. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Slice pork loin into thick medallions or serve as smaller chunks.
Plate roasted potatoes, apples, and onions. Place pork pieces beside.
Drizzle pan sauce over pork and vegetables. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Glazed Chicken Bonbons, Sweet Potato Cloud, Tomato-Chili Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A pristine large white bone china plate anchors the composition. Three to four glistening, perfectly golden-brown glazed chicken bonbons are artfully arranged, their surfaces reflecting light from the sweet-spicy glaze. Adjacent, a single, ethereal quenelle of pale orange sweet potato and ricotta cloud rests, its texture appearing incredibly light and airy. A vibrant crimson-orange pool or delicate brushstroke of the tomato-chili gastrique adds a bold color accent, its viscous sheen inviting. Elegant, amber-toned potato and carrot shards stand upright, providing a delicate architectural element and crisp contrast. A dusting of vibrant green basil powder or a few tiny basil microgreens offers a final aromatic and visual flourish. Abundant negative space surrounds the central composition, emphasizing the precision and minimalism of the plating. The entire arrangement is set on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin in a precise triangle to the side. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and texture, ensuring the dish is the singular focal point in an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: For the Chicken Bonbons: Trim chicken breast. Cut into 16-20 uniform bonbon shapes. Season with salt. Vacuum seal chicken pieces. Cook sous-vide at 65°C for 1 hour. Chill immediately in ice bath. Remove from bag. Pat dry. Sear bonbons in a hot pan with a touch of olive oil until golden. Glaze with a small amount of the prepared tomato-chili gastrique during searing. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.

For the Sweet Potato Cloud: Peel and dice sweet potatoes. Steam until very tender. Pass through a fine sieve or food mill. Whip sweet potato puree with ricotta cheese, a pinch of salt, and a dash of basil oil (from basil leaves blended with olive oil). Achieve a light, airy consistency. Keep warm.

For the Tomato-Chili Gastrique: Halve cherry tomatoes. Slice red chili thinly. Mince garlic. Combine tomatoes, chili, garlic, sugar, and vinegar in a small saucepan. Simmer gently over low heat for 20 minutes until tomatoes break down. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Reduce liquid over medium heat until syrupy. Whisk in butter off heat. Season with salt.

For the Potato & Carrot Shard: Peel and finely grate potato and carrot. Blanch briefly in boiling water. Drain and pat very dry. Puree into a smooth paste. Spread a very thin layer onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Bake at 150°C until completely dry and crisp, about 20-30 minutes. Break into irregular shards.
For Basil Dust: Blanch basil leaves briefly. Shock in ice water. Squeeze dry. Blend with a tiny pinch of salt until a fine powder forms. Alternatively, use fresh basil microgreens.

To Assemble: On a large white plate, place 3-4 glazed chicken bonbons. Create a delicate quenelle or a light smear of sweet potato cloud next to them. Drizzle or create a small pool of tomato-chili gastrique. Stand 1-2 potato and carrot shards elegantly. Finish with a dusting of basil powder or a few basil microgreens. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken bonbons are cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C.
The sweet potato cloud must be light and airy, avoid overmixing.
The tomato-chili gastrique should be balanced between sweet, sour, and spicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Peach & Rosemary Compote with Almond Oat Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the Fermented Peach & Rosemary Compote with Almond Oat Crumble is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in an earthy cream tone. The compote, a natural blend of soft, golden-orange fermented peach wedges and their slightly thickened, translucent liquid, is nestled at the bottom, showing subtle textural variations. Scattered generously on top is the golden-brown almond oat crumble, its irregular, crisp clusters providing a contrasting texture. A delicate, small sprig of fresh green rosemary is placed artfully on the crumble, adding a touch of vibrant color and an aromatic hint. The overall presentation is minimalistic, highlighting the pure ingredients and their natural forms. The bowl sits on a light, reclaimed wood table, accompanied by a natural beige linen napkin and soft, diffused natural light from the side, creating a serene, inviting atmosphere.
instructions: Wash peaches. Slice into 2 cm wedges. Do not peel.
Combine water, 20g sugar, and 10g salt in a clean jar. Stir until dissolved.
Add peach wedges and rosemary sprig to the jar. Ensure peaches are submerged. Use a fermentation weight if available.
Cover with an airlock lid or loose lid. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Check daily for activity. Skim any mold. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate when ready.
Drain fermented peaches. Reserve fermentation liquid.
Place peaches in a saucepan. Add lemon juice and 50 ml of the reserved fermentation liquid (or water if too tangy).
Simmer over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes. Stir occasionally. Peaches should soften but retain some shape. Mash lightly with a fork if desired for a thicker compote.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
In a bowl, combine oats, almond flour, 30g sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Cut cold butter into small cubes. Add butter to dry ingredients.
Use fingertips to rub butter into dry ingredients until coarse crumbs form.
Spread crumble mixture onto a baking sheet. Bake for 12-15 minutes. Crumble should be golden brown and crisp. Let cool completely.
Spoon warm compote into individual serving bowls. Top generously with cooled almond oat crumble. Garnish with a small fresh rosemary sprig or a thin slice of a fresh peach.
notes: The fermentation liquid can be used as a probiotic drink or in salad dressings.
Peach pits and skins from fresh peaches can be boiled to make a light stock for other uses, contributing to zero-waste.
Adjust sugar based on peach sweetness and desired tanginess from fermentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Ayam Balado
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Ayam Balado is presented on a rustic, round Indonesian ceramic plate, showcasing homely comfort. Golden-brown fried chicken pieces, such as drumsticks or thighs, are generously coated in a vibrant, glossy, deep red balado sauce. The sauce appears rich and slightly textured, with visible flecks of coarsely ground red chili, tomato, and shallot. The chicken pieces are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping. Next to the chicken, a modest, fluffy mound of white steamed rice is perfectly portioned. A few thin, crisp slices of fresh cucumber are casually placed beside the rice, offering a cooling contrast. The dish is set on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually draped, textured cloth napkin. Simple, everyday fork and spoon are placed alongside the plate. Warm, natural lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy family kitchen atmosphere. The background is minimal, focusing on the inviting, authentic meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed white rice.
Accompany with fresh cucumber slices to balance the chili heat.
Serve with kerupuk (Indonesian crackers) for added crunch.

ingredients.name: Bird's eye chilies (small, optional for heat)

instructions: Clean chicken pieces. Pat dry. Season chicken with 2g salt and 1g white pepper.
Heat cooking oil in a large wok or frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry chicken pieces until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Prepare balado paste: coarsely grind or blend red chilies, bird's eye chilies, shallots, garlic, and tomatoes until a rough paste forms.
Melt rendered beef fat in the same wok. Add lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the balado paste to the wok. Cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 10-15 minutes. Cook until the paste darkens, thickens, and the oil separates from the paste.
Season the paste with remaining 3g salt, 5g sugar, and 1g white pepper. Stir well.
Add the fried chicken pieces to the bal balado paste. Toss gently to coat all chicken pieces evenly.
Simmer for 5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Serve hot.
notes: Adjust the quantity of bird's eye chilies to control the spice level.
The beef fat adds a rich, savory depth to the balado sauce, which is traditional in some regional Indonesian cooking.
traditional_techniques: Bumbu Halus (Grinding spices into a fine paste)
Menumis Bumbu (Sautéing the spice paste until oil separates)

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Herb Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Herb Chicken is centrally plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown seared chicken thigh is the focal point. Around the chicken, a vibrant medley of roasted vegetables is artfully arranged. Tender, golden-brown roasted potato wedges and substantial chunks of sweet, caramelized carrots are interspersed with burst, softened cherry tomatoes. Scattered throughout are softened, aromatic smashed garlic cloves. A generous crumble of creamy white feta cheese melts slightly over the warm ingredients. Fresh green basil leaves and delicate oregano sprigs are thoughtfully placed for color and aroma. The dish exhibits a balance of rustic textures and bright colors. Moderate negative space surrounds the components. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard silverware, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Rustic bread
Simple green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a large bowl, combine quartered potatoes and carrot chunks.
Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray. Roast for 20 minutes.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt, pepper, and half of the fresh oregano.
In the same bowl, combine cherry tomatoes, smashed garlic, and sliced chili (if using). Drizzle with remaining 30ml olive oil. Toss gently.
After 20 minutes, remove tray from oven. Add seasoned chicken thighs and tomato mixture to the tray, arranging them among the roasted vegetables.
Return tray to oven. Roast for another 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Remove from oven. Crumble feta cheese over the hot dish.
Let rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with fresh basil and remaining fresh oregano.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Mushrooms and Basil
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Cacciatore is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Two whole, golden-brown boneless chicken thighs are nestled within a rich, reddish-brown tomato sauce. The sauce is studded with tender, quartered cremini mushrooms and vibrant diced red and green bell peppers. Minced garlic and diced onion are integrated into the sauce. The chicken appears succulent. The dish is garnished with fresh, torn green basil leaves and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese, adding contrasting colors. Moderate negative space surrounds the central dish. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table. A white linen napkin is beside the bowl. Standard silver flatware is arranged alongside. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Can be served alongside a simple pasta like tagliatelle or polenta.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, quartered mushrooms, dried oregano, and red pepper flakes. Cook for 3-4 minutes until mushrooms soften.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Remove lid. Simmer uncovered for another 5-10 minutes to slightly thicken the sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Stir in most of the fresh basil just before serving. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve hot, garnished with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Green Bean and Chicken Salad with Spicy Ginger Dressing
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl, placed on a rustic wooden dining table. Blanched green beans, vibrant green, form the base. Shredded chicken pieces, off-white, are casually mixed throughout, alongside delicate white flakes of crab meat. The dish is generously coated in a glossy, light brown spicy ginger dressing, showing flecks of red chili, minced garlic, and ginger. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, as if served from a family kitchen. Components touch and overlap, creating a hearty, comforting look. A few stray shallot slices and chili pieces from the dressing are visible. The table setting includes a simple, batik-patterned cloth napkin and basic ceramic plates. Lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy home environment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Accompanied by Kerupuk (Indonesian crackers).
Often part of a larger meal with multiple dishes.
instructions: Boil chicken breast in salted water until cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken, let cool slightly, then shred into small pieces.

Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add trimmed green beans, cut into 3 cm pieces. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender. Drain immediately and refresh in ice water. Drain well.

Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, combine finely sliced chilies, finely sliced shallots, minced garlic, grated ginger, lime juice, soy sauce, palm sugar, and vegetable oil. Whisk until sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt, sugar, or lime as needed.
In a large mixing bowl, combine blanched green beans, shredded chicken, and flaked crab meat.
Pour the dressing over the ingredients. Toss gently to coat everything evenly.
Serve immediately at room temperature or chilled.
notes: Adjust chili amount to preferred spice level.
For extra flavor, lightly toast the shredded chicken in a dry pan before adding to the salad.
This salad is best served fresh.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin, Mushroom Duxelles, Confit Cherry Tomatoes, Smoked Chili Jus
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a minimalist, architectural composition on a pristine, large white bone china plate. A perfectly seared, medium-rare beef tenderloin medallion, roughly 4cm thick, sits as the centerpiece, its rich brown crust contrasting with the succulent pink interior. Adjacent to the beef, a small, elegant quenelle of finely textured, dark brown mushroom duxelles rests. Nearby, three to four deeply red, glossy confit cherry tomatoes are artfully scattered, their slightly wrinkled skins indicating their slow roast, providing a burst of concentrated color and form. A rich, dark mahogany-colored smoked chili jus is meticulously spooned around the components, forming an organic pool that subtly reflects light. The jus has a smooth, velvety texture. The plate features abundant negative space, highlighting the precise placement of each element. A single delicate sprig of vibrant green microgreens is precisely placed atop the beef, offering a final touch of fresh color and height. The overall aesthetic is one of understated luxury and culinary precision, with natural compositions.
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C. Place cherry tomatoes in a small oven-safe dish. Pour 100ml olive oil over them. Season lightly with salt. Roast for 45-60 minutes until very tender and slightly shriveled. Set aside.

Finely dice mushrooms, shallots, and garlic. Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add shallots and garlic; sauté until softened, about 2 minutes. Add diced mushrooms. Cook, stirring frequently, until all moisture evaporates and mushrooms are deeply browned, about 10-15 minutes. Stir in fresh thyme leaves. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

In a saucepan, combine beef stock and red wine. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half until slightly thickened, about 15-20 minutes. Stir in smoked paprika hot sauce. Whisk in 25g cold butter until incorporated and sauce is glossy. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on all sides. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan (cast iron preferred) over high heat until shimmering. Carefully place beef medallions in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Add remaining 25g butter to the pan during the last minute of cooking, basting the beef.
Remove beef from pan and let rest on a cutting board for 5-7 minutes. This is crucial for juiciness.

Place a small, precise quenelle or neat mound of mushroom duxelles slightly off-center on each plate. Carefully arrange 3-4 confit cherry tomatoes near the duxelles. Place a rested beef medallion next to the duxelles and tomatoes. Spoon a generous pool of the smoked chili jus around the beef and components, ensuring some jus covers part of the beef. Garnish with a small, delicate sprig of microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sea Bass with Spicy Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. A pan-seared sea bass fillet, with crisp, golden-brown skin and flaky white flesh, sits prominently as a whole piece. A vibrant, glistening pan sauce, infused with minced garlic, red pepper flakes, and white wine, pools artfully beneath and around the sea bass. Over the fish, a bright green gremolata of finely chopped fresh parsley and finely grated lemon zest provides a burst of color and aromatic freshness. The palette features golden-brown fish, rich amber sauce, and vivid green and yellow gremolata. Textures include crispy skin, tender fish, and fresh herbs. The plate has appropriate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table, with a cotton napkin and traditional flatware beside the plate, under natural, even lighting, creating a modern bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple roasted asparagus or sautéed spinach.
A small portion of creamy risotto or soft polenta can accompany the dish.
Pair with a crisp dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Pat sea bass fillets dry. Season both sides with salt and black pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place sea bass skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip fillets. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 63°C (145°F). Remove sea bass from pan. Keep warm.
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the pan. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not burn garlic.
Pour in white wine. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in butter, lemon juice, and half of the chopped parsley. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Combine remaining chopped parsley with lemon zest for the gremolata.
To serve, spoon sauce onto plates. Place a sea bass fillet on top. Sprinkle generously with gremolata.

recipes.recipe_name: Szechuan Cavolo Nero & Tofu Stir-Fry
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Szechuan Cavolo Nero & Tofu Stir-Fry is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The dish is centrally mounded, showcasing a vibrant mix of deep green roughly chopped cavolo nero, bright orange julienned carrots, and golden-brown pan-fried tofu cubes. The ingredients are evenly coated in a glossy, reddish-brown Szechuan sauce. A sprinkle of thinly sliced green spring onions and a scattering of white toasted sesame seeds adorn the top. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A set of dark wooden chopsticks is placed neatly to the right of the plate, beside a small, white rice bowl. A folded white cotton napkin is positioned to the left. Natural, even lighting creates soft shadows. The background is a slightly blurred, warm-toned restaurant setting, suggesting a casual, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
instructions: Press tofu. Dice into 2cm cubes. Toss with cornstarch until coated.
Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add tofu cubes. Pan-fry until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Remove tofu from wok. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add julienned carrots. Stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add chopped cavolo nero. Stir-fry 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return crispy tofu to the wok.
Pour Szechuan sauce, soy sauce, and rice vinegar over ingredients. Toss to coat evenly.
Cook 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly and coats all ingredients.
Remove from heat. Drizzle with sesame oil.
Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice. Garnish with sliced spring onions and toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ajillo con Patatas Asadas
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Ajillo con Patatas Asadas is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. Two golden-brown, pan-seared chicken thighs, with visibly crispy skin, are placed prominently. Alongside them, a generous scattering of rustic, roasted potato wedges displays a rich, golden-brown hue and crisp edges, contrasting with their fluffy interiors. A glossy, garlic-infused pan sauce glistens over the chicken and potatoes. The dish is garnished with a vibrant sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the textures and rich colors. A white cotton napkin rests beside the plate, and the background is a soft, natural, evenly lit restaurant setting with a casual atmosphere, hinting at a bistro environment. A small, rustic ceramic bowl for extra sauce or a small basket of crusty bread might be subtly visible in the background, enhancing the Spanish authenticity without distracting from the main dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the garlic pan sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Pair with a dry Spanish white wine like Albariño or Verdejo.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into thick wedges. Place in a large bowl.
Add 30 ml olive oil, smoked paprika, rosemary sprigs, salt, and pepper to potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and golden brown, flipping halfway.
While potatoes roast, pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Do not move chicken during this time.
Flip chicken. Add sliced garlic to the skillet around the chicken. Sauté garlic for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Do not burn garlic.
Pour in white wine or chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover skillet and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C. Uncover for the last 5 minutes if a thicker sauce is desired.
Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest for 5 minutes. Discard rosemary sprigs from potatoes.
Plate chicken thighs alongside roasted potato wedges. Spoon pan sauce over chicken and potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and a lemon wedge. Serve immediately.
notes: Using bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs provides the most flavor and a crispy skin texture.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing chicken; sear in batches if necessary.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of golden-brown roasted chicken and potatoes rests on a rustic ceramic plate. Two crispy-skinned chicken thighs are positioned naturally. Thick-cut potato wedges, roasted to a deep golden hue with soft interiors, are scattered around the chicken. Bright red, blistered cherry tomato halves and softened, light brown roasted garlic cloves are interspersed among the potatoes, adding pops of color and texture. Fresh green rosemary and thyme leaves cling to the roasted ingredients. The arrangement is casual, as if scooped directly from a family pan, filling the plate without overcrowding. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Simple, everyday flatware and a casually folded cloth napkin are nearby. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the comforting, homely atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place chicken thighs, potato wedges, halved cherry tomatoes, and smashed garlic cloves in a large roasting pan.
Add rosemary sprigs and thyme sprigs to the pan.
Drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt and black pepper.
Toss all ingredients together to coat evenly.
Arrange in a single layer in the roasting pan.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Spicy Chili-Lime Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared salmon fillet, golden-brown and crispy-skinned, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The salmon is a whole piece, showcasing its flaky texture. Beside it, vibrant green broccoli florets, blanched then briefly sautéed, are neatly arranged with earthy brown, thinly sliced shiitake mushrooms. A glossy, deep amber chili-lime glaze is drizzled over the salmon and lightly pools around the vegetables. Fresh bright green cilantro leaves are scattered artfully, and a bright lime wedge sits at the plate's edge. The presentation is organized and balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin and chopsticks alongside. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting fresh colors and inviting textures. The background suggests a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed jasmine rice.
Chopsticks are traditionally used for eating this style of dish.
instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Prepare the chili-lime glaze: In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, soy sauce, honey, minced red chili, grated ginger, and sesame oil. Set aside.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Place salmon fillets skin-side down. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip salmon fillets. Cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until cooked through to your desired doneness. Remove salmon from pan and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to the same pan. Add minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced shiitake mushrooms to the pan. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until tender and lightly browned.
Meanwhile, bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Add blanched broccoli to the pan with mushrooms. Sauté for 1-2 minutes, tossing to combine with mushrooms and garlic.
Briefly re-whisk the chili-lime glaze. Pour half of the glaze over the salmon fillets.
Serve salmon immediately with sautéed broccoli and mushrooms. Drizzle remaining glaze over vegetables and plate. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and a lime wedge.
notes: Adjust chili quantity for desired spice level. For less heat, remove seeds from chili.
Ensure salmon skin is very dry before searing for maximum crispiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Sup Ayam Ikan Kuah Bening
recipes.visual_description: A comforting bowl of Indonesian clear chicken and fish soup is presented on a well-used wooden dining table. The ceramic bowl, with subtle imperfections, holds a generous single portion. The clear, amber broth, subtly colored by dark soy sauce, fills the bowl. Tender, shredded chicken pieces and thick chunks of white fish gently rest amidst soft, translucent bean thread noodles. Cubed firm tofu adds another texture. Vibrant green kaffir lime leaves are visible in the broth, alongside bright red sliced Thai chilies, adding pops of color. A simple garnish of fresh chopped coriander and crispy fried shallots is sprinkled on top. A traditional Indonesian soup spoon rests in the bowl. The scene is lit with warm, cozy light, typical of a homely family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed white rice.
Offer a small bowl of sambal (chili paste) for extra heat.
Enjoy with kerupuk (Indonesian crackers) on the side.
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté minced garlic, sliced shallots, and sliced ginger until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Add chicken pieces to the pot. Sear chicken until lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in chicken stock or water. Add bruised kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove chicken from pot. Shred chicken meat into bite-sized pieces. Set aside.
Add fish chunks and tofu cubes to the simmering broth. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until fish is flaky and cooked.
Add bean thread noodles to the pot. Cook for 2-3 minutes, until noodles are tender.
Return shredded chicken to the pot. Stir in dark soy sauce. Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped coriander, fried shallots, and sliced Thai chilies.
notes: For a richer broth, simmer chicken longer.
Adjust chili quantity for desired spiciness.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Tomato Jus and Potato Skin Crisps
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in natural cream, atop a light bamboo or reclaimed wood surface. Soft, natural light highlights a single, golden-skinned roasted chicken thigh placed prominently. Beside it, a neat mound of fluffy cooked rice. Roasted potato wedges, vibrant bell pepper chunks (red, yellow), and onion wedges are artfully arranged around, showcasing caramelized edges and natural colors. A glistening, amber-hued fermented tomato jus is sparingly drizzled over the chicken and vegetables. A few golden-brown, irregularly shaped potato skin crisps delicately crown the dish, adding textural contrast. The composition is clean, minimalist, with ample negative space. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige rests nearby. The background is uncluttered, hinting at natural elements.
instructions: Pre-preparation (Fermented Tomatoes): Wash tomatoes. Quarter them.
Prepare brine: Dissolve 20g unrefined sea salt in 1 litre water.
Place quartered tomatoes in a clean jar. Pour brine over, ensuring tomatoes are submerged.
Seal jar loosely or use an airlock. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess. Burp daily if not using airlock.
Strain fermented tomatoes. Reserve liquid (jus). Blend solids into a rough paste.
Day of Cooking: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Prepare Potatoes: Wash potatoes thoroughly. Peel potatoes, reserving all skins. Cut peeled potatoes into 2cm wedges.
Prepare Peppers & Onions: Core and deseed bell peppers. Cut into 2cm chunks. Peel onions. Cut into 2cm wedges.

Roast Vegetables & Chicken: On a large baking sheet, toss potato wedges, pepper chunks, and onion wedges with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Arrange chicken thighs among vegetables. Add thyme/rosemary sprigs if using. Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and vegetables are tender-crisp.

Make Potato Skin Crisps: Pat reserved potato skins very dry. Toss lightly with 15ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread in a single layer on a separate baking sheet. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until golden and crispy. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Cook Rice: Rinse rice. Cook rice according to package instructions. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Prepare Fermented Tomato Jus: Gently warm the reserved fermented tomato liquid (jus) in a small saucepan. Reduce slightly to concentrate flavor. Stir in some blended fermented tomato solids if a thicker consistency is desired.

Plate: Place a scoop of cooked rice on one side of a handcrafted ceramic plate. Arrange roasted chicken thigh next to it. Artfully place roasted potato wedges, pepper chunks, and onion wedges around the chicken. Drizzle with the warm fermented tomato jus. Garnish with a few potato skin crisps.
notes: This recipe maximizes flavor and minimizes waste by utilizing potato skins and leveraging fermentation for a complex, tangy sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken, Cherry Gastrique, Onion Puree, Cheddar-Pasta Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, its skin golden and crispy, anchors the pristine large round bone china plate, resting on a premium grey veined Carrara marble surface. A graceful, elongated smear of smooth, light brown caramelized onion puree forms its base. Vibrant, glossy cherry gastrique is artfully drizzled in organic lines over the chicken and puree, its deep red contrasting beautifully. Two to three irregular, golden cheddar-pasta crisps are arranged thoughtfully, some standing for height. A delicate sprig of fresh thyme provides a final verdant touch. The minimalist plating emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the refined textures and sophisticated colors. Dramatic lighting and a precisely folded white linen napkin complete the luxurious, uncluttered setting.

ingredients.name: fresh or frozen tart cherries, pitted
Small sprigs of fresh thyme or microgreens

instructions: Prepare Onion Puree: In a heavy-bottomed pot, melt 25g butter over medium-low heat. Add sliced yellow onions and shallots. Cook slowly for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and very soft. Deglaze with 50ml chicken stock, scraping up any browned bits. Transfer to a blender, add remaining 25g butter and remaining 50ml chicken stock. Blend until perfectly smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Keep warm.

Prepare Cherry Gastrique: In a small saucepan, combine pitted cherries, red wine vinegar, and sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Cook for 10-15 minutes, until cherries soften and liquid reduces to a syrupy consistency. Add 50ml chicken stock and simmer for another 5 minutes. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing on solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Return liquid to pan and reduce gently until it coats the back of a spoon. Keep warm.

Prepare Cheddar-Pasta Crisp: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Lay lasagna pasta sheets flat on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Bake for 8-10 minutes, until dry and slightly crisp. Remove from oven. Evenly sprinkle grated cheddar over the pasta sheets. Return to oven and bake for another 5-7 minutes, or until cheddar is melted and bubbly, and the pasta is golden and fully crisp. Let cool completely, then gently break or cut into irregular, elegant shards.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry thoroughly with paper towels. Season generously on all sides with sea salt and black pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in an oven-safe, heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place chicken breasts skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes until the skin is deeply golden-brown and crispy. Flip chicken breasts. Transfer skillet to the preheated 180°C (350°F) oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) at the thickest part. Remove from oven and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes before plating.

Plate Dish: On a large, round expensive bone china plate, create a graceful, elongated smear of the warm caramelized onion puree. Place one whole, perfectly seared chicken breast slightly off-center on the puree. Artfully drizzle the vibrant cherry gastrique around and over a portion of the chicken and puree. Arrange two to three irregular, golden cheddar-pasta crisps elegantly near the chicken, some standing upright for height, others flat for texture contrast. Garnish with a small, delicate sprig of fresh thyme or a few microgreens for a touch of color and freshness. Ensure ample negative space on the plate for a minimalist, sophisticated presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Comté and Caramelized Onion Quiche
recipes.visual_description: A generous, triangular wedge of golden-brown Comté and Caramelized Onion Quiche is centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The quiche features a flaky, golden crust and a rich, creamy yellow custard filling. Visible within the custard are soft, deep amber caramelized onion slices and distinct flecks of melted Comté cheese. The top surface of the quiche is lightly browned and slightly puffed. A scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh chives is sprinkled over the quiche wedge. A small, artfully arranged side salad of crisp, dark green mixed greens (e.g., frisée or baby spinach) with a light vinaigrette is positioned neatly beside the quiche. The plate rests on a simple, rustic light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware (fork and knife) are placed beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature.
Traditionally served with a simple green salad.
instructions: Prepare pastry: Combine flour and salt. Cut in cold butter until crumbly. Add water slowly. Mix until dough forms. Knead briefly. Wrap and chill 30 minutes.
Roll out dough on floured surface. Line a 24 cm tart tin. Trim edges. Prick base with fork. Chill 15 minutes.
Blind bake crust: Preheat oven to 190°C. Line crust with parchment paper. Fill with baking beans. Bake 15 minutes. Remove beans and paper. Bake 5-7 minutes more until light golden. Cool.
Caramelize onions: Heat olive oil in large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 30-40 minutes. Onions should be deeply golden brown and soft.
Prepare filling: In large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, cream, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Stir in grated Comté cheese and caramelized onions.
Assemble and bake: Pour filling into cooled, blind-baked crust.
