Bake at 180°C for 35-45 minutes. Center should be just set. Top should be golden. Knife inserted near center should come out clean.
Cool quiche for 10-15 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Lemon and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown roasted chicken, a bone-in, skin-on thigh, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Surrounding the chicken are quartered roasted baby potatoes, their skins lightly crisped and interiors tender. Halved vibrant red cherry tomatoes and whole, glossy Kalamata olives are interspersed among the potatoes, adding bursts of color and texture. Fresh sprigs of oregano and thyme are artfully placed over and around the chicken, providing a verdant contrast. A few thin lemon wedges are nestled on the side, ready for squeezing. The dish exhibits a natural, rustic elegance, with ingredients scattered organically rather than rigidly arranged. The colors are warm and inviting, showcasing the chicken's crispy skin and the rich hues of the vegetables. The plate has appropriate negative space, presented on a simple wooden surface with natural, soft lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Halve or quarter baby potatoes, depending on size. Halve cherry tomatoes. Slice one lemon into thin wedges. Juice the second lemon.
In a large roasting pan, combine potatoes, halved tomatoes, Kalamata olives, minced garlic, oregano sprigs, and thyme sprigs.
Add chicken thighs to the pan. Drizzle all ingredients with olive oil. Toss gently to coat everything.
Pour chicken broth and lemon juice into the pan.
Arrange lemon wedges among the ingredients.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Potatoes should be tender.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beef and Mushroom Risotto is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto features a fluid, creamy consistency that flows naturally across the plate. It is not molded or dry. Deeply seared 3cm chunks of beef and quartered golden-brown cremini mushrooms are distributed throughout the glossy, pale rice. The dish is finished with a sprinkle of finely minced fresh parsley. The bowl rests on a dark wood table in a modern bistro setting. A clean white cotton napkin and a polished silver spoon sit beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures of the tender meat and earthy mushrooms. The arrangement is professional, organic, and clean with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a shallow bowl (piatto piano) to allow the risotto to spread.
Provide extra grated Parmesan on the side.
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti.
instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pan. Set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until golden brown. Remove and set aside.
Lower heat to medium. Melt half the butter.
Add onion and garlic. Sauté until translucent.
Add rice. Toast for 2 minutes while stirring.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid evaporates.
Add one ladle of warm stock. Stir constantly until absorbed.
Repeat stock process until rice is al dente.
Fold in the seared beef and mushrooms.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining butter and parmesan.
Adjust consistency with a splash of stock if needed. Risotto must be fluid.
Garnish with parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Do not rinse the rice; the starch is essential for creaminess.
Ensure the stock is warm to maintain a consistent cooking temperature.
The beef should remain in whole chunks to preserve its juices.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Italian Sausage and Mushroom Risotto with Crispy Pasta and Garlic Breadcrumbs
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous individual portion of creamy Italian Sausage and Mushroom Risotto is presented in a shallow, matte white ceramic bowl, placed slightly off-center on a simple light wooden table. The risotto is fluid ("all'onda"), not stiff, showcasing the natural creamy texture of properly cooked Arborio rice. Visible within the golden-hued risotto are irregular chunks of browned Italian sausage, varying shades of earthy sautéed sliced mushrooms, and bursts of vibrant red from softened halved cherry tomatoes. A light scattering of freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly coats the surface. Sprinkled artfully over the risotto are golden, irregular shards of crispy fried pasta, providing a textural contrast. Alongside, a small mound of golden-brown garlic breadcrumbs adds another layer of crunch and visual interest. A sprinkling of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh counterpoint to the rich colors. The background is a soft, out-of-focus modern bistro setting with a neutral wall and subtle hint of a dark chair. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. A simple, folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware (fork and spoon) are neatly arranged beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up any remaining sauce.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a light Italian white wine like Pinot Grigio or a dry Rosé.
instructions: Prepare Breadcrumbs: In a small pan, heat 15ml olive oil. Add breadcrumbs and 1 minced garlic clove. Toast until golden and crispy. Set aside.

Prepare Crispy Pasta: Cook small pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. In a separate small pan, heat 15ml olive oil. Fry the cooked pasta until golden and crispy. Set aside.

Brown Sausage: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, heat 15ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Add Italian sausage, breaking it up. Cook until browned and no pink remains. Remove sausage with a slotted spoon; set aside.

Sauté Aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to the pot. Add diced onion and remaining 3 minced garlic cloves. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add Mushrooms and Tomatoes: Add sliced mushrooms and halved cherry tomatoes to the pot. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown, and tomatoes soften, about 7-10 minutes.
Toast Rice: Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains are translucent.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Cook Risotto: Begin adding warm broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring frequently. Wait until each ladleful is almost completely absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente.
Finish Risotto: Stir in the cooked sausage and grated Parmesan cheese. Remove from heat. Let rest for 2 minutes. The risotto should be fluid and creamy.
Serve: Ladle risotto into shallow bowls. Garnish with crispy pasta, garlic breadcrumbs, and fresh parsley. Serve immediately with extra Parmesan.
notes: The key to good risotto is patience and consistent stirring, adding broth gradually.
Adjust the amount of broth to achieve desired creamy, flowing consistency.
Ensure all ingredients are prepped before starting the risotto cooking process.

recipes.recipe_name: Perkedel Udang, Ikan & Ayam
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Perkedel Udang, Ikan & Ayam is arranged on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Two golden-brown, flat, round fritters are casually stacked, showcasing their crispy, irregular edges. Finely chopped shrimp, fish, and chicken mixture is visible, hinting at a tender interior. A vibrant red dollop of homemade Sambal sits beside the fritters. Fresh green cilantro leaves are loosely scattered. The plate rests on a well-used dark wooden dining table, bathed in warm, natural light. A traditional Indonesian-style spoon and fork are casually placed. The background suggests a homely, lived-in family kitchen, with a simple patterned cloth napkin, creating an inviting, comforting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with Sambal
fresh cucumber slices
lime wedges

ingredients.name: white fish fillet (e.g., cod, snapper), skinless, boneless

instructions: Finely chop shrimp and fish. Combine with ground chicken in a bowl.
Add minced garlic, minced chili, sliced spring onion, egg, flour, salt, and white pepper.
Mix well until combined. Do not overmix.
Form mixture into small, flat patties, about 5 cm diameter and 1.5 cm thick.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or wok to 175°C (350°F). Ensure oil is hot enough.
Carefully place patties into hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Internal temperature of chicken must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove fritters with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot.
notes: Adjust chili quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Roasted Pepper Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual Chicken and Roasted Pepper Pie is presented in a classic white ceramic ramekin, centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-brown puff pastry crust is visibly puffed and flaky, with a rich, inviting sheen from an egg wash. A small vent in the center allows steam to escape. The ramekin is filled to the brim, showcasing the hearty pie. Visible through the golden-brown crust and around the edges are hints of the robust filling: generous chunks of seared chicken, approximately 2-3cm, mixed with vibrant red and yellow roasted bell pepper squares, 2cm, all suspended in a thick, creamy, herb-flecked gravy. The colors are warm and inviting. A crisp, folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface with natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a relaxed restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed green vegetables, such as broccoli florets or green beans.
Often accompanied by creamy mashed potatoes or thick-cut chips (fries).
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut bell peppers into 2cm squares. Roast peppers on a baking tray for 15 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.
Cut chicken thighs into 2-3cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks in batches until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan. Dice onion and finely mince garlic. Add onion to the pan and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, creating a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken stock, ensuring no lumps. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.

Stir in double cream and thyme leaves. Return seared chicken and roasted bell peppers to the pan. Simmer for 5 minutes, ensuring chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Stir in fresh parsley. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Let filling cool slightly.
Divide filling among four individual pie dishes or ramekins (approx. 15cm diameter).

Roll out puff pastry. Cut four circles slightly larger than the pie dishes. Place pastry circles over each dish, pressing edges to seal. Trim excess pastry. Create a small slit in the center of each pastry top to vent steam.
Whisk egg with a splash of water for an egg wash. Brush egg wash over the pastry tops.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown and puffed. Serve hot.
notes: Ensure the pie filling cools slightly before topping with pastry to prevent a soggy bottom.

recipes.recipe_name: Banana and Bacon Bread Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely portion of golden-brown banana bread pudding rests on a simple, round ceramic plate. The pudding's surface is rustic and slightly uneven, revealing soft, caramelized banana slices and tender bread cubes. Scattered over the top are small, dark, crispy pieces of crumbled bacon, offering a contrasting texture and color. The sides of the pudding show a custardy interior. The plate sits on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden kitchen table. A plain, sturdy fork is placed casually beside the dish. The lighting is soft and inviting, typical of a cozy home kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Serve with a drizzle of caramel sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x20cm baking dish with butter.
Cook bacon in a frying pan over medium heat until very crispy. Drain on paper towels. Crumble into small pieces.
Peel and slice bananas into 1 cm thick rounds.
Cut stale bread into 2-3 cm cubes.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla extract, and cinnamon until well combined.
Add bread cubes and sliced bananas to the egg mixture. Gently fold to coat. Add most of the crumbled bacon, reserving some for garnish.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish. Press bread down gently to ensure it soaks up the liquid.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until the pudding is set, golden brown, and a knife inserted into the center comes out mostly clean.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly.
Serve warm. Garnish each portion with reserved crispy bacon.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Turkey and Ricotta Macaroni
recipes.visual_description: A hearty portion of Baked Turkey and Ricotta Macaroni is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish has a golden-brown, bubbly top from the melted and slightly crisped mozzarella cheese. Below the cheese, plump macaroni pasta is coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato sauce. Visible throughout the sauce are tender, pale chunks of diced turkey fillet, approximately 2cm cubes, interspersed with creamy white dollops of ricotta cheese, creating pockets of soft texture. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley sits on top, adding a pop of color. The overall appearance is warm and inviting, showcasing natural, comforting colors and textures. The scene is lit by warm, cozy kitchen light, with a casually placed cloth napkin nearby. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced turkey fillet to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until browned on all sides and cooked through. Ensure turkey reaches 75°C (167°F).
Stir in crushed tomatoes and dried oregano. Season with salt and black pepper. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
In a large bowl, combine cooked macaroni, turkey and tomato sauce, and ricotta cheese. Mix gently until well combined.
Pour the mixture into a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Sprinkle shredded mozzarella cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and golden brown and the mixture is bubbly.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Turkey Fillet with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Turkey Fillet with Creamy Mushroom Sauce is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. A golden-brown seared turkey fillet, kept whole, rests slightly off-center. Rich, creamy mushroom sauce, studded with browned mushroom slices and finely diced onion, generously covers and pools around the turkey, showing its smooth, fluid consistency. A sprinkle of vibrant chopped fresh parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of green against the earthy tones of the turkey and sauce. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed cloth napkin and standard flatware. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the homely scene, capturing the comforting textures and natural colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with mashed potatoes or roasted root vegetables.
Accompanied by a simple green salad.
instructions: Pat turkey fillets dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear turkey fillets 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove turkey from skillet. Set aside on a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over mushrooms and onions. Stir well. Cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer. Cook, stirring, for 2-3 minutes until sauce begins to thicken.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for another 2 minutes. Season sauce with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Return cooked turkey fillets to the skillet. Spoon creamy mushroom sauce over turkey.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Potato Braise
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Potato Braise is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Two or three golden-brown, tender braised chicken thighs, whole pieces, are nestled among large, rustic 3-4 cm potato chunks. The rich, reddish-brown sauce, clinging to the chicken and potatoes, features visible specks of smoked paprika, softened diced red bell pepper, and onion. Dark, pitted Manzanilla olives are scattered throughout the dish, providing a contrasting color and briny accent. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley covers the top, adding a fresh, aromatic finish. The dish has a comforting, natural arrangement with moderate negative space. It is placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a small side plate holding a few slices of crusty artisan bread for dipping. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Pair with a dry Spanish red wine, such as Tempranillo or Garnacha.

ingredients.name: Waxy potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold, Red Bliss)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides, about 4-5 minutes per side. Do not overcrowd the pot. Work in batches if necessary. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Add the bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and braise for 25 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken braises, peel potatoes and cut into 3-4 cm rustic chunks.
Add potato chunks to the pot. Stir gently to submerge. Continue to braise, covered, for another 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Stir in pitted olives. Cook for 2-3 minutes more to heat through.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Roasted Vegetables and Tomato-Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed with thoughtful negative space. A mound of fluffy, golden-brown brown rice is positioned slightly to one side. Adjacent to the rice, a perfectly seared, thick beef medallion with a rich, dark crust and a hint of pink interior takes prominence. Surrounding the beef and rice is a vibrant array of roasted vegetables: deep purple eggplant cubes, bright orange carrot diagonal slices, verdant green beans, tender broccoli florets, golden corn kernels, rustic red onion wedges, and colorful bell pepper squares, all showing slight caramelization. Scattered among the vegetables are dark, glossy Kalamata olive halves. A rustic, bright red tomato-basil sauce, with visible pieces of burst cherry tomatoes and flecks of green basil, is artfully spooned over the beef and drizzled onto a portion of the vegetables. The entire composition is garnished with a scattering of fresh, vibrant green basil leaves. The knife work on all vegetables is precise and clean, showcasing their natural forms. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a subtly blurred, inviting restaurant background.
instructions: Rinse brown rice. Combine rice with 500ml vegetable broth or water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 35-40 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Keep warm.

Preheat oven to 200°C. In a large bowl, combine eggplant cut into 2cm cubes, carrot cut into 1cm thick diagonal slices, trimmed green beans, red onion cut into 2cm wedges, bell pepper cut into 2cm squares, potato cut into 2cm cubes, broccoli cut into small florets, and corn kernels. Add 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized, stirring halfway. Add halved olives for the last 5 minutes of roasting.

While vegetables roast, in a small saucepan, heat 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Add cherry tomatoes. Cook for 8-10 minutes, mashing tomatoes gently, until they break down into a rustic sauce. Stir in half of the chopped fresh basil. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add beef. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness.
Transfer seared beef to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil and let rest for 5-7 minutes.
If desired, add red wine to the hot skillet, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer for 1 minute, then pour over resting beef or add to sauce.

Place a scoop of brown rice on each plate. Arrange roasted vegetables attractively beside the rice. Place a seared beef medallion next to the vegetables. Spoon fresh tomato-basil sauce over and around the beef and some vegetables. Garnish with remaining fresh basil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Nashville Hot Chicken and Potato Skewers
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Nashville Hot Chicken and Potato Skewers is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two skewers are artfully arranged, showcasing golden-brown, charred chicken cubes and tender, slightly crispy potato wedges. The chicken and potatoes are coated with a glossy, vibrant red-orange Nashville hot sauce, creating a rich, inviting color. Cubed chicken pieces are visibly succulent, contrasting with the soft, slightly blistered potato exteriors. A small pile of bright green, finely chopped chives is sprinkled over the skewers. Beside the skewers, a few crisp, green dill pickle slices provide a fresh, contrasting element. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a neatly folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, set against a blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crisp dill pickle slices to balance the heat.
instructions: Place halved baby potatoes in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil.
Cook for 8-10 minutes until fork-tender but still firm. Drain well.
In a small saucepan, melt butter over medium-low heat. Stir in cayenne pepper, brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and 5g salt. Whisk until smooth. Keep warm.
Cut chicken breast into 3cm cubes.
Thread alternating chicken cubes and potato halves onto skewers. Aim for 2-3 skewers per person.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. Brush skewers lightly with vegetable oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Grill skewers for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally. Cook until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are charred and tender.
Brush grilled skewers generously with the warm Nashville hot sauce.
Finely chop fresh chives. Garnish skewers with chives.
Serve immediately with dill pickle slices on the side.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Tartelette de Ricotta, Vanille et Croustillant de Pain Fermenté
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant Tartelette de Ricotta, Vanille et Croustillant de Pain Fermenté is centered on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The tartlet features a perfectly golden, crisp pâte sablée crust, its edges slightly fluted. The interior holds a creamy, off-white ricotta filling, baked to a smooth, delicate set. A generous sprinkle of golden-brown, irregular fermented baguette crumbs cascades over a portion of the tartlet, adding a rustic texture and subtle sheen. Adjacent to the tartlet, a small cluster of vibrant, plump red raspberries or blueberries rests, their natural colors contrasting gently with the neutral tones of the dish. A delicate, translucent, and irregularly shaped Gruyère tuile, thin and golden-amber, stands upright or leans gracefully against the tartlet, offering a surprising, architectural element. The overall presentation is minimalistic and clean, emphasizing natural textures and colors. The plate sits on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood surface. ingredients.name: Stale baguette, cut into small cubes

instructions: Combine flour, powdered sugar, and salt in a bowl. Cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add egg yolk and cold water. Mix until dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

In a small bowl, combine baguette cubes, sourdough discard (if using), and water. Mix well to coat. Cover loosely and let sit at room temperature for 4-6 hours, or overnight in the fridge, allowing slight fermentation.

Preheat oven to 160°C. Spread fermented baguette cubes on a baking sheet. Bake for 15-20 minutes until dried and lightly golden. Remove, toss with melted butter and granulated sugar. Return to oven for 5-7 minutes until caramelized and crisp. Let cool completely. Crush lightly into coarse crumbs.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll out chilled dough to 3mm thickness. Cut out four 10cm rounds. Press into four individual tartlet molds. Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper, fill with pie weights. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake for another 5-7 minutes until lightly golden. Let cool.
In a bowl, whisk drained ricotta, egg, natural sweetener, vanilla schnapps (or extract), and lemon zest (if using) until smooth.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Create four small, thin circles (approx. 5cm diameter) of grated Gruyère, spaced apart. Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and bubbly. Let cool completely on the parchment paper; they will crisp up.
Reduce oven temperature to 160°C. Pour ricotta filling into blind-baked tartlet shells. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until filling is set but still slightly wobbly in the center.

Let tartlets cool completely in molds. Carefully remove. Top each tartlet with a sprinkle of the fermented baguette crumb. Arrange a few seasonal berries or a small dollop of compote next to the tartlet. Gently place one Gruyère tuile upright or leaning against the tartlet.
notes: Using stale baguette is a key zero-waste practice for this recipe.
The slight fermentation of the baguette enhances its flavor complexity.
Draining the ricotta thoroughly is crucial for a firm, creamy filling.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme with Potato Pavé and Asparagus Purée
recipes.visual_description: A single, expertly plated Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme rests on a premium bone china plate. The chicken, a golden-brown whole piece with perfectly crisped skin, is positioned off-center. Adjacent to it, a precisely cut, golden-edged rectangular Potato Pavé showcases its layered texture and crisp exterior. A vibrant green, silky smooth dot of asparagus purée provides a precise pop of color. A glossy, deep amber chicken jus is artfully drizzled, forming an elegant pool. The composition features abundant negative space, highlighting each element's refined execution. The plate sits on a pristine white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing textures and colors against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Jus: Roast chicken bones/wings in an oven at 200°C until deeply golden. Sauté chopped shallot and garlic in a pot until softened. Add roasted bones, cover with 1 litre cold water. Add 2 thyme sprigs. Simmer gently for 2 hours, skimming impurities. Strain the liquid, then reduce over medium heat until a glossy, viscous jus forms. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Potato Pavé: Peel potatoes. Slice thinly (1-2mm) using a mandoline. Layer potato slices tightly in a small, parchment-lined loaf tin (approx. 10x6 cm), brushing each layer with melted butter (20g) and seasoning lightly with salt and pepper. Press firmly after each layer. Cover with parchment. Bake at 160°C for 75 minutes, or until tender. Remove from oven, place a weight on top, and cool completely. Once cool, trim edges. Cut into two precise rectangular blocks (e.g., 4x6 cm).

Prepare Asparagus Purée: Trim woody ends from asparagus. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well. Blend asparagus with 10g butter and a tablespoon of warm water or chicken stock until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Cook Chicken Supreme: Pat chicken supremes thoroughly dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Add 20g butter and remaining thyme sprig to the pan. Baste chicken with butter. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken on a wire rack for 5-7 minutes.
Cook Potato Pavé: While chicken rests, heat a separate pan with 20g butter. Place potato pavé blocks in the pan. Pan-fry over medium heat until golden brown and crispy on all sides.

Assemble and Serve: Place a crisp potato pavé on one side of a warm bone china plate. Position the rested, whole chicken supreme elegantly beside it, skin-side up. Create a small, vibrant dot or a delicate swipe of asparagus purée on the plate. Drizzle the rich chicken jus artfully around the chicken and pavé. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Suprême Rôti, Pomme Purée, Jus aux Herbes
recipes.visual_description: A Michelin-starred French dish presented on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle rim. A smooth, glossy quenelle of silken pomme purée is artfully placed slightly off-center. Next to it, a perfectly roasted chicken suprême, with its golden-brown, crispy skin glistening, rests as a whole piece, showcasing its perfectly cooked interior. The color palette is refined, featuring the creamy white of the potato, the deep golden-brown of the chicken, and the dark amber of the jus, with a delicate scattering of vibrant green finely chopped chives providing a singular pop of contrasting color. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the dish's minimalist elegance. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the textures and contours of the food.

Pair with a light red Burgundy or full-bodied white wine
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken suprêmes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken suprêmes skin-side down until deep golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes.
Flip chicken. Add thyme, rosemary, and crushed garlic to the pan.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C, about 12-15 minutes.
Remove chicken from oven. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 10 minutes.
While chicken roasts, prepare potato purée. Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform 2cm chunks.
Place potato chunks in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil.
Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain thoroughly.
Pass hot potatoes through a fine-mesh sieve or a potato ricer into a clean saucepan.
Heat cream and butter in a separate small saucepan until butter melts and cream is hot. Do not boil.
Gradually whisk hot cream and butter into the riced potatoes until completely smooth and silken. Season with salt. Keep warm.
For the jus, pour off excess fat from the chicken searing pan, leaving pan drippings.
Add chicken stock to the pan. Bring to a simmer, scraping up browned bits.
Reduce stock by half until slightly thickened and flavorful, about 8-10 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.
To plate, spoon a generous quenelle or swirl of pomme purée onto the center of each plate.
Present chicken suprêmes as whole pieces or sliced once lengthwise. Place next to the purée.
Spoon chicken jus around the chicken and purée.
Garnish with finely chopped chives.
notes: Ensure potatoes are very dry before ricing for the silkiest purée
Do not overcook the chicken; use a thermometer for precision

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Ballotine with Pomme Purée, Asparagus, and Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant serving is presented on a large, round white bone china plate, maximizing negative space. Three thick, round medallions of golden-brown seared chicken ballotine are positioned slightly overlapping or side-by-side, showcasing the moist interior with a delicate herb-flecked farce. Adjacent to the chicken, a smooth, glistening quenelle of creamy white pomme purée sits precisely. A rich, deep amber chicken jus is artfully pooled beside the chicken, catching the light. Three vibrant green asparagus tips are arranged gracefully next to the chicken, providing a pop of color and verticality. The plate rests on a premium grey veined marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and polished silver cutlery (knife and fork) are positioned to the side. Dramatic professional lighting creates subtle shadows, emphasizing the textures and forms against an ultra-minimalist background, highlighting the dish as the sole focus.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Ballotine: Butterfly each chicken breast. Pound gently to uniform thickness (approx. 0.5 cm).

For the farce: Finely mince 50g of chicken trim. Mix with 1 tablespoon heavy cream, minced shallot, 1 teaspoon chives, salt, and pepper. Spread thin layer of farce over each pounded chicken breast. Roll tightly into a cylinder. Secure with kitchen twine.

Cook Ballotine: Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear ballotines until golden brown on all sides. Transfer pan to preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest 5 minutes before slicing.

Make Pomme Purée: Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes. Place in cold salted water. Bring to boil, cook until tender (15-20 minutes). Drain well. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a warm bowl.
Heat butter and heavy cream in a small saucepan until butter melts. Gradually whisk hot butter-cream mixture into riced potatoes. Season with salt and pepper. Whisk until silky smooth.

Prepare Chicken Jus: In same pan used for chicken, deglaze with a splash of water, scraping up browned bits. Add chicken stock, minced garlic, and thyme sprig. Bring to simmer. Reduce by half until slightly thickened and glossy. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Season to taste.
Blanch Asparagus: Bring small pot of salted water to boil. Add asparagus spears. Cook 2-3 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender. Immediately transfer to ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

Plate Dish: Slice each chicken ballotine into 3 thick, round medallions. Arrange 3 medallions on each plate. Place a quenelle or swirl of pomme purée beside the chicken. Spoon chicken jus around the components. Arrange 3 blanched asparagus tips elegantly on each plate. Garnish with remaining chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Pomme Purée and Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim holds a single, perfectly seared chicken breast, its golden-brown skin glistening. Beside it, a gracefully shaped quenelle of silky, pale yellow pomme purée. A rich, dark brown chicken jus is artfully drizzled in an organic arc around the chicken and purée, creating a sense of movement. Dramatic, focused lighting creates soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's contours. The background is minimal, a blurred, soft grey to maintain focus on the food.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Jus: Slice shallot and garlic. Sauté shallot and garlic in a tiny bit of olive oil in a small saucepan. Add chicken stock and thyme. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half until thickened. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

Prepare Pomme Purée: Peel potatoes. Cut into even 2cm chunks. Place in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender (approx. 15-20 minutes). Drain well. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a warm bowl. Heat milk and butter in a small saucepan until butter melts. Gradually whisk warm milk-butter mixture into riced potatoes until smooth and silky. Season with salt.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (fan-assisted) for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes.

Plate Dish: Spoon a generous quenelle of pomme purée onto each plate, slightly off-center. Slice chicken breast in half lengthwise. Place chicken beside the purée. Drizzle chicken jus around the plate. Garnish with finely chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Pomme Purée, Asparagus, Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A refined, minimalist presentation on a pristine, oversized white bone china plate. ingredients.name: Full-fat milk or heavy cream, warmed

instructions: Prepare Chicken Jus: Pour chicken stock into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce by half, or until syrupy and coats the back of a spoon. Skim any impurities. Keep warm.

Prepare Pomme Purée: Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform 2cm pieces. Place potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain thoroughly. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Add cold butter cubes, whisk vigorously until melted and incorporated. Gradually whisk in warm milk or cream until very smooth and silky. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Asparagus: Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch asparagus for 1-2 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

Prepare Chive Oil: Blanch chives in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain and squeeze dry. Blend chives with olive oil in a high-speed blender until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for a clear oil. Discard solids.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts very dry with paper towels. Season skin and flesh generously with salt and pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add a thin layer of olive oil. Place chicken breasts skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crisp. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Plate Dish: Spoon a generous quenelle or swirl of pomme purée onto the center of each large, warm plate. Slice each chicken breast diagonally into 2-3 thick pieces. Arrange chicken artfully beside the purée. Lean 3-4 blanched asparagus spears against the chicken or purée. Drizzle chicken jus around the plate. Dot the plate with small drops of chive oil. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken is thoroughly patted dry for maximum skin crispness.
Achieve a truly silky purée by using a ricer and whisking vigorously with cold butter and warm milk.
The chicken jus can be made in advance and gently reheated.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thigh, Confit Potato Terrine, Tarragon Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, its skin a rich, golden-brown and impeccably crisp, rests centrally on a pristine, matte white ceramic plate. Adjacent to it, a precisely cut rectangular block of confit potato terrine stands, its edges seared to a delicate golden crust, revealing the finely layered potato within. Three vibrant green asparagus spears are arranged with intentional asymmetry, adding a burst of fresh color and architectural height. A glossy, amber-hued tarragon chicken jus is artfully pooled around the main components, its organic form contrasting with the precise cuts of the food. The plate features abundant negative space, emphasizing the minimalist composition. The setting is a white Carrara marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin and polished silver flatware subtly placed to the side. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sophisticated elegance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Peel potatoes. Slice thinly, 1.5mm thick, using a mandoline. Layer potato slices in a small, oven-safe terrine mold or loaf pan (approx. 15x8 cm), alternating with duck fat, thyme, smashed garlic, 3g salt, and 1g pepper. Press layers firmly. Cover mold tightly with foil. Bake 1.5 hours, or until potatoes are very tender. Remove from oven. Place a weighted object on top of the foil to press potatoes. Chill completely for at least 4 hours, or overnight.

Heat 2ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add diced shallot; cook 2 minutes until translucent. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently until stock reduces by half and thickens slightly (approx. 10-15 minutes). Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids. Keep warm over low heat. Just before serving, whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, until emulsified and glossy. Stir in chopped tarragon. Season with salt.

Pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. Season both sides with 2g salt and 1g pepper. Heat 5ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to the preheated 160°C oven. Cook 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from oven. Rest 5 minutes on a cutting board.
Bring a small pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add asparagus spears. Blanch 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp and bright green. Drain immediately.

Remove chilled potato terrine from mold. Cut into two precise rectangular portions (approx. 4x6 cm each). Heat a non-stick pan with a little duck fat or olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear potato terrine portions 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crispy. Place one seared chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange one seared potato terrine rectangle next to the chicken. Place three blanched asparagus spears artfully on the plate. Spoon the warm tarragon jus around the chicken and potato, creating an organic pool. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Silky Pomme Purée and Truffle Jus
recipes.visual_description: A masterfully plated dish on a pristine white bone china plate, centered with abundant negative space. A perfectly seared chicken breast, sliced into two thick pieces, golden-brown and glistening, rests beside a pristine, silky quenelle of pomme purée. The chicken skin is visibly crisp, while the interior appears juicy. A rich, dark truffle jus is artfully spooned around the main components, forming a natural, flowing pool. The purée is a smooth, light ivory. A few precisely snipped chives, vibrant green, are delicately scattered over the purée and chicken, adding a singular touch of color. ingredients.name: Black Truffle (freshly grated or truffle oil)

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with sea salt and white pepper.

Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden and crisp. Flip chicken. Reduce heat to medium. Cook for another 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest on a wire rack for 5 minutes.
Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform 2 cm pieces. Place in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes.

Drain potatoes thoroughly. Pass through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a warm pot. Heat milk and 100g butter in a separate saucepan until butter is melted and hot. Gradually whisk hot milk mixture into riced potatoes until smooth and silky. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.

In a small saucepan, gently heat chicken stock. Reduce by half until slightly thickened. Stir in remaining 20g butter until emulsified. Grate truffle into the jus or add truffle oil. Season to taste. Keep warm.

Slice rested chicken breast into two thick, clean pieces. Plate a generous quenelle or swirl of pomme purée in the center of a warm plate. Place chicken next to purée. Spoon truffle jus elegantly around the chicken and purée. Garnish with finely snipped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Truffled Pomme Purée, Asparagus, Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely plated dish set on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. A large, elegant bone china plate, subtly patterned, holds the main elements. A generous, organically shaped quenelle of ultra-smooth, pale ivory truffled pomme purée rests slightly off-center. instructions: Prepare Chicken Jus: In a small saucepan, combine chicken stock, diced shallot, smashed garlic, and thyme. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and gently simmer for 20-25 minutes, until liquid reduces by half and flavors intensify. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pan. Keep warm.

Prepare Pomme Purée: Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform 3cm chunks. Place in a large pot, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender (15-20 minutes). Drain thoroughly. Pass hot potatoes through a potato ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a warm bowl. In a separate saucepan, heat milk and 100g butter until butter melts. Gradually whisk hot milk-butter mixture into riced potatoes until smooth and creamy. Season with salt. Stir in shaved truffle or truffle oil if using. Keep warm.

Prepare Asparagus: Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking and preserve color. Drain well. Pat dry.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts very dry with paper towels. Season skin side generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Do not move chicken during this time. Flip chicken breasts. Add remaining 50g butter and a sprig of thyme to the pan. Baste chicken with melted butter. Transfer pan to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Finish Asparagus: In a small pan, heat remaining 15ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Quickly sear blanched asparagus spears for 1-2 minutes until slightly charred and heated through. Season with salt.

Plate Dish: Place a generous quenelle or dollop of truffled pomme purée slightly off-center on each warm plate, creating a flowing, organic shape. Place a whole pan-seared chicken breast beside the purée. Artistically arrange 5-6 seared asparagus spears next to the chicken. Spoon a generous amount of warm chicken jus around the chicken and purée. Garnish with a few delicate microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Breast, Pomme Puree, Asparagus, Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, impeccably plated portion of seared chicken breast, featuring a deeply golden, crispy skin. The chicken is positioned artfully off-center on a large, round bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim. Beside it, a generous, flowing swirl of silken, pristine white pomme puree creates an organic form. Six vibrant green asparagus spears, blanched and lightly seared, are precisely arranged. instructions: Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper.
Vacuum seal each chicken breast individually.
Cook chicken breasts in a sous vide bath at 70°C for 1.5 hours.
While chicken cooks, prepare pomme puree. Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform chunks.
Place potatoes in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil.
Cook potatoes until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Pass hot potatoes through a ricer or a fine-mesh tamis into a warm bowl.
Gradually whip cold butter cubes into the riced potatoes until fully incorporated and smooth.
Slowly add warmed heavy cream, whisking until the puree is incredibly silky and light.
Season pomme puree with salt to taste. Keep warm.
Prepare asparagus. Bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Prepare an ice bath.
Blanch asparagus spears in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp.
Immediately transfer asparagus to the ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Prepare chicken jus. Pour chicken stock or demi-glace into a small saucepan.
Simmer over medium-low heat. Reduce until it coats the back of a spoon. Keep warm.
Finish chicken. Remove chicken breasts from sous vide bags. Pat very dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place chicken breasts skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear undisturbed for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken breasts. Sear for 1-2 minutes to finish cooking. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Quickly sear blanched asparagus in the same pan for 1 minute until slightly caramelized.
To plate, spoon a generous, flowing swirl of pomme puree onto one side of a large white plate.
Place one whole seared chicken breast next to the puree.
Arrange 6 asparagus spears artfully beside the chicken.
Spoon a pool of rich chicken jus onto the plate, near the chicken.
Garnish with a single fresh chervil sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Chicken Breast with Truffled Potato Foam and Asparagus Tips
recipes.visual_description: A single perfectly seared sous vide chicken breast, precisely cut into two thick medallions, rests off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. Adjacent to the chicken, a delicate, airy quenelle of truffled potato foam, glistening with subtle sheen, creates a soft counterpoint. Three vibrant green asparagus tips, blanched to crisp-tender perfection, are artfully placed near the foam, their natural lines adding visual flow. A rich, dark chicken jus, reduced to a glossy sheen, is meticulously drizzled as an accent, enhancing depth. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space highlighting the precise execution and premium quality of each element. Colors are harmonious: golden-brown chicken, creamy white foam, emerald asparagus, and deep amber jus. The dish is presented on a polished white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a folded white linen napkin and subtle, dramatic lighting creating soft shadows.
instructions: Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Vacuum seal each breast.
Preheat a water bath to 63°C. Cook sealed chicken breasts for 90 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C for safety during searing.
Peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or potato ricer into a saucepan for ultimate smoothness.
Add 30g butter and heavy cream to the potatoes. Whisk vigorously until smooth and creamy. Stir in truffle oil. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Trim asparagus. Use only the top 5cm tips. Blanch asparagus tips in boiling salted water for 1 minute until vibrant green and crisp-tender. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Pour chicken stock into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer and reduce over medium heat until it coats the back of a spoon, about 10-15 minutes. This is your jus. Keep warm.
Remove chicken from sous vide bags. Pat breasts completely dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add remaining 20g butter.
Sear chicken breasts, presentation side down, for 2-3 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear briefly on the other side, about 1 minute.
To plate, place one chicken breast off-center on each plate. Cut each breast into two thick medallions.
Adjacent to the chicken, create a delicate quenelle of truffled potato foam. Alternatively, use an iSi siphon for foam.
Artfully arrange 3-4 blanched asparagus tips near the potato foam.
Meticulously drizzle the reduced chicken jus around the chicken and potato foam. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Chicken Breast, Potato Pavé, Asparagus, Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated serving of seared chicken breast, potato pavé, asparagus, and chicken jus. The seared chicken breast, golden-brown and crisp-skinned, rests perfectly cooked. Beside it, a precisely cut rectangular portion of potato pavé stands, exhibiting crisp, golden-brown edges and visible thin layers within. Four to five vibrant green asparagus spears are artfully arranged, some with subtle char marks, adding a pop of color and linear elegance. A rich, glossy chicken jus forms a deliberate pool on the plate, reflecting light. The plating is minimalist, featuring significant negative space on an expensive bone china plate with a subtle, refined pattern. The setting is a premium light grey veined marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits beside the plate. Lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows to enhance texture and depth. The overall presentation is one of sophisticated simplicity and culinary precision.
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Vacuum-seal chicken breasts. Cook sous-vide at 63°C for 1.5 hours. Remove from bag, pat very dry. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, 5-7 minutes. Flip, cook 1-2 minutes. Remove from pan, rest 5 minutes.

Peel potatoes. Slice very thinly, mandoline recommended. Melt 30g butter. Brush a small rectangular baking dish (approx. 15x10cm) with butter. Layer potato slices tightly, seasoning each layer lightly with salt and pepper. Pour melted butter evenly over layers. Press firmly to compact. Bake at 180°C for 60-75 minutes, until tender. Place a weight on top (e.g., another tray with cans). Chill overnight. Once chilled, cut into 4 precise rectangular portions (e.g., 4x6cm). To reheat: Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan. Sear pavé portions on all sides until golden and crisp. Finish in oven if needed.

Trim woody ends from asparagus. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Pat dry. Just before serving, heat 10ml olive oil in a pan. Quickly sear asparagus for 1-2 minutes to warm through and add slight char. Season with salt.

Finely chop shallot and garlic. Heat 10ml olive oil in a small saucepan. Sauté shallot and garlic until softened. Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half or until slightly thickened. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Whisk in 20g cold butter. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Place a potato pavé portion slightly off-center on each plate. Rest a seared chicken breast beside the pavé. Arrange 4-5 asparagus spears artfully beside the chicken and pavé. Spoon a generous pool of chicken jus next to the chicken or as a base. Garnish with microgreens or chervil if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Ballotine, Truffled Pomme Purée, Asparagus Beurre Noisette
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisitely plated portion on a large, round, pristine white bone china plate set on a polished white Carrara marble surface. A substantial piece of golden-brown, perfectly seared chicken ballotine, cut on a slight bias to reveal its tender interior, is positioned off-center. Adjacent to it, a graceful, organic swoosh of silken, ivory-colored truffled pomme purée flows elegantly. Three vibrant green asparagus spears, precisely aligned and artfully arranged, slightly overlap and are glistening with a delicate drizzle of brown butter, nestled alongside the purée. A few delicate sprigs of fresh chervil provide a precise, verdant accent. Abundant negative space surrounds the meticulously placed elements, emphasizing their intentionality and the dish's sophisticated simplicity. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the varied textures and rich colors. Polished silver flatware and a crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, complete the ultra-minimalist, luxurious setting.

ingredients.name: Black truffle paste or finely minced fresh truffle

instructions: Prepare chicken ballotines: Carefully debone chicken thighs, leaving skin intact. Pound flat to even thickness (approx. 1 cm). Season inside with salt, pepper, and a pinch of truffle paste. Roll tightly into a cylindrical shape. Secure with butcher's twine.

Cook ballotines: Preheat a water bath to 68°C. Place ballotines in vacuum-seal bags with a small knob of butter, a thyme sprig, and smashed garlic. Vacuum seal. Cook in water bath for 2 hours. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C after searing.

Prepare truffled pomme purée: Peel potatoes. Cut into uniform chunks. Place in a pot of cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender. Drain well. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine mesh sieve into a warm bowl. Heat 100g butter and heavy cream in a small saucepan until melted and hot. Gradually whisk hot butter-cream mixture into potatoes until smooth and silky. Stir in truffle paste and truffle oil (if using). Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Prepare asparagus: Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

Sear ballotines: Remove ballotines from bags. Pat dry thoroughly. Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Sear ballotines on all sides until golden brown and crispy. This should take 3-4 minutes per side. Rest for 5 minutes.
Make beurre noisette: In a small saucepan, melt remaining 50g butter over medium heat. Cook until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty. Do not burn. Remove from heat immediately.

Plate the dish: Cut each ballotine on a slight bias into one substantial piece. Place one ballotine piece off-center on a large, pristine white plate. Create a graceful, organic swoosh of truffled pomme purée next to the ballotine. Arrange 3-4 asparagus spears elegantly alongside the purée. Drizzle asparagus with beurre noisette. Garnish with microgreens or chervil.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Suprême with Truffled Potato Puree and Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of pan-seared chicken suprême rests on a pristine white bone china plate. The chicken boasts a perfectly golden-brown, crisp skin and tender, moist flesh. Beside it, a velvety, creamy truffled potato puree forms an elegant, organic swoop. Four vibrant green, blanched asparagus spears are precisely arranged, adding a crisp textural contrast. A glossy, deep amber chicken jus pools artfully around the chicken, enhancing its richness. The composition is minimalist with abundant negative space, showcasing the precision and quality of each element. The setting is a premium grey veined marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin and dramatic professional lighting, creating soft shadows that highlight the dish's sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken suprêmes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Do not move.
Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
For the potato puree: Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Pass through a ricer or mash well. Add butter, heavy cream, and truffle oil. Season with salt and pepper. Whisk until silky smooth.
For the asparagus: Blanch asparagus spears in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
For the chicken jus: Pour off excess fat from the skillet, leaving 1 tablespoon. Add diced shallot and minced garlic. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Deglaze pan with a splash of chicken stock, scraping up browned bits. Add remaining chicken stock and thyme sprig. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce jus by half, until slightly thickened. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate: Spoon a graceful swoop of truffled potato puree onto a pristine bone china plate. Place one seared chicken suprême atop the puree. Arrange 4-5 blanched asparagus spears artfully beside the chicken. Spoon a generous drizzle of rich chicken jus around the chicken and puree. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Chicken Breast, Confit Potato, Asparagus Puree, Crispy Skin, Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single seared chicken breast, its golden-crisp skin glistening, rests centrally on a pristine, large white bone china plate. Beside it, three perfectly round, golden-brown confit potato slices are artfully stacked or subtly overlapped. A vibrant, deep green asparagus puree forms a smooth, elegant swipe or a precise dollop on the plate's edge, contrasting with the ample white space. A rich, dark amber chicken jus is delicately drizzled around the main components, forming an inviting pool or an intentional line. The plating is minimalist, emphasizing precision and the natural beauty of each component. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its perfectly cooked interior and crispy exterior. The scene is set on a super-premium white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates subtle, soft shadows, highlighting the dish's architectural precision and sophisticated simplicity. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle, sits to the side.
instructions: Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Place each chicken breast in a separate vacuum-sealable bag with a small knob of butter. Vacuum seal bags.
Preheat a water bath to 63°C. Cook chicken breasts in the water bath for 1.5 hours.

Peel potatoes. Using a mandoline, cut into uniform 1cm thick rounds. Arrange potato rounds in a single layer in a small oven-safe dish. Add garlic cloves and thyme sprigs. Pour olive oil over potatoes until just covered.
Preheat oven to 150°C. Cook potatoes for 60-75 minutes, or until fork-tender but still holding their shape. Remove from oil and drain on paper towels. Season with flaky sea salt.
Trim woody ends from asparagus. Blanch asparagus in salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Blend blanched asparagus with 2 tablespoons of chicken stock and a small knob of butter until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with salt. Keep warm.
In a saucepan, reduce chicken stock over medium-high heat until it thickens to a syrupy consistency. Skim any foam. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Remove chicken from sous vide bath. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of olive oil. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and very crispy. Flip and sear flesh-side down for 1 minute.

Place a spoonful of asparagus puree artistically on one side of a large white plate. Arrange 3-4 confit potato rounds next to the puree. Place one seared chicken breast centrally on the plate. Drizzle chicken jus around the chicken and potatoes. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken with Crispy Potatoes and Blistered Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown pan-seared chicken thighs, cooked to perfection, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Surrounding the chicken are artfully arranged, quartered crispy roasted potatoes, their skins a deep golden-brown, offering a satisfying contrast in texture. Alongside, vibrant green blistered asparagus spears are neatly placed, adding a fresh pop of color. A bright lemon wedge and a sprig of fresh parsley garnish the dish, enhancing its visual appeal. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin, and polished stainless steel cutlery. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting textures. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced composition with appropriate negative space, reflecting a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp green salad.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and quarter the new potatoes. In a large bowl, toss potatoes with 30ml olive oil, chopped rosemary, thyme leaves, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown. Flip halfway through.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.

Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down if applicable, for 6-8 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for another 5-7 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Transfer skillet to oven for final cooking if needed.
While chicken cooks, trim woody ends from asparagus. In a bowl, toss asparagus with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Add asparagus to the skillet with chicken during the last 5-7 minutes of cooking, or roast separately on a small baking sheet until tender-crisp and slightly blistered.
Remove chicken from skillet. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over chicken.
Plate chicken, potatoes, and asparagus. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and an extra lemon wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Lemon-Herb Potatoes and Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Lemon-Herb Potatoes and Asparagus is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crisp-skinned chicken thigh, cooked whole, anchors the plate. Roasted potato wedges, their skins slightly crisped, are arranged alongside. Bright green, tender-crisp asparagus spears are neatly placed. The dish is subtly garnished with fresh, finely chopped green parsley for color and freshness. A roasted lemon half adds visual appeal. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting textures and rich colors, against a blurred, casual bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up pan juices.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Wash and halve or quarter small new potatoes. Place in a large roasting pan.
Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Set aside.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Mince garlic cloves. Roughly chop fresh oregano and thyme. Zest one lemon. Halve the other lemon.
In a small bowl, combine 45ml olive oil, minced garlic, chopped oregano, chopped thyme, and lemon zest. Mix well.
Toss potatoes with half of the herb-garlic-lemon oil mixture in the roasting pan. Spread in a single layer.
Arrange chicken thighs among the potatoes in the roasting pan. Drizzle remaining herb-garlic-lemon oil mixture over chicken.
Roast for 25 minutes. Flip chicken and potatoes. Add lemon halves to the pan. Continue roasting for another 15 minutes.
Add asparagus spears to the roasting pan. Drizzle asparagus with remaining 15ml olive oil. Squeeze juice from roasted lemon halves over chicken and vegetables. If pan seems dry, add chicken broth.
Continue roasting for 10-15 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and asparagus is tender-crisp. Potatoes should be golden and tender.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish dish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Adjust roasting time based on chicken thigh size and oven calibration.
For extra crispy potatoes, ensure they are in a single layer and not overcrowded.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Rosemary Potatoes and Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast is the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, cooked to a golden-brown crust, is presented whole or in two thick, juicy chunks, revealing a tender white interior. Alongside, a generous portion of roasted potato wedges, their skins golden and slightly crisp, with fluffy interiors, are artfully arranged. Bright green asparagus spears, tender-crisp from sautéing, are neatly placed beside the chicken and potatoes. The dish is subtly garnished with a small sprig of fresh rosemary and a vibrant lemon wedge, adding a touch of freshness. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting, set on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or small red potatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Cut into 2 cm wedges or cubes. Place in a large bowl.
Mince garlic. Chop fresh rosemary leaves. Add garlic and rosemary to potatoes. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and golden brown.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Carefully place chicken breasts in the hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

While chicken rests, trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Add asparagus to the same skillet (or a clean pan) over medium heat. Sauté for 3-5 minutes until tender-crisp. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
To serve, slice chicken into thick medallions or keep whole. Arrange chicken, roasted potatoes, and sautéed asparagus on individual plates.
Garnish with a fresh rosemary sprig and a lemon wedge if desired.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully cooked to 75°C for food safety.
Adjust roasting time for potatoes based on size and desired crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Kimchi Bokkeumbap with Quick-Pickled Onion
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of 'Sustainable Kimchi Bokkeumbap' is presented in a handcrafted, matte ceramic bowl in an earthy beige tone. The bowl rests on a light, natural wood table surface. A mound of golden-brown kimchi fried rice forms the base, with visible bits of red kimchi and translucent diced onion. A perfectly cooked fried egg, with a slightly runny yolk, is placed centrally on the rice. Around the rice, three distinct, small piles are arranged: vibrant green blanched spinach, thinly sliced, translucent quick-pickled red onion, and a sprinkle of bright green chopped scallions over the egg and rice. The arrangement is organic and minimalist, highlighting each component's natural color and texture. Ample negative space surrounds the dish. Accompanying the bowl are a pair of simple metal chopsticks and a traditional Korean metal spoon. A small, undyed linen napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a natural, well-lit setting with a hint of a green plant in the distance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small side dish of danmuji (yellow pickled radish).
Offer a simple clear anchovy or vegetable broth on the side.
Eat using traditional metal chopsticks and a spoon.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.quantity: 1 large (half diced for cooking, half thinly sliced for pickling)

ingredients.name: Seasonal greens (e.g., spinach or bok choy)

instructions: Prepare quick-pickled onion: Combine water, rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small pot. Bring to a boil. Pour over thinly sliced onion in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate.
Cook eggs: Fry or soft-boil 4 eggs to desired doneness. Set aside.
Blanch seasonal greens: Briefly blanch spinach or bok choy in boiling water. Drain. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Heat a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add 5ml sesame oil. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add kimchi: Add chopped kimchi to the pan. Sauté 3-4 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add rice: Add day-old rice to the pan. Break up clumps. Stir-fry 5 minutes until rice is heated through and slightly crispy.
Season: Add soy sauce, remaining sesame oil, and gochujang (if using). Stir well to combine. Cook 2 more minutes.
Assemble: Divide rice among 4 bowls. Top each with a cooked egg, a portion of blanched greens, and some quick-pickled onion. Garnish with chopped green onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Supreme, Potato Mille-Feuille, Asparagus, Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Roasted Chicken Supreme is artfully presented on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim. The golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken supreme, with its first wing bone intact, is positioned as the focal point, slightly off-center. Adjacent to it, a perfectly formed, golden-layered Potato Mille-Feuille block stands tall, showcasing its delicate, compressed layers. Three vibrant green, blanched asparagus spears are meticulously arranged beside the potato, adding a pop of color. A rich, glossy, dark brown chicken jus is artfully pooled on the plate, reflecting light and adding depth. The composition is minimalist, featuring abundant negative space. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. Silver flatware rests beside the plate, and a crisp white linen napkin is precisely folded into a triangle.
