Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and elegance. The background is ultra-minimalist and out of focus.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).

For the Potato Mille-Feuille: Peel potatoes. Slice thinly using a mandoline, 1-2mm thick. Melt 50g butter. Lightly grease a small baking dish (approx. 10x15cm). Layer potato slices, brushing each layer with melted butter and seasoning with salt and pepper. Press layers firmly. Bake for 45-60 minutes, or until tender. Remove from oven. Place a weight on top. Chill completely. Once cold, trim edges. Cut into two equal rectangular blocks.

For the Chicken Supreme: Pat chicken supremes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp. Flip chicken. Add remaining 25g butter, garlic clove, and thyme sprigs to skillet. Baste chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

For the Chicken Jus: While chicken roasts, finely dice shallot. In a small saucepan, add 25g butter. Sauté shallot until translucent. Add chicken stock and reserved thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half, until slightly thickened. Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Keep warm.

For the Asparagus: Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch asparagus spears for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Just before plating, gently warm asparagus in a touch of butter.

To Plate: Place one potato mille-feuille block off-center on a warm plate. Arrange a few blanched asparagus spears neatly beside the potato. Place one rested chicken supreme adjacent to the potato. Spoon a generous pool of chicken jus beside the chicken. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Roasted Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh with golden-brown, crispy skin sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Around it, roasted potato wedges display tender interiors and slightly caramelized edges. Vibrant red halved cherry tomatoes are nestled alongside softened, golden-brown apple wedges. Roughly chopped roasted onion pieces are interspersed throughout. A light glistening of pan juices coats the elements. Fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs are scattered for garnish. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad.
Offer crusty bread to soak up pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

In a large roasting pan or oven-safe skillet, toss potato wedges, onion, and minced garlic with 30 ml olive oil, half the rosemary, and half the thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Spread in an even layer.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes.
Place seared chicken thighs skin-side up on top of the vegetables in the roasting pan.
Toss apple wedges and halved cherry tomatoes with the remaining rosemary and thyme. Add to the roasting pan around the chicken and potatoes.
Pour chicken broth into the roasting pan.
Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for safety.
Adjust roasting time based on chicken thigh size and oven calibration.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Croquette, Caramelized Onion Puree, Toasted Brioche
recipes.visual_description: Twelve meticulously crafted canapés are presented with architectural precision on a large, polished white Carrara marble slab. Each miniature canapé features a cylindrical, golden-brown chicken and potato croquette, about 3cm long, exhibiting a perfectly crispy exterior and creamy interior. It rests atop a thin, precisely cut 4cm square of toasted brioche, which provides a delicate, pale golden base. A small, dark amber, glossy dollop of caramelized onion puree is subtly piped between the croquette and brioche. Each piece is crowned with a single, vibrant green, finely cut chive baton, offering a precise pop of color. Abundant negative space surrounds the canapés, emphasizing their individual elegance. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures and refined color palette of golden, amber, white, and green. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a sharp triangle, anchors the corner of the ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Cool. Finely mince the cooked chicken.

Peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Boil until very tender. Drain thoroughly. Mash potatoes until completely smooth. Combine mashed potato with minced chicken and grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Form the chicken and potato mixture into 12 small, precise cylinders, approximately 3cm long and 1.5cm in diameter. Chill for 30 minutes to firm.
Prepare breading station: Place flour, beaten egg, and panko breadcrumbs in separate shallow dishes. Dredge each chilled croquette in flour, then egg, then panko, ensuring full coverage.
Thinly slice brioche bread. Cut into 4cm square crisps. Toast in a dry pan or oven until golden and crisp.

Thinly slice the yellow onion. In a small saucepan, melt butter and olive oil over low heat. Add sliced onion. Cook very slowly, stirring occasionally, for 45-60 minutes until deeply caramelized and very tender. Add chicken stock and simmer until absorbed. Blend the caramelized onion into a smooth, glossy puree. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat neutral frying oil in a deep pot to 170°C (340°F). Fry croquettes in batches for 2-3 minutes, until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

To assemble: Place one toasted brioche crisp on a platter. Pipe a small dot of caramelized onion puree onto the crisp. Gently place one fried chicken and potato croquette on top of the puree. Garnish each canapé with a tiny chive baton.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Brown Butter Potato Foam, Crispy Skin, Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and tender, rests elegantly on a pristine white bone china plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, precisely cut into thick medallions, showcasing its perfectly cooked interior. Beside it, a delicate, airy quenelle of light tan brown butter potato foam adds a contrasting texture and sophisticated visual. A few shards of dark, crispy chicken skin lean artfully against the chicken, providing a textural counterpoint. A rich, glossy pool of concentrated chicken jus is artfully drizzled around the base of the chicken, reflecting the ambient light. A scattering of vibrant green finely chopped chives provides a fresh, precise pop of color. The composition is minimalist with abundant negative space, highlighting each element's perfection. The plate is set on a premium grey-veined Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a crisp triangle, sits to the side. Dramatic, focused professional lighting creates soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision and luxurious appeal.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Carefully remove skin from breasts. Set skin aside.
Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper.

Place chicken skin between two sheets of parchment paper. Place a heavy pan on top. Bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes until crisp and golden. Remove, blot excess fat, and season lightly. Break into large shards.
Peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Place in a pot with cold salted water. Bring to a boil and cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
While potatoes cook, prepare the jus. Mince shallot and garlic. In a small saucepan, melt 15g butter. Add shallot and garlic. Cook until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add chicken stock to the saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half until slightly thickened. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.
Drain cooked potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot pot over low heat for 1 minute to dry. Pass potatoes through a ricer or mash thoroughly until smooth.
In a separate small saucepan, melt remaining 85g butter. Cook over medium heat until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty (brown butter). Strain out any solids.
Heat milk and cream in a small saucepan until just simmering.

Add brown butter, hot milk, and cream to the mashed potatoes. Whisk vigorously until light and fluffy. Season with salt and pepper. For true foam, transfer to a siphon and charge with N2O. If no siphon, continue whisking until light.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts skin-side down (where skin was) for 4-5 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken breasts. Transfer skillet to a preheated 180°C oven. Roast for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before plating.

To plate, place a quenelle or elegant dollop of potato foam off-center on each plate. Slice chicken breasts into thick medallions. Arrange chicken next to foam. Drizzle chicken jus around the chicken. Garnish with crispy chicken skin shards and finely chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Pork & Pickled Strawberry Rice Bites
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic platter of Slow-Cooked Pork & Pickled Strawberry Rice Bites. Eight to twelve perfectly formed, compressed short-grain rice rounds, approximately 4 cm in diameter, are arranged with clean, consistent spacing on a light-colored, natural stone platter. Each rice round is topped with a small, artfully mounded pile of rich, shredded slow-cooked pork, exhibiting a tender, moist texture and warm brown hue. Resting delicately atop the pork is a vibrant, ruby-red half of a quickly pickled strawberry, its glossy surface catching the light and offering a striking contrast. A sprinkle of finely chopped bright green chives adds a fresh, verdant accent. The platter sits on a light bamboo table surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural textures and colors of the ingredients against a clean, minimalist background with subtle green foliage.
instructions: Pat pork shoulder dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork on all sides until deeply browned.

Add 200 ml water to the pot. Cover. Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F). Cook for 3-4 hours, or until pork is fork-tender and easily shredded. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove pork from pot. Shred meat using two forks. Reserve cooking liquid.
Cook short-grain rice according to package instructions until tender and slightly sticky. Let cool slightly.
While pork cooks, prepare pickled strawberries. Combine rice vinegar, sugar, and 50 ml water in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar dissolves. Let cool.
Wash and hull strawberries. Cut each strawberry in half or into thick slices, depending on size.
Place strawberry pieces in a clean jar. Pour cooled pickling liquid over strawberries. Seal jar. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
To assemble, form cooled rice into small, compressed rounds or squares, about 4 cm in diameter. Aim for 8-12 pieces.
Place a small mound of shredded pork on top of each rice piece. Lightly moisten pork with a spoonful of reserved cooking liquid.
Place one pickled strawberry half or slice on top of the shredded pork.
Finely chop fresh chives. Garnish each canapé with a sprinkle of chives before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Roasted Chicken Breast with Potato Fondant and Saffron Velouté
recipes.visual_description: A single, pan-roasted chicken breast, skin rendered golden and crisp, rests elegantly beside a perfectly cylindrical potato fondant. The chicken, with its rich brown skin, contrasts subtly with the creamy, light golden interior of the potato fondant, which displays a delicate, moist texture. A vibrant, saffron-infused velouté forms a flowing, organic pool around the main elements, its pale yellow hue hinting at the aromatic spice. The sauce's consistency is fluid, gently caressing the base of the chicken and potato. A sparse, precise scattering of bright green, finely chopped chives provides a singular, fresh color accent. The composition is minimalist and architectural, with abundant negative space on a pristine white bone china plate, allowing each element to command attention. The dish is presented on a luxurious grey-veined marble surface, illuminated by dramatic, professional lighting that casts subtle shadows, enhancing depth and sophistication. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware is arranged thoughtfully, completing the elegant fine-dining presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into thick cylinders (approx. 5cm diameter, 4cm height).
Heat 30g butter and 10ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear potato cylinders on both flat sides until golden brown.
Add 100ml chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and smashed garlic cloves to the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pan. Transfer to the preheated oven. Cook 20-25 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 5ml olive oil in a separate oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down. Sear 6-8 minutes until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Transfer pan with chicken to the 180°C oven. Roast 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest chicken 5 minutes after cooking.
For the Saffron Velouté, melt 50g butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add diced shallot. Sauté until softened, 2-3 minutes.
Stir in flour. Cook, stirring, 1 minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in remaining 150ml chicken stock until smooth. Bring to a simmer.
Add saffron threads. Simmer 5-7 minutes, whisking occasionally, until sauce thickens.
Season velouté with salt and pepper. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for smoothness.
To plate, place one potato fondant in the center of a large plate.
Carefully place the whole, rested chicken breast beside the potato.
Spoon a generous pool of saffron velouté around the chicken and potato.
Garnish with a few finely chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Roulade, Pomme Purée, Jus de Volaille Clarifié
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a study in refined simplicity on a pristine white bone china plate. A single, elegant quenelle of silken, pale yellow pommes purée anchors the composition. Beside it, two perfectly seared, golden-brown chicken roulade medallions, revealing a delicate, truffle-flecked interior, are arranged organically. A glossy, deep amber pool of clarified jus de volaille gently embraces the components, its rich sheen contrasting with the matte textures. A sparse scattering of vibrant green snipped chives provides a precise pop of color. The generous negative space on the plate emphasizes the architectural precision and understated luxury of each element. The setting features a superpremium wooden table, a folded white linen napkin, and professional, soft lighting creating subtle shadows.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).

Prepare Jus: Combine chicken stock, thyme, garlic in a small saucepan. Simmer gently. Reduce by half until flavorful. Strain. Cool slightly. Whisk in egg white. Bring to a simmer without stirring. Skim solids. Strain through fine mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Keep warm.

Prepare Pomme Purée: Dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Place in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Pass potatoes through a ricer or fine mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Add cold butter cubes, one at a time, whisking vigorously until fully incorporated and smooth. Gradually whisk in hot cream until purée is silky. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Chicken Roulade Farce: Melt 15g butter in a small pan over medium heat. Add shallot. Sauté until translucent, about 2 minutes. Add diced mushrooms. Cook until softened and liquid evaporates, about 5 minutes. Stir in minced truffle and thyme. Remove from heat. Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and white pepper. Cool completely.
Assemble Roulade: Lay chicken thighs flat. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Spread cooled farce evenly over each thigh, leaving a small border. Roll each thigh tightly. Secure with kitchen twine.

Cook Roulade: Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear roulades on all sides until golden brown. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F), about 12-15 minutes. Rest roulades 5 minutes. Remove twine. Slice each roulade into 2-3 thick medallions.

Plate: Spoon a quenelle of pomme purée onto each plate. Arrange 2-3 roulade medallions next to the purée. Spoon a generous pool of jus de volaille around the elements. Garnish with snipped chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Truffled Potato Puree, Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, sliced into two thick, moist pieces, rests alongside a velvety, bright white quenelle of truffled potato puree. Four vibrant green asparagus spears are artfully arranged. Delicate chervil sprigs are precisely placed for subtle freshness. The composition features abundant negative space on a pristine, round bone china plate with a subtle pattern. The chicken skin is golden and crisp, contrasting with the smooth, creamy puree. Asparagus retains its vibrant green hue. Colors are sophisticated and harmonious. The plate is set on a premium white Carrara marble surface. A crisp white linen napkin, folded precisely, lies to the left. Classic silver flatware is arranged. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting textures. The background is ultra-minimalist and blurred, emphasizing the dish as the sole focal point.

ingredients.name: Black Truffle (freshly shaved or high-quality truffle oil/paste)

instructions: Prepare potatoes: Peel potatoes. Cut into even 3cm chunks. Boil in heavily salted water until very tender. Drain thoroughly.

Make puree: Pass hot potatoes through a ricer or fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Add 80g unsalted butter and warm heavy cream. Whisk vigorously until smooth and emulsified. Season with salt. Stir in truffle. Keep warm over low heat.
Cook asparagus: Blanch asparagus spears in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

Sear chicken: Pat chicken breasts very dry. Season generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until deep golden brown and crispy.
Finish chicken: Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C. Cook for 8-12 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

Plate dish: Spoon a generous quenelle of truffled potato puree onto each plate. Slice each chicken breast into two or three thick, diagonal pieces. Place chicken alongside the puree. Artfully arrange asparagus spears. Garnish with chervil or microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Tataki Beef & Pineapple Canapés
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve exquisitely plated canapés arranged with architectural precision on a polished white Carrara marble slab. Each canapé features a single, thick-cut seared beef rectangular piece, cooked tataki-style to a rare pink interior, resting atop a delicate, translucent rice tuile. Adjacent to the beef, a small, precisely cut cube of compressed golden pineapple adds a vibrant counterpoint. A gleaming, deep ruby-red cherry-dark chocolate reduction is artfully dabbed onto the tuile beside the beef. A sprinkle of savory olive crumble and a thin, crisp mushroom chip provide textural contrast. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the sophisticated interplay of colors—rich brown, vibrant pink, golden yellow, deep red, and crisp white. Lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows.
instructions: Prepare Rice Tuiles: Rinse rice. Cook rice with 200 ml water until very soft. Blend cooked rice with 150 ml water and cornstarch until smooth. Strain mixture through fine-mesh sieve. Spread thin layers onto silicone mat or parchment paper. Bake at 150°C for 20-30 minutes until crisp and golden. Break into small, irregular tuiles.

Prepare Compressed Pineapple: Peel pineapple. Cut into 1 cm cubes. Place cubes in vacuum-seal bag. Vacuum seal. Chill for 30 minutes. If no vacuum sealer, press firmly between two plates with weight for 1 hour.

Prepare Cherry-Dark Chocolate Reduction: Combine cherries, 50 ml water, sugar, soy sauce, mirin, and rice vinegar in small saucepan. Simmer 10 minutes until cherries soften. Stir in dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Simmer gently until slightly thickened. Strain sauce through fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

Prepare Mushroom Crisps: Thinly slice King Oyster mushrooms (1-2 mm thick). Toss with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Bake at 160°C for 15-20 minutes until crisp. Alternatively, pan-fry until golden and crisp.

Prepare Olive Crumble: Finely mince pitted Kalamata olives. Spread on parchment paper. Bake at 100°C for 30-45 minutes until dry and crumbly. Pulse in food processor if needed to achieve crumbly texture.

Prepare Beef Tataki: Pat beef tenderloin dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat olive oil in heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until smoking. Sear beef on all sides for 1-2 minutes per side until deep golden brown crust forms. Remove from heat. Rest beef for 5 minutes. Cut into 1.5 cm thick rectangular pieces.

Assemble Canapés: Place rice tuiles on serving platter. Top each tuile with a seared beef piece. Arrange a compressed pineapple cube next to the beef. Drizzle a small amount of cherry-dark chocolate reduction onto the tuile. Sprinkle with olive crumble. Garnish with a mushroom crisp. Serve immediately.
notes: For desired doneness, sear beef to an internal temperature of 50-55°C for rare to medium-rare.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Chicken Thigh, Duck Fat Confit Potato, Thyme Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single seared sous vide chicken thigh, golden-browned and presented as a whole, succulent piece, rests slightly off-center on a pristine, matte white bone china plate. Beside it, three to four irregularly cut, golden-brown duck fat confit potato chunks are artfully arranged, their slightly crisp exteriors contrasting with the tender interior. A small, glossy pool of dark amber thyme chicken jus, perfectly reduced, is spooned onto the plate, partially beneath the chicken, catching the light. A single, delicate shard of crispy chicken skin stands upright, adding architectural height and texture. A tiny, vibrant sprig of fresh chervil provides a subtle touch of green. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space on the round plate. The setting is a polished white Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded into a triangle, is positioned at the top left. Dramatic, focused overhead lighting creates soft shadows that emphasize texture and depth, ensuring a refined, minimalist, and ultra-sophisticated presentation.
instructions: Preheat a sous vide water bath to 68°C (154°F). Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper. Place each thigh into a separate vacuum-sealable bag with one sprig of thyme. Vacuum seal bags.
Cook chicken thighs in the sous vide bath for 2 hours. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) if pan-searing is minimal.

While chicken cooks, prepare potatoes. Peel potatoes. Cut into irregular, rustic 2-3 cm chunks. Place potato chunks in a small saucepan. Cover with duck fat. Add smashed garlic clove and remaining thyme sprigs.

Gently heat potatoes over very low heat. Cook for 30-40 minutes until fork-tender but not falling apart. Do not boil. Remove potatoes from duck fat using a slotted spoon. Reserve duck fat for future use. Season potatoes lightly with salt.

Prepare the thyme jus. In a small saucepan, sauté minced shallot in a teaspoon of duck fat (from the confit) until translucent. Add chicken stock and two sprigs of fresh thyme. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half until slightly thickened and glossy. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Whisk in butter off heat. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.

Remove chicken from sous vide bags. Pat very dry with paper towels. Reserve rendered chicken skin. Carefully separate skin from one thigh to create a single crisp. Place skin between two sheets of parchment paper and two baking sheets. Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 10-15 minutes until golden and crisp. Break into a delicate shard.

Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of duck fat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 3-4 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Flip and sear flesh side for 1 minute. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.
Heat a separate pan with a small amount of duck fat. Sauté confit potato chunks over medium-high heat until golden and slightly crisp on all sides. Season with salt.

To plate, place one seared chicken thigh slightly off-center on a warm plate. Arrange 3-4 golden potato chunks artfully beside the chicken. Spoon a small pool of thyme jus onto the plate, partially under the chicken. Garnish with the crisp chicken skin shard and a tiny sprig of fresh chervil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Sausage and Potato Bake with Melted Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A generous scoop of the spicy sausage and potato bake is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Diced roasted potatoes, browned crumbled sausage, tender diced onions, and vibrant halved cherry tomatoes are visible, coated in a rich, savory sauce. Melted, bubbly mozzarella cheese forms a golden-brown crust over the top, with some strands stretching invitingly. Thin slices of fresh green chili and bright green chopped parsley are scattered over the cheese, adding pops of color and freshness. The dish showcases varied textures: crispy potato edges, tender sausage, and gooey cheese. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under even natural lighting, reflecting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes. Boil potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes. Drain well.

Remove sausage from casings. Crumble into a large oven-safe skillet or baking dish. Cook over medium-high heat until browned. Break up large pieces. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from skillet; set aside.
Dice onion. Thinly slice chili. Mince garlic.
Add olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion and sliced chili. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Add to skillet. Cook 3 minutes until slightly softened.
Return cooked sausage and par-cooked potatoes to the skillet. Add hot sauce, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Evenly spread mixture in the skillet. If not oven-safe, transfer to a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Shred mozzarella cheese. Evenly top the mixture with mozzarella.
Bake 15-20 minutes, until cheese is melted and bubbly golden brown.
Roughly chop fresh parsley. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosemary Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Garlic Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken thigh, skin-on and golden-brown, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its crispy texture. Beside it, a generous portion of roasted potato chunks, some with their skins on, are interspersed with tender, caramelized red onion wedges and softened garlic cloves. A light scattering of grated Parmesan cheese coats the potatoes, adding a subtle creamy white hue. A glossy, rich pan sauce is drizzled over both the chicken and potatoes, creating appealing highlights. Fresh rosemary sprigs are placed as a garnish. The arrangement is balanced, with moderate negative space, presented on a simple wooden table surface, illuminated by natural, even lighting. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate, completing the modern bistro setting.

ingredients.name: Large potatoes (e.g., Maris Piper or Russet)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Halve 4 garlic cloves. Roughly chop red onion into large wedges.
Toss potato chunks, garlic halves, and onion wedges with 30 ml olive oil, 2 rosemary sprigs (leaves picked and roughly chopped), salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Spread in a single layer.
Roast potatoes for 25 minutes, or until fork-tender and slightly golden.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Pick leaves from remaining 2 rosemary sprigs and finely chop.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown. Do not move chicken.
Flip chicken thighs. Add remaining 2 whole garlic cloves (smashed) and chopped rosemary to the skillet. Reduce heat to medium.
Cook for another 5 minutes, basting chicken with pan drippings.
Transfer skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from oven. Transfer chicken to a cutting board. Let rest for 5 minutes.
While chicken rests, place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add chicken stock to deglaze, scraping up browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Stir in butter until melted and sauce slightly thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Add roasted potatoes and onions to a large bowl. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan cheese. Toss gently to combine.
Portion roasted potatoes onto individual plates. Place one whole chicken thigh beside potatoes. Drizzle chicken and potatoes with pan sauce. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Veal Medallions with Roasted Root Vegetables and Fermented Cauliflower
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented with minimalistic elegance on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, resting on a light, reclaimed wood surface. A single, perfectly seared veal medallion, its exterior a rich golden-brown, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Beside it, a thoughtful arrangement of roasted vegetables includes thick-cut carrot batons, rustic potato wedges, and large, tender cauliflower florets, each bearing a light char and caramelized edges. Their earthy tones of deep orange, golden-brown, and creamy white create a natural palette. A glossy, rich mushroom-Dijon jus is generously spooned over the veal and vegetables, adding depth and sheen. Scattered around the plate are a few bright, almost translucent florets of fermented cauliflower, offering a vibrant counterpoint and delicate tang. A sprig of fresh thyme provides a touch of verdant green. The composition emphasizes natural textures and clean lines, with ample negative space. The setting includes an undyed linen napkin and classic French flatware, under soft, natural lighting, with a subtle, clean background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a light, crusty baguette.
Pair with a glass of dry French red wine.
instructions: Prepare fermented cauliflower: Cut half cauliflower into small florets. Place in a clean jar. Boil 200ml water with 100ml white wine vinegar and 5g salt. Pour hot brine over cauliflower. Seal jar. Let cool. Ferment at room temperature 3-5 days. Refrigerate once fermented.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Prepare roasted vegetables: Peel carrots and potatoes. Cut carrots into thick batons. Cut potatoes into wedges. Separate remaining cauliflower into large florets. Halve garlic head horizontally.
Toss carrots, potatoes, large cauliflower florets, and garlic with 30ml olive oil, salt, pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast vegetables for 30-40 minutes. Turn halfway. Vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
Prepare veal: Pat veal medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear veal medallions 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove veal from skillet. Keep warm.
Prepare mushroom jus: Add butter to the same skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and remaining fresh thyme sprigs. Sauté 5-7 minutes until browned.
Pour in beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Stir in Dijon mustard. Reduce heat. Simmer 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate: Arrange roasted carrots, potatoes, and cauliflower on plates. Place a veal medallion beside vegetables. Spoon mushroom jus over veal and vegetables. Drain and add a few fermented cauliflower florets to each plate.
notes: Fermentation time can vary based on desired tanginess.
Use vegetable scraps for homemade stock to reduce waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Roasted Potatoes and Herb Pan Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Roasted Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Crispy, golden-brown roasted potato wedges are artfully arranged in a neat pile on one side of the plate. Adjacent to the potatoes rests a perfectly seared, whole chicken thigh, its skin a deep, glistening golden-brown, showing a crisp, inviting texture. A light, amber-hued pan sauce, enriched with herbs, is generously spooned over the chicken and gently pools around the base. The dish is garnished with a vibrant sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley over both the chicken and potatoes, alongside a small, bright yellow lemon wedge positioned near the chicken. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface with a folded cotton napkin placed beside it, under natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable bistro setting.

ingredients.name: Small potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or red potatoes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2cm wedges. In a large bowl, toss potatoes with 30ml olive oil, half the minced garlic, salt, pepper, and leaves from one rosemary sprig and one thyme sprig.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden brown.
Pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Do not move chicken.
Flip chicken thighs. Add remaining minced garlic, rosemary sprig, and thyme sprig to the skillet around the chicken. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven.
Roast chicken for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) at the thickest part.
Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside on a cutting board to rest for 5 minutes.

Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add chicken broth to deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Squeeze in juice from half a lemon. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly reduces.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley into the pan sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Plate roasted potatoes. Place one whole chicken thigh next to potatoes. Spoon pan sauce over the chicken and potatoes. Garnish with a lemon wedge and extra fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Lemon Herb Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crispy, is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken rests on one side of the plate, its skin glistening from roasting. Beside it, a generous portion of golden-yellow potato wedges, each with a crisp exterior and tender interior, is arranged organically. Interspersed among the potatoes are roasted whole garlic cloves and thin, caramelized lemon slices. A few fresh sprigs of vibrant green rosemary and thyme are placed thoughtfully over the chicken and potatoes as garnish. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are positioned beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, even natural light, creating a professional yet inviting ambiance. The background is minimal, keeping focus on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon vinaigrette.
Offer crusty artisan bread to soak up the pan juices.
Pair with a dry white wine like Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2.5 cm wedges or large chunks. Mince 3 garlic cloves. Keep remaining 3 garlic cloves whole.
Halve the lemon. Slice one half into thin rounds. Juice the other half.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the skillet. Add potato wedges, minced garlic, whole garlic cloves, and rosemary and thyme sprigs. Toss to coat.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, skin-side up, nestled among the potatoes.
Pour chicken broth and lemon juice over the chicken and potatoes. Arrange lemon slices on top of chicken and potatoes.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Potatoes should be tender and golden.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Adjust roasting time based on chicken thigh size and oven calibration.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin crispy and glistening, rests off-center on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, several rustic roasted potato wedges, approximately 2-3 cm thick, are scattered casually, their edges slightly caramelized and interiors tender. Thin, charred lemon slices and whole roasted garlic cloves are nestled among the chicken and potatoes, adding pops of color and texture. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley garnishes the dish, enhancing its freshness. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware, under natural, soft lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread to sop up the flavorful pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into rustic wedges, approximately 2-3 cm thick.
Slice one lemon into thin rounds. Halve the remaining lemon.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, rosemary sprigs, thyme sprigs, and unpeeled garlic cloves. Drizzle with 45ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange potatoes and herbs in a single layer in the pan. Place lemon slices over the potatoes.
Nestle chicken thighs, skin-side up, among the potatoes. Drizzle chicken skin with remaining 15ml olive oil.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Remove pan from oven. Pour chicken broth into the pan around the chicken and potatoes. Squeeze juice from the halved lemon over the dish.
Return to oven. Continue roasting for 20-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish the dish with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ajillo con Patatas Crujientes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Ajillo con Patatas Crujientes is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, bone-in chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is placed centrally. Beside it, a generous pile of rustic, golden-brown potato chunks, their surfaces crisp, are neatly arranged. A rich, reddish-brown garlic and paprika sauce, glistening slightly, is spooned over and around the chicken. The dish is garnished with a vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley and delicate lemon zest. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting highlights the dish's appealing textures and warm colors against a subtly blurred restaurant background. No fanned meat; chicken is served whole.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pan) for dipping in the sauce
Accompany with a small dish of olives or alioli
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into 2cm chunks. Place in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook 8-10 minutes until just tender. Drain well.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Add potatoes. Cook 15-20 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and crispy. Season with salt. Remove from pan, set aside.

Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the same pan. Add chicken thighs, skin-side down. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Sear 5 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pan, set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced garlic to the pan. Cook 1-2 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Do not burn.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in smoked paprika and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.

Return chicken to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in sauce. Cover the pan. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Bake 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Remove pan from oven. Stir in lemon juice and zest. Sprinkle with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve chicken immediately with crispy potatoes.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken with Crispy Smashed Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The Mediterranean Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A single, generously portioned chicken thigh or drumstick sits prominently, its skin deeply caramelized to a rich golden-brown with visible specks of roasted herbs. Beside it, a cluster of golden, crispy smashed potatoes are irregularly shaped, their blistered skin revealing a fluffy interior. Bright yellow roasted lemon wedges are scattered nearby, along with vibrant green sprigs of fresh rosemary and thyme. A light sheen of pan juices glistens on the plate. The composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and standard flatware, evoking a relaxed, yet refined bistro atmosphere under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with lemon vinaigrette.
Offer crusty artisanal bread for dipping in the flavorful pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Wash and halve or quarter small potatoes. In a large bowl, toss potatoes with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Arrange potatoes in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Mince garlic cloves. Chop rosemary and thyme leaves.
In the same bowl, combine remaining 50 ml olive oil, juice and zest of one lemon, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and chopped thyme.
Add seasoned chicken pieces to the marinade. Toss to coat evenly.
Place chicken pieces among the potatoes on the baking tray. Add wedges from the second lemon to the tray.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip chicken pieces. Pour chicken stock into the baking tray around the ingredients.
Continue roasting for another 25-35 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden-crisp.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest on the tray for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken and roasted potatoes rests on a clean white round porcelain plate. The boneless, skin-on chicken thigh, golden-brown with a crispy skin, is presented whole, positioned slightly off-center. Beside it, a generous cluster of halved or quartered baby potatoes, roasted to a golden-brown with a slight crisp on the exterior and a fluffy interior, are arranged naturally. A light, golden-hued pan sauce is delicately spooned over the chicken and potatoes, adding a subtle sheen without pooling. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the dish for a vibrant color contrast and freshness. A small, vibrant lemon wedge is placed beside the chicken. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, with a subtly blurred background suggesting a casual, elegant bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Wash baby potatoes. Halve or quarter larger ones. Toss with 30ml olive oil, leaves from 1 rosemary sprig, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 25-30 minutes. They should be tender and golden.
Pat chicken thighs very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deep golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Add thinly sliced shallots, minced garlic, and remaining rosemary and thyme sprigs to the pan.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium heat. Add white wine (if using) or 50ml chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits.
Pour in remaining chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce liquid by half.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and juice from half a lemon. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
To serve, arrange roasted potatoes on a plate. Place one whole chicken thigh beside them. Spoon the pan sauce over the chicken and potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken with Paprika Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken with Paprika Potatoes is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two whole, braised chicken thighs with crisped, golden-brown skin are nestled amidst rustic, irregular chunks of tender, paprika-stained potatoes. Vibrant red and yellow bell pepper strips, along with softened onion, are interspersed throughout the rich, reddish-brown tomato and paprika sauce that lightly coats all ingredients. A small pool of the savory sauce collects at the base of the chicken and potatoes. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of coarsely chopped fresh green parsley, providing a bright color contrast. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, with a folded cotton napkin positioned beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish. A small terracotta cazuela, containing extra sauce or a side of crusty bread, is subtly blurred in the background, hinting at traditional Spanish dining.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pan de pueblo) to soak up the rich sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
Red bell pepper, cored and cut into 2 cm strips
Yellow bell pepper, cored and cut into 2 cm strips

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the pan. Add chopped onion and sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and bell pepper strips. Cook for 5-7 minutes until peppers soften slightly.
Stir in smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chopped tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan. Nestle chicken among the vegetables and liquid.
Add potato chunks to the pan. Ensure potatoes are mostly submerged in the liquid.
Cover the pan, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and potatoes are tender. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C.
Uncover and simmer for an additional 5-10 minutes if sauce needs to thicken slightly.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
The sauce should be rustic and flavorful, not overly thick.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Paprika Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Roasted Chicken Thighs with Paprika Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. One golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh sits prominently. Around it, rustic wedges of roasted waxy potatoes are arranged, their skins a rich reddish-orange from the paprika. Scattered fresh green parsley adds a vibrant contrast. The chicken skin is visibly crisp, while the potato wedges show tender, slightly browned edges. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and warm colors. A simple white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The background is a subtly blurred, modern bistro setting, emphasizing the dish as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Pair with a glass of Spanish red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (fan 180°C).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs, skin-side down, in the hot skillet. Sear 8-10 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip. Sear 2 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
While chicken sears, cut potatoes into 2 cm wedges. Slice onion thinly. Mince garlic.
Add remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil to the skillet. Add potato wedges and sliced onion. Sauté 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, smoked paprika, and rosemary. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, skin-side up, nestling them among the potatoes.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Roast 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender.
Remove from oven. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the chicken and potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
Serve immediately with crusty bread.
traditional_techniques: Use of Pimentón de la Vera (smoked paprika)

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Chicken and Potatoes rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, appearing whole and robust, is the focal point. Surrounding the chicken are substantial, rustic chunks of tender, golden-yellow potatoes, some with slightly browned edges. Interspersed among them are vibrant strips of softened red and green bell peppers and translucent slices of onion. A rich, reddish-brown braising liquid, subtly thickened, coats the ingredients. The dish is generously garnished with bright green, freshly chopped parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is inviting, with moderate negative space, showcasing the natural textures and warm colors of the components. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware, under natural, even lighting, evoking a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pan) to soak up the flavorful sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette complements the richness of the dish.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or red potatoes)

instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add sliced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and saffron (if using). Bring mixture to a simmer.
Cut potatoes into 3-4 cm chunks. Add potato chunks to the pot.
Nestle chicken pieces back into the pot with skin-side up.
Cover the pot. Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and potatoes are tender.
Remove lid for the last 10 minutes to allow chicken skin to re-crisp slightly.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish with parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Blanc with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh and a drumstick, both with golden-brown, crispy skin, are centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is partially submerged in a rich, glossy, light-brown white wine sauce. The sauce is studded with tender, whole pearl onions, rustic quartered cremini mushrooms, and vibrant orange carrot batons. Adjacent to the chicken are several roasted new potato halves, golden and slightly crusted. The dish is generously garnished with fresh, finely chopped green parsley. The plate rests on a simple dark wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, creating a refined yet approachable bistro ambiance. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the delicious sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken pieces dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Add bacon lardons. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve rendered fat.
Add chicken pieces to the pot, skin-side down. Sear until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pot. Discard excess fat, leaving about 2 tablespoons.
Add pearl onions, quartered mushrooms, and carrot batons to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until lightly browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in chicken broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Return chicken and bacon to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 30 minutes.
While chicken braises, toss new potatoes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast in the oven for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown.
After 30 minutes, remove pot from oven. Remove chicken and bacon from pot. Keep warm. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
In a small bowl, combine butter and flour to make a beurre manié. Whisk small pieces of beurre manié into the simmering sauce until desired thickness is achieved. Simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Return chicken and bacon to the pot. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve individual portions of chicken and sauce with roasted potatoes. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Garlic Chicken with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Garlic Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. A bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, cooked to a rich golden-brown with visible crispy skin, is the focal point. Surrounding the chicken are several rustic, golden-brown roasted potato wedges, their edges slightly crisped. A generous scattering of aromatic, lightly browned garlic cloves is interspersed among the chicken and potatoes. A glistening, light amber pan sauce, rich with chicken drippings, white wine, and paprika, is spooned over the chicken and pooled around the potatoes. The dish is garnished with a vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley and a bright lemon wedge placed beside the chicken. The overall impression is one of comforting, robust flavors and textures, with natural, inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (like a baguette) to soak up the flavorful sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Pair with a glass of dry Spanish white wine or a light-bodied red.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.quantity: 1 whole head, peeled, cloves lightly smashed

ingredients.name: Dry white wine (e.g., Fino sherry or Sauvignon Blanc)
Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1, half sliced for garnish, half for juice

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into rustic wedges. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 20 minutes.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crisp.
Flip chicken. Add smashed garlic cloves to the skillet around the chicken. Cook for 2 minutes.
Deglaze the skillet with white wine, scraping up any browned bits.
Add chicken broth to the skillet. Bring to a simmer.

Transfer the skillet with chicken and garlic to the oven alongside the potatoes. Roast for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Remove skillet from oven. Transfer chicken and potatoes to a serving platter. Cover loosely to keep warm.
Place skillet back on stovetop over medium-high heat. Reduce pan sauce for 3-5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in chopped parsley and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice into the sauce.
Spoon sauce over chicken and potatoes. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents roasted chicken thighs and potato wedges on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thighs are placed centrally. Around them are scattered golden-edged potato wedges. Fresh lemon wedges, with bright yellow rinds, are arranged beside the chicken. A light drizzle of pan juices coats the chicken and potatoes. The dish is garnished with vibrant green fresh oregano leaves. The overall composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple light wooden table, with a linen napkin and classic silver cutlery beside the plate. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene. A small bowl of creamy white tzatziki and a fresh Greek salad are placed slightly in the background as cultural accompaniments.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of tzatziki sauce.
Accompany with a traditional Greek salad.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken with 3g salt and 1g black pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into 2 cm thick wedges.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges with 30ml olive oil, 5g dried oregano, 2 minced garlic cloves, 10ml lemon juice, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Add chicken thighs to the same bowl. Drizzle with remaining 30ml olive oil, 5g dried oregano, 2 minced garlic cloves, and 20ml lemon juice. Toss to coat.
Arrange chicken and potatoes in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Ensure chicken skin side is up.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Pour 120ml chicken broth over potatoes. Stir potatoes gently.
Return to oven. Roast for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh oregano or parsley. Serve immediately with pan juices.
notes: Always ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Squeeze additional fresh lemon juice over the dish before serving for extra brightness.
traditional_techniques: Marinating with olive oil and lemon

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Loaded Potato Bites
recipes.visual_description: A platter of golden-brown Homestyle Loaded Potato Bites rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. Each potato half is a rustic, comforting boat, generously filled with a savory mixture of ground beef and ground chicken, subtly combined with creamy mashed potato flesh. The top is covered with a melted, bubbly layer of golden-orange cheddar cheese, slightly browned at the edges from baking. A sprinkle of vibrant green, thinly sliced green onions provides a fresh contrast. The potato skins are visibly crispy and slightly wrinkled, showcasing their baked texture. The pieces are arranged casually on an everyday ceramic serving platter with natural imperfections, spaced naturally without overcrowding. A simple, folded cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. The overall scene is one of inviting, homely comfort, as if just served from a family kitchen.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash potatoes. Pierce skins several times with a fork. Bake directly on oven rack for 45-60 minutes, or until tender.
While potatoes bake, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add finely diced onion. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add ground beef and ground chicken to the skillet. Cook, breaking up meat with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature. Drain excess fat.
Add minced garlic, Worcestershire sauce, and dried thyme to the meat mixture. Cook for 1 minute more, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.

Once potatoes are cool enough to handle, cut each potato in half lengthwise. Carefully scoop out most of the flesh, leaving a 5mm border in the skin to maintain structure. Place scooped flesh in a bowl.
Lightly mash the scooped potato flesh. If desired, add milk and butter for creaminess. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine the mashed potato flesh with the cooked meat mixture. Mix well.
Fill each potato skin half generously with the meat and potato mixture. Arrange filled potato skins on a baking sheet.
Sprinkle grated cheddar cheese over each filled potato skin.
Return to oven and bake for 10-15 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and potato skins are heated through.
Remove from oven. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Herb Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous serving of Potato and Herb Salad rests on a simple, everyday ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim, showcasing its homely appeal. The potatoes are roughly diced into 2 cm cubes, their creamy, pale yellow interior contrasting with specks of green chopped fresh parsley and thyme, and small, vibrant purple-red pieces of finely diced red onion. A light, glistening coating of the oil-based dressing subtly coats each potato cube, indicating a well-mixed texture. The salad is casually mounded, allowing some ingredients to overlap naturally. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, suggesting a relaxed family meal. A simple, folded cloth napkin and basic flatware are placed nearby, enhancing the unpretentious, comforting atmosphere.
instructions: Wash potatoes thoroughly. Place potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Add a generous pinch of salt.
Bring water to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium. Simmer until potatoes are fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes. Do not overcook.
Drain potatoes immediately. Let them cool slightly, about 10 minutes. Peel if desired, or leave skin on for rustic feel.
Dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper. This is the dressing.
Add diced potatoes to the bowl with the dressing. Add finely diced red onion, chopped fresh thyme, and chopped fresh parsley.
Gently toss all ingredients until potatoes are evenly coated. Be careful not to mash the potatoes.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Bistro-Style Braised Beef and Chicken with Garlic Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Bistro-Style Braised Beef and Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The plate holds one golden-brown, bone-in chicken thigh alongside two to three rich, dark brown braised beef cubes, approximately 4-5 cm. A generous pour of the glossy, deep red wine sauce cascades over the meats, pooling slightly on the plate. Scattered beside the meats are golden-brown roasted potato chunks, 3-4 cm, with a slightly crisp exterior and tender interior, some exhibiting a light garlic char. Visible within the sauce are tender, rustic diced carrots, celery, and quartered mushrooms. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of coarsely chopped fresh green parsley, providing a vibrant contrast. The setting features a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and classic French-style flatware, under natural, even lighting. The background is minimal, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the rich sauce
Traditionally accompanied by a simple green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Season beef cubes generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef cubes on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.

Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pot. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp. Flip and sear other side. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter, diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Stir in beef broth, fresh thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Return seared beef to the pot. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 1.5 hours.
Add seared chicken thighs and quartered mushrooms to the pot with the beef. Ensure chicken is submerged in liquid.
Return to oven and continue to braise for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef and chicken are fork-tender and reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While meats braise, prepare potatoes: In a large bowl, toss potato chunks with the whole head of garlic (unpeeled, cut in half horizontally), a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes and garlic on a baking sheet. Roast in the preheated oven for 30-40 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden brown and tender.
Remove bay leaves and thyme sprigs from the braise before serving.
Serve the braised beef and chicken generously with its rich sauce alongside the roasted garlic potatoes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on an off-white ceramic plate with a rustic, uneven rim. Two golden-brown, bone-in chicken pieces (thigh and drumstick), skin crisp from roasting, are centered. Substantial potato wedges, deeply caramelized and tender, are scattered around the chicken, some overlapping. Thick wedges of roasted onion, softened and sweet, are interspersed. Bright yellow lemon slices, slightly charred, peek out. The dish is garnished with fresh chopped parsley and small rosemary sprigs. The arrangement is casual, asymmetrical, filling the plate adequately. The scene is on a well-used wooden dining table, lit by warm kitchen light. A folded linen napkin and basic silver flatware rest beside the plate. A small, rustic bowl of olive oil and crusty bread sit nearby, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up the pan juices.
Enjoy family-style, with dishes passed around the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, potato wedges, and onion wedges.
Add olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, thyme leaves, salt, and pepper.
Squeeze juice from one lemon over the ingredients. Toss well to coat everything evenly.
Arrange chicken and vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Place lemon slices among the chicken and vegetables.
Roast for 45-55 minutes.
Turn chicken and vegetables halfway through cooking.
Chicken is cooked when internal temperature reaches 75°C and juices run clear. Potatoes should be tender and golden.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: For extra crispiness, broil for the last 5 minutes.
Adjust herbs based on preference; oregano also works well.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Potato Curry served in a shallow ceramic bowl on a dark wooden table. The chicken is cut into large 4cm chunks, coated in a thick, vibrant orange-brown gravy. Beside the chicken, 3cm potato cubes appear soft with rounded edges from simmering. The curry sits naturally over a mound of fluffy, long-grain white basmati rice. A functional garnish of chopped fresh cilantro is scattered on top. The plate is accompanied by a small side of lime wedges and pickled red onions. Lighting is warm and directional, highlighting the steam and glossy sauce texture. The arrangement is casual and asymmetrical, showing the entire plate in a lived-in kitchen setting with authentic utensils.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges for acidity.
Include a side of pickled red onions.
Eat with a traditional spoon or clean hands.
instructions: Wash rice. Soak in water for 20 minutes.
Boil rice in salted water until tender. Drain.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 3cm cubes.
Cut chicken into 4cm chunks.
Heat oil in a pot.
Sauté diced onion until golden.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir 1 minute.
Add turmeric, cumin, and coriander. Stir well.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned.
Add potato cubes and chopped tomato.
Add 250ml water.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in garam masala and salt.
Serve curry over rice.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches a safe 75°C.
Use waxy potatoes to ensure they hold their shape during simmering.
Soaking the rice ensures long, separate grains.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Lemon Herb Chicken with Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Mediterranean Lemon Herb Chicken with Roasted Potatoes is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin crispy and glistening, rests centrally. Beside it are several golden-brown potato wedges, their skins slightly blistered and interiors fluffy. Scattered around the plate are vibrant red roasted cherry tomatoes and softened, caramelized red onion wedges. Fresh sprigs of roasted rosemary and thyme are nestled among the ingredients, along with a few charred lemon slices. The dish has a natural, inviting arrangement, showcasing varied textures from crispy chicken skin and potato exteriors to tender chicken and soft vegetables. A light sheen of pan juices reflects natural light. The plate is set on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin beside it, under even, natural lighting. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fresh Greek salad.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve lemons. Squeeze juice from one lemon half. Slice remaining lemon halves into thick rounds.
In a large roasting pan, toss chicken thighs with 30ml olive oil, half the smashed garlic, dried oregano, salt, and pepper.
Cut potatoes into 2-3 cm wedges. Toss potatoes in a separate bowl with remaining 30ml olive oil, remaining smashed garlic, salt, and pepper. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs.
Arrange chicken, potatoes, whole cherry tomatoes, and red onion wedges in the roasting pan.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip chicken and potatoes. Add lemon slices to the pan. Continue roasting for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Squeeze roasted lemon halves over the chicken and potatoes before serving.
notes: Ensure potatoes are cut uniformly for even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Creamy Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, whole and plump, rests prominently on the right side of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Adjacent, a rectangular portion of creamy potato gratin is placed; its top is bubbly, golden, and crisped, revealing layers of thinly sliced, tender potatoes. A small cluster of vibrant green beans, lightly buttered, is neatly arranged on the left, providing contrasting color and texture. The dish showcases warm browns and golds from the chicken and gratin, contrasted by the bright green of the beans. The chicken skin is crisp, gratin creamy, and beans tender-crisp. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even light illuminates the dish. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Slice peeled potatoes thinly, approximately 2mm thick.
Rub an oven-safe gratin dish with 20g butter.
Layer potato slices in the dish. Season each layer with salt, black pepper, minced garlic, and fresh thyme leaves.
Pour heavy cream evenly over the potatoes. Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese on top.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until the gratin is golden brown, bubbly, and potatoes are tender when pierced.
Season chicken breasts generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil and remaining 10g butter in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4 minutes per side, until golden brown crust forms.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Continue cooking chicken for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While chicken cooks, bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add trimmed green beans.
Blanch green beans for 3 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Rest cooked chicken breasts for 5 minutes before plating.
Cut the potato gratin into four equal rectangular portions.
Plate one whole pan-seared chicken breast alongside a portion of potato gratin and a cluster of blanched green beans.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ajillo con Patatas Asadas
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Ajillo con Patatas Asadas is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. Two golden-brown, pan-seared chicken thighs, with visibly crispy skin, are placed prominently. Alongside them, a generous scattering of rustic, roasted potato wedges displays a rich, golden-brown hue and crisp edges, contrasting with their fluffy interiors. A glossy, garlic-infused pan sauce glistens over the chicken and potatoes. The dish is garnished with a vibrant sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space, showcasing the textures and rich colors. A white cotton napkin rests beside the plate, and the background is a soft, natural, evenly lit restaurant setting with a casual atmosphere, hinting at a bistro environment. A small, rustic ceramic bowl for extra sauce or a small basket of crusty bread might be subtly visible in the background, enhancing the Spanish authenticity without distracting from the main dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the garlic pan sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Pair with a dry Spanish white wine like Albariño or Verdejo.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into thick wedges. Place in a large bowl.
Add 30 ml olive oil, smoked paprika, rosemary sprigs, salt, and pepper to potatoes. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and golden brown, flipping halfway.
While potatoes roast, pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
